10.1016/j.cej.2026.177865.abstract: Interzeolite conversion (IZC) remains a central challenge in the synthesis of metastable zeolites, where even minor fractions of undesired phases can compromise catalytic performance and industrial value. Typical ex situ process monitoring by X-ray diffraction (XRD), although effective for structural characterization, requires sample extraction and expert analysis, preventing real-time intervention in industrial synthesis and complicating the capture of metastable phases. In this work, we demonstrate the use of in situ Raman spectroscopy as an inline process analytical technology to monitor the transformation of faujasite (FAU) into gismondine (GIS) during hydrothermal crystallization, probing solid and liquid phases. Non-negative least squares (NNLS) algorithm was employed to track the relative abundances of FAU and GIS throughout the crystallization process using only the pure FAU and GIS Raman spectra in operational conditions as inputs. The resulting Raman-derived FAU and GIS phase fractions show strong agreement with XRD-based Rietveld refinements, enabling continuous tracking of crystalline phase evolution without invasive sampling. Complementary DFT-based vibrational calculations provide molecular-level interpretation of framework-specific Raman signatures, confirming the structural origin of characteristic bands. A preliminary multivariate regression model further demonstrates the feasibility of predicting GIS weight fractions directly from Raman spectra. Overall, the results establish Raman spectroscopy as a robust, non-destructive, and temporally resolved tool for quantifying zeolite crystallization kinetics. The methodology is directly applicable to industrial process monitoring and offers a foundation for future real-time control strategies in zeolite synthesis and other crystallization-driven chemical manufacturing processes.
10.1016/j.cej.2026.177865.title: Process monitoring of zeolite crystallization: Bridging in situ Raman spectroscopy, ex situ XRD, and predictive machine learning models

10.1016/j.foodhyd.2025.111843.abstract: Cashew apple bagasse (CAB) is increasingly recognized for its role in promoting a circular bioeconomy. Emerging research on this agro-industrial byproduct highlights its nutritional benefits and its versatility as a biomass platform for developing bioproducts through innovative technologies. This study investigates the impact of ultrasound on natural protein-polysaccharide complexes (PPC) of CAB and aims to understand the underlying mechanisms behind their modified functional properties. Ultrasound induced two major transformations: a modification of the composition through the extraction of new proteins, leading to a protein content increase from 18.04 % to 20.64 %, and a structural reorganization of the constituents, characterized by an increase in β-sheet level from 26.75 % to 65.65 %. The reduction in polysaccharide content from 32.52 % to 25.24 % and the enrichment in proteins reduced protein-polysaccharide interactions, while protein-protein interactions were strengthened through increased surface hydrophobicity (rising from 131 to 304) and enhanced interfacial elasticity (from ∼11 mN/m to ∼30 mN/m). These rearrangements led to an improvement in interfacial properties, including a reduction of interfacial tension measured by tracker from 16 mN/m to 6 mN/m, despite an overall decrease in solubility (from 27.8 % to 23.6 %). Ultrasound enabled the formation of a more robust complex, enhancing the long-term emulsifying stability index (ESI) from 237 min to 262 min, although the initial emulsifying activity index (EAI) was moderately reduced (from 26.1 to 24.6 m2/g). Correlation analyses, including heatmap visualization, revealed strong interrelations between PPC secondary structure, surface hydrophobicity, interfacial properties, and solubility, key factors influencing emulsion functionality. These findings highlight ultrasound-assisted extraction as an effective approach to tailor PPC composition and structure, enabling their use in innovative, sustainable plant-based food formulations that can overcome limitations of traditional protein emulsifiers.
10.1016/j.foodhyd.2025.111843.title: Ultrasound-enhanced extraction and structural dynamics of protein-polysaccharide complexes from cashew apple bagasse: structure–function relationship

10.1016/j.cej.2026.177517.abstract: Separating liquid–liquid dispersions in gravity settlers is critical in chemical, pharmaceutical, and recycling processes. The dense-packed zone height is an important performance and safety indicator but it is often expensive and impractical to measure due to optical limitations. We propose a framework to estimate phase heights by combining a PINN model with readily available volume flow measurements, without requiring phase height measurements during deployment. To this end, a physics-informed neural network (PINN) is first pretrained on synthetic data and physics equations derived from a low-fidelity (approximate) mechanistic model to reduce the need for extensive experimental data. While the mechanistic model is used to generate synthetic training data, only volume balance equations are used in the PINN, as incorporating droplet coalescence and sedimentation submodels would be computationally prohibitive. The pretrained PINN is then fine-tuned with scarce experimental phase height and flow-rate data to capture the actual dynamics of the separator. We then deploy the differentiable PINN as a predictive model in an Extended Kalman Filter inspired state estimation framework, enabling the phase heights to be tracked and updated using flow-rate measurements only. We first test the two-stage trained PINN by forward simulation from a known initial state against the mechanistic model and a non-pretrained PINN. We then evaluate phase height estimation performance with the filter, comparing the two-stage trained PINN with a two-stage trained purely data-driven neural network. All model types are trained and evaluated using ensembles to account for model parameter uncertainty. In all evaluations, the two-stage trained PINN yields the most accurate phase-height estimates.
10.1016/j.cej.2026.177517.title: Estimating dense-packed zone height in liquid–liquid separation: A physics-informed neural network approach
10.1016/j.cej.2026.177517.source: ScienceDirect official citation and abstract BibTeX export

10.1016/j.cej.2025.171870.abstract: Although design of reactor geometry is a crucial task, most existing optimization studies have considered only operating parameters on a fixed geometry, due to the high computational cost of computational fluid dynamics (CFD). To address this, we present an inverse-design framework that does not require CFD data by incorporating a geometry-aware learning concept into a physics-informed neural network (PINN), which can generalize flow fields across any arbitrary geometry. The PINN predicted velocity profiles with a relative root-mean-squared error (RMSE) below 4 % across six geometries. Additionally, a compartment model was employed to efficiently couple the velocity profiles with chemical reactions, and the PINN-based compartment model successfully reproduced ethylene distribution in a polymerization reactor within 3 min at a given blade design. To further leverage this, we jointly optimized the blade geometry and operating parameters to produce a desired molecular weight distribution (MWD). The optimized blade design and condition achieved an MWD matching the target, with an R2 of 0.994. It does not require CFD data for training and is generally applicable to any non-ideal reactor design problems, confirming the potential of generalizable PINNs as a practical tool for reactor geometry optimization without repeated CFD simulations.
10.1016/j.cej.2025.171870.title: Simultaneous optimization of reactor design and operating conditions using geometry-aware physics-informed neural network

10.1016/j.cej.2025.171550.abstract: Photonic crystal (PC) biosensors have been widely used in protein detection, leveraging their cost-effectiveness and operational simplicity. However, they confront challenges in balancing detection sensitivity and analysis speed. In this paper, an intelligent biosensing platform integrating a PC-plasmonic nanoantenna (PC-PN) coupling system with an optimized UNet model was constructed. By precisely tuning the localized surface plasmon resonance (LSPR) properties of Au@Ag-Au core-shell nanoparticles, efficient coupling with the intrinsic resonance of PC is achieved. Angle-resolved spectroscopy (ARS) was employed to acquire multi-dimensional spectral datasets in 10 s, replacing conventional single-point reflectance spectral measurements that require 1–2 h. An optimized UNet model, featuring hierarchical feature fusion and anti-noise convolutional layers, was designed to establish a regression model for target protein concentration. Using interleukin-6 (IL-6) as target protein, the system exhibits linear detection over the range of 5–100 pg/mL, with a detection limit as low as 5 pg/mL. Notably, the entire detection process, from biosensing interface identification to AI-driven concentration prediction, can be completed within 15 min, which satisfies the requirements of both high sensitivity and rapid PC-based sensing.
10.1016/j.cej.2025.171550.title: Photonic crystal-plasmonic nanoantenna coupling biosensor for AI assisted protein biomarker detection

10.1016/j.cej.2025.171477.abstract: Electrocatalytic nitrogen reduction has emerged as a highly promising and environmentally friendly approach for ammonia synthesis. In this study, density functional theory (DFT) calculations were systematically performed to explore the catalytic performance of MM-Salen-COF-based diatomic catalysts in the nitric oxide reduction reaction (NORR). A total of 21 transition metals (TMs) from 3d to 5d (TM = V, Cr, Mn, Fe, Co, Ni, Cu, Zn, Nb, Mo, Ru, Rh, Pd, Ag, Ta, W, Re, Os, Ir, Pt, Au) were screened via a three-step computational approach. Subsequently, ten heteronuclear MM'-Salen-COFs catalysts were further designed by combining promising homonuclear catalysts. The performance indicators, including structural stability and catalytic activity, were thoroughly assessed and compared. Notably, heteronuclear Cu/Ag, Cu/Cr and Ag/Cr catalysts exhibited comparable or even superior performance relative to their homonuclear counterparts. Furthermore, a machine learning (ML) model was employed to predict NO adsorption energies using computationally derived descriptors. This combined DFT and ML approach provides valuable insights for rational NORR catalyst design, opening pathways toward novel diatomic catalyst development.
10.1016/j.cej.2025.171477.title: Enhancing electrocatalytic nitric oxide reduction to ammonia on diatomic Salen-COFs: Integrated density functional theory and machine learning studies

10.1016/j.cej.2025.172198.abstract: Intelligently designing molecules based on composite material properties is the ideal goal across many areas of materials science. For solid propellants, where high-energy molecules critically affect performance, property-driven molecular design is highly desirable but remains unrealized. To this end, we present an AI workflow that integrates property prediction, feature attribution, and generative modeling to enable interpretable molecular design for high-energy solid propellants. A curated dataset of over 16,000 molecules supports both accurate multi-target prediction models and a generative framework. The predictor attains high accuracy for Hydroxyl-terminated polybutadiene (HTPB) system formulations (R2 ≥ 0.996) and generalizes to Glycidyl Azide Polymer (GAP) and NitrateEster Plasticized PolyetherPropellant (NEPE) systems (R2 ≥ 0.970). SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) analysis highlights oxygen balance (OBCO > −10 %) and nitrogen content (35–45 wt%) as key factors. Guided by these insights, latent space optimization using a Junction Tree Variational Autoencoder and Bayesian optimization yields over 200 novel high-energy molecules with predicted Isp above 265 s. This work demonstrates an interpretable pipeline for accelerating high-energy molecules discovery and propellant formulation design.
10.1016/j.cej.2025.172198.title: Intelligent high-energy molecules design for solid propellants via interpretable machine learning and latent space optimization

10.1016/j.cej.2025.172197.abstract: With continuous advancements in Li-ion battery technology, it has become imperative to develop battery health assessment with general applicability. In particular, the batteries can satisfy a range of energy demands for diverse end products, which has motivated previous studies to develop State of Health (SoH) frameworks across various configurations. However, to achieve general applicability, a SoH estimator was required to train separately for each battery configuration, leading to substantial inefficiency. Hence, in this paper, we propose BADA (By capturing Attention in a transformer, assessing state of lithium-ion batteries with Distinguished health indicators Applicable to various configurations). This novel approach explores the five most significant health indicators (HIs) and leverages them to enable configuration-agnostic health diagnostics without additional training on different configurations. It further employs a multi-objective transformer with key HIs, achieving effective performance in SoH estimation while exhibiting limited effectiveness in battery configurations classification, which in turn helps ensure reliable assessment across different battery configuration units. BADA, constructed with dominant HIs and transformer encoders, demonstrated its general applicability. Notably, this transformer-based framework showed an RMSE of 1.90×10−2 for a 7P module despite being trained on single cells with an RMSE of 1.33×10−2. Accordingly, this transformer-based framework is expected to significantly enhance the general applicability of configuration-agnostic battery health estimation through transfer learning, effectively addressing all potential scenarios encountered under real-world usage.
10.1016/j.cej.2025.172197.title: Transformer-based framework for configuration-agnostic Li-ion battery SoH estimation by exploring novel health indicators

10.1016/j.cej.2025.172184.abstract: Mg-CO₂ batteries are promising for energy conversion and CO₂ fixation, but designing optimal single-atom catalysts (SACs) is challenging due to the lack of effective descriptors for complex chemical microenvironments. We developed a machine learning (ML) approach to uncover MgCO₃ adsorption mechanisms and identify key controlling factors. Using gradient boosting regression (GBR), we successfully identified a concise and universal descriptor ϕ″ through feature cleaning and importance analysis. This descriptor enables rapid, accurate evaluation of adsorption energies across diverse coordination environments, advancing catalyst design for Mg-CO₂ batteries. In general, the mathematical expression of ϕ″ can be viewed as the digital fingerprint for SACs with specific coordination environments. We anticipate that such a robustness and transferability descriptor ϕ″ can be extended and applied to other fields of catalytic science.
10.1016/j.cej.2025.172184.title: Machine learning-assisted the directed evolution of descriptor for Mg-CO2 batteries

10.1016/j.cej.2025.172413.abstract: Machine learning (ML) has emerged as a pivotal tool for predicting and optimizing the performance of advanced oxidation processes (AOPs), which are widely applied for degrading persistent organic pollutants. Notwithstanding, a systematic summary of ML-based applications in AOPs remains lacking. To address this gap, this review presents a comprehensive analysis of recent advancements in ML utilization within AOPs, focusing on methodologies, mechanisms, and practical case studies. Additionally, a parameter importance analysis was performed to assess key factors in AOPs, with specific emphasis on catalyst site construction, oxidation pathway regulation, and reaction condition optimization, which are thoroughly analyzed. For catalytic site construction, ML overcomes limitations of univariate experiments by demystifying the “black-box” of biochar active site formation, revealing that higher heating values and pyrolysis temperature are dominant factors governing the generation of carbon- and nitrogen-containing sites. Regarding oxidation pathway regulation, ML accurately establishes the complex nonlinear relationship between catalyst structure and 1O2 generation in biochar/peroxymonosulfate system, pinpointing the optimal catalyst structure to enhance 1O2 performance. In terms of reaction condition optimization, ML employs high-throughput screening of pollutant molecular descriptors to determine degradation mechanisms mediated by SO4•-, •OH, and O3, and unveils optimal reaction conditions by establishing complex relationships among key parameters. This review delineates critical predictive capabilities of ML in AOPs, demonstrating how ML enables high-throughput catalyst fabrication and targeted oxidation pathway modulation through predictions of active sites and reactive species, while consolidating data-driven optimization strategies for AOPs. The findings herein provide valuable guidance for the intelligent development of AOPs.
10.1016/j.cej.2025.172413.title: Machine learning-enabled advanced oxidation processes: Catalytic active site engineering, oxidation pathway regulation, and reaction condition optimization

10.1016/j.cej.2025.172333.abstract: Catalytic reforming of biogas provides an environmentally sustainable pathway for hydrogen production, wherein Ni-based bimetallic catalysts play a crucial role. Nonetheless, rapid and cost-efficient screening of such catalysts remains a significant challenge. In this study, machine learning methods, specifically random forest (RF) and multilayer perceptron (MLP) models, were employed for preliminary catalyst screening. The catalytic activity, selectivity, and stability were evaluated jointly by predicting CH4 conversion, CO2 conversion, H2/CO ratio, and the change of CH4 conversion in extended testing periods. The RF model exhibited superior predictive accuracy (R2 > 0.9, RMSE ≤5.01) across all performance metrics compared to the MLP model. Through integrated interpretative approaches, the optimal characteristics of Ni-based bimetallic catalysts and operational parameters influencing catalytic performance were elucidated. Catalyst stability was found to be strongly dependent on catalyst properties with smaller Ni particle sizes (< 7 nm) and lower specific surface areas (< 225 m2/g) contributing positively to stability. Additionally, temperature and weight hourly space velocity (WHSV) significantly impacted CH4 conversion, with maximum conversion observed at temperatures above 725 °C and WHSV below 132 L·g−1·h−1. Importantly, the doping metals in the Ni-based bimetallic catalysts were screened based on ML models, revealing that alkaline-earth and lanthanide dopants exhibited promising performance at low temperatures, whereas fifth- and sixth-period transition metal promoters had advantages at elevated temperatures.
10.1016/j.cej.2025.172333.title: Accurate prediction and screening of Ni-based bimetallic catalysts for hydrogen production from biogas reforming: An interpretable machine learning study

10.1016/j.cej.2025.172350.abstract: Biomass-derived hard carbon is a low-cost, sustainable anode candidate for sodium-ion batteries, yet the structural evolution mechanisms governing its performance remain unclear. A novel two-step predictive approach was developed and compared with the conventional one-step model. This approach not only slightly improved the prediction accuracy for electrochemical performance, but also established interpretable correlations between input features and electrochemical performance outputs, and further enabled the prediction and analysis of rate performance indicators. The framework first uses biomass three-component ratios and thermal parameters to infer key structural descriptors (SSA, d002, ID/IG, La, Lc), which are then combined with current density to predict electrochemical performance. The target space extends beyond experimental capacity (QM,E) and initial Coulombic efficiency (ICE), encompassing rate-related parameters (QM,F, τ, n) and long-cycle capacity (QM,100) within a unified interpretable model. Trained on an expanded dataset covering diverse biomass compositions and carbonization conditions, the model captures both kinetic and durability behaviors across a wide compositional space. SHAP and PDP analyses reveal that moderate disorder (ID/IG ∼ 1.5–1.8), narrow interlayer spacing (∼0.37–0.38 nm), and lateral domain sizes of 3.5–5.0 nm synergistically enhance reversible capacity, while their kinetic response reflects a trade-off rather than optimal rate capability—a behavior instead observed at smaller or larger lateral domain sizes. These capacity-favorable structures are typically achieved using cellulose-rich precursors with tuned hemicellulose and lignin content under optimized carbonization protocols. This study offers mechanistic insights and practical guidance for designing high-performance hard carbon anodes in sodium-ion batteries.
10.1016/j.cej.2025.172350.title: Multi-staged machine learning-driven investigation of biomass-derived hard carbon anodes for sodium-ion batteries: Connecting precursor, structure, and performance

10.1016/j.cej.2026.172634.abstract: The design of copolymers with tailored thermal properties is crucial for advanced applications in aerospace, the automotive industry, and electronics. However, the development of data-driven models for this task is severely hampered by the scarcity of structured, high-quality datasets, as copolymer data remains buried in the unstructured text of scientific literature. Here, we demonstrate a large language model (LLM)-powered pipeline to overcome this data bottleneck and enable the inverse design of novel copolymers. We developed a method to accurately extract copolymer names and their thermal properties (glass transition temperature, Tg, and melting temperature, Tm) from 393 research articles, achieving a high extraction accuracy (F1 score = 0.7834) and constructing a curated dataset of 1195 entries. This LLM-generated dataset was used to train machine learning models that rival the performance of models built on manually curated data. Our forward prediction models achieved R2 values of 0.791 and 0.845 for Tg and Tm, respectively, on an independent manually labeled test set. Critically, we deployed an inverse model for de novo design, generating 2052 novel, valid copolymer structures targeting high Tg, which exhibited a 189.5 % increase in average predicted Tg. The thermal properties of eight selected AI-generated copolymers were validated with molecular dynamics simulations, confirming their predicted performance with a mean relative error of 4.17 %. This work establishes LLMs as a powerful and reliable tool for automating scientific data extraction, effectively bridging the data gap in materials science and paving the way for accelerated discovery of high-performance polymers.
10.1016/j.cej.2026.172634.title: Large language models for automated data extraction and inverse design of copolymers with targeted glass transition temperatures

10.1016/j.cej.2026.172675.abstract: The growing alcoholic beverage market and stringent quality control standards have heightened the demand for precise detection technologies for alcohol components. Traditional metal oxide semiconductors (MOS) sensors face significant challenges in terms of selectivity and cross-sensitivity, which seriously hinder the accurate discrimination of alcohol components. Herein, we developed an electronic nose system utilizing a sensor array composed of In2O3, ZnO, and In2O3/ZnO heterojunction sensors, all of which have demonstrated high sensitivity and stability in the detection of alcoholic gases. To facilitate effective gas differentiation and classification, four machine learning algorithms, including K-nearest neighbors (KNN), support vector machine (SVM), Gaussian naive Bayes (GNB), and logistic regression (LR), were employed and compared. Through parameter optimization via grid search and cross-validation, we achieved classification accuracies of 91 % for KNN and SVM, 87 % for GNB, and 89 % for LR for single gases. Notably, the E-nose demonstrated a remarkable 94.12 % accuracy in recognizing mixed gas samples containing ethanol and methanol/n-butanol, highlighting its potential for rapid detection of alcohol volatiles.
10.1016/j.cej.2026.172675.title: Machine learning-assisted oxide semiconductor sensor array for accurate discrimination of alcohol gases
10.1016/j.cej.2026.172675.source: ScienceDirect official citation and abstract BibTeX export

10.1016/j.cej.2026.172806.abstract: The development of gas sensors with ultrahigh sensitivity and selectivity is crucial for public safety, environmental protection, and early warning of hazardous leaks. However, achieving real–time, portable, and reusable sensing platforms with distinct visual responses remains a key challenge. Herein, we report a deep learning–assisted sensing strategy that integrates multifunctional metal–organic framework (MOF)–based hydrogels with artificial intelligence (AI) for visual ammonia (NH₃) monitoring. Gemini surfactant–modified zirconium metal–organic framework hydrogels (GS6–ZrMOF@gel and GS10–ZrMOF@gel) were engineered, combining the high porosity of MOFs, amphiphilic surfactant functionality, and the mechanical robustness of hydrogels (tensile strength ≈ 1.52 MPa; toughness ≈ 4.48 MJ m−3). Notably, GS10–ZrMOF@gel exhibits sub–ppm sensitivity toward ammonia vapor (limit of detection ≈0.27 ppm) alongside excellent selectivity and recyclability. The sensing mechanism was systematically elucidated through combined experimental investigations and density functional theory (DFT) calculations. Furthermore, deep learning–enabled image analysis allowed direct visualization and accurate classification of ammonia concentrations, achieving 100% recognition accuracy. As a proof of concept, a wireless alarm system integrating the sensing hydrogels with AI algorithms was successfully demonstrated for real–time gas–leakage monitoring. This work establishes a universal strategy for real–time visual gas detection by coupling multifunctional materials with intelligent data analytics, and highlights its strong potential for environmental monitoring, industrial safety, and healthcare applications.
10.1016/j.cej.2026.172806.title: Deep learning–assisted amphiphilic metal–organic framework–based hydrogel sensor for visual and wireless ammonia monitoring

10.1016/j.cej.2026.172969.abstract: The present study is devoted to the development of a methodology based on artificial intelligence to model and optimize a novel process for efficient ethylene production on a large scale. To this end, a wall-cooled multi-tubular reactor for the catalytic oxidative dehydrogenation of ethane that benefits from MoVTeNbO catalysts was modeled and optimized with different plans of artificial neural networks (ANNs). A mathematical model was then employed to generate a large database (1440 runs at varied process conditions) for this process. Having screened with a relevancy analysis, the dataset was then utilized to analyze different ANN designs based on single-layer perceptron (SLP) and single-layer cascade feed-forward (SLCFF) modes and different training functions. These designs were compared with radial basis function (RBF) as well. The impacts of train function (Broyden-Fletcher-Goldfarb-Shanno Quasi-Newton (trainbfg) and Levenberg-Marquardt (trainlm)) and hidden layer size were also monitored rigorously. Although the RBF ANN failed to describe this system, the SLP and SLCFF plans could represent the outputs precisely. Based on a robust statistical analysis of the errors, as well as kernel density and histogram analyses, it was proven that the calculations of SLP and SLCFF ANN models were reliable. The model composed of SLP-trainbfg with 20 neurons in the hidden layer was selected as the most accurate and fastest one, which was then combined with a multi-objective genetic algorithm method to search for the optimum operating conditions of the system in terms of higher feed conversion and ethylene generation with lower carbon oxide release. The observations signified that the process working under optimum conditions produces a considerable amount of ethylene at moderate temperature and pressure while releasing small quantities of carbon oxides.
10.1016/j.cej.2026.172969.title: AI-assisted modeling and optimization of large-scale ethylene production by catalytic oxidative dehydrogenation of ethane in a shell-and-tube multi-tubular reactor

10.1016/j.cej.2026.173744.abstract: Lateral flow immunoassay (LFIA), as a portable point-of-care testing (POCT) platform, shows significant potential for applications in clinical diagnostics. However, conventional LFIA sensors typically suffer from low sensitivity, which greatly limits their application in trace analyte detection. In this study, we developed a machine learning (ML)-assisted LFIA platform based on metal-AIEgen frameworks (MAFs) for ultrasensitive and intelligent detection of Pseudomonas aeruginosa (P. aeruginosa). By regulating the carboxyl density and arm rigidity of the AIE ligand, the synthesized MAF-1 exhibited outstanding luminescent performance and excellent biocompatibility. After integrating it into the LFIA system, the resulting MAF-1-LFIA achieved a detection limit (LOD) of 10 CFU/mL, with sensitivity enhanced by approximately 100-fold, 100-fold, and 10-fold compared with gold nanoparticles-based LFIA (AuNPs-LFIA), time-resolved fluorescent microsphere-based LFIA (TRFM-LFIA) and Enzyme-Linked Immunosorbent Assay (ELISA), respectively. In addition, the MAF-1-LFIA has been successfully applied to the detection of P. aeruginosa in tap water and milk samples, with a recovery rate ranging from 98.23% to 106.82% and a relative standard deviation (RSD) of 3.11% to 8.34%, demonstrating excellent accuracy and practicality. Furthermore, the incorporation of ML algorithms enabled efficient classification and precise quantification of the detection signals, with a classification accuracy of 100% and a concentration prediction accuracy of 99.04%. In summary, this work proposes a promising strategy that integrates MAFs materials with artificial intelligence for high-performance detection in complex biological matrices, paving the way for the development of next-generation intelligent POCT biosensors.
10.1016/j.cej.2026.173744.title: AIEgen-regulated metal-organic framework enabled machine learning-assisted lateral flow immunoassay sensor for intelligent diagnosis of P. aeruginosa
10.1016/j.cej.2026.173744.source: ScienceDirect official citation and abstract BibTeX export

10.1016/j.cej.2026.173148.abstract: Pollination by bees underpins agriculture and ecosystem health but is increasingly threatened by American foulbrood (AFB) caused by Paenibacillus larvae. Conventional AFB diagnostics are slow and costly, underscoring the need for portable sensors targeting the key biomarker 2,5-dimethylpyrazine (2,5-DMP). Here, natural language processing is applied to mine a large corpus of scholarly literature. A domain-adaptive SensBERT model evaluates 514,088 bimetallic ion–organic ligand combinations for gas sensing, with similarity scores near unity indicating high applicability. Integrated analysis of application context, physicochemical traits, and MOFs performance identifies three optimal systems: Sm(III)/Sn(II) with 3,3′,3″-((1,3,5-triazine-2,4,6-triyl)tris(azanediyl))tribenzoic_acid (H3TATAB); In(III)/Zn(II) with 4-(1H-tetrazol-5-yl)benzoic_acid (H2TZBA); and Tm(III)/Sn(II) with furan-2,5-dicarboxylic_acid (FDCA). Sm/Sn–H3TATAB exhibits superior sensitivity and selectivity toward 2,5-DMP. After plasma conversion, the derived metal oxides retain highly specific 2,5-DMP recognition with excellent response consistency and stability. Density functional theory (DFT) calculations model adsorption of multiple AFB-related VOCs at the atomic scale, revealing a uniquely strong binding preference for 2,5-DMP; coupling DFT-generated data with a deep neural network further clarifies the sensing mechanism. The resulting sensor achieves a detection limit of 20 ppb for 2,5-DMP, with a response of 2.7 at 20 ppb. This work establishes a synergistic paradigm that integrates deep learning, first-principles computation, and experimental validation to deliver a high-performance, non-invasive platform for rapid AFB detection, highlighting the promise of cross-disciplinary strategies for environmental monitoring and agricultural biosecurity.
10.1016/j.cej.2026.173148.title: AI–DFT-DNN-guided dopant–ligand engineering of MOF-derived chemiresistors for ppb-level 2,5-Dimethylpyrazine detection
10.1016/j.cej.2026.173148.source: ScienceDirect official citation and abstract BibTeX export

10.1016/j.cej.2026.174829.abstract: Photochemical reactions are highly sensitive to parameters such as light intensity, wavelength, irradiation time, and moisture content. The lack of precise control and real-time monitoring often makes these reactions difficult to reproduce and purify, prompting many researchers to favour non-photochemical alternatives. To overcome these limitations, we present the UV–Visible Auto-Reactometry (UVAR) platform an AI-integrated, continuous flow microfluidic system designed for autonomous optimization and acceleration of photochemical synthesis. Leveraging large language models (LLMs) for dynamic planning and real-time parameter control, UVAR enables precise, reproducible, and efficient screening of reaction conditions. The platform demonstrated broad applicability across four key photochemical transformations: cross-coupling, rearrangement, cycloaddition, and isomerization, successfully synthesizing 36 structurally diverse molecules, including the late-stage functionalization of the Apixaban (APX) active pharmaceutical ingredient (API).
10.1016/j.cej.2026.174829.title: UV–visible Auto-Reactometry enabled parallel screening for accelerating chemical synthesis development with LLM
10.1016/j.cej.2026.174829.source: ScienceDirect official citation and abstract BibTeX export

10.1016/j.cej.2026.174323.abstract: Three-dimensional (3D) nanoengineered surface-enhanced Raman scattering (SERS) substrates enable ultrasensitive molecular detection by amplifying localized electromagnetic fields. To overcome the complexity and limitation associated with fabricating 3D SERS substrates, a facile and cost-effective 3D SERS platform was designed by coupling silver (Ag) nanoparticles with a polycaprolactone–chitosan (PCL–CHT) biopolymer matrix. The hybrid nanostructure generates densely distributed electromagnetic hotspots, expands the Raman-active region, and effectively minimizes the impact of laser defocusing during measurement. The optimized Ag@PCL-CHT substrate exhibits a strong analytical enhancement factor of 1010, enabling trace-level detection of methylene blue (MB) down to picomolar concentrations. Furthermore, to address reproducibility and complex data interpretation issues commonly faced in biomedical sensing, an artificial intelligence-assisted multi-diagnostic model was integrated with the 3D substrate. The unique nanoarchitecture ensures consistent and reliable SERS responses from diverse biofluids, including sweat, urine, and serum, enabling simultaneous monitoring of creatinine, uric acid and pH. This multiplex sensing platform minimizes dependence on multiple single-analyte tests and provides a holistic evaluation of metabolic states. The proposed strategy demonstrates a controllable and scalable route for constructing highly sensitive and reproducible SERS sensors, advancing the practical deployment of 3D SERS technology for point-of-care diagnostics and personalized health monitoring.
10.1016/j.cej.2026.174323.title: Design of three-dimensional SERS-active biopolymer platform: Towards highly sensitive molecular detection and artificial intelligence-enhanced multi-biomarker diagnosis
10.1016/j.cej.2026.174323.source: ScienceDirect official citation and abstract BibTeX export

10.1016/j.cej.2026.174718.abstract: Two-dimensional (2D) metal-organic framework nanosheets (MONs) with nanozyme activity hold great promise, yet their scalable and eco-friendly synthesis remains challenging. Herein, bioinspired Cu-MON was synthesized via a rapid one-step coordination self-assembly of expired phloroglucinol drugs with Cu2+ in water at room temperature enabling high-value recycling of expired pharmaceutical waste. Cu-MON exhibits excellent laccase-like and peroxidase-like activities, significantly outperforming natural enzymes and other Cu-based nanozymes in catalytic efficiency, kinetics, and stability. Its superior performance stems from the ultrathin mesoporous structure, high copper content, and engineered defects, which enhance the adsorption and activation of substrates. Density functional theory calculations demonstrated the key role of coordination shell regulation in reducing the energy barrier and promoting electron transfer. Notably, this work reveals the synergistic effect of Metal-Ligand-Substrate, involving not only the CuII-CuI redox cycle but also the simultaneous coordination and electron transfer between the redox-active functional groups of ligands and the metal sites/substrates. Leveraging its laccase-like behavior and differential responses, a machine learning-enabled, smartphone-integrated colorimetric sensor array was developed for on-site discrimination of structurally similar phenolic contaminants. Unlike traditional “detection-only” platforms, our system integrates “sense and kill” functionality, further enabling efficient contaminant removal. Moreover, a novel degradation-polymerization dual-removal pathway for tetracycline antibiotics was discovered, ensuring near-complete removal and detoxification. Finally, a peroxidase-driven dual-mode ratiometric fluorescence-colorimetric sensor was constructed for dopamine detection in biological fluids, with cross-validation ensuring high reliability and accuracy. This “One-MON-Three-Functions” strategy provides a new perspective for designing next-generation multifunctional nanozymes for pollutant monitoring, environmental remediation, and biosensing.
10.1016/j.cej.2026.174718.title: Design of green multifunctional mesoporous nanosheets for trace biomarker detection, AI-enhanced pollutant discrimination, and synergistic catalytic degradation

10.1016/j.cej.2026.175131.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is transforming the design of energetic materials (EMs), which are essential in military, aerospace, and industrial applications. From the molecular, crystal, and composite perspectives, this article highlights how machine learning models enable property and performance prediction in high-throughput virtual screening, offering density functional theory-level accuracy at a fraction of the computational cost. Meanwhile, generative models, as a new paradigm in the AI era, enable target-driven design of molecules and crystals. Despite much progress, challenges remain in data scarcity, insufficient interpretability, and limited cross-scale integration. Advances in the quantity and quality of data, interpretable and physics-informed models, multiscale frameworks, and EMs-specific foundation models will pave the way toward a data-driven and efficient paradigm for the discovery of next-generation EMs.
10.1016/j.cej.2026.175131.title: Artificial intelligence for energetic materials: design on the levels of molecule, crystal and composite

10.1016/j.cej.2026.175189.abstract: The biosynthesis of volatile organic compound (VOC) signaling is essential for plant adaptation under disease stress. However, the efficient identification of VOCs remains a significant challenge. In this study, we engineered a biomimetic colorimetric sensor array by integrating stimulus-responsive dyes into a highly porous three-dimensional covalent organic framework (3D COF), which is coupled with artificial intelligence analysis. These 3D COF@dye sensors exhibit high surface areas and interconnected large channels, facilitating highly sensitive colorimetric sensing of VOCs. The resultant platform demonstrated markedly enhanced sensitivity towards target VOCs, with detection limits ranging from 0.081 to 0.95 ppm. Furthermore, AI-assisted information fusion and perceptual analysis considerably improved the accuracy of VOC sensing processes, enabling direct visualization and classification of VOCs with ≥95% accuracy within 24 h of inoculation. This design, which leverages molecular recognition capabilities, amplifies host-guest interactions, thereby facilitating the differentiation of VOCs by their polarity, size, and shape. The platform effectively distinguished VOCs emitted by Botrytis cinerea, Alternaria solani, and Phytophthora infestans. Our findings provide a generalizable platform of intelligent, nano-enabled sensors for precision agriculture and non-invasive plant health monitoring.
10.1016/j.cej.2026.175189.title: Highly sensitive colorimetric 3D covalent organic framework sensors with artificial intelligence analysis enabled early detection of plant diseases
10.1016/j.cej.2026.175189.source: ScienceDirect official citation and abstract BibTeX export

10.1016/j.cej.2026.174923.abstract: In-situ quantitative techniques for pathogens across diverse scenarios can transform detection from a retrospective “laboratory tool” into a proactive “field decision-making tool,” which is crucial for precise early warning of pathogens. Herein, we developed an enhanced metal-organic framework (MOF) by anchoring dual single atoms (DSAs) Co-Cu onto an MOF carrier (Co/Cu@EnMOF). Low-cost aptamer-functionalized Co/Cu@EnMOF enabled specific bacterial recognition. In addition to increasing the sensitivity of the sensing signal through DSAs anchoring of the MOF structure, the anti-interference capability against the food matrix was also achieved by using targeted magnetic nanoflowers that increase the binding sites for target bacteria. Addressing the main issue restricting sensing sensitivity, the two-step sensitization technology has comprehensively enhanced the signal for E. coli O157:H7 and the anti-interference ability in food, enabling rapid early warning of trace pathogens. To achieve portable bioanalysis, we engineered a novel crystalline sensing carrier by immobilizing the chromogenic substrate o-Phenylenediamine (OPD) onto cellulose paper matrices. Under the catalytic action of Co/Cu@EnMOF, OPD is oxidized to generate a product that exhibits both color change and fluorescence emission, enabling dual-mode signal output. The newly developed multi-signal integrated reading device enables sensitive in-situ detection and, when combined with deep learning, can accurately read RGB values. The proposed smart crystal paper sensor enables dual-mode in-situ quantitative detection, with detection limits of 38.73 and 97.72 cfu/mL for colorimetric and fluorescence modes, respectively. It demonstrates excellent performance when applied to complex food matrices, offering a new approach for in-situ monitoring and early warning of pathogens.
10.1016/j.cej.2026.174923.title: Enhanced metal-organic framework-driven deep learning-assisted magnetic crystal paper aptsensor for two-step sensitization and in-situ detection of pathogenic bacteria
10.1016/j.cej.2026.174923.source: ScienceDirect official citation and abstract BibTeX export

10.1016/j.cej.2026.175301.abstract: Environmental contamination by microplastics (MPs) and heavy metals (HMs) has raised global concerns due to their potential ecological risks, but the mechanisms underpinning synergistic migrations of these two pollutants remain unclear. To achieve this purpose, batch experiments, laboratory column experiments, microscopic characterization, density functional theory (DFT) calculations, molecular dynamics (MD) simulations, and interpretable machine learning (ML) were integrated to investigate the adsorption and co-migration of fresh and UV-aged polypropylene (PP) and polyethylene (PE) with respect to their interactions with copper ions (Cu2+) and cadmium ions (Cd2+). The results showed that aging significantly improved the adsorption performance of MPs. For aged PP, the equilibrium adsorption capacity for Cu2+ reached 1.31 mg/g, indicating a 50% increase compared with fresh PP, while that for Cd2+ was 0.624 mg/g, representing an increase of nearly 20%. Moreover, aged MPs significantly promoted the migration of HMs, with aged-PP increasing the Cu2+ recovery rate by 8.28% compared with that without aged PP. DFT calculations indicated that the adsorption energy of Cu2+ with PE (−2.26 eV) was stronger than that of Cd2+ (−1.73 eV). MD simulations confirmed that electrostatic interaction was the main binding driving force. Among various ML models, the CatBoost model (R2 = 0.85, RMSE = 0.217) performs the best. By integrating molecular-scale simulations (DFT/MD), batch and column experiments, and ML-based feature attribution, this multi-scale framework linked local HM–MP binding mechanisms to macroscopic co-migration processes in saturated porous media, overcoming the fragmentation and biases inherent to conventional studies that rely on a single technique, thus providing a mechanistic framework that may help evaluate MP-facilitated HM transport under controlled groundwater-relevant conditions.
10.1016/j.cej.2026.175301.title: Revealing the key factors of synergistic transport of microplastics and heavy metals in groundwater: Batch experiments, density functional theory calculations, molecular dynamics simulations, and machine learning modeling
10.1016/j.cej.2026.175301.source: ScienceDirect official citation and abstract BibTeX export

10.1016/j.cej.2026.175701.abstract: Biomass valorization is a critical pathway toward sustainable energy and resource utilization; however, catalyst design for biomass refining remains challenging due to the chemical diversity of feedstocks, coupled reaction parameters, and the coexistence of structured numerical data and unstructured textual knowledge dispersed across the literature. These complexities impose substantial manual effort in prescreening catalytic pathways and hinder rapid catalyst discovery. In this work, we propose an agentic artificial intelligence (AI) framework that integrates small language models (SLMs) for contextual text interpretation with automated machine learning (AutoML) for quantitative performance prediction. The framework autonomously extracts domain-relevant knowledge from unstructured experimental reports, links qualitative insights to structured datasets, and performs predictive screening of catalytic pathways with minimal human intervention. By bridging unstructured textual information and numerical modeling, the system accelerates the catalyst design cycle while maintaining interpretability and data security through local deployment. Multiple SLM architectures were systematically benchmarked with respect to domain specificity, response efficiency, and feature identification accuracy, leading to the selection of a lightweight model suitable for laboratory-scale deployment. The agentic workflow enables iterative database updates without retraining large models and supports seamless adaptation to domain-specific datasets. Experimental validation using biomass-derived deoxygenation reactions suggests that the proposed framework shows promising potential for guiding catalyst screening and pathway selection. This study establishes a practical agentic AI approach for accelerating biomass catalyst discovery by unifying contextual reasoning and numerical prediction within a single autonomous workflow. The framework is readily extensible to other catalysis and chemical engineering applications where unstructured knowledge and limited datasets constrain conventional machine learning approaches.
10.1016/j.cej.2026.175701.title: Agentic AI framework for accelerated catalyst design in biomass valorization via small language models and automated machine learning
10.1016/j.cej.2026.175701.source: ScienceDirect official citation and abstract BibTeX export

10.1016/j.cej.2026.175353.abstract: The technology of ammonia production via electrochemical nitrate reduction reaction (NO3RR) offers a sustainable solution for addressing nitrate pollution in water bodies and recovering nitrogen resources. Among this technology, the design and selection of efficient catalysts are the key to achieving high selectivity and stable nitrogen conversion in NO3RR. This study employed machine learning (ML)-powered density functional theory (DFT) to develop a strategy for designing NO3RR catalysts based on geometric-electronic-adsorption properties. The stability and activity of 282 single-atom catalysts (SACs) with high carbon‑nitrogen stoichiometric ratios of CxN3 (M-CxN3, M-X-CxN3, X = Cl, Br, I) are evaluated. Four high-performance catalysts are screened, among which Ru-Cl-C₇N₃ exhibits the optimal catalytic activity (limiting potential = −0.38 V). This study further extracts 15 key characteristic parameters of four categories through data mining and constructs eight ML prediction models. It is found that Random Forest Regression has the best predictive performance for the NO3RR activity of SACs (test set: R2 = 0.923). The DFT-ML collaborative prediction framework not only significantly provides an effective strategy for designing NO3RR catalysts, but also offers certain guidance for the rational design of materials and resource recovery in sustainable energy technologies.
10.1016/j.cej.2026.175353.title: Machine learning-powered high-throughput designing and screening of electrocatalysts for nitrate reduction to ammonia

10.1016/j.cej.2026.175829.abstract: Vacuum pressure swing adsorption (VPSA) processes stand out among CO2 capture technologies for their low energy requirement, environmental sustainability, and operational flexibility. Most existing VPSA-based CO2 capture studies have focused on coal-fired flue gas (~15% CO2). However, the ongoing shift toward natural gas-fired power plants, which emit flue gas with lower CO2 concentrations (< 10% CO2), highlights the need for systems optimized for dilute CO2 streams. Moreover, previous studies have largely been limited to small-scale systems with simplified cycle configurations, restricting their industrial applicability. This study optimizes the operating conditions and cycle configurations of industrial-scale poly-bed VPSA processes for CO2 capture by introducing a novel parallel batch multi-objective Bayesian optimization framework utilizing artificial neural network ensembles. The optimization considered three objectives of CO2 purity, recovery, and total annualized cost (TAC), with a focus on the role of pressure equalization (PE) steps in minimizing energy consumption during desorption. A pronounced trade-off was found: adding PE steps enhances CO2 purity and recovery and lowers energy consumption, but raises TAC. Notably, the optimization results indicated that incorporating three or more PE steps was essential for achieving optimal performance. Global sensitivity and techno-economic analyses were conducted to identify key variables and to examine the effects of PE steps, CO2 emission penalties, and electricity prices. To rationalize the need for PE steps, a net CO2 recovery was introduced to consider both process-level CO2 recovery and indirect CO2 emissions associated with energy consumption. This study provides a comprehensive optimization framework that balances energy efficiency, cost, and separation performance, contributing to the sustainable design of next-generation VPSA systems for low-concentration CO2 flue gas.
10.1016/j.cej.2026.175829.title: Techno-economic optimization and cycle schedule analysis of poly-bed VPSA process for CO2 capture from natural gas combustion emissions using parallel Bayesian optimization with ANN ensembles
10.1016/j.cej.2026.175829.source: ScienceDirect official citation and abstract BibTeX export

10.1016/j.cej.2026.175822.abstract: Electrocatalytic CO2 reduction is central to sustainable fuel and chemical production, facilitating the conversion of greenhouse gases into valuable products. Progress in this field is hindered by complex reaction pathways, competing intermediates, and a high−dimensional design space, posing challenges for mechanistic understanding and material selection. Modern catalyst design increasingly relies on systematic, principle−driven approaches that link physicochemical properties to catalytic performance. Machine learning has emerged as a powerful data−centric methodology, accelerating discovery and revealing hidden patterns in extensive catalyst datasets. This review examines the role of machine learning in electrocatalytic CO2 reduction, emphasizing descriptor frameworks that connect catalyst structure with reactivity and selectivity. It considers key sources of CO2RR − related data−computed, measured, or literature−based−and analyzes strategies for constructing and validating electronic and thermodynamic descriptors. By highlighting case studies, we illustrate how machine learning models predict performance trends and screen catalysts across diverse composition spaces, offering mechanistic insights overlooked by traditional methods. We prioritize the reliability and interpretability of descriptor−based models to guide researchers in effectively utilizing machine learning in CO2RR and reshaping rational electrocatalyst discovery principles.
10.1016/j.cej.2026.175822.title: Machine learning and multi−scale descriptor frameworks for accelerated discovery of CO2 electrocatalysts
10.1016/j.cej.2026.175822.source: ScienceDirect official citation and abstract BibTeX export

10.1016/j.cej.2026.176134.abstract: Saline water electrolysis has emerged as a promising strategy for sustainable hydrogen production due to the abundance of seawater resources. However, commercialization is hindered by reliance on precious-metal catalysts and the difficulty of maintaining selective reaction pathways under saline conditions. Here, we introduce a high-entropy alloy (HEA) catalyst design strategy enabled by an active learning, multi-objective framework that simultaneously optimizes activity, selectivity, and cost. By combining Gaussian process regression with the expected improvement acquisition, we efficiently explore the vast compositional space of HEAs using only a limited number of density functional theory calculations, achieving high predictive accuracy at ∼1.2% of the computational cost of full-space exploration. Computational results reveal distinct optimal compositions for seawater electrolysis. Cu-rich HEA compositions at the anode maximize oxygen evolution reaction activity while effectively suppressing the competing chlorine evolution reaction, providing a cost-effective alternative to conventional noble-metal-based catalysts. In addition, Ni-rich compositions exhibit hydrogen evolution reaction activity comparable to that of pure Pt while significantly reducing precious-metal content at the cathode. Overall, this active learning-driven, multi-objective protocol accelerates HEA discovery for seawater electrolysis and is readily transferable to other electrochemical energy-conversion and catalyst-design problems requiring simultaneous optimization of multiple competing objectives.
10.1016/j.cej.2026.176134.title: Active learning-driven multi-objective design of high-entropy alloy catalysts for saline water electrolysis

10.1016/j.cej.2026.176093.abstract: Plasmonic MOF materials offer a promising solution to the low affinity of volatile organic compounds (VOC) toward conventional pure-metal surface-enhanced Raman scattering (SERS) substrates. However, the widely adopted bottom-up synthesis approaches often suffer from the irregular aggregation of metal nanostructures, impairing signal reproducibility, and the formation of flexible MOF with ligand defects, compromising selectivity. Here, we report a purely electrochemical top-down strategy to fabricate a Turing-patterned plasmonic MOF SERS substrate, in which the electrochemically sculptured Turing-patterned Ag enables highly reproducible Raman signal amplification, while the subsequently current-grown rigid ZIF-8 layer—with restricted ligand dynamics—selectively enriches volatile organic compounds via hierarchical porosity and non-covalent interactions. Notably, the Turing-patterned Ag@ZIF-8 enables instantaneous readout of the molar ratios of chloroform, benzene, and benzaldehyde in the gaseous mixtures solely by their Raman intensity ratios. By integrating spectral collection via portable Raman spectrometers with machine learning-assisted spectral analysis, we can readily distinguish colorectal cancer-related VOC profiles from healthy ones in simulated breath samples with an accuracy up to 94.0%. This work presents a novel practical approach for constructing low-cost, high-performance plasmonic MOF SERS substrates, advancing point-of-care diagnostics by leveraging SERS technique and artificial intelligence.
10.1016/j.cej.2026.176093.title: Electrochemical construction of Turing-patterned plasmonic MOF substrate for machine learning-assisted SERS analysis of volatile organic compounds

10.1016/j.cej.2026.176185.abstract: Accurate determination of crystal size distribution (CSD) and kinetics is crucial for understanding and controlling crystallization. This study presents a hybrid framework integrating a crystal segmentation model (CSM) with a physics-informed neural network (PINN). The CSM, based on a YOLO instance-segmentation backbone, converts raw process images into structured CSDs and distinguishes crystals from bubbles. These CSDs and process variables are then input into a PINN that embeds the population balance equation (PBE) as soft constraints to predict CSD evolution and infer growth and nucleation kinetics directly from experimental visuals. Across multiple cooling runs, the framework accurately reconstructs full CSDs and extracts interpretable kinetic parameters. The results demonstrate that computer vision can serve as a virtual sensor providing high-quality data for PINNs, enabling physically consistent learning from experiments and advancing crystallization process modeling and control.
10.1016/j.cej.2026.176185.title: Modeling of crystallization processes using physics-informed neural networks and in-situ image analysis
10.1016/j.cej.2026.176185.source: ScienceDirect official citation and abstract BibTeX export

10.1016/j.cej.2026.176136.abstract: Water-stable metal–organic frameworks (MOFs) for CO2 capture from wet flue gas face critical challenges, such as competitive H2O adsorption and humidity-induced structural degradation. This study presents an artificial intelligence (AI)-based descriptor engineering for inverse design framework integrating the Cascaded Tabular Generative Adversarial Network (CasTGAN) and Tabular Prior-data Fitted Network (TabPFN) to accelerate the discovery of high-performance water-stable MOFs. Analysis of the CoRE MOF 2019 dataset using correlation and mutual information methods identified pore confinement parameters (pore volume and largest cavity diameter) and framework electronegativity (metallic percentage and weighted electronegativity) as critical selectivity determinants under humid conditions. CasTGAN demonstrated superior synthetic data quality and enabled realistic MOF descriptor engineering, achieving a Fréchet inception distance of 0.017, which was lower than that of conventional GAN (1.384). Moreover, TabPFN achieved exceptional predictive accuracy (R2 of 0.959 and 0.943 for CO2/H2O and CO2/N2 selectivity, respectively), outperforming other AI models. SHAP-based explainable AI validated key descriptor contributions and guided systematic screening to identify five promising candidates: OKAYEG, OHIHET, QOKCID, QUXRIM, and ZERQOE. Density functional theory confirmed the preference of OKAYEG and QOKCID on CO2 binding (−39.48 kJ/mol and − 42.08 kJ/mol) over competing H2O (+3.82 kJ/mol and + 4.2 kJ/mol) and N2 (−30.12 kJ/mol and − 25.17 kJ/mol). This study showed that a lack of open metal sites, small pore size, and unique structural orientation enhance the CO2 uptake capacity of OKAYEG over H2O and N2. This integrated computational pipeline offers a transformative approach for the rational design of water-stable MOFs under realistic industrial flue gas conditions.
10.1016/j.cej.2026.176136.title: Inverse design of water-stable MOFs for CO2 capture from wet flue gas via AI-based descriptor engineering and theoretical investigation using DFT
10.1016/j.cej.2026.176136.source: ScienceDirect official citation and abstract BibTeX export

10.1016/j.cej.2026.176395.abstract: Circulating miRNAs (e.g., miR-155 and miR-21) hold great potential as biomarkers for gastric cancer (GC) diagnosis, yet their extremely low abundance in body fluids and high sequence homology pose substantial challenges for clinical applications. Herein, an ultrasensitive electrochemical biosensing platform has been developed for precise detection of GC-associated miRNAs based on engineered core-shell nanozymes and a cascade enzymatic amplification strategy. Specifically, a miRNA-initiated SDA enabled CRISPR/Cas12a amplification strategy (miSCAS) was designed to achieve automatic signal amplification in a single-tube setup. Subsequently, the activated Cas12a cleaved the sensing-interface hairpin probes, thereby exposing the phosphate groups. Simultaneously, the ZrFe-MOF@PtSn core-shell nanozymes were synthesized by in situ growth of a ZrFe-MOF shell onto the PtSn core. This engineered architecture not only endows the nanozyme with stronger catalytic activity but also utilizes the Zr element in the ZrFe-MOF shell to form Zr-O-P bonds with the phosphate groups exposed by the probe, thereby achieving efficient amplification cascade integration of nanozyme catalysis and miSCAS. Benefiting from the synergistic signal enhancement of ZrFe-MOF@PtSn nanozymes and miSCAS, the developed biosensing method achieved an attomolar-level limit of detection (1.349 aM for miR-155 and 1.428 aM for miR-21) and demonstrated high agreement with the gold standard RT-qPCR (R2 > 0.96) in clinical sample validation. Crucially, the integration of a Lasso machine learning model enabled intelligent classification, significantly improving the accuracy of the biosensor in diagnosing GC based on dual-target current response values to 98%. This work deeply integrated nanozyme catalysis, Cas12a-based cascade amplification, and machine learning to construct a universal miRNA biosensing system, which provided a translational strategy for the precise diagnosis of GC.
10.1016/j.cej.2026.176395.title: Engineered ZrFe-MOF@PtSn core–shell nanozymes enable ultrasensitive Cas12a-mediated miRNA biosensing for machine learning-aided gastric cancer diagnosis
10.1016/j.cej.2026.176395.source: ScienceDirect official citation and abstract BibTeX export

10.1016/j.cej.2026.176606.abstract: The early and precise diagnosis of lung cancer is crucial for improving patient prognosis. This study constructs an integrated cluster based on bioinformatic design and matrix-derived energy supply for building in vitro and in vivo detection models. Through bioinformatic analysis, the highly expressed miRNA-21 in lung cancer is identified as a key biomarker. A metal-organic framework (MOF) is employed to encapsulate natural enzymes, leveraging its acid-responsive properties for controlled enzyme release. The material surface is modified with an aptamer specifically targeting miRNA-21, enabling the cluster to actively seek out and bind to the target. Innovatively, the system utilizes glucose in clinical body fluids as an endogenous fuel, converting chemical energy into electrical energy through enzyme-catalyzed redox reactions to achieve self-powering operation, thereby driving electrochemical signal output. Simultaneously, the fluorophore-modified aptamer enables synchronous fluorescence signal output, making it suitable for different clinical detection scenarios. Finally, the collected signal data are integrated with a machine learning algorithm to construct a early-warning model for lung cancer. This work establishes a streamlined pipeline from biomarker discovery to predictive clinical analysis.
10.1016/j.cej.2026.176606.title: An integrated self-powered platform featuring acid responsive MOF probes for machine learning based early warning of lung cancer
10.1016/j.cej.2026.176606.source: ScienceDirect official citation and abstract BibTeX export

10.1016/j.cej.2026.176504.abstract: Efficient heterogeneous catalysts play a pivotal role in the aerobic oxidation of benzylamine to imine. However, conventional “trial-and-error” approaches for catalyst development are often cost-prohibitive and labor-intensive. The advent of interpretable machine learning (ML) offers a transformative solution, enabling the accelerated discovery and rational design of high-performance catalysts. Herein, we developed an interpretable XGBoost model to decode the relationship between feature descriptors and catalytic performance. Leveraging this model, we rapidly pinpointed optimal catalyst compositions with exceptional activity. Guided by these insights, we synthesized a cost-effective dual-site catalyst, FeNP-FeSA@NC-800, which demonstrated outstanding performance with complete conversion of benzylamine and 98% selectivity for imine under mild conditions (90 °C, 8 h). Moreover, the catalyst exhibited broad substrate compatibility and excellent recyclability. Control experiments and theoretical calculations revealed that the synergistic interplay between dual active sites is key to the enhanced catalytic efficiency. Specifically, the coexisting Fe nanoparticles (FeNP) effectively modulated the d-band center of Fe single atoms (FeSA), optimizing the adsorption capacity for oxygen and benzylamine, thereby accelerating the aerobic oxidation of benzylamine.
10.1016/j.cej.2026.176504.title: Interpretable machine learning guides rational design of dual-site catalysts for synergistic aerobic oxidation of benzylamine
10.1016/j.cej.2026.176504.source: ScienceDirect official citation and abstract BibTeX export

10.1016/j.cej.2026.176545.abstract: Detection of fractional exhaled nitric oxide (FeNO) in exhaled breath is essential for monitoring respiratory diseases. Despite significant progress in NO sensing, achieving sub- parts-per-billion (ppb) detection in complex environments remains challenging. Here, we introduce a highly sensitive and selective NO sensor composed of gallium nitride nanowires (GaN-NWs) coated with zinc oxide (ZnO) and cadmium sulfide (CdS) nanoparticles (CZ-GaN-NWs). The integration of ZnO and CdS onto GaN-NWs strategically enhances sensing performance through interfacial charge transfer and surface redox reactions, leading to resistance modulation upon NO adsorption. The optimized C2Z2-GaN-NWs sensor demonstrates a 3.96-fold increase in response compared to bare GaN-NWs. It offers exceptional sensitivity with a detection limit of 2 ppb and a high signal-to-noise ratio in highly humid exhaled breath, surpassing the performance of current state-of-the-art NO sensors. Sensor arrays are further employed to enable pattern recognition capable of discriminating between simulated biomarkers and controlled breath. Validated through exhaled breath analysis, the sensor successfully distinguishes between healthy individuals and those with respiratory diseases. Moreover, advanced machine learning models accurately predict NO concentrations and classify disease stages. The proposed e-nose breath sensor offers a reliable, non-invasive solution for the early diagnosis and monitoring of respiratory diseases.
10.1016/j.cej.2026.176545.title: Nanostructured composite E-nose for selective exhaled nitric oxide detection and machine learning-assisted respiratory disease diagnosis
10.1016/j.cej.2026.176545.source: ScienceDirect official citation and abstract BibTeX export

10.1016/j.cej.2026.176703.abstract: Single-atom catalysts (SACs) have garnered significant attention due to their maximized atomic utilization and intrinsic catalytic activity. However, their application—particularly in multi-electron pathways—is often constrained by low metal loading and the geometric isolation of active sites. In contrast, dual-atom catalysts (DACs) offer a compelling solution by enhancing site density and fostering neighboring synergistic effects. These proximal sites provide a versatile platform for breaking scaling relations, rendering DACs an ideal strategy for facilitating CC coupling. Here, we comprehensively review the design and application of DACs for electrochemical CO2 reduction (CO2RR) to C2 products. We first elucidate the reaction mechanisms, contrasting the “single-site dilemma” of SACs with the synergistic advantages of DACs. Furthermore, we examine the critical role of machine learning (ML) in accelerating catalyst discovery, highlighting its capability to efficiently navigate the vast compositional space for rational design. Finally, we summarize existing challenges and outline future directions for bridging the gap between laboratory-scale research and industrial applications.
10.1016/j.cej.2026.176703.title: Design of dual-atom catalysts for CO2 reduction to C2 products: From synergistic mechanisms to machine learning guidance
10.1016/j.cej.2026.176703.source: ScienceDirect official citation and abstract BibTeX export

10.1016/j.cej.2026.176854.abstract: The global burden of depression urgently requires precision diagnostics capable of overcoming the high misdiagnosis rate associated with symptom-based assessments. Concurrent recognition of interrelated biomarkers in body fluid is capable of improving diagnostic accuracy but remains technically challenging. However, it is remains technically challenging due to the structural similarity between the targets and their susceptibility to interference from complex matrices. To address these limitations, a machine learning (ML)-driven MOF-on-MOF (metal-organic framework) intelligent luminescent array was developed. This array leverages programmable heteroepitaxial growth to architecturally integrate distinct luminescent MOFs into a single hierarchical structure. This design enables precise spatial confinement of tunable emission centers, facilitating effective multi-channel signal generation. The multi-luminescent centers combine its multiple signal generation capabilities to convert spectral response datasets into interpretable diagnostic outputs of four biomarkers of depression via ML algorithms. This array sensor not only demonstrated low detection limits for the biomarkers but also realized nearly 100% accuracy for recognition of biomarkers, highlighting its potential for both sensitive detection and selective identification of biomarkers in serum and urine samples. The applicability of this sensor platform can also be extended to fingerprint and security code for anticounterfeiting. The integration of programmable MOF heterostructures with multi-channel signal emphasizing the critical role of multi-biomarker profiling in enhancing diagnostic accuracy and enabling personalized therapeutic monitoring.
10.1016/j.cej.2026.176854.title: Machine learning-driven MOF-on-MOF luminescent array for multiplexed biomarker recognition in depression diagnostics and information anticounterfeiting
10.1016/j.cej.2026.176854.source: ScienceDirect official citation and abstract BibTeX export

10.1016/j.cej.2026.176856.abstract: Portland cement (PC), the most widely used construction material globally, requires a deep understanding of its hydration mechanisms to improve its performance, with tricalcium silicates (C3S) playing a central role in determining its fundamental properties. Due to the limitations of experimental methods and the slow, inaccurate nature of traditional molecular dynamics, it is challenging to characterize reactions occurring over large temporal and spatial scales. To overcome these challenges, we used a high-precision and efficient neuroevolution potential (NEP-MLP). For the first time, we achieved atomistic-scale early-stage dynamic simulations of the complete C3S hydration process, improving computational efficiency by seven orders of magnitude compared to ab initio molecular dynamics (AIMD). Our findings show that hydration begins with surface hydroxylation, followed by inward proton transfer, calcium dissolution through two coordination mechanisms, and the formation of calcium hydroxide (CH) clusters. Calcium silicate hydrate (C-S-H) gel formation occurs through both low-energy and high-energy pathways, with matrix pitting effects enhancing deep-layer reaction kinetics. This study establishes a new paradigm for cement science by bridging the atomic and engineering scales. This paradigm shift, which integrates data and physics, not only advances the field toward predictive development but also provides a foundation for designing durable, low-carbon cementitious materials for century-scale projects.
10.1016/j.cej.2026.176856.title: Unraveling the early-stage hydration mechanism of tricalcium silicate via machine learning potentials

10.1016/j.cej.2026.176824.abstract: Lithium‑sulfur batteries (LiS), despite their high theoretical energy density, suffer from polysulfide shuttling and sluggish redox kinetics. Single-atom catalysts (SACs) offer a promising route to address these issues, but their development is impeded by both the vast chemical space and insufficient understanding of how local electronic structure controls interfacial processes. Herein, a synergistic computational strategy integrating density functional theory (DFT) with machine learning (ML) is presented to efficiently screen and design high performance SACs, using transition metal atoms anchored on black phosphorus monolayer (TM-BP) as a model system. The combined approach identifies Ti-BP, V-BP and ML-predicted Hf-BP as exceptional electrocatalysts with optimal polysulfide binding and accelerated kinetics. The underlying catalytic mechanism is further deciphered through systematic electronic structure analysis, revealing that d-p orbital hybridization plays a critical role in regulating adsorption behavior and charge transfer. Furthermore, a unique “aggregation-donation-feedback” interfacial electron transfer mechanism is proposed, which clearly elucidates the complete electronic process of Li2S on the catalyst surface, from adsorption and activation to eventual decomposition, thereby explaining the origin of catalytic activity at the quantum mechanical level. By employing the SISSO algorithm, an interpretable, low-dimensional descriptor is derived that quantitatively correlates the Li2S decomposition barrier with intrinsic properties of the metal centers, establishing a generalizable principle for catalyst design. This work establishes an efficient DFT-ML synergistic screening framework, which not only accelerates the discovery of single-atom electrocatalysts but also provides a rational design pathway for high performance cathode hosts in LiS batteries.
10.1016/j.cej.2026.176824.title: Unveiling the electronic regulation mechanism via a combined DFT-machine learning strategy to screen high performance single-atom catalysts on black phosphorus monolayer for LiS batteries

10.1016/j.cej.2026.176943.abstract: Separation of C6 alkane isomers is a key yet energy-intensive step in petroleum refining because they exhibit highly similar physicochemical properties. Here we develop a stability-aware, transferable discovery workflow to identify metal-organic frameworks (MOFs) capable of shape-selective (SS) or inverse shape-selective (IS) adsorption of C6 isomer mixtures comprising n-hexane (n-hex), 2-methylpentane (2mp), and 2,3-dimethylbutane (23dmb). We first perform computational screening on the CoRE-MOF-2024 database with 14,500 MOFs and reveal distinct SS/IS schemes governed by pore confinement and cavity-guest matching. To translate separation performance into practical viability, we then shortlist MOFs with thermal, activation and mechanical stabilities. Guided by these screening results, we train high-fidelity machine learning (ML) classifiers that achieve receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) ≥ 0.90 and robust accuracy (0.88–0.91), enabling rapid prioritization beyond the screened set. For the more extensive and diverse ARC-MOF database with 270,000 MOFs, we identify two experimentally actionable candidates that surpass training-set benchmarks, achieving TSN(SS) = 15.17 and TSN(IS) = 2.57. This study establishes a generalizable, stability-aware ML paradigm for accelerating the digital discovery of deployable MOFs for challenging hydrocarbon separations and other industrially important applications.
10.1016/j.cej.2026.176943.title: Stability-aware, transferable discovery of metal-organic frameworks for selective adsorption of C6 alkane isomers by machine learning

10.1016/j.cej.2026.177199.abstract: Methane plays a dual role in modern society, serving as a valuable energy resource while also being a major contributor to climate change and a serious safety hazard due to its explosivity. As a result, the ability to reliably detect and quantify methane is critical across a wide range of sectors, including mining, oil and gas, agriculture, and waste management. Over the past decades, a diverse array of methane sensing technologies has been developed to address these needs, spanning laboratory-scale devices, field-deployable sensors, and large-area monitoring platforms. This review examines these technologies from a practical, application-driven perspective, covering their underlying sensing principles, material systems, performance characteristics, and typical deployment contexts. Point sensors such as catalytic pellistors, non-dispersive infrared sensors, and chemiresistive devices remain central to localized safety monitoring and leak detection, where fast response and robust operation are essential. At larger spatial scales, mobile and fixed open-path optical techniques enable real-time monitoring of methane over distances ranging from tens of meters to several kilometres, while airborne and satellite-based hyperspectral imaging now plays an increasingly important role in identifying large emission sources and validating regional and global emission inventories. Rather than viewing these approaches in isolation, this review frames methane detection as a complementary, multi-scale sensing hierarchy, in which different technologies address distinct but interconnected monitoring challenges. Particular attention is given to the trade-offs that currently limit widespread deployment, including selectivity, long-term stability, environmental interference, and cost. Finally, emerging trends in sensor integration, data fusion, and the coupling of sensing platforms with Internet of Things (IoT) infrastructure and AI-based analytics are discussed as key enablers for scalable, real-time methane monitoring and more effective emission mitigation strategies.
10.1016/j.cej.2026.177199.title: Advances in methane sensor development: From fundamentals to field deployment and future perspective
