10.1016/j.cej.2026.177302.abstract: Identifying suitable materials for industrial gas separation from a vast pool of candidates and performing preliminary process-level assessment of their separation potential remain challenging and time-consuming tasks. This study proposes a new end-to-end ultrafast screening framework for identifying optimal metal-organic frameworks (MOFs) for CO2/CH4 separation processes, using deep learning-based MOF property prediction. The proposed framework integrates molecular-level and process-level MOF screening evaluations. In the molecular-level, prescreening of the MOFs was conducted considering the physical descriptors of the MOF structures. Then, a lattice constant-hybridized graph neural network (GNN) was developed to predict CO2 and CH4 adsorption uptakes by combining global structural information with local atomic representations, overcoming the limited receptive field of standard GNN. The predicted uptakes enable pressure swing adsorption (PSA) process simulations to determine process-level metrics, including CH4 recovery and CO2 working capacity. The framework was applied to experimentally reported MOFs across three industrial scenarios with varying methane concentrations: landfill gas, biogas and coalbed methane. The proposed framework identified promising optimal MOF solutions for each application to enhance separation efficiency, including 290 for landfill gas, 42 for biogas, and 33 for coalbed methane. Structural analysis of top-performing MOFs provides recommended property ranges including pore limiting diameter of 5.12 ± 1.50 Å and volumetric surface area of 1183 ± 551 m2/cm3 that can guide adsorbent design. The techno-economic analysis demonstrates that the identified MOF-based PSA reduces separation cost by up to 51% and improves energy efficiency by up to 28% compared to conventional separation processes. This proposed screening framework provides a fast tool for narrowing large MOF databases to a manageable set of promising candidates, linking molecular-level prediction with process-level and techno-economic screening indicators that can guide subsequent rigorous evaluation.
10.1016/j.cej.2026.177302.title: Deep learning and process simulation-enabled discovery of high-performance MOFs for CO2/CH4 separation: An integrated molecular-to-process screening framework

10.1016/j.cej.2026.177383.abstract: Rapid carbon-neutral industrialization has significantly increased the demand for high-performance supercapacitors. Porous carbon materials have received great attention for their tunable structures and hierarchical porosity, which can be optimized to enhance capacitance. However, further research is needed to elucidate the relationship between pore size, morphology, doping ratio, and performance for practical energy storage applications. To address this challenge, we propose an effective strategy that combines theoretical predictions with in-situ self-assembly of hypercrosslinked polymers (HCPs) to design optimal electrode materials. Machine learning identifies key features of carbon materials, while density functional theory calculations confirm the strong K+ adsorption energy (−0.33 eV) from heteroatom incorporation. Guided by these insights, nitrogen, sulfur, and oxygen-doped HCPs with tubular morphology are synthesized via the Friedel-Crafts reaction to meet the identified criteria. Further pyrolysis forms a heteroatom-enriched porous carbon nanotube with a hierarchical structure. It exhibits exceptional performance, achieving a high capacitance of 812.43 F g−1 at 0.3 A g−1 in a 6 M KOH solution, along with remarkable cycling stability, retaining 99.84% of its capacitance after 10,000 cycles at 10 A g−1. This work provides a robust strategy for the rational design of porous carbon for energy storage, leveraging advanced theoretical predictions and assembly techniques.
10.1016/j.cej.2026.177383.title: Synergizing machine learning and self-assembly to hypercrosslinked polymers-based carbon nanotubes for supercapacitors

10.1016/j.cej.2026.177366.abstract: The urgent demand for efficient bifunctional oxygen electrocatalysts motivates innovative structural designs beyond conventional planar configurations. We propose a vertically stacked dual‑oxygen-bridged bilayer architecture (TMN4-2O-TMN4@C16N3) where oxygen ligands mediate interlayer charge transfer to optimize d-band and tailor adsorption of oxygen intermediates. By integrating density functional theory (DFT) with machine learning (ML), we screened 256 bilayer configurations, identifying exceptional bifunctional catalysts such as CoN4-2O-MoN4@C16N3 (ηOER = 0.49 V, ηORR = 0.36 V), outperforming IrO2/Pt benchmarks. ML predictions achieve high accuracy with mean absolute errors of 0.09 V (OER) and 0.11 V (ORR) against independent DFT validation. Crucially, constant-potential frontier orbital analysis revealed electrode-potential-driven Fermi level shifts and orbital rehybridization, decoding dynamic adsorption mechanisms beyond neutral DFT. Extension of the machine learning framework to 768 single-layer, trilayer, and quadlayer configurations enabled high-throughput exploration of expanded structural space (ultimately extending to 1024 layer-dependent configurations), with predictions rigorously validated by independent DFT calculations. While single-layer TMN4@C16N3 suffers from high OER/ORR overpotentials due to strong oxygen intermediate binding and resultant energy barriers, the trilayer structure achieves significantly lower overpotentials through optimized pathways; performance gains saturate at quadlayers as catalytic behavior becomes governed by adjacent-layer electronic coupling and diversified charge transfer pathways, highlighting the diminishing returns and critical layer-interaction synergy in layer-dependent catalyst design. This work establishes a scalable DFT-ML workflow for accelerating the discovery of oxygen-bridged electrocatalysts across diverse architectures, with the descriptor-based ML framework readily extendable to cost-effective TM combinations for practical applications.
10.1016/j.cej.2026.177366.title: Normal/inverse sandwich structure series-engineered layer-dependent double-atom catalysts featuring bridge-bonded dual‑oxygen ligands for bifunctional oxygen electrocatalysis: Machine learning-based layer-rich extended exploration and constant-potential frontier orbital analysis

10.1016/j.cej.2026.178048.abstract: The excessive use of modern pesticides poses significant risks to the environment and human health, yet their high-throughput discrimination in complex samples remains challenging. In this study, we report a functional material of single atom anchored covalent organic frameworks (COFs) based on self-assembly of COFs and iron porphyrin (COFs–Hemin) that has atomic Fe-N catalytic site, exhibiting highly efficient oxidase-like (OXD-like) and peroxidase-like (POD-like) activities and enabling efficient reactive oxygen species (ROS) generation without external energy input. COFs–Hemin with desired functional groups and nanozyme activity is employed to construct a colorimetric sensor array that successfully classifies five representative pesticides in fresh apple samples with high-throughput capability. Furthermore, integrating with a machine learning algorithm of multilayer perceptron (MLP) model that can discriminate mono-component and multicomponent mixtures of multiple pesticides, COFs–Hemin demonstrates excellent performance in surface water samples with a 95.7% classification accuracy and area under the curve (AUC) values exceeding 0.93 across all pesticide categories. The strategy that integrates single atom anchored COFs and machine learning delivers a reliable tool for high-throughput discrimination of multiple pesticides in environmental monitoring and food safety.
10.1016/j.cej.2026.178048.title: Single atom anchored covalent organic framework assisted with machine learning for high-throughput pesticides discrimination

10.1016/j.cej.2026.178296.abstract: Antimicrobial peptides (AMPs) are the natural defense molecules of the innate immune system, and have emerged as promising alternatives to conventional antibiotics owing to their broad-spectrum activity and low resistance potential. However, their clinical translation is hindered by proteolytic degradation and slow discovery pipelines. To address this, we developed a ProtBERT-based dual-objective machine learning (ML) framework and applied it to a constrained library of 20,000 peptide variants (6–12 residues) derived from the 18-residue bee-venom AMP, Melectin. The model was trained on curated datasets (∼25,000) to simultaneously screen for high antimicrobial potency and minimal hemolytic toxicity. This targeted approach identified 16 hit candidates, from which two lead peptides emerged, each containing at least four mutations relative to known sequences. The optimized peptides exhibited potent activity against methicillin-resistant S. aureus and P. aeruginosa, while demonstrating negligible hemolysis. The D-enantiomer of the lead peptide demonstrated efficacy against drug-resistant strains within serum-rich media. In 3D-spheroid infection models, the peptides demonstrated strong antimicrobial activity and low cytotoxicity, reflecting the promise of host-defense peptides and ML-guided strategies for scalable AMP discovery.
10.1016/j.cej.2026.178296.title: Dual-objective protein language model for discovery of non-hemolytic antimicrobial peptides from the bee-melectin sequence space

10.1016/j.cej.2026.178382.abstract: Cu2+ contamination in aquatic environments poses serious ecological and health risks, requiring efficient, sustainable remediation strategies. In this study, Mn-modified algal biochar was prepared and used as a model adsorbent to elucidate fulvic-acid (FA)-mediated Cu2+ adsorption in a ternary system. Characterization analyses revealed that Mn modification substantially increased the specific surface area, mesopore volume, and oxygen-containing surface functional groups, thereby enhancing Cu2+ affinity. Batch experiments demonstrated a pronounced FA “dual effect”: at a low concentration of 10 mg·L−1, FA markedly enhanced Cu2+ adsorption capacity up to 211.6 mg·g−1 through ternary surface complexation and increased negative surface charge, whereas a higher concentration of 20 mg·L−1 inhibited adsorption through competitive complexation in solution and surface-site blockage. Kinetic and isotherm analyses indicated dominant chemisorption, best described by the pseudo-second-order and Langmuir models, respectively. Density functional theory calculations clarified the microscopic mechanism, supporting preferential Cu2+ anchoring by MnO and carboxyl sites on the biochar followed by FA bridging to form stable ternary complexes. An extreme gradient boosting machine-learning model achieved strong predictive performance (R2 = 0.941 on the test set), with FA concentration and pH identified as the most influential factors. The major contribution of this work is not only the observation of FA concentration-dependent behavior, but also the identification of a DFT-supported Cu-bridged ternary complexation pathway and the ML-based quantification of key environmental controls. These findings provide mechanistic insights into FA-mediated Cu2+ adsorption and support Mn-modified algal biochar as a promising, sustainable adsorbent for heavy-metal remediation in surface water.
10.1016/j.cej.2026.178382.title: Elucidating the dual role of fulvic acid in Cu2+ adsorption on Mn-modified algal biochar through density functional theory and machine learning analyses

10.1016/j.cej.2026.178416.abstract: Kanamycin (KANA) overuse threatens public health, necessitating precise and portable detection approaches. To address this challenge, a ratiometric fluorescence sensor (TB-Eu-MOFs@MIPs@CsPbBr₃-Rb) was innovatively developed for ultrasensitive and selective detection of KANA. This sensor integrated oriented molecular imprinting on TB-Eu-MOFs with in-situ encapsulation of CsPbBr₃-Rb perovskite quantum dots. High-affinity imprinting layer featuring covalent/non-covalent dual-recognition sites boosted the precise identification of TB-Eu-MOFs@MIPs@CsPbBr₃-Rb to KANA. Thanks to synergistic dual-mechanism of dynamic quenching and electron transfer, water-resistant CsPbBr₃-Rb (520 nm) underwent pronounced fluorescence quenching upon exposure to KANA, boosting sensitivity. Conversely, the red fluorescence (620 nm) of TB-Eu-MOFs remained unaffected. Given inherent merits, TB-Eu-MOFs@MIPs@CsPbBr₃-Rb demonstrated exceptional suitability for ratiometric fluorescence profiling of KANA, featuring a linear range of 0.075–24.000 μg/mL, a detection limit of 22.5 ng/mL, a superior imprinting factor (6.66), ultra-fast response (2 min), attractive green-yellow-pale pink-red transformation, and satisfactory recoveries (90.00–98.43%). Intriguingly, by integrating a deep learning-driven smartphone device, the proposed sensor achieved on-site identification, concentration classification, and quantitative assay of KANA, demonstrating commendable precision and desirable recoveries (90.47–109.85%) in tap water, milk, and chicken. Accordingly, the deep learning-driven fluorescence sensor exhibited portability, feasibility, high selectivity, and sensitivity, offering a powerful tool for on-site food safety and environmental monitoring with high practicality.
keywords: Ratiometric fluorescence and deep learning-assisted intelligent detection
10.1016/j.cej.2026.178416.title: Deep learning-assisted intelligent fluorescence sensor incorporating perovskite quantum dots with dual-recognition imprinting polymers for ultrasensitive and high-selectivity kanamycin detection

10.1016/j.cej.2026.178898.abstract: As the global antimicrobial resistance (AMR) crisis continues to escalate, narrow-spectrum antimicrobial peptides (AMPs) have emerged as an important direction in precision anti-infective research. However, current AMPs design strategies remain largely focused on the optimization of broad-spectrum activity, and a systematic framework centered on pathogen-specific membrane interfaces is still lacking. This review focuses on deep learning (DL)-driven de novo design of membrane-interface-centered, or membrane-targeting, narrow-spectrum AMPs. It first delineates the conceptual boundaries among selectivity, targeting, specificity, and narrow-spectrum activity, and systematically summarizes exploitable differences at the cellular membrane level. It then further discusses how membrane-associated differences can be translated into programmable constraints within DL models, on the basis of which four major design routes are summarized. Subsequently, a multi-objective evaluation framework is established, and the workflow for AMPs validation across four distinct levels is outlined. Ultimately, in view of the current state of the field and its future development, targeted questions and methodological recommendations are proposed, with the aim of providing a clearer theoretical framework and methodological reference for more advanced AMPs design.
10.1016/j.cej.2026.178898.title: Deep learning-driven strategies for the de novo design of membrane-targeting narrow-spectrum antimicrobial peptides

10.1016/j.cej.2026.179140.abstract: Early-stage liver fibrosis in metabolic dysfunction–associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) remains difficult to identify because conventional indirect fibrosis indices inadequately reflect active fibrogenesis. Procollagen type I C-terminal peptide (PICP), released during extracellular processing of type I procollagen, directly reflects collagen synthesis and provides a mechanistically relevant biomarker for fibrosis activity. Here, we present a fibrosis electrochemical impedance spectroscopy platform (FIB-EIS), a label-free impedance immunosensor for direct quantification of PICP in human plasma. The sensing interface was engineered on a gold nanoparticle–modified screen-printed carbon electrode to provide stable antibody immobilization and controlled interfacial charge transport. Upon specific PICP binding, formation of a dielectric biolayer perturbed double-layer capacitance and charge-transfer kinetics, producing a concentration-dependent increase in charge-transfer resistance. To suppress matrix-driven interfacial fouling in plasma, a Tween-20–assisted interfacial control strategy was introduced, selectively removing weakly adsorbed plasma constituents and stabilizing a reproducible dual-time-constant impedance response. This enabled mechanistically interpretable equivalent-circuit analysis by separating double-layer and biomolecular capacitive contributions under complex plasma conditions. Under optimized conditions, FIB-EIS achieved picogram-level sensitivity with a detection limit of 0.81 pg mL−1 and high selectivity against abundant plasma proteins, including procollagen type III N-terminal peptide. Because plasma dilution shifts clinically relevant PICP concentrations into the pg mL−1 regime, this sensitivity supports early-stage fibrosis discrimination. Clinical validation across biopsy-staged fibrosis (F0–F4) demonstrated 95.24% sensitivity and 100% specificity. These results establish FIB-EIS as a physics-informed and clinically translatable platform for minimally invasive fibrosis activity assessment and longitudinal MASLD monitoring.
10.1016/j.cej.2026.179140.title: Precision detection of early-stage liver fibrosis in MASLD via physics-informed interfacial impedance sensing of procollagen type I C-terminal peptide

10.1016/j.cej.2026.179250.abstract: Proton exchange membrane water electrolysis (PEMWE) is promising for green hydrogen production, but its oxygen evolution reaction (OER) suffers from high overpotential and catalyst corrosion. While transition metal alloys exhibit excellent catalytic activity, traditional experiments and density functional theory (DFT) calculations are inefficient for exploring the vast binary alloy space. Machine learning enables rapid prediction and optimization by mining DFT data to map material properties with catalytic performance. Herein, this study integrates machine learning methods, including ABR, GBR, and other ensemble models, with DFT calculations to rapidly screen of acidic OER catalysts based on binary transition metal systems. Based on model predictions, we utilize electrodeposition and Joule heating techniques to synthesize FeRu alloy in a short period of time and perform experimental validation. The as-synthesized FeRu alloy exhibits exceptional bifunctional activity, requiring ultralow overpotentials of 171 mV (OER) and 47 mV (hydrogen evolution reaction) to achieve 10 mA cm−2 in acidic media. This catalyst reaches a current density of 1 A cm−2 at only 1.65 V in PEMWE. DFT calculations confirm that alloying optimizes electronic structure and reduces the rate-determining step (RDS) energy barrier, providing theoretical support for its excellent activity and stability. This work establishes a closed-loop framework that integrates data mining with experimental validation to shorten catalyst research and development cycles. It provides an efficient approach for screening and optimizing high-performance acidic PEMWE catalysts and facilitates the industrialization of green hydrogen production via PEMWE.
10.1016/j.cej.2026.179250.title: Synthesis of highly active binary alloy acidic oxygen evolution catalysts assisted by machine learning
10.1016/j.cej.2026.179250.source: ScienceDirect official citation and abstract BibTeX export

10.1016/j.cej.2026.178937.abstract: Modulating the d-band center of transition metals by doping engineering is an efficient strategy to enhance their catalytic efficiency. However, there remains a lack of systematic theoretical explanation for how doping engineering modulates the d-band center and activates antibonding orbitals at the electronic structure scale. Herein, using α-Fe2O3 (αFO) as a model transition metal, machine learning, density functional theory calculations and experimental characterization were integrated to elucidate the doping induced d-band center shifts. The results reveal that dopants modulated the crystal field splitting energy of transition metals, which in turn tailors the d-band center, thereby enhancing the catalyst's ability to activate the antibonding orbitals of reactive species. This mechanism rationalized the efficient degradation of metronidazole observed in the Cu-αFO/DBD/persulfate process. Furthermore, to elucidate the degradation mechanism at the molecular level, this study investigated the structure-activity relationship, specifically how the molecular structure of the pollutants and the catalytic system influence the degradation efficiency. The data revealed the correlation between molecular properties (e.g., dipole moment and energy of the lowest unoccupied molecular orbital) and degradation kinetics. The proposed d-band center modulation and antibonding orbital activation mechanism provides both a theoretical foundation and a practical pathway for the rational design of high performance transition metal catalysts.
10.1016/j.cej.2026.178937.title: Crystal field splitting energy mediated d-band center regulation in transition metal for enhancing plasma/persulfate degradation of metronidazole: Experiments, theoretical calculation and machine learning study

10.1016/j.cej.2026.179276.abstract: Polyolefin elastomers are widely utilized due to their unique combination of thermoplastic processability and rubber-like elasticity. Among them, comb-branched polyolefin elastomers (CPOEs) synthesized via tandem catalytic polymerization (TCP) of ethylene and α-olefin feature amorphous backbones with long polyethylene (PE) side chains, enabling elevated melting temperatures even at high α-olefin incorporation. Because TCP integrates ethylene homopolymerization with terpolymerization of ethylene, 1-octene, and PE macromonomers (PEMs), kinetic modeling is essential for tailoring CPOE chain structures while simultaneously controlling PEM incorporation and residual content. Herein, a kinetic model based on the method of moments was developed, with an orthogonalization algorithm employed to reduce the number of parameters requiring estimation. Direct coupling of the kinetic model with differential evolution (DE) optimization using a conventional ODE solver proved computationally intensive for parameter estimations. A large-scale training dataset was generated from the kinetic model with parameter ranges aligned to literature values and experimental observations, substantially reducing the need for expensive experimental data. The ML-assisted model was validated against experimental results. Systematic analyses of catalyst concentrations, 1-octene concentration, and polymerization times elucidated their impacts on CPOE chain structure, providing mechanistic insights for CPOE design. Overall, this study demonstrates a practical ML-assisted strategy for kinetic modeling of complex polymerization systems and provides a powerful tool for rational CPOE chain structure engineering and data-driven polymer product development.
10.1016/j.cej.2026.179276.title: Machine learning-assisted modeling of tandem catalytic polymerization for tailoring comb-branched polyolefin elastomers
10.1016/j.cej.2026.179276.source: ScienceDirect official citation and abstract BibTeX export

10.1016/j.cej.2026.179947.abstract: Understanding the adsorption behavior of PFAS on humic substances (HS) is critical for predicting their environmental fate and developing effective remediation strategies. Here, we integrate molecular dynamics (MD) simulations, experimental characterization, and explainable machine learning (XAI) to resolve PFAS interactions with HS at the molecular level. Based on 410 PFAS structures, MD-derived adsorption energies reveal a clear structure-dependent adsorption trend, with a strong negative correlation (Pearson's |r| > 0.72) between molecular weight and adsorption energy magnitude. Machine learning models show robust predictive performance (R2 > 0.88), enabling accurate adsorption-energy prediction across structurally diverse PFAS. SHAP analysis reveals that PFAS adsorption onto HS is governed by a synergistic interplay of multiple molecular descriptors rather than any single molecular property. Molar refractivity, Kappa3, Number of hydrogen bond acceptors, and molecular weight emerge as the most influential descriptors, highlighting the coupled roles of electronic polarizability, molecular topology, conformational adaptability, and size in controlling adsorption. In contrast, descriptors associated with polarity and hydration tendency are more closely linked to migration behavior. Adsorption experiments and complementary spectroscopic and microscopic characterizations consistently confirmed stronger fluorine accumulation and greater compaction of the HS matrix induced by long-chain PFAS. Overall, the results converge on a unified molecular picture in which larger, more polarizable, and structurally adaptable PFAS are preferentially retained, whereas smaller and more hydration-favored PFAS remain comparatively mobile. This work provides a physics-informed and interpretable framework for predicting PFAS transport in heterogeneous organic environments.
10.1016/j.cej.2026.179947.title: Structure-resolved adsorption of PFAS on humic substances: A combined study of molecular dynamics, explainable machine learning, and experiments
10.1016/j.cej.2026.179947.source: ScienceDirect official citation and abstract BibTeX export

10.1016/j.cej.2026.179538.abstract: Microplastics-derived dissolved organic matter (MPs-DOM) comprises a chemically heterogeneous pool of dissolved organic compounds released during the environmental degradation of microplastics. Despite growing interest in the environmental implications of MPs-DOM, its molecular composition and reactivity are still poorly characterized. In this study, Fourier-transform ion cyclotron resonance mass spectrometry (FT-ICR MS) was employed to characterize MPs-DOM released from polystyrene (PS), polyamide (PA), and poly(butylene adipate-co-terephthalate) (PBAT), as well as their transformation products formed during chlorination, and a reactivity prediction model was developed based on reaction networks. The results showed that all microplastics released MPs-DOM under dark conditions, while UV irradiation altered MPs surface functional groups and the molecular composition of the released MPs-DOM, leading to differences in chlorination reactivity between the dark and UV conditions. CHO dominated DOM derived from PS and PBAT, whereas PA-DOM was relatively enriched in CHNO compounds, indicating that MPs-DOM exhibited high molecular complexity and source dependent characteristics. Both aging and chlorination induced pronounced molecular transformations, leading to a significant increase in O/C ratios. The reaction network analysis linked 111 chlorine-containing DBP molecules to 127 precursors, including 122 polymer-specific precursors, with 63, 23, and 35 detected in PS, PA, and PBAT, respectively. A machine learning model based on extreme gradient boosting (XGBoost) successfully identified double bond equivalent (DBE) and nominal oxidation state of carbon (NOSC) as the primary molecular features associated with highly reactive MPs-DOM, achieving an overall prediction accuracy of 73.53%. This work provides a molecular-level understanding of the composition, formation mechanisms, and chlorination behavior of MPs-DOM, improving our understanding of the environmental behavior and potential risks associated with MPs-DOM.
10.1016/j.cej.2026.179538.title: Molecular characterization and chlorination reactivity of microplastics-derived dissolved organic matter revealed by ultrahigh-resolution mass spectrometry and machine learning
10.1016/j.cej.2026.179538.source: ScienceDirect official citation and abstract BibTeX export

10.1016/j.cej.2026.180181.abstract: The ligand modification of the catalyst is a promising strategy to enhance the yields of the aerobic reaction of aromatic hydrocarbons. The approach of machine learning incorporating high-throughput density functional theory (DFT) calculations successfully achieves the efficient screening and design of catalysts. In this work, the impact of ligands on catalyst activity was investigated. The results reveal how ligands influence the catalyst's properties and structure, which subsequently affects its reaction activity. A unique descriptor, φ, which is the ratio of nonpolar and surface area, was identified using ML for predicting yields and efficiently capturing catalytic activity trends for a variety of ligands (R2 = 0.999, error < 1%). The optimal catalyst, Cat II (cobalt bis(2-ethylhexanoate)), was selected by ML, which exhibits the highest yield (22.81 mol%). The kinetic model achieves great predictive ability for the variation in compound concentration under different conditions. The strategy incorporates ML, experimentation, and reaction kinetics, offering significant insights into catalyst screening, modifications, aerobic reaction, and modeling of aromatic hydrocarbons.

10.1016/j.cej.2026.180395.abstract: Achieving thin, target-specific microwave absorbers remains challenging because absorber performance is governed by the coupled interplay among complex permittivity, complex permeability, and thickness, while the direct linkage between target absorption behavior, electromagnetic-property spectra, and realizable material compositions is often limited. Here, we present a physics-informed optimization framework based on Zn–Co substituted Ba–W ferrite/CNT/TPU composites, in which magnetic and dielectric responses can be tuned in a decoupled manner. Co substitution in Ba–W ferrite selectively shifts the magnetic-loss frequency through anisotropy-controlled ferromagnetic resonance, whereas CNT loading independently modulates the dielectric response without significantly perturbing the magnetic behavior. Exploiting this decoupled tunability, complex permittivity and permeability were modeled separately using Kramers–Kronig-consistent spectral representations, namely a hybrid Cole–Cole model and a Gaussian–Dawson master-curve model, and then integrated into a differential-evolution-based optimization loop. This framework transformed discrete experimental datasets into a physically constrained continuous composition space, enabling continuous prediction of composition-dependent electromagnetic properties and target-specific optimization of absorber composition and thickness. As representative demonstrations, a 1.9 mm-thick absorber achieved full X-band absorption below −10 dB, whereas a 1.5 mm-thick absorber achieved nearly full Ku-band absorption below −10 dB with a measured −20 dB EAB of 3.76 GHz. Both absorbers were fabricated as 12 × 12 cm specimens and successfully validated by free-space RL measurements. This study provides an integrated framework that connects absorber performance, electromagnetic-property prediction, and material composition within a physically grounded optimization scheme.
10.1016/j.cej.2026.180395.title: Physics-informed surrogate modeling and optimization of Zn–Co substituted Ba–W ferrite/CNT/TPU composites for microwave absorbers

10.1016/j.cej.2026.180351.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is transforming protein engineering from an empirical discipline into a predictive and data-driven paradigm, accelerating the development of next-generation biocatalysts. Nevertheless, a significant gap remains because generative models can propose candidate proteins far more rapidly than laboratories can experimentally them, and computational novelty does not guarantee the performance under most of the process conditions. This review examines recent advances in AI-assisted protein engineering, highlighting how generative models, protein language models, and structure-prediction frameworks are reshaping enzyme discovery, design, and optimization. The evolution from conventional rational design and directed evolution to modern data-centric workflows built on the Design–Build–Test–Learn (DBTL) cycle is explored. Major AI architectures, such as transformers, diffusion models, variational autoencoders, and generative adversarial networks, are evaluated for their ability to generate novel protein structures and functional sequences. Most importantly, we summarize machine learning approaches for predicting enzyme activity, substrate specificity, catalytic efficiency, thermostability, solubility, and functional annotation, which facilitate candidate prioritization and reduce the experimental burden. Reported predictive performance reaches an R2 of 0.69 for turnover number and a Pearson coefficient of 0.84 for stability change, while computational triage eliminates 50% to 80% of the design pool before synthesis. Because sequence-function relationships are inherently nonlinear, a single metric optimization is unreliable. We therefore discuss current limitations, arising from data scarcity, model interpretability, cross-family transferability, developability, and the lack of standardized benchmarks. Future perspectives are provided on integrating multimodal biological data, foundation models, and autonomous experimentation to enable scalable biocatalyst development and accelerate the transition toward AI-driven sustainable biomanufacturing.
10.1016/j.cej.2026.180351.title: AI-driven de novo protein design coupled with high-throughput screening: Challenges and opportunities

10.1016/j.cej.2026.181128.abstract: The development of high-power electronics demands polymer dielectrics with high thermal stability and dielectric performance. However, most materials suffer performance degradation in harsh environments due to increased electrical conductivity. Herein, a physics-informed data-driven topology-supported precursor screening strategy was proposed to design quasi-branched polyimides (QbPIs) with enhanced energy density (Ue) and charge-discharge efficiency (η) at elevated temperatures. By constructing automated screening workflow, key descriptors involving HOMO-LUMO gap (Gap) and dielectric constant (εr) were sufficiently evaluated to form multi-parameter ranking framework, in which melamine was identified as the optimal topological center for constructing QbPIs with tunable topological ratios (0–2.5%). Notably, the resulting star-shaped topological structure effectively regulates charge transport and dielectric behavior through a cooperative mechanism. It increases the Gap, introduces deep-level traps, and stabilizes the Ag/dielectric interface, which together suppress conduction loss and charge injection, effectively disrupting long-range charge-transport pathways. The optimized QbPI-1.75 exhibited outstanding capacitive performance, delivering 5.39 J cm−3 (Ue) with 94% (η) at 25 °C, and retaining 3.29 J cm−3 with 78.41% at 200 °C, far exceeding that of pure PI (1.35 J cm−3, 87.6% η at 25 °C). This work establishes a fundamental structure-property relationship for topological PIs and provides a facile design strategy applicable to other high-temperature polymer dielectrics.
10.1016/j.cej.2026.181128.title: Physics-informed data-driven topology-supported precursor screening strategy for designing all-organic polyimide dielectrics with deep traps and wide-temperature-range

10.1016/j.cej.2026.181081.abstract: The vast compositional space of high-entropy materials makes the discovery of superior solid electrolytes extremely challenging. Here, we introduce a hybrid artificial intelligence (AI) framework that synergistically combines unsupervised learning with crystal graph convolutional neural networks (CGCNN) in a dual-stage screening architecture. This approach navigates >1800 potential Zr-site doped Li7La3Zr2O12 (LLZO) compositions, first partitioning them into 21 distinct groups via unsupervised clustering, then focusing on a high-potential group (G19) for precise CGCNN prediction of band gaps and Li+ diffusion barriers. This AI-identified optimal high-entropy electrolyte, Li7La3Zr0.4Cr0.4Mo0.4Sn0.4Ta0.4O12 (HE-LLZO), would otherwise require years of trial-and-error. Entropy stabilization lowers the synthesis temperature to 920 °C and suppresses detrimental Li2CO3/LiOH surface formation. Bond valence site energy (BVSE) calculations, supported by solid-state NMR and geometric phase analysis, reveal that the high-entropy configuration introduces moderate lattice distortion (dσ = 0.104 Å) and significantly flattens the 3D Li+ migration energy landscape, reducing the macroscopic diffusion barrier from 1.060 eV (pristine LLZO) to 0.777 eV. Consequently, HE-LLZO achieves a high ionic conductivity of 1.05 × 10−3 S cm−1, a low activation energy of 0.287 eV, and an expanded electrochemical window of 4.81 V. All-solid-state cells with Ta-doped NCM811 cathodes retain 92.5% capacity after 250 cycles, and flexible pouch cells (NCM90|SE|Li-alloy) deliver 200.1 mAh g−1 with 86% retention after 200 cycles, demonstrating practical viability. This work establishes a generalizable, AI-guided paradigm for accelerating the discovery of high-entropy solid electrolyte toward high-energy-density batteries.
10.1016/j.cej.2026.181081.title: AI-accelerated discovery of a high-entropy garnet electrolyte with a flattened Li-ion energy landscape for practical solid-state batteries

10.1016/j.cej.2026.181186.abstract: Efficient drug delivery across the blood-brain barrier (BBB) remains a formidable challenge. While peptide-mediated transcytosis is promising, the rational de novo design of BBB-penetrating peptides lacks systematic principles. Here, we developed a novel multi-receptor, explainable, and uncertainty-aware reinforcement learning framework that integrates multi-task affinity prediction with physicochemical constraints for the de novo design of BBB-penetrating peptides. By integrating multivalent transcytosis datasets and physicochemical constraints, our model generates highly feasible, BBB-permeable candidates. Experimental validation of a representative generated peptide, 1 L, demonstrated that it drives robust nanoparticle transcytosis without compromising vascular integrity. Mechanistically, 1 L specifically targets the LRP1 receptor, orchestrating active endothelial endocytosis and vesicular trafficking. In vivo, 1 L-conjugated nanoparticles achieved profound brain parenchymal accumulation with a unique spatial selectivity—enriching in the cortex and striatum while bypassing limbic septal nuclei, thereby offering a potential “spatial selectivity pattern”, outperforming several established LRP1-targeted systems in brain parenchymal delivery. Systemic administration of 1 L-nanotherapeutics significantly suppressed tumor progression and prolonged survival in an orthotopic glioblastoma model without systemic toxicity. This AI-driven paradigm provides a powerful, generalizable strategy for designing precision neurotherapeutics.
10.1016/j.cej.2026.181186.title: Explainable reinforcement learning designs a LRP1-targeted BBB-penetrating peptide with spatial selectivity for glioblastoma therapy

10.1016/j.cej.2026.181891.abstract: Efficient discrimination of multiple volatile organic compounds using a single metal-oxide semiconductor sensor at near room temperature remains challenging. Herein, MOF-derived In-doped ZnO engineered with abundant defects and porous structure exhibits superior dual-gas sensing performance under blue-light activation at near room temperature, making it particularly well-suited for machine-learning-driven gas identification. Among the In-doped samples, comprehensive SEM, TEM, and BET analyses, together with XPS, PL, EPR, EIS, and transient photocurrent measurements, demonstrated that ZnO/In-0.1 achieved the optimal balance among surface area, oxygen vacancy (Ov), and photogenerated carrier transfer. Under 450 nm irradiation at approximately 60 °C, it delivered Δresponses of 527 and 509 to 10 ppm triethylamine (TEA) and N-butanol, respectively, with response times of 57 and 80 s and theoretical detection limits of 6.72 and 5.53 ppb, while exhibiting negligible responses in the dark. RandomForest achieved 97.8% held-out classification accuracy for gas-composition classes, while XGBoost predicted the concentrations of both gases with an overall R2 of 0.956. Density functional theory (DFT) calculations showed that In incorporation lowered the Ov formation energy, introduced defect and band-tail states, and strengthened the adsorption of TEA (−1.8253 eV) and N-butanol (−1.1814 eV). The enhanced sensing performance arises from composition-structure-function coupling among optimized In loading, defect-rich porous structure, sub-bandgap carrier activation, and preferential target-gas adsorption, providing a strategy for intelligent visible light activated dual-gas sensing.
10.1016/j.cej.2026.181891.title: Machine learning assisted identification of MOF-derived ZnO/In dual gas sensor activated by blue light at near room temperature

10.1016/j.cej.2026.181984.abstract: The commercialization of high-energy, high-voltage lithium-ion and next-generation batteries hinges on how precisely the cathode–electrolyte interphase (CEI) can be understood and controlled. Far from being a static boundary, the CEI is a dynamic, compositionally heterogeneous reaction zone in which oxidative decomposition products of the electrolyte accumulate, rearrange, and continuously evolve with cycling. This review (i) establishes the fundamentals of CEI formation, structure, and growth kinetics; (ii) surveys interphase behavior across cathode families—Ni-rich NCM/NMC, high-voltage spinels, Li-rich oxides, sodium/zinc/dual-ion systems, and solid-state cells; (iii) organizes stabilization strategies spanning electrolyte additives, solvation engineering, surface coating and doping, artificial CEIs, and dry-electrode processing; and (iv) compares advanced characterization tools including cryo-EM, in situ TEM, XPS/ToF-SIMS, and EIS/DRT. The review also examines AI and machine-learning approaches relevant to CEI research, including machine-learning interatomic potentials, physics-informed learning, electrolyte and additive screening, multiscale imaging and computational analysis, and battery-level diagnostics. We close by presenting an integrated experiment–simulation–AI framework for data-driven interphase analysis and design.
10.1016/j.cej.2026.181984.title: The cathode–electrolyte interphase meets artificial intelligence: From formation and evolution mechanisms to data-driven interphase design

10.1016/j.cej.2026.181836.abstract: The CRISPR/Cas system integrates programmable target recognition with diverse catalytic activities and versatile signal transduction mechanisms, rendering it a powerful platform for molecular detection. The performance of CRISPR/Cas-based sensors is largely determined by the properties of their core molecular components, including guide RNAs (gRNAs), Cas proteins, and signal output elements. Therefore, molecular engineering of these components represents a critical strategy for enhancing target recognition, catalytic efficiency, detection sensitivity, specificity, and overall signal fidelity. Such engineering primarily relies on rational design to regulate sensing performance, including (i) gRNA sequence and structure optimization; (ii) Cas protein engineering via site-specific mutations or functional domain fusions; and (iii) modification of signal probes. These strategies collectively enable the rational design of CRISPR/Cas sensors with tailored performance for diverse applications. With the advancement of artificial intelligence (AI), machine learning and deep learning have expanded the capabilities for designing and analyzing CRISPR/Cas components. Protein language models and computer vision further support the prediction of gRNA activity and off-target effects, the discovery and functional optimization of Cas proteins, and the intelligent analysis of detection signals. These approaches enable more efficient and accurate CRISPR/Cas system development. This paper systematically reviews molecular engineering strategies for CRISPR/Cas sensing elements at three levels: gRNAs, Cas proteins, and signal output. We discuss how rational and AI-assisted approaches leverage sequence, structural, molecular interaction, and experimental data to optimize sensing performance. AI-assisted methods are further highlighted for their potential to reduce screening costs, narrow the design space, and improve engineering efficiency. In closing, we highlight the key challenges and outline future perspectives for realizing CRISPR sensing platforms that combine high sensitivity, specificity, robustness, and broad adaptability.
10.1016/j.cej.2026.181836.title: Molecular engineering of CRISPR biosensors: From rational design to AI acceleration

10.1016/j.cej.2026.182266.abstract: Reliable prediction of lignocellulosic intermediate pyrolysis kinetics is critical for scaling up thermochemical conversion processes, yet remains challenging at high heating rates. We developed a physics-informed long short-term memory network (PINN-LSTM) integrating particle swarm optimization (PSO) with recurrent neural networks, trained on only 13 thermogravimetric/derivative thermogravimetric (TG/DTG) curves from pure components, blends, and real straws. PSO inversely determines apparent phenomenological kinetic triplets (E, A, n), embedded as Arrhenius-based soft constraints in the LSTM loss function, enforcing physical feasibility without compromising flexibility. On the three held-out straws PINN-LSTM attains RMSE values of 0.80, 0.78 and 0.80 wt%·min−1, corresponding to a 43% reduction in mean RMSE relative to the vanilla LSTM and approximately 76% relative to HRF, the strongest tree ensemble; each comparison is stated against a single named baseline rather than as a combined range. The model accurately captures shoulder-peak transitions and high-temperature tails, with peak-temperature errors below 1 K. The E-lnA relationship observed is that expected under single-heating-rate inversion and is reported as an apparent, jointly determined descriptor rather than as an independently established physical law. A web-based interface enables real-time parameter estimation (E=228 kJ·mol−1, lnA=42.1 s−1, n=2.31) with automated visualization, facilitating industrial adoption. This synergy between data-driven learning and physics-based constraints demonstrates broader applicability to thermochemical systems with mechanistic priors and data scarcity.
10.1016/j.cej.2026.182266.title: Physics-informed LSTM for lignocellulosic pyrolysis kinetics at elevated heating rates: Integrating Arrhenius constraints with data-driven modeling

10.1016/j.cej.2026.182673.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is advancing molecular and materials discovery by linking chemical data with predictive modeling, inverse design, reaction planning, experimental optimization, and increasingly integrated laboratory workflows. This review critically examines AI-assisted molecular and materials discovery from methodological, bibliometric, application-oriented, and chemical engineering perspectives. We first outline the core workflow for reliable chemical machine learning, covering data acquisition and curation, chemical representation, model construction, and evaluation, with particular attention to data regimes, generalization, uncertainty, applicability domains, interpretability, and experimental validation. A bibliometric analysis of Web of Science Core Collection records retrieved from 1 January 2016 to 10 April 2026, with 2026 treated as partial-year coverage, contextualizes the evolution and interconnection of major research themes. Four application directions are examined: property prediction and virtual screening; reaction planning, reaction engineering, and process optimization; generative inverse design; and large language model (LLM)-enabled multimodal and increasingly automated workflows. Across these directions, we compare method suitability and validation strength and distinguish computational prediction and generation from prospective experimental validation, closed-loop optimization, and autonomous experimentation. Translation to chemical engineering practice is evaluated in terms of reactor and operating constraints, transport phenomena, scale-up, process control, process safety, and techno-economic feasibility. Finally, challenges are organized into four categories: data, representation, model, and deployment, with emphasis on representative datasets, chemically and physically constrained representations, realistic validation, uncertainty-aware decisions, and tighter integration of computation, experiment, and process engineering.
10.1016/j.cej.2026.182673.title: AI-assisted molecular and materials discovery in chemistry and chemical engineering: A methodological and bibliometric review

10.1016/j.cej.2026.182346.abstract: Defective oxide supports provide reactive vacancy sites for CO2 activation, but strong initial activation alone does not guarantee favorable CO2-to-CO thermodynamics because downstream intermediate stabilization must also be optimized. Here, vacancy–metal–site (VMS) coupling in defective MgO-supported single-atom catalysts is systematically investigated by integrating density functional theory (DFT), descriptor-guided screening, multimodal transfer learning, and computational hydrogen electrode (CHE) analysis. The target-domain MgO-Ov-TM space, where Ov denotes a surface oxygen vacancy and TM denotes a transition-metal single atom, contains 120 configurations constructed from 20 3d/4d transition-metal dopants and six representative adsorption environments. DFT calculations reveal that oxygen vacancies promote CO2 bending and charge redistribution, whereas favorable CO2-to-CO thermodynamics require coordinated regulation of *COOH formation and *CO stabilization by metal identity and local adsorption environments. To enrich promising candidates, a Vacancy–Metal–Site Multimodal Transfer Learning (VMS-MTL) framework was adapted from graph–text transfer-learning strategies by integrating geometry-aware graph embeddings pretrained on the Open Catalyst 2020 (OC20) dataset with structured chemical-text representations. VMS-MTL achieved mean absolute errors (MAEs) of 0.219 eV for Eads of CO and 0.363 eV for |d-band center|, recovering eight of nine DFT-screened candidates within the top-15 out-of-fold (OOF) rankings. Subsequent CHE analysis identified Sc-T-Mg_Def, corresponding to a Sc atom coupled with the defect-neighboring Mg top site, as the most thermodynamically favorable configuration within the investigated MgO-Ov-TM space, with a limiting free-energy change (ΔGmax) of 0.316 eV. Further analysis shows that strong initial CO2 activation is not directly correlated with thermodynamic favorability, revealing a system-specific Sabatier-type trade-off. These findings establish VMS coupling as a framework linking vacancy-assisted activation with metal/site-regulated intermediate stabilization, while multimodal transfer learning enables data-efficient candidate enrichment before detailed DFT/CHE analysis.
10.1016/j.cej.2026.182346.title: Vacancy–metal–site coupling in defective MgO-supported single-atom catalysts for CO2-to-CO reduction: DFT screening assisted by multimodal transfer learning

10.1016/j.cej.2026.183009.abstract: Clinical cartilage repair remains limited by fibrocartilage formation rather than hyaline-like cartilage repair after microfracture. Engineering an instructive extracellular matrix (ECM)-mimetic microenvironment is therefore essential for directing the fate of endogenous bone marrow mesenchymal stem cells (BMSCs). Here, we introduced a data-driven strategy integrating literature-derived machine learning with native cartilage matrix analysis to guide scaffold design for cartilage regeneration. Guided by this framework, a chondrocyte-mimetic polymer scaffold (HRC) was constructed using recombinant human type II collagen (rhCol II), type I collagen (Col I), and thiolated hyaluronic acid (HA-SH). Within the scaffold, Col I self-assembled into a strong fibrous framework that provided structural support, while rhCol II participated in the intermolecular organization of the composite matrix. In vitro, HRC enhanced BMSC migration and chondrogenic differentiation. Furthermore, HRC promoted regeneration of a smooth articular surface with an ordered matrix architecture and abundant proteoglycan deposition in cartilage defect models. RNA sequencing revealed enrichment of PI3K–Akt-related signaling, while PI3K inhibition supported its involvement in the in vitro chondrogenic response. Taken together, these findings support the relevance of tissue-specific matrix design for cartilage repair. Overall, the machine learning (ML) strategy used in this study can extend to other tissues constituting with collagen such as the meniscus.
10.1016/j.cej.2026.183009.title: Artificial intelligence-driven glycosaminoglycan-mimetic polymer design for cartilage regeneration

10.1016/j.cej.2026.182875.abstract: Amid the global energy transition, digital infrastructure upgrading, and rapid growth of high-end manufacturing, the efficient recovery and high-value utilization of critical metals (Ga, Ge and In) have become important research priorities in resource recycling and strategic mineral security. To address the challenges of the dispersed distribution of Ga, Ge and In in zinc sulfate solution, and the low efficiency of their co-recovery. This study investigated the ultrasonic-enhanced goethite co-precipitation method for simultaneously pre-enriching Ga, Ge and In from a simulated acidic zinc sulfate solution. Based on these findings, an ANN-GA optimization model was developed to achieve precise optimization of multi-parameter coupling. The results indicated that ultrasonic enhancement can significantly improve the goethite formation process and the solid-liquid distribution behavior of Ga, Ge and In, enabling the efficient synergistic enrichment of three rare metals under optimized conditions (ωFe = 99.91%, ωGa = 99.81%, ωGe = 99.71%, ωIn = 99.70%). To elucidate ultrasound effects, conventional characterization techniques were combined with mineral liberation analysis (MLA), atomic force microscopy (AFM), and extended X-ray absorption fine structure (EXAFS). The results show ultrasonic cavitation enhances mass transfer, oxidation, and hydrolysis, while modifying microstructure, crystal defects, and interfacial properties of the goethite coprecipitation residue. Ultrasonic treatment produces a more porous and defect-rich goethite coprecipitation residue with increased surface accessibility, thereby promoting the enrichment of Ga, Ge, and In. Molecular dynamics simulations (MD) further indicated element dependent spatial distributions of Ge(OH)4, Ga3+, and In3+ near the goethite/water interface. Overall, ultrasound enhanced goethite co-precipitation provided an effective process for the simultaneous pre-enrichment of Ga, Ge, and In from zinc sulfate solutions and provided a scientific basis for their subsequent selective separation and recovery.
10.1016/j.cej.2026.182875.title: Ultrasound-enhanced goethite coprecipitation for synergistic enrichment of Ga, Ge and In: A combined molecular dynamics, artificial neural network and EXAFS study
10.1016/j.cej.2026.182875.source: ScienceDirect official citation and abstract BibTeX export

10.1016/j.cej.2026.183004.abstract: Metal-organic frameworks (MOFs) hold immense promise for industrial adsorption and catalysis. However, practical deployment is often hindered by insufficient simultaneous water and thermal stability under harsh hygrothermal conditions. Furthermore, the mechanistic differences and potential trade-offs underlying water and thermal stability remain largely unexplored. Here, we establish an interpretable machine-learning framework integrating molecular descriptors and synthetic parameters to decode the mechanisms governing dual stability. Subsequent feature attribution analyses quantitatively reveal the asymmetric regulation underlying dual-stability. Thermal stability is synergistically determined by multidimensional parameters, including nuclearity and synthesis conditions. In contrast, the water-stability model shows a pronounced association with elemental electronegativity, with additional variation associated with structural descriptors within the sampled chemical space. Notably, increasing certain features (e.g., ligand-to-metal ratio > 1, topological polar surface area (TPSA) > 150 Å) enhances water stability at the expense of thermal stability, exposing pronounced trade-offs. Guided by these insights, we delineate a quantitative design space for dual-stability (e.g., metal electronegativity < 1.8, TPSA < 150 Å, 0.3 < ligand-to-metal ratio < 1.1). Targeted synthesis and characterization of representative MOFs confirm that materials within these parameters reliably achieve superior stability. These findings establish quantitative design rules for overcoming stability trade-offs and enabling the rational engineering of robust MOFs, accelerating industrial application under complex hygrothermal conditions.
10.1016/j.cej.2026.183004.title: Deciphering the water-thermal stability trade-offs via interpretable machine learning for reliable design of dual-stable MOFs

10.1016/j.cej.2026.183130.abstract: The rational design of inorganic materials is often hindered by the complexity of solid-state synthesis, which remains largely empirical and reliant on trial-and-error optimization. Bridging the gap between atomistic mechanisms and macroscopic processing, we present a fully reactive computational synthesis framework capable of predicting phase evolution directly from precursor materials. By leveraging machine learning molecular dynamics (MLMD) driven by the Crystal Hamiltonian Graph Neural Network (CHGNet) potential, we successfully reproduced the experimental synthesis trajectories of the Li2S-P2S5 solid electrolyte system. Our simulations captured the composition-dependent formation of local structural environments characteristic of Li7P3S11, Li3PS4, and Li7PS6 phases from 70, 75, and 87.5 mol% Li2S precursors, respectively. Detailed structural analyses revealed the systematic cleavage of bridging sulfur bonds and the dominance of terminal PS43− tetrahedra with increasing Li content, closely mirroring experimental thiophosphate speciation. Although limited simulation timescales restricted full crystallization, the resulting structures exhibited high fidelity to experimentally reported glassy intermediates, as confirmed by structure factor calculations and SOAP-based similarity analysis. This work demonstrates the feasibility of a “virtual reactor” for exploring synthesis pathways, offering a safe and efficient strategy to accelerate the discovery of complex solid-state materials.
10.1016/j.cej.2026.183130.title: Unveiling the atomic scale synthesis dynamics of lithium thiophosphate electrolytes via machine learning interatomic potentials

10.1016/j.cej.2026.183437.abstract: Wearable sensors have emerged as a technology for advancing healthcare through non-invasive, continuous, and real-time monitoring of physiological signals. Despite progress, healthcare systems face challenges in prevention, screening, diagnosis, and management due to reliance on invasive procedures, intermittent measurements, bulky equipment, and interventions. Although wearable sensors can generate data and improve accessibility, their ability to provide clinical insights remains limited. Meanwhile, the complexity of wearable health data places demands on clinical interpretation. Machine learning (ML) offers an approach to uncover patterns from datasets and establish relationships between physiological signals and health outcomes. However, the integration of wearable sensors and ML into practice remains constrained by challenges of data quality, model robustness, interpretability, privacy, and regulatory compliance. In this review, we examine recent advances in wearable sensor-ML systems for healthcare applications. We first introduce the operating principles and classifications of wearable sensors alongside the concepts and methodologies of ML. Then we survey the application of wearable sensor-ML technologies across a wide range of diseases, highlighting representative studies and comparing the performance, advantages, and limitations of ML approaches in wearable healthcare scenarios. Furthermore, we discuss the technical, clinical, and ethical barriers to real-world implementation and summarize strategies to overcome these limitations. By integrating developments with an assessment of challenges, this review underscores the potential of wearable sensor-ML systems for enabling more accurate, continuous, and personalized healthcare. The perspectives provide a roadmap for future research and translation, accelerating the development of intelligent healthcare technologies and advancing the realization of predictive, preventive, personalized, and participatory (4P) medicine.
10.1016/j.cej.2026.183437.title: Machine learning-integrated wearable sensors for intelligent disease diagnosis and personalized healthcare
10.1016/j.cej.2026.183437.source: ScienceDirect official citation and abstract BibTeX export

10.1016/j.cej.2026.183238.abstract: Continuous disposal of various organic wastes and polymers causes environmental and economic drawbacks. Pyrolysis converts scrap tyres, waste plastics, and biomass into bio-oil, syngas, and char, via co-processing. However, optimizing yield and quality across these heterogeneous feedstocks demands models that can navigate highly nonlinear, scale-dependent thermochemistry. This review uniquely couples artificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning (ML) for all three waste streams in a single mechanistic and automation-oriented framework. The present review documents the reaction kinetics of tires, plastics and biomass and maps these pathways directly to input features and explainable AI techniques. A comparative synthesis of reported R2, RMSE, and MAE data across various feedstocks in literature show that gradient-boosted tree ensembles (XGBoost, LightGBM) outperform deep neural architectures on small pyrolysis datasets. For instance, a deep mixture of experts model collapsed under 10-fold cross validation on a 468-record dataset, underscoring that model complexity without adequate data is counterproductive. The challenges with AI/ML applications in pyrolysis are briefly outlined and mapped with possible recommendations. In addition, an autonomous robotic development platform was framed as a future scope of the present review.
10.1016/j.cej.2026.183238.title: Role of artificial intelligence and machine learning techniques in pyrolytic liquefaction of biomass and waste polymers: From mechanistic insights to process automation
10.1016/j.cej.2026.183238.source: ScienceDirect official citation and abstract BibTeX export

10.1016/j.cej.2026.183775.abstract: Inverse design is an emerging data-driven paradigm for efficiently navigating vast chemical spaces to discover new materials with targeted properties, and in the context of heterogeneous catalysis, surface generative models have recently advanced this goal by directly generating catalyst surface-adsorbate structures. However, these models typically operate at the slab level and do not provide the corresponding parent bulk structure, making it difficult to assess bulk-dependent properties such as formation energy, surface energy, crystallographic symmetry, and synthesizability. Here, we address this missing slab-to-bulk connection as a retrieval problem and introduce CatRetriever, a contrastive representation learning model that aligns slab and bulk crystal representations in a shared latent space. From a slab query, CatRetriever accurately retrieves plausible parent bulk candidates with R@1 > 91% and R@3 > 98%. We further extend the CatRetriever framework into an adsorption energy-guided candidate screening pipeline that combines bulk retrieval, generative search space expansion, and adsorption energy distribution analysis. This workflow evaluates candidates by both structural compatibility with the query slab and their ability to access the target adsorption energy range across diverse surface environments. CatRetriever therefore provides a scalable route for connecting catalyst generative models with physically plausible and adsorption energy compatible bulk catalyst discovery.
10.1016/j.cej.2026.183775.title: CatRetriever: Contrastive representation learning for slab-to-bulk retrieval in generative catalyst discovery
10.1016/j.cej.2026.183775.source: ScienceDirect official citation and abstract BibTeX export

10.1016/j.cej.2026.183461.abstract: With the growing global demand for long-duration energy storage technologies, redox flow batteries (RFBs) have become a major research hotspot owing to their decoupled power and capacity and high safety. Nevertheless, challenges including slow screening of active materials, complex multi-physics field coupling and insufficient accuracy of system state monitoring hinder their large-scale commercialization. For aqueous systems in particular, inherent challenges throughout the entire lifecycle of research, development and operation remain, such as coupled pH-potential effects, solubility-potential trade-offs, aqueous solvation effects, as well as hydrolysis and polymerization side reactions. As an emerging data-driven technology, machine learning (ML) features powerful nonlinear fitting and cross-scale modeling capabilities, which are transforming the research paradigm of aqueous flow batteries at an unprecedented rate. This paper systematically reviews the state-of-the-art applications of machine learning across the full lifecycle of flow batteries. First, it summarizes data-driven strategies for property prediction and high-throughput screening of electrolyte molecules in terms of material design. Second, hardware optimization covers membrane design, electrode optimization, and flow-field simulation and topology optimization. Third, the applications of machine learning in state of charge and state of health estimation during system operation are elaborated. Furthermore, the great potential of machine learning in mapping and regulating the full-cycle operation of aqueous flow batteries is demonstrated in the development of surrogate models and digital twins. Finally, this paper concludes the overall research advances and highlights the key challenges facing the future development of intelligent research and innovation systems for aqueous flow batteries.
10.1016/j.cej.2026.183461.title: From molecular discovery to system management: A mini-review on machine learning driving full-cycle optimization of aqueous flow batteries

10.1016/j.cej.2026.183652.abstract: Antimicrobial resistance (AMR) has evolved from a clinical challenge into a system-level engineering problem that demands therapeutic platforms capable of retaining efficacy in protease-rich, heterogeneous, and dynamically evolving infection microenvironments. Conventional antimicrobial peptides (AMPs) are limited by inadequate proteolytic stability and insufficient selectivity, while isolated advances in AI-driven sequence design, non-natural peptide chemistry, and supramolecular self-assembly have yet to be integrated into a coherent engineering framework. This review presents an integrative perspective on the co-design of molecular composition, supramolecular organization, and computational prediction for self-assembling non-natural peptide antimicrobial nanostructures. We survey chemistry-aware graph encoders, conditional generative models, and multi-task phenotype predictors, and critically assess the evidence for their applicability to peptoid, halogenated, and stapled scaffolds. On the materials side, we analyze stimulus-responsive shape transformation for biofilm eradication, self-assembling hydrogels for infected wound repair, and supramolecular shielding as a safety-by-design strategy. The review makes four engineering contributions: (i) an AI-ready minimum characterization data set spanning six interoperable domains; (ii) a critical analysis of four major AMP clinical failures (pexiganan, omiganan, iseganan, brilacidin) with translatable lessons; (iii) a manufacturability framework linking continuous-flow SPPS to closed-loop design; and (iv) a maturity-tiered assessment of what AI-guided peptide design can and cannot yet deliver. We argue that the field is mature enough to generate chemically-expanded libraries and integrate manufacturability constraints, but not yet ready to replace in vivo validation with in silico surrogates.
10.1016/j.cej.2026.183652.title: Engineering precision antimicrobials: AI-driven design of self-assembling non-natural peptide nanostructures

10.1016/j.jmsy.2025.12.011.abstract: Milling is widely employed in precision component manufacturing for aerospace and other high-precision industries. Indirect tool wear monitoring via machining signals provides critical references for timely tool replacement in real-world, ensuring production quality and cost efficiency. However, due to practical constraints (e.g., sensor costs), some machining signal channels may be missing, while sensor failures (e.g., poor contact or damage) can lead to abnormal signals in other channels. Consequently, historical models trained on intact data often fail when confronted with such heterogeneous data. To address this issue, this paper proposes a physics-informed multi-task heterogeneous transfer learning network for robust milling tool wear prediction under anomalous data conditions. The framework employs channel-specific autoencoders, jointly pre-trained via inter-channel adaptation on intact historical data, along with physics-informed attention, to homogenize heterogeneous data. Furthermore, a Frank-Wolfe solver based multi-task loss weighting strategy, inter-domain adaptation, and soft/hard physical constraints guide the predictor's learning process, ensuring consistency with prior physical knowledge and enabling parallel prediction of multi-blade wear. Finally, the max predicted wear is utilized to estimate remaining useful life. Comparative studies with state-of-the-art (SOTA) models in related domains validate the superior accuracy and robustness of the proposed method. Extensive experiments on two public datasets further demonstrate that the proposed method achieves high generalizability. Taking PHM2010 dataset as an example, compared to the best-performing comparative model, the MAE of the proposed model tested on normal or heterogeneous data are 13.8 % and 25.8 % lower, respectively. And the degradation rates of MAE, RMSE and R2 are 0.15, 3.12, and 3.86 % points lower, respectively, when tested on simulated channel-failure data.
10.1016/j.jmsy.2025.12.011.title: Physics-informed multi-task heterogeneous transfer learning network for robust milling tool wear and RUL prediction under anomalous data conditions

10.1016/j.jmsy.2025.11.024.abstract: Deep learning-based tool wear monitoring methods often suffer from poor interpretability, parameter redundancy, and limited cross-domain generalization, especially under variable operating conditions and when only small sample sizes are available. These limitations hinder their practical deployment in practical manufacturing environments. To overcome these challenges, this study proposes a highly interpretable and lightweight tool wear monitoring framework tailored for small-sample, variable-condition scenarios. The method randomly extracts fixed-length segments from vibration signals to construct small-sample datasets, utilizing both signal envelope spectrum and cutting time as input features. Guided by the degradation law of tool wear, explicit physical constraints are imposed on the solution space of a Kolmogorov‑Arnold Fourier neural network, yielding a physics‑informed data‑driven model. SHAP analysis is employed to quantify the contribution of each feature, enhancing model transparency. Validation on public datasets under both single‑ and multi‑condition settings demonstrates that the proposed method delivers excellent performance across diverse operating conditions, achieving a stable prediction R² of up to 95 %, an inference latency of only 2 ms, and a reduction of approximately 90 % in model parameters. This solution can be integrated into the edge computing platform of CNC systems, making it particularly suitable for machining scenarios with high real-time requirements. It offers a lightweight, precise, and efficient monitoring capability for smart factories, contributing simultaneously to improvements in product quality and manufacturing efficiency.
10.1016/j.jmsy.2025.11.024.title: PI-KAF: A physics-informed constrained online interpretable monitoring method for tool wear

10.1016/j.jmsy.2026.01.002.abstract: Data-driven methods have shown remarkable promise across manufacturing disciplines. However, their application to manufacturing processes, where physical behaviors dominate, faces several limitations including the need for large datasets, the risk of physically implausible results, and limited interpretability. Physics-informed machine learning (PIML), which incorporates governing physical laws into deep neural networks, has emerged as a promising direction for overcoming these limitations by enabling physically consistent and data-efficient modeling. In this article, we systematically analyze PIML applications from a manufacturing-process perspective. We organize the manufacturing landscape into five representative categories based on their dominant physical mechanisms and the availability of relevant literature: mechanical processes, chemical processes, thermal-driven processes, additive manufacturing, and semiconductor fabrication. We comprehensively review and discuss domain-dependent characteristics, including governing physics, data regimes, and modeling objectives across manufacturing processes. We further discuss fundamental challenges of PIML approaches, along with practical considerations for real-world deployment. This review aims to provide a foundation for accelerating physics-informed learning and its advancement within manufacturing research and practice.
10.1016/j.jmsy.2026.01.002.title: Physics-informed machine learning across manufacturing processes: Recent advances, challenges, and directions

10.1016/j.jmsy.2026.01.015.abstract: Embodied intelligence systems are becoming integral to smart manufacturing, driven by the human-centric, sustainable, and resilient vision of Industry 5.0. While robots have achieved remarkable success in manipulating rigid objects, robust handling of deformable fabrics in garment manufacturing remains challenging, particularly for pick-and-place operations required in sewing processes. In production environments, robots often struggle to adapt gripping strategies to different fabric properties and deformation behavior, limiting smart manufacturing development. To address these challenges, this paper proposes a physics-informed embodied intelligence framework tailored for smart garment manufacturing. The system integrates task-aware planning, enabled by vision–language understanding of the surrounding environment, with physics-informed manipulation, which incorporates material property inference and finite element analysis. This integration enables robots to perform garment manufacturing tasks with greater adaptability, precision, and intelligence. Experiments conducted in real-world scenarios validate the effectiveness of the proposed framework in supporting flexible and intelligent production processes.
10.1016/j.jmsy.2026.01.015.title: A physics-informed embodied intelligence framework for smart garment manufacturing

10.1016/j.jmsy.2026.04.024.abstract: Digital twins are emerging as a core module of next-generation information-based manufacturing systems, providing novel research perspectives for reliability engineering and quality engineering. However, challenges persist in the establishment of digital twins for new scenarios. The scarcity of labeled samples hinders the direct application of various algorithms to drive programs in these scenarios. For welding robots, a typical manufacturing system, the characteristics of high temperature and intense noise reduce the robots’ precision retention and restrict the operating conditions of precision measurement equipment. Considering the latest advancements in physics information neural networks (PINNs), this study proposes a digital twin method, which is called physics-informed modal alignment neural network. Without real labels for precision degradation, the method can predict the robots’ precision degradation and welding failure risks using laboratory degradation data and unlabeled data from the target scenario, assisting enterprise users in adjusting maintenance strategies. This method establishes an equivalence relationship between two industrial robot systems through a physical modal loss term. It decomposes the robot dynamic signals in an orthogonal basis vector space to learn the underlying consistency of degradation processes across different hardware platforms, and employs a cross-attention mechanism to focus on the optimal matching pattern between different datasets. Ultimately, it establishes the relationship between sensor signals and end-positioning precision. Validation was conducted by laboratory data and real production data, the performance of different methods is compared with real welding defect records and precision calibration data, and module ablation experiments and parameter robustness tests were carried out. Results demonstrate that the proposed physical modal loss significantly improves the accuracy of degradation state transfer evaluation, achieves the best performance in real machining failure data, and highlights the advantages of PINNs. The proposed algorithm and the developed digital twin system have been applied in enterprises, reducing additional costs caused by unexpected downtime. This study provides up-to-date references for industrial applications of digital twins and helps the academic community understand the further development goals of robotic manufacturing systems.
10.1016/j.jmsy.2026.04.024.title: Welding robot digital twin and precision degradation prediction based on physics-informed neural networks
