10.1016/j.jmsy.2026.03.016.abstract: Tool wear monitoring is one of the key technologies for enabling predictive maintenance of machining processes. However, the physical model and mechanism model have poor generalization across various cutting conditions. Current data-driven methods also lack explicit representations of the underlying tool-wear mechanisms, which limits their ability to provide deep insights into the physical wear processes and hinders further mechanism-driven optimization. This paper proposes a novel physics-informed, data-driven method for tool-wear monitoring that enhances monitoring performance while providing deeper understanding into the physical mechanisms. Firstly, the tool wear mechanism model is abstracted and embedded to construct mechanism-based recurrent unit. Secondly, the monitoring network is constructed by stacking mechanism-based recurrent unit with Transformer. Thirdly, the mapping between input signals and tool flank wear is established according to the statistical features and the proposed method. Finally, milling experiments were conducted to verify the generalizability and analyze the dynamic evolution of the tool wear mechanism. The proposed tool wear monitoring method achieves substantial performance improvement, reducing the average monitoring error by 36.9%–47.5% compared with recent state-of-the-art methods. In addition, the method demonstrates strong robustness and generalization across diverse cutting conditions. Benefiting from the embedded mechanism model, it further extracts the dynamic evolution characteristics of the underlying wear mechanisms, thereby offering improved interpretability. These advances provide a solid theoretical foundation for predictive maintenance, as well as for process and tool optimization in intelligent manufacturing systems.
10.1016/j.jmsy.2026.03.016.title: Physics-informed data-driven framework for tool wear monitoring with limited samples: Mechanism-embedded learning

10.1016/j.jmsy.2026.05.005.abstract: Laser Powder Bed Fusion (L-PBF) additive manufacturing involves low-volume, highly flexible part designs that generate heterogeneous process data. When equipped with in-situ sensors, these systems produce massive volumes of high-dimensional data, creating significant challenges for real-time quality monitoring. This paper proposes a Distributionally Robust Asynchronous Federated Learning (DRO-AFL) framework for collaborative thermal process anomaly detection across multiple L-PBF operations without sharing sensitive process data. The framework integrates three key components: (1) asynchronous federated learning with convolutional autoencoders for flexible client participation; (2) multilinear principal component analysis for efficient dimensionality reduction of high-dimensional tensor data; and (3) distributionally robust optimization for improved model generalization across heterogeneous data distributions. Unlike conventional synchronous federated learning, DRO-AFL accommodates immediate updates from available clients without waiting for stragglers, making it well-suited to manufacturing environments with diverse computational resources. Trained using real L-PBF thermal imaging data, DRO-AFL achieves comparable reconstruction accuracy to FedAvg, centralized, and individual learning baselines and demonstrates improved spatio-temporal anomaly detection capability through a hybrid scoring approach. The results highlight DRO-AFL as a robust approach for thermal anomaly detection in distributed manufacturing systems.
10.1016/j.jmsy.2026.05.005.title: Distributionally Robust Asynchronous Federated Learning for Anomaly Detection in Laser Powder Bed Fusion

10.1016/j.jmsy.2026.06.022.abstract: This study presents a novel approach for estimating cutting forces in CNC machining by integrating feed drive dynamics and motor current signals with machine learning (ML) algorithms. The methodology leverages the mechanical behavior of feed drive components, modeling the interactions among servomotors, leadscrews, and other elements to analytically estimate cutting forces, incorporating a Stribeck friction model to accurately represent frictional losses. By utilizing data directly from CNC controllers, the proposed method offers a practical and scalable solution for in-process force monitoring, without the need for external sensors or costly instrumentation. To enhance prediction accuracy, a hybrid Physics-Informed Machine Learning (PIML) framework based on physics-based feature augmentation was developed combining analytically estimated forces based on feed drive model with servo signals and machining parameters. This framework not only improves the accuracy of the analytical model but also reduces the need for extensive experimentation used in direct data driven approaches. The results highlight the effectiveness of this approach, with R² values exceeding 98% and significantly reduced root mean square error (RMSE) values. Notably, the proposed PIML framework achieved an improvement of approximately 28–32% in prediction accuracy compared to the standalone analytical model, and 15–22% over conventional ML models that rely solely on data-driven inference. This integration not only captures nonlinearities and dynamic behavior but also retains the interpretability of the analytical model. The findings underline the added value of incorporating domain knowledge into ML algorithms, enabling more reliable force estimation directly from CNC controller data. Furthermore, the model demonstrated strong generalization capabilities when tested on unseen data, reinforcing its applicability in real-world manufacturing environments.
10.1016/j.jmsy.2026.06.022.title: Physics-informed machine learning for intelligent process monitoring: A sensorless approach for cutting force estimation based on feed drive dynamics and motor current

10.1016/j.jmsy.2026.06.014.abstract: Rapid and high-fidelity prediction of assembly deviations is critical for the digital assembly of high-precision products. In the assembly of bolted flange connections, bolt preload induces micro-scale deformations that are intrinsically coupled with complex contact mechanics. However, resolving these deformations via Finite Element Analysis (FEA) is computationally intensive, while purely data-driven models often lack physical consistency and generalization robustness. To address this, we propose a Physics-Informed Graph Neural Network (PI-GNN) framework for rapid displacement field prediction. This architecture explicitly encodes the topological dependencies of unstructured meshes via graph learning while embedding Navier–Cauchy equilibrium residuals into the loss function to enforce physical validity. Crucially, to address the sharp stress gradients inherent in contact surface, a distance-weighted supervision mechanism is introduced to stabilize training on sparse datasets. Comprehensive benchmarks on L-block assemblies demonstrate that the proposed method achieves simulation-grade fidelity with minimal data dependence. Compared to the purely data-driven baseline, the PI-GNN exhibits superior extrapolation robustness, reducing the axial Mean Absolute Error (MAE) by up to 48.8% in OOD regimes. Finally, the method is applied to the assembly deviation prediction of a two-stage flange connection. Experimental validation focusing on physical end-face tilt measurements confirms the model’s ability to accurately characterize macroscopic assembly posture variations, verifying its potential as a reliable framework for intelligent assembly and in-process quality monitoring.
10.1016/j.jmsy.2026.06.014.title: Facilitating digital assembly: A physics-informed graph learning framework for prediction of assembly deviations in bolted flange connections
10.1016/j.jmsy.2026.06.014.source: ScienceDirect official citation and abstract BibTeX export

10.1016/j.jmsy.2026.07.028.abstract: Accurate and reliable tool wear monitoring (TWM) is essential for ensuring machining quality, production efficiency, and operational safety. However, data-driven methods generally lack physical interpretability, while physics-based methods often rely on simplified assumptions and fixed empirical equations. To address these limitations, this study proposes a physics-informed gated Mamba (PIGM) framework with adaptive feature reconstruction. First, a training-set-guided adaptive feature reconstruction mechanism reconstructs multi-domain sensor features through correlation-based and temperature-controlled weight allocation. A gating mechanism is then incorporated into the Mamba backbone to regulate information flow and enhance wear-related feature modeling. In addition, a physics-consistency surrogate branch (PCSB) introduces a learnable wear-rate consistency constraint, while an uncertainty-based adaptive weighting strategy balances monitoring accuracy and physical consistency during training. The proposed framework was evaluated on the PHM2010, carbon-fiber-reinforced polymer (CFRP), and titanium alloy (TiA) milling datasets. Compared with PIMamba, PIGM achieved average percentage reductions of 57.91% and 55.78% in RMSE and MAE, respectively, on PHM2010. Comparisons with recent time-series regression models further demonstrated improved monitoring accuracy across representative test subsets. Ablation experiments confirmed the contribution of each designed module. Additional analyses of noise interference and single-sensor failure showed that PIGM maintains stable monitoring under moderate signal disturbance and some redundant sensor failures, while remaining sensitive to process-specific key sensors. Shapley additive explanations (SHAP) and physics-consistency analyses further provided feature-level interpretation and evidence of improved physical plausibility. These findings indicate that PIGM provides an accurate and physically plausible framework for TWM across the evaluated milling cases without requiring an explicit empirical wear equation.
10.1016/j.jmsy.2026.07.028.title: A physics-informed gated Mamba framework with adaptive feature reconstruction for accurate and interpretable tool wear monitoring

10.1016/j.jmsy.2026.07.025.abstract: With the rapid adoption of new energy vehicles, the demand for disassembly of end-of-life battery continues to increase in maintenance, echelon utilization, and recycling. Under anomalous conditions, end-of-life battery disassembly heavily relies on the operational experience of skilled workers. When such experience is used for novice workers or machine adaptation, the extraction and structured representation of such knowledge remain difficult because the relevant knowledge is mainly held by individual workers. Therefore, the effective extraction and representation of operational experience provide an important basis for supporting human-AI collaborative evolution. To address the difficulties in extracting operational experience, representing fine-grained operational semantics, and organizing anomaly-related knowledge under anomalous operating conditions, this paper proposes a method for extracting and representing disassembly operation knowledge of end-of-life battery under anomalous operating conditions. Based on first-person disassembly videos, the proposed method performs temporal modeling and visual perception of disassembly actions and obtains action-tool-component triadic structures through semantic reasoning. Meanwhile, using the standard-condition disassembly sequence as the backbone, the method supplements anomaly types and anomalous operation branches to construct an operation knowledge graph for end-of-life battery disassembly under anomalous operating conditions, enabling the unified representation of standard procedures and anomalous operation knowledge. Experimental results show that the proposed method extracts key operational elements in anomalous disassembly scenarios more accurately. Specifically, Abnormal Operation Node Accuracy improves by about 8.0% compared with the conventional method. This improvement enhances the ability of the knowledge graph to represent anomalous operating conditions and supports knowledge accumulation, experience reuse, and human-AI collaborative evolution in end-of-life battery disassembly.
10.1016/j.jmsy.2026.07.025.title: An LLM-KG empowered manner for extracting and representing operational knowledge under abnormal conditions: A case study in end-of-life battery disassembly

10.1016/j.jmsy.2026.08.004.abstract: Advances in sensing and data acquisition have enabled the integration of machine learning into electronics manufacturing for process optimization. However, purely data-driven models often require large experimental datasets and provide only point predictions, limiting the assessment of prediction reliability. These limitations are critical in component placement optimization, where experimental data collection is costly and reliable prediction is required for robust control. To address these challenges, this study proposes a physics-informed, uncertainty-aware framework for component placement optimization in surface mount technology. A physics-based model generates synthetic data to pre-train a neural network that is fine-tuned with limited experimental data. An ensemble of fine-tuned models and a mixture density network generate continuous predictive distributions to quantify prediction uncertainty. These predictions are incorporated into a mean–variance optimization module with sampled mounter placement offsets to balance the expected positional offset and prediction variability. The proposed approach improves alignment quality by increasing end overlap compared with existing placement methods while maintaining side overhang quality. Overall, the framework improves data efficiency and enables robust placement optimization under predictive uncertainty and mounter placement variability.
10.1016/j.jmsy.2026.08.004.title: PI-UA-Opt: Physics-informed, uncertainty-aware optimization framework for pick-and-place process in surface mount technology

10.1016/j.foodhyd.2025.112136.abstract: The application of granular starch is inherently limited by its large particle size and highly hydrophilic surface. To address this challenge, this study explores the co-electrospinning of starch and whey protein as an approach to fabricate a composite nanofiber with enhanced interface properties: Starch offers structural rigidity and pH stability, while whey protein contributes surface activity. A deep-learning neural network is constructed and validated to systematically analyze the morphological behavior of co-electrospinning, revealing a synergistic effect on crafting. While starch alone fails to produce fibers at low solid fraction (<0.1, <41 % electrospinnability), the incorporation of protein (20 w/w% and 40 w/w%) enables a bead-to-fiber transition (100 % electrospinnability) by reducing the surface energy. By tuning the protein-starch ratio, the fiber diameter can be controlled from 142 to 581 nm. Visualization techniques confirm the uniform distribution of embedded proteins within the carbohydrate backbone. Post-spin thermal treatment induces aminolysis of the nanofibers, effectively reducing protein leaching (from 10 % to 3 %) and reinforcing the structural integrity. The rod-shaped particles derived from these thermal-activated composite nanofibers show higher oil-water interfacial activity and produce stable Pickering emulsions. Using edible biopolymers, this research explores strategies to engineer morphological and surface properties, thereby expanding material applications. This study also demonstrates the capability of deep learning as a versatile platform to design functional materials.
10.1016/j.foodhyd.2025.112136.title: Crafting surface-active composite fibers from protein-fortified starch via synergistic Co-electrospinning and deep learning

10.1016/j.foodhyd.2025.112313.abstract: Excess sodium intake poses a global health challenge, particularly in processed meats where NaCl is critical for functionality and flavor. While potassium chloride (KCl) offers a sodium reduction strategy, its use is limited by bitterness and texture loss. The mechanisms by which hydrocolloids like κ-Carrageenan (KC) might overcome these limitations through microstructural modulation remain poorly understood, particularly in complex protein matrices. This study systematically investigated the synergistic effects of KCl and KC on myofibrillar protein (MP) gelation dynamics across the “solution-gelation-gel” continuum. Partial NaCl replacement with KCl (10–50 %) reduced MP solubility by 2.63–30.59 % and altered protein conformation. The addition of KC enhanced surface hydrophobicity, sulfhydryl content, thermal stability, and viscosity while facilitating MP structural unfolding and aggregation through hydrophobic and hydrogen bonds. KC significantly improved gel network density (1.05–1.13 folds in fractal dimension), increased hardness (8.94–20.07 %), and enhanced water holding capacity by 4.38–23.21 %. By fusing CLSM images with physicochemical data, we developed a multimodal neural network architecture that accurately predicted taste and texture attributes (R2 > 0.9), identifying water migration, fractal dimension, and disulfide bonds as key contributors. Our findings demonstrated that KC masked KCl-induced bitterness through sulfate-mediated binding of K+ within a densified protein network, which strategically limited potassium release while maintaining saltiness perception. The multimodal deep learning model provided unprecedented insights into structure-taste relationships in low-sodium protein systems, offering a robust framework for predicting and optimizing sensory outcomes in reformulated meat products.
10.1016/j.foodhyd.2025.112313.title: Synergistic κ-Carrageenan/KCl modulation of myofibrillar protein gelation: decoding gel structure-bitterness masking intrinsic correlation via multimodal neural network

10.1016/j.foodhyd.2026.112664.abstract: Polysaccharide–protein conjugate emulsifiers, which occur naturally and are non-toxic, exhibit excellent emulsifying stability. However, because polysaccharide–protein conjugates are complex biomacromolecules, conventional approaches provide limited capacity to elucidate the intrinsic and precise relationships between polysaccharide structures and emulsifying stability. Therefore, this study introduced a machine learning–Shapley (ML–SHAP) strategy to automatically predict the emulsifying performance of polysaccharide–protein conjugates and provide insightful interpretation of the predictive outcomes. A series of corn fiber gum–soy protein isolate (CFG–SPI) conjugates with diverse structural features were prepared using acid hydrolysis, enzymatic hydrolysis, ultrasound treatment, and steam explosion. Based on datasets of CFG physicochemical, structural information and corresponding emulsification data, an AutoML–SHAP framework was established to elucidate the structure–function relationships between CFG and emulsifying performance. Physicochemical and structural parameters of CFG (molecular weight, monosaccharide composition, and glycosidic linkages) were used as model inputs, while emulsifying performance indicators (particle size, Turbiscan stability index [TSI], and zeta potential) served as outputs. The AutoML–SHAP model demonstrated high predictive accuracy, with R2 values of 0.896, 0.952, and 0.913 for particle size, TSI, and zeta potential, respectively. Interpretability analysis (SHAP) further revealed that 1,4-Xylp, 1,2,3,4-Xylp, T-Araf, 1,3-Araf, 1,2-Araf, Ara, molecular weight were the predominant physicochemical and structural factors influencing the emulsifying and stabilizing properties of CFG–SPI conjugates. These findings provide a theoretical basis for advancing the understanding of structure–function relationships in polysaccharide–protein conjugate emulsifiers and offer new perspectives for studying other polysaccharides.
10.1016/j.foodhyd.2026.112664.title: Advancing structure–emulsifying property relationships of corn fiber gum–soy protein isolate conjugates through machine learning

10.1016/j.foodhyd.2026.113038.abstract: This study developed a data-driven two-stage ultrasound strategy to improve the functional and digestive properties of yeast protein (YP). A Box-Behnken design was first used to establish the optimal single-stage ultrasound condition, and Bayesian optimization combined with random forest further identified a low-to-high power treatment of 180 W for 5 min followed by 520 W for 5 min as the most favorable two-stage condition. Compared with untreated YP and the optimal single-stage ultrasound-treated YP, the two-stage ultrasound-treated YP showed better solubility, in vitro digestibility, interfacial functionality, and water- and oil-holding capacities. Structural analyses showed that SSB was associated with more pronounced structural disruption, whereas TSB exhibited a more balanced structural state, as reflected by smaller particle size, higher fluorescence intensity and surface hydrophobicity, reduced disulfide bond content, lower thermal transition activation energy, and more coordinated structural evolution during digestion. These findings demonstrate that two-stage ultrasound is an effective and controllable strategy for improving functional and digestive properties of YP.
10.1016/j.foodhyd.2026.113038.title: Enhancing bioaccessibility and interfacial functional properties of yeast protein via the strategy of two-stage ultrasound processing: insights from the Bayesian optimization, structural characterization and kinetics

10.1016/j.foodhyd.2026.113031.abstract: Plant protein fibrils are increasingly exploited in food structuring and the fabrication of sustainable materials. Moringa oleifera seed protein (MOSP), as a novel plant protein resource, possesses significant potential for forming amyloid fibrils. This study aims to investigate the conversion of MOSP into amyloid fibrils (AFs) and explore the underlying conversion mechanism. Thioflavin T (ThT) kinetics and Congo Red binding assays confirmed a nucleation-dependent growth mechanism, characterized by a typical sigmoidal profile and time-dependent spectral shifts. Circular dichroism and FTIR spectroscopy revealed a pronounced secondary-structure transition from α-helix–dominated MOSP to β-sheet–rich assemblies, while TEM and AFM captured the morphological evolution from globular aggregates to mature, entangled fibrillar networks. MOSP AFs exhibited exceptional solubility, and as processing time increased, the viscosity and viscoelastic properties of MOSP AFs were enhanced. To elucidate the molecular basis of this assembly, peptidomics was integrated with deep-learning-based amyloid fold prediction (RibbonFold). Peptidomic profiling identified a temporal shift toward increased hydrophobicity, highlighting specific 15–19 aa peptides as the “master building blocks” with high structural propensity (average TM-score ≥0.68), particularly the sequence ISVGNAVPVWYNM (TM-score 0.89054). Cleavage-site enrichment analysis suggests that acidic conditions promote Asp-adjacent bond cleavage, liberating hydrophobic segments that May drive β-sheet stacking via hydrophobic collapse and aromatic interactions. This study provides a multiscale framework for MOSP fibrillation, offering a theoretical foundation for the rational design of protein-based functional nanostructures.
10.1016/j.foodhyd.2026.113031.title: Unveiling the self-assembly mechanism of moringa (Moringa oleifera Lam.) seed protein amyloid fibrils: A multi-scale study integrating peptidomics and artificial intelligence
10.1016/j.foodhyd.2026.113031.source: ScienceDirect official citation and abstract BibTeX export

10.1016/j.biomaterials.2026.124209.abstract: Non-alcoholic fatty liver disease (NAFLD) and cardiovascular disease (CVD) frequently co-occur, driven by inter-organ metabolic crosstalk that current single-target therapies fail to disrupt. This review reframes NAFLD-CVD comorbidity through a materials-first lens and advances a translational design framework that couples pathophysiology with engineering principles. We synthesize three major pathological axes, including lipid overflow and impaired reverse cholesterol transport, inflammation-oxidative stress amplification driven by Kupffer cell-NLRP3 and mitochondrial ROS/MAPK signaling, as well as gut-liver-vascular dysregulation involving bile acid FXR/TGR5 pathways and microbiota-derived metabolites, and further map these mechanisms to organ-selective and stimulus-responsive therapeutic interventions. Specifically, we highlight liver-heart co-targeting via GalNAc/ASGPR and VCAM-1 ligands, HDL-mimetic and exosome platforms that restore cholesterol efflux, ROS/pH/enzyme-responsive carriers that achieve microenvironment-triggered release and mitochondria-addressed nanodevices including antioxidant nanozymes, Mito-therapeutics, and optogenetically guided CRISPR/RNA payloads that recalibrate energy/redox homeostasis. We further outline macrophage-reprogramming strategies using cytokine mRNA and miRNA modulators to resolve chronic inflammation, and propose closed-loop systems that integrate AI-guided design with synthetic biology circuits for adaptive, multi-organ control. Across platforms, we distill actionable criteria covering clinical translation, biodistribution fidelity, barrier traversal, compensation-proof multi-pathway control, and safety-by-design. This materials-anchored roadmap moves the field from single-organ symptom control to systemic metabolic reprogramming, positioning advanced materials as catalysts for durable, precision therapy in NAFLD-CVD comorbidity.
10.1016/j.biomaterials.2026.124209.title: Advanced materials for non-alcoholic fatty liver disease and cardiovascular disease comorbidity therapeutics

10.1016/j.cej.2025.171519.abstract: For complex diseases, sensing and decoding patterns in biofluids are crucial for accurate diagnosis. However, it has been challenged by suboptimal sensitivity and inadequate information processing for accessing measurable outcomes. To address this gap, we present an intelligent diagnostic sensor platform that synergistically integrates fabrication-compatible silicon-based surface-enhanced Raman spectroscopy (SERS) biosensing chips with a self-learning explainable artificial intelligence (XAI) framework by enabling digital biomarker-based diagnosis of early-stage hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC). The SERS biosensing chip, named SEARCH (Silicon-Etched Au-Reduced silver electro-Chemical deposition Heuristic), exploit hierarchical noble metal nanoarchitectures with dense electromagnetic hot spots, high enhancement of Raman signals, and superior inter-batch consistency, enabling sensitive detection of vibrational molecular fingerprints in serum. To interpret the high-dimensional Raman spectra, we developed a self-learning convolutional neural network (CNN)-based XAI framework that autonomously identifies and refines class-specific digital biomarkers, allowing it to dynamically adapt to population heterogeneity via iterative learning and unveil multidimensional spectral signatures encoded in serum-derived Raman spectra. In a multi-population cohort (N = 300), our platform demonstrated exceptional diagnostic performance, consistently achieving area under the curve (AUC) values above 0.93 across multiple classifiers in distinguishing early-stage HCC from both healthy controls and high-risk individuals. Comparative analysis revealed that SEARCH-derived digital biomarkers outperformed three conventional HCC serum markers. This work underscores the translational potential of combining scalable SERS biosensing with intelligent spectral analysis for digital cancer biomarker learning. The platform offers a robust, cost-efficient (<1.4 USD per test), and clinically actionable solution for the early diagnosis of HCC, showcasing the future of intelligent biosensing in precision oncology.
10.1016/j.cej.2025.171519.title: AI-driven SERS biosensing chip for digital biomarker detection in diagnosis and monitoring of early-stage HCC

10.1016/j.cej.2025.171530.abstract: Accurate detection of triethylamine (TEA) is essential for environmental and industrial safety. However, conventional metal oxide semiconductor sensors exhibit insufficient sensitivity and selectivity. This study develops an intelligent TEA sensor based on Cr-doped WO3 nanomaterials integrated with machine learning. The 1 wt% Cr-WO3 sensor exhibited optimal performance, with a response of 330.1 to 50 ppm TEA at 240 °C (4.78 times higher than pristine WO3), rapid response/recovery times (11 s/44 s), and a low detection limit of 42 ppb. The sensor also demonstrated excellent selectivity, repeatability, and stability, attributed to Cr-induced surface oxygen vacancies that enhance gas interactions. Based on machine learning, we established a gas recognition model using the KNN algorithm and a concentration prediction model using the neural network algorithm. This work integrates material optimization and intelligent algorithms to establish a “high-sensitivity detection-smart analysis” framework, thereby advancing gas sensors toward systematic intelligence for next-generation monitoring systems.
10.1016/j.cej.2025.171530.title: Machine learning-assisted development of high-performance Cr-doped tungsten oxide triethylamine gas sensors

10.1016/j.cej.2025.171522.abstract: Doping abuse presents a persistent challenge in competitive sports and public health. To address the limitations of conventional detection methods, we developed a flexible, skin-adhesive hydrogel-based SERS sensor with wearable potential for non-invasive, on-body detection of doping agents in sweat. The ASP hydrogel (Au@Ag NRs/S-CNF/PAA/PAAM) was fabricated by embedding sulfonated cellulose nanofiber (S-CNF)-stabilized Au@Ag NRs into a PAA/PAAM double-network matrix. This design enhances nanoparticle dispersion, mechanical flexibility, and sweat absorption. The sensor achieved detection limits of 1.75 × 10−8 M (HCTZ), 1.0 × 10−9 M (TMZ), and 8.86 × 10−8 M (SAL), with excellent signal uniformity (RSD = 4.58 %) and 60-day storage stability. Mechanical tests confirmed optimized tensile strain (176.6 %) and good adhesive strength. The ASP hydrogel also demonstrated strong antibacterial activity against both E. coli and S. aureus (inhibition rate > 99 %) and high biocompatibility (cell viability >96 %), ensuring long-term skin safety during wear. Furthermore, machine learning algorithms enabled accurate spectral classification of the three stimulants, achieving 100 % test accuracy and AUC = 1.0. This multifunctional hydrogel platform integrates high sensitivity, mechanical durability, antimicrobial protection, and intelligent data processing, offering strong potential for real-time on-body stimulant monitoring in anti-doping, sports medicine, and personalized health management.
10.1016/j.cej.2025.171522.title: A hydrogel-based SERS sensor with wearable potential and machine learning integration for sweat stimulant detection

10.1016/j.cej.2025.171649.abstract: Endometriosis (EM) affects approximately 10 % of reproductive-aged women globally, with a postoperative recurrence rate as high as 50 %. However, the underlying targets and mechanisms of recurrence remain incompletely understood, hindering the development of effective targeted therapies. In response to this challenge, this study proposes an innovative strategy integrating information technology (IT) and biotechnology (BT), based on clinical samples from recurrence and non-recurrence EM patients. LncRNA and mRNA expression chip data from patients were initially acquired using microarray technology, and potential recurrence targets were identified using 8 machine learning algorithms. Subsequently, high-sensitivity biosensors were developed to validate the functional activity of these targets and screen for regulatory components. Finally, the biological regulatory effects of the molecules on the targets were confirmed using lesion cell models, providing experimental evidence for precision treatment. Results showed that two genes, vascular endothelial growth factor A (VEGFA) and Galectin-3 (LGALS3), were identified as potential recurrence targets from 55,148 differentially expressed genes (DEGs). The developed biosensors exhibited high sensitivity, with a detection limit as low as 1 fM and a quantification range from 1 fM to 1 mM. Additionally, 21 critical quality attributes (CQAs) were identified using the biosensors, with two CQAs, geraniol and salvianolic acid B, showing strong interactions with VEGFA/LGALS3 targets. Ultimately, the therapeutic efficacy of these two CQAs in treating EM recurrence was validated through lesion cells models. This work offers a novel framework by integrating IT and BT technologies, addressing critical challenges in the identification of recurrence targets and therapeutic components in EM, and will be broadly useful for the research and development of clinical precision medicine.
10.1016/j.cej.2025.171649.title: Novel discovery of geraniol and salvianolic acid B in regulating endometriosis recurrence targets LGALS3/VEGFA via integrating AI and biosensors

10.1016/j.cej.2025.171716.abstract: Global wastewater management is undergoing a paradigm shift from traditional pollutant removal toward circular resource valorisation. Electro-bioreactor (EBR) systems have emerged as promising platforms for coupling biological and electrochemical processes, yet conventional configurations face limitations in treating recalcitrant contaminants, achieving energy efficiency, and enabling scalable resource recovery. This review introduces the concept of next-generation hybrid electro-bioreactor (H-EBR) networks, which integrate bioelectrochemical systems, photocatalytic oxidation, membrane bioreactors, and enzymatic redox cycles within a unified treatment framework. Recent advances in multi-contaminant elimination, renewable energy harvesting, and nutrient and byproduct valorisation are critically examined, with particular focus on how artificial intelligence-powered digital twins and quantum-enhanced real-time sensing could enable self-optimising, adaptive control strategies. The performance of H-EBRs is compared with conventional treatment technologies, and their potential within circular water-energy-nutrient systems is explored through techno-economic assessments, life cycle evaluations, and policy integration. Finally, research gaps are identified and a forward-looking roadmap is proposed toward developing intelligent, decentralised, and carbon-negative wastewater infrastructures. This review positions H-EBR networks as a transformative pathway for achieving sustainable and resilient wastewater valorisation.
10.1016/j.cej.2025.171716.title: Intelligent hybrid electro-bioreactor networks for wastewater valorisation: AI-driven bioelectrochemical treatment, multi-scale resource recovery, and circular water-energy-nutrient systems
10.1016/j.cej.2025.171716.source: ScienceDirect official citation and abstract BibTeX export

10.1016/j.cej.2025.171494.abstract: Efficient micromixing is critical in chemical microreactors, yet predictive modeling remains challenging due to complex flow dynamics. This study investigates micromixing performance in micro-coiled flow inverter tubes (MCFIs) using artificial neural networks (ANN), adaptive neuro-fuzzy inference systems (ANFIS), and genetic algorithms (GA). Experimental data were collected for six MCFI geometries using the Villermaux–Dushman reaction, with the segregation index (Xs) as the primary measure of mixing efficiency. Model inputs included the number of 90° bends, flow rate ratio of alkaline to acid solutions (r = Qalkaline/Qacid), and acid concentration, while outputs were Xs and pressure drop (ΔP). ANN achieved the highest prediction accuracy (Xs: 4.217 % MRE; ΔP: 1.30 % MRE), outperforming ANFIS (Xs: 6.481 %; ΔP: 1.91 %) and GA (Xs: 12.43 %; ΔP: 4.28 %). GA-driven multi-objective optimization revealed optimal MCFI designs that balance Xs and ΔP, offering practical guidance for reactor design. The results highlight the potential of data-driven models for the accurate prediction and optimization of micromixing in complex microreactor geometries. Unlike previous studies that focused on single-objective or simulation-based optimization, this work integrates experimentally validated data with AI-driven surrogate modeling and multi-objective optimization to quantitatively explore the trade-off between micromixing efficiency and energy consumption in micro-coiled flow inverters.
10.1016/j.cej.2025.171494.title: AI-assisted experimental analysis of geometry and flow effects in microstructured reactors

10.1016/j.cej.2025.172023.abstract: The practical application of flexible strain sensors is often limited by their unidirectional sensitivity and structural vulnerability caused by additional encapsulation processes. To overcome these issues, this work introduces an omnidirectional and self-encapsulated flexible strain sensor fabricated via liquid-in-liquid printing. The achieved sensor incorporates a branched graphene network that ensures uniform strain response in all designed directions, and it effectively inhibited the directional dependence typical of conventional sensors. Meanwhile, the self-leveling behavior of the liquid substrate allows the sensing element to be seamlessly encapsulated in a single step, enhancing interfacial integrity and long-term durability. Experimental results demonstrate that the sensor exhibits highly linear response, low hysteresis, and stable performance over 5000 stretching-releasing cycles. When integrated with a ResNet50 deep residual network, the sensor achieves human action recognition with an average accuracy of 96.15 %, and enables orientation-independent control of a robotic hand, highlighting its potential in human-machine interaction and intelligent industrial systems. This study establishes a scalable and efficient strategy for developing high-performance, durable flexible sensors through synergistic material and structural design.
10.1016/j.cej.2025.172023.title: Liquid-in-liquid printing and machine learning assisting the achievement of omni-directional, self-encapsulated flexible strain sensors

10.1016/j.cej.2025.171812.abstract: Per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS) are persistent environmental pollutants with significant health risks, necessitating the development of efficient and cost-effective detection methods beyond conventional techniques. This study modulated the pore microenvironment of single-atom nanozymes (SAzymes) using Pluronic surfactants to enhance their oxidase-like (OXD-like) and laccase-like (LAC-like) activities. The optimized material, Fe/NC-@L31, exhibited improved surface area and pore volume, facilitating substrate diffusion and active site accessibility. A machine learning-assisted sensor array was then constructed based on the differential inhibitory effects of PFAS on the dual-enzyme activities. The Random Forest (RF) algorithm accurately discriminated seven categories of PFAS, and regression models achieved quantitative detection with recoveries of 85–103 % in real water samples. This classification-regression strategy provides a robust and intelligent platform for PFAS monitoring in environmental matrices.
10.1016/j.cej.2025.171812.title: Machine learning-assisted sensor array based on enhanced dual enzyme-like activities of Fe SAzymes modulated via Pluronic surfactant for multi-category perfluoroalkyl intelligent recognition and quantification

10.1016/j.cej.2025.172189.abstract: Pesticides are widely used in modern agriculture to enhance crop yields and are recognized as environmental pollutants, making it crucial to monitor pesticide residue for the food safety and environmental protection. Herein, a sensitive and non-destructive strategy was developed to detect thiram in different fruit juices using surface-enhanced Raman spectroscopy (SERS). The high SERS sensitivity relies on the effective interaction of analyte molecules with the substrate via the charge-transfer processes or within the hotspot regions. To explore the synergism of electromagnetic and chemical effects, a composite was constructed by decorating silver nanoparticles (Ag NPs) via an in-situ process onto the hydrothermally grown nickel‑iron layered double hydroxide (NiFeLDH) on the delaminated MXene. The Ag NPs/NiFeLDH/MXene composite exhibits high SERS sensitivity towards probe molecules (thiram, methylene blue (MB) and malachite green (MG)) due to the strong electrostatic attraction of the positively charged NiFe ions from the LDH to the negatively charged groups of MXene and the efficient anchoring of Ag NPs to the hydroxyl group of NiFeLDH. The composite demonstrates a significant SERS enhancement effect (up to 1010) and strong SERS performance towards MB, MG and thiram with the lowest detectable concentration of 1.24 × 10−12 M, 1.59 × 10−12 M and 2.8 × 10−11 M, respectively. Moreover, thiram at different concentrations was successfully detected in real-samples such as tomato, orange and apple juices. Additionally, a support vector machine (SVM) model applied to the SERS spectra of thiram in different real-samples achieved a classification accuracy exceeding 97 %. These results demonstrate the practicality of Ag NPs/NiFeLDH/MXene for the trace level detection of pesticides and organic pollutants.
10.1016/j.cej.2025.172189.title: Smart SERS platform with a machine-learning approach for the detection of thiram in fruit juices using an Ag NPs/NiFeLDH/MXene composite

10.1016/j.cej.2026.172561.abstract: Multifunctional electronic skin has attracted remarkable attention for its promising applications in health monitoring and human-machine interaction. However, it is still challenging to develop a multifunctional sensor via a single functional material or structure that achieves high sensitivity and multi-signal decoupling. This paper proposes a dual-mode flexible tactile sensor that generates distinct capacitive responses to both temperature and pressure stimuli. By synergy effect of hierarchical micropyramids structure and compressible PVA/MXene ionic gel electrolyte, the sensor demonstrates remarkable pressure sensitivity of 23.22 % kPa−1 with the range of 0–133.5 kPa, temperature sensitivity of 0.975 % °C−1 with the range of 25–75 °C. According to the capacitive response characteristics of temperature and pressure, the machine learning-enhanced multifunctional sensor can simultaneously identify and distinguish capacitance signals generated by temperature-pressure stimuli, achieving an impressive accuracy rate of 98.52 %. Finally, a 4 × 4 sensor array was printed to detect braille of six different meanings with accurate identification. Owing to the simple ‘sandwich’ structure design, ionic transport mechanisms, and machine learning algorithms, the sensor provides a cost-effective and promising method to multimodal signals decoupling, which paves the development of e-skin and human-computer interaction applications.
10.1016/j.cej.2026.172561.title: Ultrasensitive dual-mode sensor with machine learning-decoupled pressure-temperature perception

10.1016/j.cej.2025.172384.abstract: Constructed wetlands enable sustainable nitrogen removal but are constrained by electron donor scarcity. Although iron–sulfur (FeS) substrates provide sustained redox energy, the mechanisms linking their thermodynamic properties with microbial metabolism remain unresolved, hindering rational design. Here, we propose an energy–metabolism coupling framework, where mechanistic insights yield a guiding rule and data-driven modeling translates it into FS substrate optimization. Results demonstrate that strongly reductive environments accelerate early nitrogen removal but cause redox imbalance and ion accumulation, whereas moderate redox potentials activate the TCA cycle and enrich denitrifies such as Pseudomonas and Shewanella, supporting long-term stability. Functional gene analysis further shows that electron oversupply upregulates iron transporter genes, imposing energetic burdens. These insights point to a central guideline: effective FeS regulation requires balancing electron availability with metabolic adaptability. Building on these insights, we developed a machine-learning model that predicts denitrification performance across FeS ratios, enabling rational optimization. In 200-day validation experiments, the optimized system consistently maintained nitrogen removal efficiencies above 90 % with minimal fluctuation (standard deviation <5 %). Taken together, this study establishes a scalable FeS regulation strategy and provides a blueprint for designing efficient and resilient constructed wetland systems.
10.1016/j.cej.2025.172384.title: From mechanism to design: Thermodynamic–metabolic coupling and data-driven optimization of FeS substrates in constructed wetlands

10.1016/j.cej.2026.172696.abstract: This study developed a high-performance 3D molecularly imprinted surface-enhanced Raman scattering substrate (3D-MIP-SERS substrate) with glucose-selective recognition capabilities, and combined it with deep learning ensemble model to establish a non-invasive urine glucose detection platform. The theoretical low detection limit of the 3D-MIP-SERS substrate for glucose is as low as 0.02 mM, and it exhibits excellent selectivity towards interfering molecules such as fructose. The substrate can directly incubate with urine samples without complex preprocessing to obtain high-quality spectra. To achieve precise glucose concentration identification, a deep learning model integrating channel attention and spatial attention mechanisms was designed, and combined with ensemble learning strategies to classify the spectra of artificial urine with different glucose concentrations, achieving a classification accuracy of 95.2 %. This study constructed a urine glucose detection system that combines high selectivity and sensitive recognition by molecularly imprinted SERS substrates and efficient data analysis by intelligent algorithms, offering a new technical path for early screening and home monitoring of diabetes.
10.1016/j.cej.2026.172696.title: A urinary glucose detection platform based on 3D-MIP-SERS substrate and deep learning ensemble model

10.1016/j.cej.2026.172753.abstract: Traditional detection techniques are difficult to distinguish and detect multiple β-lactam antibiotics simultaneously. The detection performance of sensor arrays is also limited due to the poor catalytic activity of nanozymes or the preparation of multiple receptor units. Here, inspired by the microenvironment of amino acid residues in the natural enzyme catalytic active center, a histidine-functionalized copper-based nanozyme (Cu-HAc@His) was constructed through a defect engineering strategy. Compared with the parent nanozyme (Cu-HAc), the obtained Cu-HAc@His nanozyme has higher peroxidase-like (POD) activity. Given the significant difference in catalytic activity of Cu-HAc@His nanozyme under different pH, a sensor array was constructed using three different pH values for efficient identification of nine β-lactam antibiotics. Meanwhile, relying on the improvement of various machine learning (ML) models, the precision of the concentration-irrelevant classification system built using this array has been enhanced to 93.52%. This result has played a role in promoting blind sample recognition. More importantly, combining regression algorithms with sensor arrays enables precise quantitative analysis of multiple β-lactam antibiotics. This work is not only of great significance for improving the identification of β-lactam antibiotics in actual samples, but supplies a point of reference and direction for developing highly active POD nanozymes down the line.
10.1016/j.cej.2026.172753.title: Histidine-engineered Cu-HAc nanozyme with boosted peroxidase-like activity for accurate intelligent identification of β-lactam antibiotics through machine learning

10.1016/j.cej.2026.172903.abstract: In advanced electronic manufacturing, additives play a pivotal role in achieving high-quality metal interconnect by enabling precise pattern filling during electrodeposition. Currently, due to complex mechanisms, vast molecular spaces and lack of predictive models, the development of additives still relies on inefficient trial-and-error methods. In this work, a machine learning (ML)-based data-driven framework is developed to accelerate the discovery of cobalt electrodeposition additives. Focusing on molecular adsorption dynamics at the cobalt electrolyte interface during electrodeposition, this work employs quantum chemical properties to guide the construction of machine learning models for identifying molecules with ideal adsorption potential. Bayesian optimization is employed to optimize model accuracy by tuning hyperparameters, and SHAP analysis provides interpretable chemical insights. Three novel additives are identified, which are 2-aminopyrazine (APZ), 1-methylimidazole-4,5-dicarbonitrile (MIDCN), and 2-amino-4-ethylpyridine (AEP). Electrochemical and electroplating validation confirms that all additives exhibit strong inhibition effects, enabling grain refinement that reduces cobalt film surface roughness below 10 nm Ra, with the optimal performer achieving 4.58 nm Ra. Furthermore, superconformal filling of through‑silicon vias (TSVs) with aspect ratios >5 is achieved. This work establishes a machine learning-based data-driven strategy as an effective tool for accelerating the discovery of high-performance electrodeposition additives. The identified additives provide new insights into industrial metallization solutions for scaled-down nodes.
10.1016/j.cej.2026.172903.title: Data-driven discovery of novel additives for superconformal cobalt electrodeposition in 3D interconnects

10.1016/j.cej.2026.172908.abstract: Inspired by biomimetic strategies, crack-based strain-sensing technology has greatly advanced the hardware foundation of human–machine interfaces. However, conventional crack sensors face a critical trade-off among ultralow detection thresholds and broad-range operational ranges, which remains a key bottleneck limiting their overall performance. Here, drawing inspiration from the multilayered distribution of mechanoreceptors in human skin, we propose a hierarchical, multidimensional strain sensor architecture composed of vertically graphene (VG), MXene, and carbon nanotubes (CNTs). By introducing microchannels pattern in the VG layer together with a multi-step stretch–release coating strategy for the MXene and CNT layers, each material layer is structurally engineered in a targeted manner to form a stepwise conductive network. The synergistic coupling of these multilayer conductive pathways reduces the lower limit of detection 0.05‰ and expands the upper limit of detection to 80%, enabling a sensing range spanning five orders of magnitude. Beyond material engineering, a dual-mode machine learning framework, combining eXtreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost) for static posture classification and Bidirectional Encoder Representations from Transformers (BERT) for dynamic motion recognition, achieves classification accuracies exceeding 99%. This cross-disciplinary integration of hierarchical material design and intelligent data analysis paves the way for next-generation wearable interfaces and health-monitoring systems.
10.1016/j.cej.2026.172908.title: Skin-inspired hierarchical strain-partitioned sensor for ultralow detection thresholds and broad-range strain detection, empowered by dual-mode machine learning
10.1016/j.cej.2026.172908.source: ScienceDirect official citation and abstract BibTeX export

10.1016/j.cej.2026.173211.abstract: To address environmental challenges from electronic/industrial wastes accumulation, this study fabricated multifunctional glass-ceramics using waste printed circuit boards (WPCBs) and coal gangue/ash (CG/CA), integrating experimental techniques with machine learning (ML) to uncover structure-property-function relationships. First, the CaO-Al2O3-SiO2 glass-ceramic system was optimized by adjusting Al2O3/SiO2 ratio, glass network structure, crystallization behavior, and micromorphology. AS2 sample (Al2O3/SiO2 = 0.28) was identified as the base composition due to its superior performance, achieving high crystallinity (89.53%), bending strength (BS = 342 MPa), dielectric constant (εr = 6.62), low dielectric loss (tan δ = 1.14 × 10−3), and low thermal expansion coefficient (CTE = 5.86 × 10−6/K). Incorporating CA and CG provided cost-effective and sustainable alternatives. CA25 (CA/PCBA = 25/75) achieved comparable properties (BS = 289.5 MPa, εr = 6.77, tan δ = 4.24 × 10−3, CTE = 5.74 × 10−6/K), making it suitable for electrical applications. CG75 (CG/PCBA = 75/25) exhibited excellent BS (373 MPa) and magnetic properties (saturation magnetization = 5.71 emu/g, coercivity = 990 Oe), indicating potential for magnetic recording and magnetic separation. Three ML models, particularly random forest, revealed complex, nonlinear relationships and synergistic effects among structural features that influence performance by incorporating interaction terms and combining with statistical analysis. The process immobilized heavy metals (leaching below limits), reduced energy consumption, and achieved a 2680.09 CNY/t gross profit. This work provided an eco-friendly and cost-effective route for waste valorization into high-value materials.
10.1016/j.cej.2026.173211.title: Innovative utilization of waste printed circuit boards and coal gangue/ash for multifunctional glass-ceramics: structure-property insights via data-driven analysis

10.1016/j.cej.2026.172976.abstract: Facial nerve injury (FNI) results in devastating sequelae, including impaired eyelid closure, dysphagia, and permanent facial asymmetry, leading to long-term functional deficits and profound psychosocial impacts that pose significant rehabilitation challenges. In this study, to address these challenges, we developed an injectable hydrogel conjugated with a C-X-C motif chemokine ligand 12 (CXCL12)-mimetic peptide (CMP) to facilitate FNI repair. The results demonstrate that CMP promotes the reprogramming of Schwann cells (SCs) into repair-related phenotypes, enhancing their proliferation, migration, and neurotrophic expression. RNA sequencing suggests that the CXCR4-MAPK signaling pathway may play a role in CMP-mediated SCs reprogramming, which was further corroborated through siRNA knockdown and MAPK (ERK/JNK/P38) inhibitor experiments. A CMP-loaded hydrogel (CMP@Gel) was then constructed and characterized, exhibiting favorable mechanical properties and excellent biocompatibility. Additionally, the composite hydrogel could promote the recruitment and M2 polarization of macrophages, and angiogenesis in vivo. Furthermore, injection of CMP@Gel in rats with facial nerve crush injury, effectively enhanced the postinjury nerve motor functional recovery and structural restoration, demonstrating its superior therapeutic efficacy of the composite hydrogel. Taken together, these results highlight CMP-conjugated hydrogel as a promising biomaterial-based strategy for FNI repair, which creates an optimal microenvironment that integrates Schwann cells reprogramming, immunoregulation, and revascularization for nerve repair.
10.1016/j.cej.2026.172976.title: CXCL12-mimetic peptide-conjugated hydrogel orchestrates the neural microenvironment to accelerate facial nerve repair

10.1016/j.cej.2026.173184.abstract: Layered metal dichalcogenides (LMDCs) have attracted widespread attention in piezoelectric systems, particularly for miniaturized energy devices and wearable sensing applications. However, insufficient output performance and limited sensing accuracy remain critical challenges. In this work, we developed a van der Waals heterostructure (vdWH) composed of molybdenum disulfide/tin disulfide (SnS2/MoS2) by using chemical vapor deposition (CVD). The enhancement of intrinsic piezoelectricity was further confirmed by piezoelectric force microscopy (PFM). Furthermore, the as-fabricated SnS2/MoS2 vdWH was assembled into a piezoelectric nanogenerator (SM-PENG) device and demonstrated as a self-powered healthcare sensor to monitor diverse human motions. A sequential fast data density functional transform (s-fDDFT) model was also employed to improve the prediction accuracy of the designed sensor. Most importantly, the SM-PENGs were integrated into a multi-channel facial expression recognition platform for affective computing applications. We believe that this SM-PENG not only shows great potential for future ultrathin active sensors, but also represents a promising step toward personalized healthcare monitoring and emotion recognition.
10.1016/j.cej.2026.173184.title: Deep learning-assisted piezoelectric nanogenerators based on layered SnS2/MoS2 heterostructures for interactive sensing and affective computing applications
10.1016/j.cej.2026.173184.source: ScienceDirect official citation and abstract BibTeX export

10.1016/j.cej.2026.173116.abstract: Rapid detection of multiple cancers offers remarkable advantages, particularly when the type of cancer is unknown, and enables the discovery of undiagnosed cancers through screening. Cancer development causes abnormal alterations in metabolites, many of which are excreted in the urine. Recognizing changes in urinary metabolites can reveal specific characteristics of various cancer types and aid in their diagnosis. Herein, we analyzed 218 urine samples from healthy individuals and patients with pancreatic, prostate, lung, and colorectal cancers using plasmonic materials to obtain label-free surface-enhanced Raman scattering signals. Applying artificial intelligence-based analytical methods, we achieved a diagnostic accuracy of >99% across all five groups. To identify urinary metabolic biomarkers, we compiled a library of known urinary metabolites and applied the multivariate curve resolution–alternating least squares method, a bilinear algorithm model, to relatively quantify the secretion levels of selected metabolites. This approach combines SERS signals from plasmonic materials with AI analysis and mathematical modeling to propose biomarkers. The technology is expected to provide a versatile platform not only for multicancer diagnosis but also for diagnosing various diseases, offering a promising tool for early detection and personalized medicine.
10.1016/j.cej.2026.173116.title: A single urine test-based SERS–AI–BAM for on-site multiple cancer diagnosis and metabolite profiling
10.1016/j.cej.2026.173116.source: ScienceDirect official citation and abstract BibTeX export

10.1016/j.cej.2026.173177.abstract: Spinal cord injury (SCI) is a serious nerve system disease characterized by high mortality and disability rates. Currently, few effective therapies can significantly promote functional recovery after SCI. Stem cell therapy is considered as a highly promising strategy. Though neural stem cells (NSCs) represent an ideal source of cell therapy due to the ability of differentiating into neurons and glial cells, most NSCs differentiate into glial cells rather than neurons. This results in low utilization of transplanted cells. Nevertheless, we find that NSCs treated with black phosphorus quantum dots (BPQDs) could significantly promote the repair of SCI and had no toxic side effects on the organs of mice. In vitro, BPQDs could inhibit the membrane receptor Notch1 to promote neuronal differentiation of NSCs. Furthermore, Notch1 inhibition could also suppress LPS-induced microglial inflammation effectively. This suggests that Notch1 may be an essential cross-target for multi-level repair of SCI. Moreover, NSCs transplantation combined with BPQDs effectively promoted nerve regeneration and functional recovery of SCI mice in vivo. It indicates that BPQDs have a comprehensive restorative effect on SCI from various aspects and perspectives. Thus, our study demonstrates that NSCs transplantation combined with BPQDs may be an effective and promising strategy for the treatment of SCI.
10.1016/j.cej.2026.173177.title: Black phosphorus quantum dots regulate inflammation and neural stem cells differentiation via Notch1 signaling through cell adhesion

10.1016/j.cej.2026.173290.abstract: The restoration of hand function is pivotal for regaining autonomy and quality of life following neurological or orthopedic impairments. Multidimensional assessment of finger forces is essential for motor recovery, yet current rehabilitation solutions are often constrained by insufficient multidimensional force sensing capability and poor wearing comfort. Here, we present a real-time monitoring system for assisted hand rehabilitation, integrating a fully customizable triaxial force sensing finger cot with a residual fully connected neural network (Res-FCNN) for force component decoupling. Using high-resolution digital light processing (DLP) three-dimensional (3D) printing, the customizable triaxial force sensing finger cot is fabricated combining complex structures with microscale precision and ergonomic design. The sensitivities of the triaxial force sensor of the system are 0.0213 and 0.0625 N−1 in tangential and normal directions, respectively. The proposed Res-FCNN model enables precise decoupling of triaxial force components, achieving an R2 greater than 0.95 across all axes. Moreover, experimental validations (including finger motion trajectory distinction and grasp stability assessment) demonstrate that the real-time monitoring system integrating the customizable wearable hardware with algorithm-based signal decoding provides a practical framework for quantitative analysis and evaluation of hand rehabilitation training.
10.1016/j.cej.2026.173290.title: A customizable three-dimensional-printed triaxial force sensing finger cot with residual fully connected neural network algorithm for wearable hand rehabilitation

10.1016/j.cej.2026.173408.abstract: As artificial intelligence technology advances rapidly, machine learning shows great potential in materials science. It can efficiently process and analyze large-scale data, uncover complex patterns, and offer new approaches for material prediction and design. This review focuses on the application progress of machine-learning models in biomedical nanomaterial design. Firstly, it presents the basic principles, development history, and advantages of machine learning in this field. Then, it provides a deep analysis of the technical breakthroughs in machine-learning models for predicting physicochemical properties, optimizing synthesis routes, and analyzing biological interactions of nanomaterials. Finally, it addresses the challenges of insufficient data quality and limited model interpretability in machine learning, and proposes solutions like developing more explainable machine-learning methods, standardizing data-reporting formats, combining machine learning with traditional molecular simulations, and enhancing result verification. Overall, this review aims to promote a shift from experience-driven to data-driven approaches in the field of biomedical nanomaterial design and to facilitate innovation and clinical translation in this area.
10.1016/j.cej.2026.173408.title: Application of machine learning in the design of biomedical nanomaterials

10.1016/j.cej.2026.173418.abstract: While traditional synthetic antioxidants are efficient, their toxicity presents ecological drawbacks. This study harnessed multi-scale simulation and machine learning to design a high-performance, eco-friendly phenolic antioxidant. Inspired by natural antioxidants, this study analyzed the influence of natural antioxidant molecular structure on the bond dissociation energy (BDE), and established a database containing phenolic antioxidants' structural information and BDE, then bioinspired-designed a high-performance phenolic botannical acid-derived antioxidant (CAA) by machine learning. The Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) model was employed to predict the bond dissociation energy of antioxidants with high accuracy (R2 = 0.87, RMSE = 11.71 kJ/mol). The new phenolic antioxidant CAA with low BDE was designed by mapping substituent descriptors to molecular descriptors. We further investigated the toxicological effects and anti-aging mechanisms of CAA through integrated experimental and multi-scale simulation methods. A quantitative analysis of the chemical reactions and. physical behaviors was conducted, comparing CAA with sinapic acid, syringic acid, gallic acid, butylated hydroxyanisole (BHA), and 2,4,6-Tri-tert-butylphenol (2,4,6-TTBP). Toxicity simulations indicated that CAA has lower acute/chronic toxicity than BHA and 2,4,6-TTBP, with no mutagenicity or bioaccumulation. Moreover, multiscale simulations revealed its high antioxidant capacity, characterized by a low BDE (280.3 kJ·mol−1) and a low transition state (TS) energy barrier (20.4 kJ·mol−1). Furthermore, the CAA-incorporated natural rubber (NR) composite exhibited exceptional thermo-oxidative stability, retaining 87.8% of its tensile strength after 72 h of thermal aging. Additionally, migration tests confirmed the superior anti-migration stability of CAA, evidenced by a minimal change (9.2%) in change ultraviolet (UV) absorption intensity within the NR composite. Therefore, the designed antioxidant CAA is environmentally benign and exhibits superior resistance to thermo-oxidative aging and migration. This work provides valuable guidance for screening and designing high-performance, eco-friendly antioxidants.
10.1016/j.cej.2026.173418.title: Inspired by natural antioxidants: Design of high-performance phenolic antioxidants based on machine learning and its application in NR

10.1016/j.cej.2026.173311.abstract: Computational modeling of multiphase flow systems is crucial across various fields, including chemical engineering, energy, environmental science and aerospace industry, enabling cost-effective design and analysis. However, accurate simulation, prediction, control, and optimization remain difficult due to the high-dimensional, chaotic behavior and dynamic interfaces of multiphase flows. Artificial intelligence (AI), particularly deep learning, physics constrained learning, generative models, and reinforcement learning offer promising tools to overcome these challenges. This review presents the current landscape of AI in multiphase flow research. It highlights AI-enhanced numerical solvers for interface dynamics, including explicit interface tracking and implicit interface capturing, as well as intelligent sparse grid processing. AI-extended simulation implementations are also explored, with an emphasis on generative models such as generative adversarial networks (GANs), variational autoencoders (VAEs) and large language models (LLM)-driven agents that synthesize physically consistent samples and automate complex modeling and simulation workflows. Moreover, AI-oriented control and optimization methods – such as Bayesian optimization (BO), reinforcement learning (RL), and automatic differentiation (AD) – are analyzed for optimizing mixing, stability, and phase distribution, particularly in industrial settings that require real-time, high-performance solutions. Finally, we provide a critical assessment of the challenges and opportunities of learning-based algorithms, emphasizing dataset normalization and model-design regularization to enhance generalization. Overall, this review bridges multiphase-flow mechanics, data science, AI, and computational chemical engineering, and documents an ongoing digital and intelligent progression from fully physics-based equation solving approaches to a physics-coupled, and data-driven integrated computational framework.
10.1016/j.cej.2026.173311.title: Integrating data and physics: A review of data-driven methods for computational multiphase flow

10.1016/j.cej.2026.173579.abstract: Developing flexible sensing materials that integrate high conductivity, mechanical robustness, self-healing capabilities, and environmental stability remains a critical challenge for next-generation wearable electronics. However, conventional hydrogels often suffer from intrinsic trade-offs between these properties and are prone to freezing-induced deactivation. Herein, a multifunctional POAL hydrogel was engineered via a synergistic strategy combining the double-helix network of agar, dynamic Schiff base crosslinking of oxidized sodium alginate (OSA), and ionic coordination of LiCl. This unique multi-network architecture endows the hydrogel with outstanding comprehensive properties, including a tensile strength of 111.9 kPa, an elongation at break of 158%, and a self-healing efficiency of 48.9%. Notably, the hydrogel exhibits exceptional ionic conductivity (2.25 S/m and anti-freezing tolerance down to −42.1 °C, ensuring reliable operation in harsh environments. Leveraging its excellent rheological properties, micro-triangular pyramidal arrays were precisely fabricated via Digital Light Processing (DLP) 3D printing to construct a high-performance triboelectric nanogenerator (POAL-TENG). By maximizing the effective contact area, the device achieved a peak output voltage of 239.9 V and a superior pressure sensitivity of 89.14 mV Pa−1, effectively harvesting mechanical energy. Furthermore, to realize intelligent sensing, a hybrid Deep Learning model (ResNet-18 + Bidirectional LSTM) was integrated to process handwriting signals, achieving a 97% recognition accuracy. This work presents a comprehensive strategy for designing robust, freeze-tolerant, and intelligent self-powered sensing systems, expanding the horizons of human-machine interaction (HMI).
10.1016/j.cej.2026.173579.title: 3D-printed microstructured ionic hydrogel and nano-friction generator for self-powered electronic skin and deep learning character recognition

10.1016/j.cej.2026.173593.abstract: Nanoplastics are increasingly recognized as emerging stressors that impair photosynthesis in photosynthetic organisms, and their co-occurrence with environmental pollutants can further intensify phytotoxic effects. To address the fragmented understanding of these combined impacts, we integrated a meta-analysis of 1067 experimental observations with explainable machine learning to quantify how nanoplastics and co-pollutants jointly influence photosynthetic processes. The results showed predominantly negative effects across light reactions and rubisco enzyme activity, with organism species, nanoplastics dose, size, and exposure duration identified as major determinants of photosynthetic inhibition. High-sensitivity indicators of photosynthetic stress were identified, and corn emerged as a particularly sensitive organism. By linking physicochemical properties and exposure conditions to quantitative photosynthetic outcomes, this study provides a clearer and more accessible framework for predicting phytotoxicity and supports improved ecological risk assessment and management strategies.
10.1016/j.cej.2026.173593.title: Nanoplastics and co-pollutants negatively affect the photosynthesis of photosynthetic organisms: insights from meta-analysis and machine learning

10.1016/j.cej.2026.173378.abstract: Continuous carbon fiber-reinforced poly(phthalazinone ether sulfone ketone) (CF/PPESK) composites exhibit exceptional high-temperature resistance and mechanical properties, rendering them promising candidates for aerospace applications. However, the degradation mechanisms and service lifetime of these composites under prolonged thermo-oxidative aging remain insufficiently elucidated. This study systematically investigates the structure-property evolution of CF/PPESK composites at 250–290 °C through integrated multiscale characterization and machine learning approaches. After 1008 h of thermo-oxidative aging at 250 °C, the interlaminar shear strength (ILSS) retention decreases by 87.8%, primarily due to interfacial debonding and microcrack propagation. While short-term cross-linking of PPESK at 290 °C enhances ILSS by 20%, prolonged exposure at this temperature leads to a 50.7% reduction in flexural strength, mainly attributed to molecular chain scission and interfacial degradation. The competitive temperature-dependent mechanism is quantitatively described through Starink kinetic analysis. Based on this, a machine learning model is constructed to precisely quantify the complex and nonlinear relationship that governs the material performance and its post-aging chemical state. The optimized Random Forest model demonstrated high prediction accuracy for the retention of both flexural strength and ILSS, with mean absolute errors as low as 0.22 and 0.19, and coefficients of determination reaching 0.96 and 0.97. This model provides an analytical tool for understanding and modeling the degradation behavior of CF/PPESK composites.
10.1016/j.cej.2026.173378.title: Thermo-oxidative aging mechanism and machine learning-assisted lifetime prediction of CF/PPESK composites

10.1016/j.cej.2026.173727.abstract: The pursuit of new high-energy density materials with desirable sensitivity properties has been a prominent research focus in recent years. However, the intrinsic trade-off between energy and sensitivity poses a major obstacle in the design of advanced energetic materials. In this work, machine learning assisted high-throughput virtual screening (ML-HTVS), integrated with experimental validation, was employed to accelerate the discovery of high-energy density and low-sensitivity materials. Through this approach, we rapidly identified 3-amino-7-nitro-[1,2,4]triazolo[1,5-b][1,2,4,5]tetrazine-2-oxide (ICM-107) as a promising candidate molecule. Subsequently, we successfully synthesized this compound starting from 3,6-bis(3,5-dimethyl pyrazol-1-yl)-1,2,4,5-tetrazine (DMPT) through a five-step process. ICM-107 exhibits an impressive experimental density of 1.973 g·cm−3 and outstanding calculated detonation performance (Dv: 9584 m·s−1, P: 40.0 GPa) as well as experimental measured detonation performance (Dv: 9290 m·s−1, P: 39.5 GPa). Among all [5,6]fused-ring energetic materials, ICM-107 stands out with the highest recorded detonation performance, approaching that of the benchmark explosive CL-20. Additionally, it features a favorable decomposition temperature (Td: 212 °C) and low sensitivity characteristics (impact sensitivity, IS: 20 J; friction sensitivity, FS: 324 N). These highly promising properties make it highly attractive as a high-energy and low-sensitivity energetic materials.
10.1016/j.cej.2026.173727.title: Discovery of high-energy-density materials via machine learning-assisted high-throughput virtual screening and experimental approach

10.1016/j.cej.2026.173615.abstract: The gas distribution zone (GDZ) is a critical flow field component for enhancing the overall performance of proton exchange membrane fuel cells (PEMFCs). However, conventional monolithic designs often cause problems such as uneven gas distribution, low mass transfer efficiency, and inadequate water-thermal management. To address these challenges, this study proposes a partitioned GDZ design concept for precise gas distribution control and a two-stage optimization framework based on limited data for the synergistic improvement of performance metrics. In the first stage, the GDZ was divided into primary and secondary distribution zones, and then seven configurations were evaluated using a 3D two-phase PEMFC model. A hybrid configuration was identified as the optimal case (dots in primary and ribs in secondary distribution zones). Building on this configuration, four key geometric parameters of the GDZ were further optimized in the second stage. An orthogonal array was first employed to efficiently design 16 runs of experiments, with four targets defined: net output power density (Wnet), oxygen concentration non-uniformity (UO2), flow velocity non-uniformity (Uflow), and membrane water content (λ¯). The Taguchi method and analysis of variance (ANOVA) were then applied to assess parameter significance and quantify their contribution rates. Finally, grey relational analysis (GRA) delivered the optimal solution, which improved all four targets versus the first-stage baseline: a 4.328% increase in Wnet, a 0.612% increase in λ¯, and reductions of 6.160% in UO2 and 10.913% in Uflow. Compared to the first-stage optimum, three targets were further enhanced, with the slight Wnet loss (only 1.838%) outweighed by gains in UO2, Uflow, and λ¯. This study validates the novel partitioned GDZ design concept and establishes a comprehensive, transferable optimization framework for the systematic design of various PEMFC components.
10.1016/j.cej.2026.173615.title: Structure design for the gas distribution zone of PEMFC bipolar plates: A data-driven multi-objective optimization framework integrating the Taguchi method and grey relational analysis

10.1016/j.cej.2026.173707.abstract: The escalating need for efficient carbon dioxide (CO2) capture has positioned ionic liquids (ILs) as promising candidates due to their tunable structures and high CO2 affinity. However, systematic strategies that integrate machine learning (ML) predictions with experimental validation remain limited, and the prediction accuracy and reliability of single ML methods for new ILs needs to be improved. In this study, we introduced four ensemble frameworks that strategically integrates five classical graph neural networks (GNNs), capitalizing on their complementary strengths to effectively mitigate the inherent limitations of single-model approaches. When predicting the CO2 absorption capacity and viscosity of novel ILs, the ensemble frameworks generally outperformed traditional ML methods, with the optimal ensemble model achieving R2 values of 0.9258 and 0.9250, respectively. To enable high-throughput screening, we generated a virtual library of 7616 ILs via pairwise combination of 112 cations and 68 anions, and established multi-dimensional criteria (CO2 absorption mole fraction >0.1, viscosity <100 mPa·s at 40 °C and 101.325 kPa, SAScore <3.5) to select ILs balancing performance and synthetic feasibility. Finally, we screened 176 new high-performance candidates and validated four ILs experimentally, with close consistency between predicted and experimental properties (relative deviations: 4.21%, 8.85%, 18.32% and 16.14%, respectively). The framework accelerates the design of ILs with exceptional CO2 absorption capacity and reduced viscosity, thereby establishing a generalizable and interpretable ensemble ML approach for molecular materials discovery.
10.1016/j.cej.2026.173707.title: Multiple ensemble graph neural networks for the high-throughput screening of ionic liquids for carbon capture: Modeling study and experimental validation
