10.1016/j.cej.2026.173942.abstract: Dissolved hydrogen is a key early indicator of insulation faults in oil-immersed transformers, yet in situ electrochemical sensors for its detection are frequently limited by liquid-electrolyte leakage, slow hydrogen transport in viscous oil, and poor long-term durability. Here we develop a quasi-solid-state hydrogen sensor that integrates composition-tuned Pd0.8Ni0.2 nanoalloys, uniformly anchored on hydroxyl-functionalized multi-walled carbon nanotubes, with a leakage-resistant PVDF-HFP/[EMIM][TFSI] ionogel in a fully encapsulated probe. Density-functional-theory-guided alloy design and strong metal-support interactions optimize hydrogen adsorption and reduce interfacial resistance, enabling a wide 1–15,000 ppm linear range with a 1 ppm detection limit and nA·ppm−1 level sensitivity. In the unified gas/oil diffusion architecture, the response time of 93 s at 500 ppm reflects the headspace-oil-membrane mass-transport pathway, while the electrochemical interface remains stable over 180 days with >78% retention of the 500 ppm signal. The probe shows robust H2 selectivity, delivering >10 higher response than the strongest interferent (CH4, CO, C2H2), and retains nearly constant sensitivity across ISO VG 46–100 transformer oils. In ISO VG 68 oil, probe-derived dissolved H2 matches headspace gas chromatography (R2 ≈ 0.99), validating calibration transfer and accurate concentration readout under real transformer-oil matrices. This mechanism-guided materials-electrolyte-device integration provides a scalable route to reliable, long-term dissolved-gas analysis in power-grid transformers.
10.1016/j.cej.2026.173942.title: Mechanism-guided Pd0.8Ni0.2 nanoalloy/MWCNT-ionogel probe for long-term electrochemical monitoring of dissolved hydrogen in transformer oil

10.1016/j.cej.2026.173582.abstract: Based on the Hofmeister effect to optimize interfacial interactions, this study combined a chemical-physical dual cross-linking strategy and integrated machine learning algorithms to successfully fabricate a wearable wood-based finger-code. This device exhibits a response time of only 212 ms, a low detection limit of 0.19% strain, and also features environmental friendliness and low cost, which is used to achieve precise capture of subtle finger joint deformations and conversion between sign language movements and letter signals. The sensor uses wood cellulose as a natural three-dimensional support framework, with polyacrylic acid (PAA) and polyacrylamide (PAM) as functional fillers. The interfacial synergy between the framework and fillers provides a structural basis for the device's excellent performance. Meanwhile, Hofmeister effect modulated hydrogel micro-crosslinking structure; sulfate ions (SO₄2−) optimized hydrogel stiffness and flexibility via regulating interfacial water arrangement, hydrogen bonds and hydrophobicity. It not only achieves a longitudinal tensile stress of 12.49 MPa and a transverse tensile stress of 0.83 MPa, but also exhibits high mechanical strength, outstanding adhesion, favorable cyclic stability, and superior electrochemical performance. In practical application scenarios, after wearing this wearable device, model training and gesture recognition analysis were conducted using the Stochastic Gradient Descent (SGD) Classifier machine learning algorithm. Finally, an ultra-high recognition accuracy of 98.46% was achieved, enabling real-time and accurate analysis of gesture movements and rapid output of corresponding letter signals, thus truly realizing green, low-cost, and high-sensitivity sign language-text conversion. This research not only provides a new functional device with excellent performance for the field of intelligent human-computer communication, but also opens up a new direction for barrier-free communication through an economical and efficient technical route, showing broad application prospects.
10.1016/j.cej.2026.173582.title: Implementation of excellent tensile strain for sign language translation using wood-based finger-code supported by machine learning algorithms

10.1016/j.cej.2026.173939.abstract: Biliary atresia (BA) is a rare but life-threatening neonatal liver disease and remains one of the leading causes of pediatric liver transplantation worldwide. If untreated, the 2-year survival rate is below 10%, and delayed diagnosis markedly reduces the success rate of Kasai portoenterostomy. Current diagnostic methods rely primarily on dried blood spots (DBS) and ELISA, which require relatively large blood volumes, are time-consuming, and are poorly suited for routine newborn screening, creating an urgent need for rapid and neonate-friendly diagnostic tools. Here, we present an AI-assisted biosensing platform for rapid and quantitative detection of matrix metalloproteinase-7 (MMP7), a clinically validated biomarker for BA. The platform integrates an electric double-layer extended-gate field-effect transistor (EDL-EGFET) with an AI-based calibration strategy that compensates for chip-to-chip variation and enables consistent quantification across sensors. By incorporating process parameters into model training, the AI system effectively reduces chip-to-chip variability, significantly improving the robustness of the sensing platform. Clinical validation using 20 patient samples demonstrated a strong correlation with ELISA-based quantification. The Pearson correlation coefficient improved from 0.80 using the conventional method to 0.96 with the AI-enhanced model. The system achieved a limit of detection of 0.32 ng/mL, covered the clinically relevant MMP7 range, and reduced the total diagnostic time from 8 h to 10 min. Only 10 μL (one drop) of blood was required per test. This innovative AI-driven EDL-EGFET platform demonstrates strong potential for advancing precise clinical diagnostics, enhancing neonatal care, and addressing the diagnostic challenges associated with this neglected disease.
10.1016/j.cej.2026.173939.title: AI-driven process-tolerant BioFET sensing model for precise biliary atresia diagnosis of infants with a single drop of blood

10.1016/j.cej.2026.174093.abstract: This study reports a novel room-temperature chemical resistance gas sensor, which is based on the flower-like Bi2WO6/In2O3 heterojunction and is co-integrated with a machine learning algorithm, achieving high-performance and selective detection of volatile organic compounds. The composites synthesized by the combined hydrothermal-calcination method have a unique microstructure, in which In2O3 nanoparticles are uniformly anchored to Bi2WO6 nanospheres to form effective n-n-type heterojunctions. The optimized sensor (labeled B/I-2 with a Bi:In molar ratio of 1:2) demonstrates excellent sensing performance at 25 °C: a response value of up to 16.8 to 100 ppm n-butanol, which is approximately 7.3 times higher than pure Bi2WO6 (2.3), along with a low detection limit (55 ppb), fast response/recovery time (55 s/77 s), excellent repeatability, and up to 31 days of stability. In addition, the sensor maintains a significant response (10.4) in high humidity (74% RH) environments. To overcome the inherent selectivity challenges of metal oxide sensors, four machine learning models are introduced: random forests, convolutional neural networks, long short-term memory networks, and genetic algorithm-optimized backpropagation networks. Five interfering VOCs (n-butanol, n-propanol, ethanol, acetone, and xylene, all at concentrations of 100 ppm) were classified and identified. Among them, the random forest model achieved the highest recognition accuracy of 95.74%, demonstrating the effectiveness of machine learning in improving sensor selectivity. Diffuse reflection infrared Fourier transform spectroscopy revealed the reaction path on the surface of the material, confirming the oxidation of n-butanol to CO2 and H2O. Finally, by integrating the B/I-2 sensor with the STM32 microcontroller, a portable prototype device was built, which successfully realized real-time monitoring of n-butanol and visual LED alarms, verifying its practical application potential.
10.1016/j.cej.2026.174093.title: Machine learning-assisted discrimination and detection of volatile organic compounds based on chemiresistive gas sensors made with Bi2WO6/In2O3 heterojunctions
10.1016/j.cej.2026.174093.source: ScienceDirect official citation and abstract BibTeX export

10.1016/j.cej.2026.174089.abstract: The rapid and on-site monitoring of peroxide value (PV) is crucial for assessing the quality and safety of edible oils. To address this need, two enzyme-free optical sensing strategies were developed based on iodide-mediated chromogenic systems, utilizing 3,3′,5,5′-tetramethylbenzidine (I-TMB) and triangular gold nanoprisms (IAu NPRs), respectively. The IAu NPRs system exhibited a wider linear detection range and a faster response, attributed to localized surface plasmon resonance (LSPR) shifts due to peroxide-induced iodide etching. A linear correlation was established across a PV range of 0.0045 to 27.85 mmol·kg−1 using UV–vis spectrophotometry, with a calculated detection limit of 0.0015 mmol·kg−1. Validation with real oil samples demonstrated satisfactory recovery rates (98.94–101.40%) and relative standard deviations (RSD) between 2.30% and 3.53%. Furthermore, a portable detection platform was constructed by integrating this sensing strategy with the Kendryte K210 smart chip and a deep learning algorithm. This integrated system provided results consistent with laboratory-based UV–vis measurements, indicating its potential for practical field analysis of edible oils. The combination of nanoprism-based sensing with portable artificial intelligence analytics represents a significant step toward rapid food quality monitoring technologies.
10.1016/j.cej.2026.174089.title: Fusing nanoprisms and embedded AI: a portable sensor for intelligent peroxide value monitoring in edible oils
10.1016/j.cej.2026.174089.source: ScienceDirect official citation and abstract BibTeX export

10.1016/j.cej.2026.173906.abstract: Active Pharmaceutical Ingredients (APIs) face significant challenges in end-to-end continuous flow synthesis, including low throughput, inefficient condition optimization, and discontinuous multi-step processes. This study develops a methodological framework for the continuous flow synthesis of fluconazole, centered on three key innovations: a milliliter-scale 3D microfluidic chip (MFC) with a high-density Barker transform structure, which achieves >99% mixing efficiency within 6 s (Reynolds number 3–350) and overcomes the volume limitation of traditional microfluidics; a synergistic optimization strategy combining Bayesian Optimization (BO) and in-line UV monitoring, which identifies optimal reaction conditions with minimal experiments; and a fully uninterrupted flow process integrating in-line extraction and circulating flow, eliminating off-line workup and streamlining time-consuming steps. Applied to fluconazole synthesis, this framework achieves an 86% yield in 2 h and 40 min, outperforming traditional batch processes and existing continuous flow routes. This work provides a scalable methodological paradigm for the full-process continuous synthesis of other APIs, highlighting the value of integrated device-design, real-time analytics, and process regulation in pharmaceutical manufacturing.
10.1016/j.cej.2026.173906.title: Continuous flow synthesis of fluconazole monitored by inline ultraviolet spectroscopy: 3D microfluidic platform and Bayesian optimization
10.1016/j.cej.2026.173906.source: ScienceDirect official citation and abstract BibTeX export

10.1016/j.cej.2026.174300.abstract: In this study, a deep learning-assisted Smartphone-based, MOF-powered, Amine-Responsive, Traceability (SMART) label was developed for the real-time monitoring and precise prediction of food freshness through the food supply chain. This non-destructive freshness assessment is achieved by photographing the SMART label with a smartphone for deep-learning-based image analysis. An anthocyanin @ zeolitic imidazolate framework-8 (A @ ZIF-8) nanocomposite was synthesized using a one-pot method, in which anthocyanins were encapsulated within the MOF framework and subsequently embedded in a hydrogel matrix. The strategy of MOF encapsulation effectively enhances the structural stability of the loaded anthocyanins, which worked as a freshness indicator, while the integration of MOFs and hydrogels significantly enhances the response sensitivity of the SMART label. Considering the strong influence of ambient lighting on smartphone-based freshness assessment, representative real-world lighting conditions (~50 lx, ~500 lx, ~5000 lx, and ~ 50,000 lx) were simulated to construct a dataset. A cascaded light-adaptive convolutional neural network (CNN) model achieved prediction accuracies exceeding 91% when trained on 5760 marked images, outperforming representative other end-to-end CNN models, showing its desirable sensing stability in variable lighting conditions. Coupled with the self-developed “FoodSense” application, the proposed system provides a practical and reliable platform for rapid food freshness prediction and early risk warning across the food supply chain.
10.1016/j.cej.2026.174300.title: A deep learning-assisted SMART label for food freshness monitoring and prediction under variable lighting conditions

10.1016/j.cej.2026.174246.abstract: Sodium-ion batteries (SIBs) are emerging as a cost-effective alternative to lithium-ion batteries for large-scale energy storage. However, their commercialization has been hindered by the lack of low-cost and high-performance cathode materials. Here, we report a machine learning–guided strategy for designing multi-metal Prussian blue analogues (PBAs), establishing a paradigm of synergistic elemental modulation. The optimized PBA-MCNF delivers a reversible capacity of 102.59 mAh g−1 at 1C and maintains 97.07% of its capacity after 2500 cycles (based on 105.68 mAh g−1 at the first cycle). The synergistic effect among Mn, Cu, Ni, and Fe simultaneously broadens the Na+ migration channels and enhances both conductivity and structural stability. Cost analysis reveals that, compared with LiFePO4, the cathode material cost is reduced by 33.8%, with an average energy storage cost as low as 0.083 $/kWh. By integrating machine learning, DFT calculations, experimental validation, and techno-economic analysis, this work provides a comprehensive framework for advancing SIB research and opens a new avenue for practical large-scale deployment.
10.1016/j.cej.2026.174246.title: Machine learning unlocks multi-metal synergy in Prussian blue cathodes toward ultralow-cost sodium-ion grid storage
10.1016/j.cej.2026.174246.source: ScienceDirect official citation and abstract BibTeX export

10.1016/j.cej.2026.174301.abstract: Due to the widespread application of hydrogen sulfide (H2S) in industries such as chemical, medical, and food, highly selective detection of H2S at low temperatures is of great significance. Chemiresistive gas sensors based on metal-oxide-semiconductor (MOS) have been widely used for detecting various gases; however, due to the low efficiency of electron transfer in individual MOSs, their gas-sensing performance is far from satisfactory. Herein, a porous bimetallic oxide In2O3@Co3O4 heterojunction has been obtained by elaborately constructing metal-organic framework (MOF)-on-MOF conjugate (MIL-68@ZIF-67). The developed In2O3@Co3O4 sensor achieves great sensing performances for H2S (100 ppm), exhibiting outstanding selectivity, high sensitivity (110.2), and rapid recovery speed (47 s) at a low working temperature (100 °C), which are significantly better than that of pristine In2O3 and Co3O4. The large mesoporous architecture, rich active sites generated by composite Co3O4, and formation of type II charge transfer pathway are primarily accountable for the improved H2S-sensing capabilities. Moreover, density functional theory (DFT) calculations show that In2O3@Co3O4 has a higher adsorption energy for H2S compared to other comparative gases. The optimal sensor demonstrates high-accuracy (R2 = 0.9907) H2S concentration prediction capability driven by Machine Learning. The ability to predict H2S concentration by combining high-performance sensor with regression prediction model provides a feasible approach for the next generation of devices in environmental monitoring and other related fields.
10.1016/j.cej.2026.174301.title: Hetero In2O3@Co3O4 derived from MOF-on-MOF conjugate combined synergistically with exponential-trigonometric optimization-support vector regression enables high-precision quantitative detection of H2S
10.1016/j.cej.2026.174301.source: ScienceDirect official citation and abstract BibTeX export

10.1016/j.cej.2026.174378.abstract: Smart bearings offer a promising approach for real-time motion and condition monitoring in rotating machinery by embedding sensing functionality directly into the bearing structure. However, most existing smart bearing designs remain constrained to single-modal motion sensing, typically capturing only rotational or vibrational motion. In this paper, a novel smart thrust ball bearing (STBB) is proposed, incorporating a mosaic-patterned polarized electret for enhanced multi-modal motion sensing. Charges are injected into the electret film in a patterned manner using silicon shadow masks fabricated via deep reactive ion etching (DRIE). The coupled signal from simultaneous rotational and vibrational motions is fully decoupled through the dual Fourier transform (DFT) algorithm. The results show that the STBB exhibits high linearity, with R2 = 0.9999 and R2 = 0.9998 for rotation and vibration, respectively, and a rotational sensitivity of 7.48 rpm·Hz−1. The STBB is further integrated into a six-joint robotic arm for dynamic monitoring. Combined with a long short-term memory (LSTM) neural network, the STBB achieves 90.33% fault classification accuracy. These findings highlight its potential as a scalable and multi-modal sensing solution for intelligent maintenance systems.
10.1016/j.cej.2026.174378.title: AI-driven fault diagnosis in smart bearings using mosaic-patterned electret for multi-modal motion sensing

10.1016/j.cej.2026.174547.abstract: The development of highly efficient photosensitizers is crucial for advancing photodynamic therapy (PDT), yet current approaches largely rely on traditional trial–and–error synthesis coupled with iterative performance screening, which slows down its extensive application. Herein, we present a machine learning–based platform that predicts the photophysical properties of functionally tailored photosensitizers through regression and classification models, enabling rapid screening and identification of TMPB as an optimal candidate. Experimental validation confirmed that TMPB exhibits robust reactive oxygen species (ROS) generation via both Type I and Type II pathways, achieving a high relative singlet oxygen quantum yield of 95.4% and strong superoxide anion radical production. Moreover, TMPB displays bio-responsive fluorescence and a synergistic antibacterial mechanism combining contact–mediated membrane disruption with light–triggered photodynamic inactivation. The multi-cationic nature of TMPB enables facile loading onto various fabric materials (T@Fabric), effectively blocking pathogen transmission via synergistic “capture–contact–photodynamic” functions, highlighting their promise for photodynamic antimicrobial fabrics. Overall, the machine learning techniques presented in this study offer an innovative and efficient approach for the data-driven screening and development of next-generation medical protective materials.
10.1016/j.cej.2026.174547.title: Machine learning–guided screening of highly efficient multi-cationic photosensitizers for capture–contact–photodynamic antibacterial fabrics

10.1016/j.cej.2026.174425.abstract: This study presents a bimodal human-machine interaction panel based on a honeycomb electrode structure. The device is designed in accordance with the principle of triboelectric nanogenerators and is capable of recognizing contact and non-contact handwriting inputs. By embedding CaCu₃Ti₄O₁₂ particles into the Ecoflex triboelectric layer, the output performance in non-contact mode is significantly improved, achieving a voltage output of 8.3 V at a distance of 30 mm. When integrated with a convolutional neural network model, the device demonstrates high-precision recognition of 26 English letters in non-contact mode, as well as contact-based Chinese characters and numeric combinations, with an average recognition accuracy exceeding 95%. Furthermore, a human-machine interaction system was developed using the BHMIP, where tapping out Morse code are employed to control directional commands and non-contact input is used for numerical input, enabling precise control of Sudoku games. This system effectively demonstrates the application potential of BHMIP in gesture recognition, self-powered signal acquisition, and intelligent input control. Although surface charge stability under high humidity and signal decoupling in complex scenarios remain challenging, this work presents a solution for the development of self-powered, multi-dimensional human-machine interfaces.
10.1016/j.cej.2026.174425.title: Honeycomb electrode-based triboelectric nanogenerator for deep learning-derived bimodal human-machine interaction systems

10.1016/j.cej.2026.174690.abstract: Pseudomonas aeruginosa (P. aeruginosa), a widespread multidrug-resistant pathogen, threatens public health through rapid transmission, high virulence, and resilient biofilm formation, resulting in significant mortality. Consequently, it is imperative to develop rapid, sensitive detection methods and efficient elimination strategies for P. aeruginosa. We synthesized durian-like Cu5Pd4Au NPs via a facile one-pot co-reduction strategy. Efficient electronic structure of Cu5Pd4Au NPs leads to balanced adsorption energy, endowing them with exceptional peroxidase-like activity (32.21 U/mg), which is 5.5-fold higher than that of Pd NPs. Leveraging the robust catalytic activity and high antibody-loading capacity, we constructed a multifunctional platform integrating immunoassays and antibacterial function. Combined with machine learning algorithms, the platform achieves rapid and sensitive discrimination of bacterial concentrations. Furthermore, Cu5Pd4Au NPs effectively eliminate multidrug-resistant bacteria and biofilms through synergistic reactive oxygen species generation and photothermal effects. This work not only provides a high-activity nanozyme but also establishes a new paradigm for designing multifunctional nanozymes.
10.1016/j.cej.2026.174690.title: Efficient electronic configuration and adsorption energy balance enabled by trimetallic nanozymes: Toward AI-powered visual identification of Pseudomonas aeruginosa

10.1016/j.cej.2026.174489.abstract: Fe-N-C single atom catalysts exhibits a promising potential in contaminant degradation processes due to the high activity, availability, and stability. However, the experience-based recognition covers little of the rapidly expanding research boundary, which has objectively limited the efficient field development for lacking the forward-looking opinions. A bibliometric approach was employed in this study to clarify the strategic development feature by analyzing 3195 publications related to single atom catalysts with 870 specifically on Fe-N-C structure collected, confirming the hotspot status of Fe-N-C single atom catalyst-mediated advanced oxidation processes. By precisely identifying key publication nodes within the citation network and systematically integrating the structural design-research method-application system knowledge maps, a comprehensive conceptual framework integrating the entire chain of ‘structure design-mechanism selection-targeting specific pollution control’ technology has been established, which highlights the emergence patterns of two breakthrough advancements: FeN5 coordination structure and PMS-free catalytic oxidation mechanism. Furthermore, in-situ soil remediation has been identified as an advanced application system (technological capabilities = 2.8, attention level = 40.57, market potential = 41.86). Based on the established frontier technology layout, an application mode coupling high-spin electroactive structure with low secondary risk release was designed, while key technical challenges such as precise structural optimization and scenario dependency were identified. This study provides a solid data-driven research map, and establishes a forward-looking technical decision guidance for Fe-N-C single atom catalyst-mediated targeted contaminant degradation applications.
10.1016/j.cej.2026.174489.title: Data-driven analysis on Fe-N-C single atom catalyst-based targeted contaminant degradation: hotspots and promising prospects

10.1016/j.cej.2026.174706.abstract: Additive manufacturing of high-performance filled rubber composites with industrially relevant mechanical and chemical performance remains a significant challenge, particularly at silica loadings required for stiffness, durability, and chemical resistance. This study presents a dual-curable waterborne latex-silica ink system that enables direct ink writing (DIW) of carboxylated styrene-butadiene rubber composites with up to 50 wt% silica, without compromising printability or final performance. The ink incorporates a photocurable N-vinylpyrrolidone/triethylene glycol divinyl ether interpenetrating network, which provides immediate green strength upon UV exposure, followed by a secondary ZnO-activated sulfur vulcanization step that constructs a robust polysulfidic network. Rheological characterization revealed tunable yield stress and shear-thinning behavior, which are suitable for extrusion across a wide composition range. To ensure consistent print fidelity across 30–50 wt% silica, a machine-learning-based adaptive viscous filament printing (ML-AVFP) framework was implemented;which uses experimentally determined rheological descriptors and filament-printing calibration data to automatically rewrite G-code with composition-specific Z-offset and print-speed profiles, thereby improving filament flattening and interlayer overlap, suppressing printing-induced porosity, and reducing final post-vulcanization shrinkage by ∼17–30% versus fixed-parameter DIW. The resulting dual-cured composites exhibited tensile strengths of up to 21 MPa, elongations approaching 800%, high toughness, low compression set from −40 to 100 °C, and excellent oil resistance. Functional components, such as gaskets, bellows, and brake diaphragms, were successfully printed withdense, pore-free microstructures and reliable performance under realistic mechanical and fluid-exposure conditions. This study establishes a scalable hybrid materials-process strategy for the digital manufacturing of industrially relevant elastomer parts via DIW.
10.1016/j.cej.2026.174706.title: Adaptive direct ink writing of dual-curable, silica-filled rubber latex composites via a hybrid physics-machine learning framework

10.1016/j.cej.2026.174909.abstract: To meet the demand for early identification and dynamic assessment of age-related hand function decline, an all-textile integrated piezoelectric sensor based on PVDF-TrFE/MWCNTs composite nanofibers is developed. Using commercial silver fabric electrodes and in-situ electrospun nanofiber membranes, the sensor enables passive, accurate grip strength monitoring. MWCNTs improve the dielectric properties and charge collection efficiency, and increase the piezoelectric β-phase content from 85.5% to 90.4%. The sensor shows high sensitivity (126.03 mV/N), a wide working range (0.1–6 N), and good stability over 16,000 cycles. Integrated with deep learning, the hand motion monitoring system achieves high-precision motion recognition (R2 = 96.51%). Grip strength, control stability, and finger coordination are quantitatively evaluated on 10 young and 11 elderly subjects. This work provides a wearable strategy for early warning and rehabilitation assessment of hand function decline in the elderly, facilitating the application of flexible electronics in aging-related health management.
10.1016/j.cej.2026.174909.title: All-textile piezoelectric sensors for machine learning-enabled wearable muscle strength assessment in older adults

10.1016/j.cej.2026.174748.abstract: Neural electrodes are critical components for recording and stimulating neural signals in neuroscience and clinical applications. Despite their widespread adoption in clinical practice, current technology continues to face limitations in signal sensitivity and biocompatibility. Herein, antibacterial neural electrodes functionalized with carbon dots (CDs) are developed, whose nanostructured surfaces and rich oxygen-containing functional groups facilitate rapid charge transfer and interfacial compatibility. The CDs electrodes reduced impedance by 64.6% compared to bare electrodes (160.14 ± 6.81 vs. 451.9 ± 13.9 MΩ·μm2) and enhanced cathodic charge storage capacity by 5.4-fold, while maintaining excellent interfacial stability. The CDs electrodes achieve 99.2% microbial inhibition within 1 h and mitigate oxidative stress through enzyme-mimicking decomposition of reactive oxygen species, thereby reducing implant-associated infection risk. In vivo neural recordings in rats revealed a 2.5-fold increase in oscillation amplitude and a 2.13-fold enhancement in signal-to-noise ratio, thereby validating the improvement in bioelectric sensitivity. This study developed a CDs-modified neural interface that combines anti-infection properties with enhanced bioelectric performance, offering a promising strategy to improve biosafety in the precise diagnosis and treatment of neurological disorders.
10.1016/j.cej.2026.174748.title: Bioactive carbon dots as antibacterial neural interface for neuron recording

10.1016/j.cej.2026.174764.abstract: Noble-metal nanoparticle (NP) decoration has emerged as an effective strategy to enhance the performance of gas sensors, yet the underlying principles governing selectivity tuning remain poorly understood. In this study, we decorated two-dimensional (2D) tungsten disulfide (WS2) flakes with noble-metal NPs using a solution-based process without reducing agents, leading to a dramatic shift in selectivity. The decorated WS2 flakes enabled clear discrimination among nitrogen dioxide (NO2), ammonia (NH3), and hydrogen (H2), with a level of selectivity rarely observed in conventional three-dimensional metal-oxide nanostructures. This distinctive behavior originates from the synergy between the layered, edge-enriched architecture of WS2 and the catalytic/electronic effects of the noble-metal NPs. By integrating machine learning algorithms, we further demonstrate robust analyte classification and predictive capability across multiple gases. We propose a selective sensing mechanism based on charge-transfer interactions between target gas molecules and the functionalized sensing surface, which underpins the observed discriminative response. Our findings provide fundamental insights into the design of next-generation sensor arrays based on 2D materials, offering a strategic pathway for superior gas selectivity.
10.1016/j.cej.2026.174764.title: Machine learning-enabled sensor array using noble metal–functionalized WS2 nanoflakes for drastic selective gas sensing

10.1016/j.cej.2026.175019.abstract: Volatile organic compounds (VOCs) pose significant risks to indoor air quality and industrial safety, underscoring the need for fast, selective, and low-power monitoring technologies. Here, we develop a flexible, room-temperature sensing platform based on printable poly(vinylidene fluoride) films incorporating chemically diverse ionic liquids. The tailored polymer–ionic liquid interactions enable selective detection of structurally similar VOCs -acetone, isopropanol, and ethanol - using nanoparticle-free inks compatible with scalable additive manufacturing. Custom-designed capacitive transducers enhance sensitivity and produce rapid, stable responses suitable for continuous operation. A four-sensor array integrated with a low-cost Arduino acquisition system achieves response times below 60 s and recovery times below 10 s without external heating. Machine-learning models applied to the cross-selective outputs reach 99.89% classification accuracy and enable quantitative prediction of acetone and isopropanol at concentrations below their IDLH thresholds, and ethanol at levels relevant to long-term exposure guidelines. This platform offers an energy-efficient and scalable solution for indoor air-quality assessment and industrial VOC surveillance.
10.1016/j.cej.2026.175019.title: Machine-learning-enabled cross-selective VOC sensing in ionic-liquid-based printed gas sensors

10.1016/j.cej.2026.175113.abstract: Paper-based lateral flow assays (LFIAs) have become a central platform for decentralized cancer diagnostics, offering rapid, low-cost testing that enables decentralized analysis. Over the past decade, substantial engineering advances have expanded the performance envelope of paper-supported tumor biomarker detection, driven primarily by the integration of functional nanomaterials with increasingly sophisticated device architectures. This review synthesizes these developments from a chemical engineering perspective, focusing on how surface-engineered nanomaterials (e.g., gold and magnetic nanoparticles, quantum dots) modulate mass transport, reaction kinetics, and signal transduction within porous cellulose matrices to enhance sensitivity and dynamic range. In parallel, smartphone-based optical readout systems, when integrated with machine learning algorithms, have proven effective in mitigating intrinsic signal variability and enabling objective, quantitative interpretation. Beyond analytical performance, we critically examine persistent engineering barriers to clinical translation, such as substrate heterogeneity, flow irreproducibility, reagent instability, and manufacturing scalability challenges. Accordingly, we outline a translational roadmap prioritizing robustness, standardization, and system-level design to accelerate the conversion of lab-on-paper prototypes into clinically deployable diagnostic tools.
10.1016/j.cej.2026.175113.title: Nanotech-enabled and AI-driven paper-based analytical devices (PADs) for cancer screening: From material engineering to intelligent diagnostics

10.1016/j.cej.2026.175302.abstract: Anaerobic ammonia oxidation (anammox) is a promising energy-efficient biological nitrogen removal technology, but its widespread application is constrained by slow bacterial growth, prolonged startup periods, and strict dependency on nitrite. This study systematically investigated the enhancement effects of applied voltage on biofilm-based anammox systems using big data analysis and machine learning (ML) approaches. Over 800 sets of literature data were collected and analyzed, revealing that nitrogen removal rate (NRR) increased 3.45-fold at optimal voltage (0.4–0.5 V) compared to non-voltage control. Four ML algorithms (Random Forest, Gradient Boosting Regression, eXtreme Gradient Boosting, and Categorical Boosting) were employed to develop predictive models for the NRR. The Categorical Boosting model exhibited superior performance, achieving R2 values of 0.974 and 0.852 for the training and testing sets, respectively. SHAP analysis identified applied voltage as the critical influencing factor, while partial dependence plots revealed its nonlinear regulatory effects and the synergistic interactions among multiple features. A 106-day continuous reactor experiment validated the model's effectiveness: at the predicted optimal voltage of 0.4 V, the system achieved an NRR of 720 mg N/(L·d) with a nitrogen removal efficiency of 87%. Notably, the system maintained stable performance even with a 24% reduction in influent nitrite concentration, alleviating the inherent nitrite dependency of anammox processes. Microbial community analysis revealed that anaerobic ammonium-oxidizing bacteria maintained 80% contribution ratio, significantly higher than other functional bacteria, confirming the strong activation effect of applied voltage. This study confirms the core role of ML in precise performance prediction and key parameter identification, providing data-driven support for the identification of optimal conditions, intelligent control, and scaled application of electrochemically enhanced anammox processes.
10.1016/j.cej.2026.175302.title: Electrochemically enhanced anaerobic ammonia oxidation: Performance prediction and mechanism elucidation based on big data and machine learning

10.1016/j.cej.2026.175043.abstract: Depression represents a major global public health concern, affecting hundreds of millions of individuals worldwide. The World Health Organization forecasts that, by 2030, depression will emerge as the primary driver of the global healthcare challenge. Consequently, the identification of biomarkers specific to anxiety (ANX), depression (DEP), and somatic symptom disorder (SSD) is crucial for early and accurate diagnosis and timely treatment. Here, we explicited a diagnosis model to screen the patients by a salivary biomarkers panel in the of a cohort consisting of healthy individuals and patients with ANX, DEP, and SSD, through a microfluidic chip. The detection results show that the expression levels of inflammatory cytokines were elevated in patients compared with healthy individuals. A four-biomarker panel was employed to train the machine learning (ML) model (M4D) based on the random forest (RF) algorithm for early and accurate differential diagnosis, which includes tumor necrosis factor-α (TNF-α), interleukin-8 (IL-8), interleukin-1β (IL-1β) and Interferon-gamma (IFN-γ). It can identify the specific type of mental disorder for an individual with AUC > 0.98, without invasive procedures. The diagnostic accuracy in the test set reached 92.22%. The proposed non-invasive diagnostic method presents promising applications in making precise diagnosis of mental disorders.
10.1016/j.cej.2026.175043.title: Exploration of salivary biomarkers for accurate diagnosis of anxiety, depression, and somatic symptom disorder by the integration of microfluidic chip and machine learning

10.1016/j.cej.2026.175401.abstract: Photocatalytic hydrogen production offers a sustainable solar-to‑hydrogen conversion route by splitting water under light irradiation. However, most systems remain confined to laboratory conditions because of limited efficiency, stability, and scalability. This review provides an overview of how materials design, system engineering, and data-driven tools can be integrated to advance photocatalytic hydrogen production toward practical deployment. Fundamental strategies for improving solar-to‑hydrogen efficiency are first summarized, focusing on band-structure modulation, charge-carrier dynamics, surface catalytic-site optimization, and stability enhancement. Representative photocatalyst families—including metal oxides, metal sulfides, MOFs, MXenes, and their heterostructures—are discussed in terms of how S-scheme and Z-scheme architectures, cocatalyst loading, facet control, and defect engineering collectively govern light absorption, charge separation, and reaction kinetics. Beyond powder suspensions, approaches such as photothermal catalysis, photoelectrocatalysis, magnetic-field-assisted photocatalysis, and photobiocatalytic systems that couple biological components with inorganic photocatalysts are highlighted. Emphasis is placed on the role of artificial intelligence in accelerating materials discovery, elucidating structure–property–performance relationships, and guiding reactor and process optimization. By linking mechanistic insights with system-level design and using quantitative performance indicators such as AQE and STH, this review outlines a framework for developing efficient, durable, and scalable photocatalytic hydrogen production technologies suitable for real-world deployment.
10.1016/j.cej.2026.175401.title: Photocatalytic hydrogen production: Materials design, system engineering, and data-driven advances

10.1016/j.cej.2026.175466.abstract: Flexible hydrogel sensors that are strong, multimodal, and recyclable are highly desirable for wearable electronics but remain difficult to realize because conventional conductive gels are mechanically isotropic, single responsive, and structurally fragile. Here, we report a loofah-inspired recyclable MXene/polypyrrole (PPy) fiber-skeleton hydrogel (PBMA) constructed from PPy, bacterial cellulose (BC) fibers, a poly(vinyl alcohol) (PVA)/tannic acid (TA) matrix, and well-dispersed Ti₃C₂Tₓ MXene, in which directional freeze-thaw processing generated an aligned loofah-like porous architecture with anisotropic mechanical and conductive pathways. The resulting hydrogel simultaneously achieves high tensile strength (~1.8 MPa), large toughness (~6 MJ·m−3), and stretchability up to ~250%, while exhibiting low hysteresis and durable piezoresistive response over 5000 loading–unloading cycles. PBMA functions as a multimodal strain–humidity sensor with a gauge factor (GF) up to 4.66, fast electromechanical response/recovery (~160 ms), and humidity sensitivity over 10–80% RH with ~10 s response time. Benefiting from strong adhesion, antibacterial activity, and thermal reprocessability that retained over 90% of its original sensing performance, PBMA enables long-term conformal monitoring of physiological motions, respiration and ambient humidity, Morse-code communication, object-diameter and spatial pressure mapping, and machine-learning-assisted gesture recognition with 99.75% accuracy. This loofah-inspired fiber-skeleton design provides a sustainable route to high-performance, recyclable hydrogel electronic skins.
10.1016/j.cej.2026.175466.title: Loofah-inspired recyclable MXene/polypyrrole fiber-skeleton hydrogels for machine-learning-assisted multimodal flexible sensor

10.1016/j.cej.2026.175467.abstract: Biomass gasification remains a key pathway for clean fuel production; however, conventional fluidized-bed reactors continue to suffer from limited carbon conversion and persistent tar formation, constraining system efficiency and industrial adoption. This study introduces a novel three-stage fluidized-bed gasifier—integrating controlled devolatilization, high-temperature steam/air reforming, and char gasification—to simultaneously enhance syngas quality and suppress tar generation. A kinetics-based Aspen Plus model was developed and rigorously validated against experimental data. To capture multivariate interactions across operating conditions, Design of Experiments (DOE) and Response Surface Methodology (RSM) were coupled with Support Vector Regression (SVR), significantly outperforming classical regression in predictive accuracy. Multi-objective optimization using NSGA-II identified Pareto-optimal trade-offs among cold gas efficiency (CGE), carbon conversion efficiency (CCE), and tar yield. Results demonstrate that increasing the reformer temperature from 1050 to 1200 °C elevates CGE from 82% to 92% and boosts CCE from 88% to 97%, while reducing tar yield from 4 to 0.3%. The optimized operating window yields hydrogen-rich syngas (up to 27% H₂) with an LHV of 7.75 MJ/Nm3, alongside near-complete carbon conversion and minimal tar yield (<0.1%). Overall, the proposed three-stage configuration—supported by advanced kinetic modeling and machine-learning-assisted optimization—establishes a robust platform for high-efficiency, low-tar biomass-to‑hydrogen conversion, offering strong potential for deployment in next-generation renewable energy and low-carbon fuel systems.
10.1016/j.cej.2026.175467.title: Kinetic modeling and machine-learning optimization of a novel three-stage fluidized-bed gasifier for hydrogen-rich and low-tar syngas production

10.1016/j.cej.2026.175418.abstract: Human skin interprets physical contact by jointly sensing surface deformation and multidimensional forces, a dual-vector capability that underpins dexterous interaction. However, existing robotic tactile sensors fundamentally lack this dual-vector perception, failing to capture simultaneously both tangential forces and deformation fields. Prompted by this gap, we present a bioinspired electronic skin (e-skin) for the high-precision perception of tangential forces and deformation fields. Inspired by the mechano-transduction pathway of Ruffini corpuscles, the e-skin features an orthogonal hydrogel grid architecture to mimic this transduction mechanism. We further employ a cascaded deep regression framework to reverse-engineer this transduction, forming a “sensing” and “perception” integrated paradigm. Crucially, this biomimetic e-skin first reconstructs deformation vectors (ΔX, ΔY) with high fidelity (MAE < 0. 5423 mm, R2 > 0.9955) over a ± 20 mm range, then infers tangential forces (Fx, Fy) from the estimated deformations with remarkable accuracy (MAE < 0.247 N, R2 > 0.9931) within ± 7.5 N. Validated through deformation field reconstruction and human-robot interaction, this system is capable of perceiving nuanced physical interactions, enabling a robot to interpret interaction intentions.
10.1016/j.cej.2026.175418.title: A bioinspired electronic skin with orthogonal hydrogel and cascaded deep learning for decoupling tangential force and deformation mapping
10.1016/j.cej.2026.175418.source: ScienceDirect official citation and abstract BibTeX export

10.1016/j.cej.2026.175529.abstract: Effective passivation of interface defect is vital for improving perovskite solar cell (PSC) performance. Traditional trial-and-error methods to identify passivators represent slow, costly, and dependent on expert input, limiting thorough exploration of potential candidates. This study introduces an automated platform, “MatInsight”, to extract key PSC parameters from literature, creating a dataset for training seven machine learning (ML) models. The categorical boosting (CatBoost) model excelled as the top predictor, identifying influential molecular descriptors—dihedral angle (Phi), topological complexity (BertzCT), molar refractivity (MolMR), and minimum absolute EState index (MinAbsEStateIndex)—for optimizing power conversion efficiency (PCE). We predicted passivation efficacy within a molecular library, followed by experimental validation. Notably, PSCs using 3-fluoro-4-aminobenzonitrile (FABN) demonstrated superior defect passivation, achieving a PCE of 25.7% and maintaining 84% efficiency over 1400 h in ambient conditions. This scalable approach offers a robust framework for rapidly identifying effective passivators, significantly advancing the development of stable, high-efficiency PSCs.
10.1016/j.cej.2026.175529.title: Data-driven discovery of high-performance surface passivators for efficient and stable perovskite solar cells

10.1016/j.cej.2026.175515.abstract: Industrial development and urban expansion exert considerable ecological pressure due to organic wastewater discharge, necessitating fast, real-time water-quality monitoring to oversee treatment processes and warn against unsafe discharge. In this study, a miniaturized electrochemical (EC) detector and artificial intelligence (AI)-based real-time water quality analysis software were developed to monitor organic components, concentrations, and chemical oxygen demand (COD) in wastewater. A nitrogen-etched boron-doped diamond (NBDD) sensing electrode, with a surface composed of relatively intact (100) diamond planes and graphene-covered nanocrystals, was employed. This electrode demonstrated high responsiveness, electrocatalytic activity, and long-term stability toward all six dyes (carmine, methylene blue, methylene green, basic fuchsin, rhodamine B, and indigo). The AI software employed principal component analysis (PCA) for dimensionality reduction; support vector machine (SVM) for dye classification; and a fusion algorithm (iterative reweighted least squares (IRLS)/multilayer perceptron (MLP)/gradient boosting machine (GBM)) for predicting COD and concentration. It achieved dye identification accuracies ranging from 82.7% to 100%. The NBDD-EC detector combined with the AI analysis system achieved high correlations between the predicted and actual values of dye concentration and COD. When deployed industrially, it predicted dye wastewater COD with 96 ± 2% accuracy, providing a reliable hardware-software solution for real-time monitoring, crucial for discharge oversight.
10.1016/j.cej.2026.175515.title: Machine learning-driven COD real-time monitoring electrochemical analysis system based on nitrogen-etched boron-doped diamond electrode

10.1016/j.cej.2026.175565.abstract: This work develops a microkinetic-surrogate-based dynamic optimization framework for identifying coke-aware operating strategies in dry reforming of methane. A neural quasi-steady-state model (NQSSM) is introduced in which the fast-reacting species are predicted using an artificial neural network, while coke coverage is retained as an ordinary differential equation(ODE) state. This structure enables transient system prediction at a fraction of the computational cost of the full microkinetic model, thereby allowing dynamic optimization that accounts for catalyst deactivation. Bayesian optimization is integrated with the NQSSM to efficiently determine dynamic operating schedules that maximize performance. Dynamic optimization under multiple coke constraints on reactor coke coverage reveals a clear trade-off between syngas production and coke accumulation. This trade-off is quantified by a weighted syngas performance index (WSPI), which is introduced in this research to reflect the productivity of H2 and CO and the consumption of CH4 and CO2 over time. With tighter constraints, the optimal operating regime shifts toward more oxidation-favoring conditions. This shift manifests systematically in the optimal profiles, including decreasing temperature, increasing pressure, and reduced early-stage flow rate. The NQSSM accurately captures these time-dependent strategic adjustments while preserving mechanistic interpretability. Overall, the proposed framework provides a mechanistically grounded and computationally efficient approach for designing degradation-aware operating strategies and can be readily extended to other reaction systems in which dynamic behavior and catalyst deactivation are closely coupled.
10.1016/j.cej.2026.175565.title: Dynamic optimization of coke formation in dry reforming of methane using a neural quasi-steady-state model

10.1016/j.cej.2026.175613.abstract: Electronic skins play a crucial role in health monitoring, human motion detection, and soft robotics. Nevertheless, achieving an integrated dual-mode electronic skin using compatible and simplified processes while reducing crosstalk between different sensing signals remains a significant challenge. This study developed dual-mode electronic skin using selective electrospinning deposition of functional layers for pressure and temperature sensing. The electronic skin consists of two parts: a top layer based on electrospun polyvinylidene fluoride-trifluoroethylene (PVDF-TrFE) nanofibers sandwiched between interlocked mortise-tenon structured electrodes for pressure sensing; and a bottom layer based on PVDF-TrFE and silver nanowires (AgNWs) for temperature sensing. The mortise-tenon structured electrode design and selective-deposition electrospun nanofiber significantly enhances the piezoelectric response. Each layer is process-compatible and specific structures are set up according to the different signals collected, thus achieving excellent sensing performance. The electronic skin utilizes two different sensing mechanisms with dual-parameter decoupling method, which successfully eliminate cross-sensitivity interference between temperature and pressure. The system inherently corrects for the temperature coefficient of the pressure signal, yielding higher accuracy than single-parameter sensors. Furthermore, an intelligent decoupling optimization algorithm via machine-learning is introduced to enable high-precision decoupling pressure and temperature stimuli to identify different materials like human perception of touch.
10.1016/j.cej.2026.175613.title: Crosstalk-free dual-mode electronic skin enabled by selective electrospinning and machine learning-based decoupling

10.1016/j.cej.2026.175632.abstract: Developing conductive hydrogel with tissue-like mechanical properties and excellent electrical properties is crucial for stable and high-performance neural interface. Herein, we copolymerized hydrophilic monomer acrylic acid (AA) and zwitterionic monomer 3-[1-(4-vinylbenzyl)-1H-imidazol-3-ium-3-yl] propane-1-sulfonate (VBIPS) in Poly(3,4-ethylenedioxythiophene):poly(styrenesulfonate) (PEDOT:PSS) to form semi-interpenetrating double-network conductive hydrogel (CH). The flexible network obtained by zwitterionic monomer provided the hydrogel with tissue-like softness (Young's modulus: ∼21 kPa) and excellent mechanical properties (tensile strain: ∼210% and fracture toughness: ∼902 J·m−2), establishing a mechanically stable and durable hydrogel interface. Due to the electrostatic shielding provided by zwitterionic network, PEDOT:PSS nanoparticle in-situ phase separated and form a conductive network that exhibited high conductivity (∼20 S·cm−1), high charge injection capability (∼248 μC·cm−2), and high charge storage capability (∼25 mC·cm−2). After being attached to Pt electrode, the hydrogel interface greatly decreased its impedance to PBS and forms stable and precise communication between nerves and electrode. After implanting the hydrogel electrode into the sciatic nerve of a rat model, knee-jerk reflection was achieved under low potential and showed long-term stability. The hydrogel interface served as good bridge between nerve and machine, providing an effective strategy for the flexible hydrogel bioelectronics.
10.1016/j.cej.2026.175632.title: Zwitterion-enhanced highly conductive hydrogel with tissue-like modulus and mechanical robustness for stable peripheral neural interface

10.1016/j.cej.2026.175516.abstract: Efficient and cost-effective utilization of biomass is crucial for mitigating energy and environmental pressures. This study proposes a new biomass polygeneration system integrating chemical looping carbon dioxide displacement of nitrogen (CLCDN) for simultaneous electricity and fuel gas production. In the proposed system, high-temperature O2 and CO2 mixtures produced by the CLCDN process are used as the gasifying agent, and externally concentrated solar energy supplies the heat required for gasification. A neural network-based multi-objective optimization model is developed to improve exergy and exergoeconomic performance, and enhance syngas quality. The model development involves two stages. First, Bayesian optimization is employed to determine the optimal hyperparameters of a multilayer perceptron (MLP). Then, multi-objective optimization is conducted using the trained MLP model. Under optimal hyperparameters, the MLP achieves a coefficient of determination of 0.99. The optimization results indicate that the proposed system achieves optimal performance at a CLCDN reaction temperature of 841.34 °C, a CO2 to biomass mass flow ratio of 0.44, and a gasification temperature of 1016.14 °C. Compared with the reference system, the exergy efficiency (74.09%) and effective carbon efficiency (99.49%) increase by 2.19% and 33.17%, respectively. Meanwhile, the CO2 mass flow rate in syngas decreases by 2.514 ton/h, while the unit exergy cost of total products (0.019 $/kWh) increases by 5.56%. Overall, the proposed system enables efficient biomass gasification and improves syngas quality. The developed optimization framework provides a theoretical basis for system design and performance improvement.
10.1016/j.cej.2026.175516.title: Neural network-based multi-objective optimization of a biomass polygeneration system with chemical looping carbon dioxide displacement of nitrogen

10.1016/j.cej.2026.175796.abstract: Organic photovoltaics (OPVs) are a leading renewable energy technology, yet the discovery of high-performance non-fullerene acceptors (NFAs) is often hindered by the vastness of chemical space and the synthetic costs of complex fused-ring systems. In this study, we develop a robust, physics-informed graph deep learning framework based on a directed message passing neural network (D-MPNN) to accelerate the predictive identification of high-potential OPVs. By representing molecules as fragment-level graphs enriched with computable descriptors—including DFT-derived frontier orbital energies and molecular mechanics-calculated structural parameters—our model achieves excellent predictive accuracy, yielding a Pearson correlation coefficient (r) of 0.93 and a mean absolute error (MAE) of 0.89% under 10-fold cross-validation. The model's capability was rigorously validated through a temporal “blind” test of 42 newly reported NFA ternary OPV devices (published after model training), where it maintained a high predictive accuracy (MAE = 1.17%) even for systems containing novel molecular fragments. Leveraging this framework, we performed high-throughput virtual screening (HTVS) of approximately 334 million ternary combinations, identifying 4904 novel systems with predicted power conversion efficiencies (PCEs) surpassing the training dataset ceiling of 19.36%. Furthermore, fragment-level Z-score analyses identified key structural motifs, such as specific non-fused rigid cores and the benefit of “No-p-spacer” architecture, providing actionable design rules for experimental development. This accurate and expandable framework offers a powerful platform for the predictive identification of high-potential ternary OPVs.
10.1016/j.cej.2026.175796.title: Accurate and expandable graph deep learning for accelerating predictive identification of high-potential organic photovoltaics

10.1016/j.cej.2026.175749.abstract: A unitized regenerative fuel cell (URFC) integrates electrolytic cell (EC) and fuel cell (FC) function, enabling unified energy storage and conversion. However, performance, durability, and precious metal cost constrain each other and hinder system-level efficiency gains and scale-up. Focusing on dual functional catalysts, a multiscale mechanistic framework based on an agglomerate model is established. At the microscale, agglomerate parameters governing reaction diffusion and oxygen transport resistances are quantified. At the macroscale, porous-media transport is coupled to achieve end to end modeling and parameter unification from the catalyst layer to the channel. In the FC mode, the rate limiting mechanism shifts from kinetics to local oxygen transport as current density increases. This yields a performance gain of approximately 42.9% relative to the comparison solution. In the EC mode, the mid-to-high current region remains kinetics-dominated. Increasing Ir content elevates the reaction exchange current density, thereby lowering the kinetic overpotential for oxygen evolution reaction. To balance performance, durability, and cost, a unified metric is adopted. The optimization results of the bifunctional catalyst are mainly rich in Pt. Compared with the comparison solution, the balanced and optimal solutions deliver superior performance and durability while reducing precious group metal cost by about 43.94%. This framework provides quantitative guidance and practical cues for the design of URFC bifunctional catalysts and the optimization of precious metal utilization.
10.1016/j.cej.2026.175749.title: Mass transport mechanisms and efficient precious metal utilization in URFCs via agglomerate model and data driven analysis

10.1016/j.cej.2026.176019.abstract: Antioxidants play a critical role in sustaining physiological balance, making the rapid and accurate identification of multiple antioxidants essential for disease diagnosis and analysis. Conventional single-mode sensing arrays often suffer from inefficiency and inconsistency. Addressing this challenge, we engineered Cu-doped Co3O4 nanozymes (Cu-Co3O4) with tunable doping ratios using a self-templating approach. By integrating the optimized Cu-Co3O4 nanozyme with near-infrared (NIR) irradiation, we developed a dual-mode sensing platform that combines colorimetric and photothermal signals for high-throughput, precise antioxidant detection. Under NIR exposure, Cu-Co3O4 demonstrates significantly enhanced catalytic oxidation of TMB, driven by synergistic non-radiative relaxation and redox reactions of photogenerated carriers, amplifying both chromogenic and photothermal responses. Leveraging the distinct reducing capacities of various antioxidants on oxidized TMB (oxTMB), our sensing array—combined with machine learning—effectively processes unique response patterns. Linear discriminant analysis enabled the discrimination and quantification of key antioxidants, including ascorbic acid, dopamine, uric acid, glutathione, and melatonin, while hierarchical clustering and random forest algorithms validated methodological accuracy. Notably, the random forest model successfully predicted component concentrations in binary antioxidant mixtures. This study not only advances the strategic modulation of enzyme-like activity and photothermal properties in transition metal oxides but also establishes a robust framework for high-throughput target analysis in complex matrixes.
10.1016/j.cej.2026.176019.title: Machine learning-assisted dual-mode sensing array: NIR-enhanced Cu-Co3O4 nanozymes for high-throughput antioxidant discrimination
10.1016/j.cej.2026.176019.source: ScienceDirect official citation and abstract BibTeX export

10.1016/j.cej.2026.175906.abstract: Abiotic stresses, particularly heavy metal contamination, induce excessive reactive oxygen species (ROS) in plants, causing oxidative damage and severe crop yield losses. Structurally defined chitobioses are promising natural antioxidants hold great promise as biostimulants to enhance plant stress tolerance in sustainable agriculture. However, their green, cost-effective synthesis remains a bottleneck. Here, we employed an artificial intelligence (AI)-driven structure-based enzyme mining strategy to identify a thermostable, highly specific endochitinase (CT10) from Paenibacillus elgii, which efficiently hydrolyzes low-cost colloidal crustacean chitin into N, N′-Diacetylchitobiose (GlcNAcβ1-4GlcNAc, AA) with minimal byproducts. Coupling CT10 with regioselective chitin deacetylases (VcCDA/NodB) in one-pot cascade reaction yielded three additional structurally defined chitobioses: GlcNAcβ1-4GlcN (AD), GlcNβ1-4GlcNAc (DA), and GlcNβ1-4GlcN (DD), all with >95% purity. Among these, DA exhibits superior hydroxyl radical (OH•) scavenging activity comparable to l-ascorbic acid. Exogenous application of the four chitobioses alleviated cadmium (Cd) stress in rice (Oryza sativa L.), restoring growth, reducing ROS/MDA accumulation, and upregulating antioxidant enzyme genes (sod, pod, cat). Notably, DA showed the most potent efficacy in promoting root biomass recovery and activating antioxidant defense pathways. This study establishes a scalable, green platform for the synthesis of structurally defined chitobioses and delineates their structure-specific roles in alleviating heavy metal toxicity, providing a nature-based strategy to improve crop resilience in abiotic stress-affected agricultural systems.
10.1016/j.cej.2026.175906.title: AI-guided discovery of an efficient chitinase enables green production of chitobioses with distinct cadmium stress-alleviating efficacy in rice
10.1016/j.cej.2026.175906.source: ScienceDirect official citation and abstract BibTeX export

10.1016/j.cej.2026.175738.abstract: Spinal cord injury (SCI) elicits complex post-traumatic microenvironmental perturbations, where sustained inflammatory milieu and compromised neural repair capacity represent two pivotal hurdles impeding clinical therapeutic efficacy. Exosomes derived from M2 macrophages, as cell-free nanocarriers, mediate intercellular signaling crosstalk and biomolecular shuttling, exerting prominent anti-inflammatory and pro-regenerative activities in preclinical SCI models. However, the clinical translation of exosome-based therapies is severely bottlenecked by the paucity of technologies enabling precise sustained release and prolonged bioefficacy of exosomes at the injury site. To tackle these critical challenges-including uncontrollable inflammation regulation time windows, short therapeutic duration, and monofunctional treatment modalities—we engineered a dual-network crosslinked hydrogel using polyvinyl alcohol (PVA) as the flexible backbone and TSPBA as the crosslinker. This injectable hydrogel possesses tunable mechanical properties, robust self-healing capability, and in-situ gelation competence, facilitating seamless conformity with the irregular cavities induced by SCI. Notably, the reactive oxygen species (ROS)-responsive borate ester linkages within the hydrogel trigger spatiotemporally controlled degradation in the high-ROS microenvironment of SCI lesions, enabling on-demand exosome release without exogenous stimuli. The resultant PVA-TSPBA/exosomes composite system serves as a multifunctional therapeutic platform integrating structural support, targeted delivery, and inflammation modulation. In vivo evaluations confirmed that this composite system significantly suppressed M1 macrophage polarization and A1 astrocyte activation, enhanced neural regeneration, and ameliorated motor function and neuroelectrophysiological activities in SCI mice. Collectively, the multifunctional PVA-TSPBA/exosomes composite hydrogel holds substantial promise for clinical translation in SCI repair, providing a novel therapeutic strategy for mitigating secondary injury and promoting neural recovery.
10.1016/j.cej.2026.175738.title: Microenvironment-responsive exosomes-hydrogel hybrid system for inflammation modulation and neural regeneration after spinal cord injury
