10.1016/j.cej.2026.176165.abstract: Early and accurate cancer classification based on circulating tumor cells (CTCs) is limited by inefficient enrichment, release-induced perturbation, and the lack of integrated strategies for cell-resolved multimodal biomarker analysis, particularly for aggressive subtypes such as triple-negative breast cancer (TN-BC). Herein, we report a unified engineering platform based on polyvalent dual-aptamer (PDApt)-DNA hydrogel that enables selective CTC encapsulation and sequential in situ quantification of membrane-bound and intracellular biomarkers without cell release or lysis. The PDApt-DNA hydrogel is constructed from two rolling-circle-amplified strands bearing polyvalent aptamers, enabling efficient and broad-spectrum CTC capture. Surface-enhanced Raman scattering/fluorescence (SERS/FL) nanoprobes are programmably organized within the three-dimensional (3D) hydrogel network via DNA hybridization, allowing in situ detection of epithelial cell adhesion molecule (EpCAM) on the cell membrane by SERS and intracellular microRNA-21 (miRNA-21) by FL. The 3D encapsulation increases z-axis electromagnetic hot-spot density, thereby enhancing SERS performance while preserving cellular viability. A two-step linear discriminant analysis (LDA) framework is further established by integrating three CTC-associated features, namely CTC count, membrane-bound EpCAM expression, and intracellular miRNA-21 expression, to enable cancer discrimination in the first step and subtype stratification in the second step. In a cohort of 31 participants, the platform enables effective separation between cancer and healthy samples and clear identification of TN-BC (100% sensitivity and 100% specificity). Overall, this work establishes a non-release, multimodal CTC engineering strategy that couples gentle enrichment of CTCs with in situ biomarkers quantification, providing a generalizable framework for CTC-based precision diagnostics and clinical stratification.
10.1016/j.cej.2026.176165.title: Machine-learning-assisted cancer detection and classification based on selective CTC capture and sequential in situ biomarkers quantification by polyvalent dual-aptamer DNA hydrogel
10.1016/j.cej.2026.176165.source: ScienceDirect official citation and abstract BibTeX export

10.1016/j.cej.2026.176120.abstract: (2S,3R)-p-methylsulfonylphenyl serine ethyl ester [(2S,3R)-p-MPSE], a key chiral building block of the aryl β-hydroxy-α-amino ester family, serves as one of the critical intermediates for the synthesis of the veterinary antibiotic florfenicol. Kinetic resolution of rac-threo-p-MPSE by lipases represents a highly promising route. However, low catalytic efficiency of natural enzymes restricted its application. In this study, a lipase BSL from Bacillus subtilis was mined and rational design was performed to obtain a series of mutants. A robust Partial Least Squares (PLS) regression model, integrated with multi-dimensional encoding from the Amino Acid Index Database (AAindex) and Fast Fourier Transform (FFT)-based data processing technology, was constructed and trained. Using this machine learning (ML)-driven enzyme engineering approach, a mutant E115F/L67D/I421Q/P317I was successfully created, showing a 15.4-fold increase in catalytic efficiency (kcat/Km). Under the load of 1 M high substrate concentration, this mutant could achieve complete resolution of rac-threo-p-MPSE within 4 h, yielding optically pure (2S,3R)-p-MPSE (e.e.s > 99%) with a yield of 97.4% (based on the theoretical amount of single enantiomer). Additionally, the inactive isomer (2R,3S)-p-methylsulfonylphenyl serine [(2R,3S)-p-MPS] was recycled via chemical racemization based on a reversible retro-aldol cleavage mechanism and re-esterification, which facilitated the recycling of the substrate. This study not only breaks through the bottleneck of low catalytic efficiency of natural lipases through a machine learning-mediated precise enzyme engineering strategy, but also establishes a high-benefit chiral preparation process for (2S,3R)-p-MPSE via an enzymatic resolution-chemical racemization coupling system.
10.1016/j.cej.2026.176120.title: Machine learning-driven lipase engineering for highly enantioselective synthesis of chiral florfenicol intermediate via enzymatic resolution-chemical racemization coupling system
10.1016/j.cej.2026.176120.source: ScienceDirect official citation and abstract BibTeX export

10.1016/j.cej.2026.176113.abstract: Polyimides (PIs) are indispensable high-performance polymers for advanced flexible electronics, owing to their remarkable thermal stability, mechanical strength, and optical properties. To accelerate the design of colorless, transparent, and thermally stable PIs, this work introduces a machine learning (ML)-driven inverse design framework. By integrating molecular fingerprinting with ML models, we first developed accurate quantitative structure-property relationship (QSAR) models. Gradient Boosting (GB) model with RDKit fingerprints was identified as the optimal predictor (R2 > 0.94) for optical absorption (λmax), charge transfer (CTe), and thermal decomposition temperature (Td5). SHAP interpretability analysis further elucidated the roles of key substructures such as flexible ether linkers, fluorinated groups and conjugated structure. Guided by polycondensation chemistry, PIs disassembled into dianhydride (A) and diamine (B) building units and combinatorially expanded through flexible ether linkages (O) to create a virtual library consisting of 1530 AB-type and 175,664 ABOC-ype hypothetical monomers. High-throughput screening under stringent criteria (λmax < 400 nm, CTe < 0.2 e, Td5 > 530 °C) using a multi-task learning sparse encoder (MTL-SE) model successfully identified top candidates, including the outstanding h-BPDA-162 and 287 high-performance h-ABOC-type PI monomers. This work provides a scalable computational framework and specific structural guidelines as leads for the rational design and synthesis of advanced PI materials.
10.1016/j.cej.2026.176113.title: Machine learning-assisted property prediction and virtual screening of polyimides for flexible electronic applications
10.1016/j.cej.2026.176113.source: ScienceDirect official citation and abstract BibTeX export

10.1016/j.cej.2026.176193.abstract: Direct interspecies electron transfer (DIET) simulation has emerged as an effective strategy to enhance methane production in anaerobic digestion (AD). However, reliable prediction and interpretation of DIET-AD performance remain challenging due to nonlinearity and limited experimental datasets. In this study, we propose an integrated, synthetic data-assisted machine learning (ML) framework to predict methane enhancement in magnetite-mediated DIET-AD systems, combining data augmentation, robust modeling, and experimental validation. The synthetic dataset was generated by generative adversarial network (GAN), which was rigorously validated from statistical, principal component, clustering analysis, and Kolmogorov–Smirov test to ensure consistency with original experimental data. Multiple ML models, including ensemble-based, neural network-based, and attention- based algorithms, were systematically evaluated. Among them, an attention-based algorithm showed superior performance and robustness, achieving an average coefficient of determination (R2) of 0.92, root mean squared error (RMSE) of 6.30, and mean absolute error (MAE) of 4.04 on test data. Explainable artificial intelligence analysis using SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) indicated that substrate concentration and magnetite dosage were dominant drivers of methane enhancement. Experimental biomethane potential (BMP) tests further confirmed model reliability, with observed enhancements of 5.1% and 15.8% falling within the predicted 95% confidence intervals of 3.5–6.6% and 15.6–21.3%, respectively. Therefore, this framework contributes to practical insight into a transferable strategy for robust prediction, interpretation, and experimental guidance of nonlinear bioprocesses under data-scarce conditions.
10.1016/j.cej.2026.176193.title: Synthetic data-driven prediction and interpretation of biomethane production in direct interspecies electron transfer-stimulated anaerobic digestion process
10.1016/j.cej.2026.176193.source: ScienceDirect official citation and abstract BibTeX export

10.1016/j.cej.2026.176278.abstract: A portable hydrogel-based colorimetric sensing material integrated with machine learning analysis has been developed for the simultaneous on-site sensing of five toxic heavy metal ions (Cd2+, Pb2+, Hg2+, Cr6+, As3+). This capability stems from atomically designed hydrogels that enable visual recognition of metal ions through coordination differences. Notably, coordination-isomerism-driven differential recognition enables the simultaneous detection of these five ions. Three hydrogel sensing units (HP1, HP2, HP3) are synthesized via Ba2+ coordination of sodium alginate (SA) backbone molecule (Pr2) with response molecules (Pr4, Pr6, Pr8) featuring thiocyanate (–S–C≡N) and isothiocyanate (–N=C=S) groups. These units are spatially arranged in a 3D-printed device. The dominant coordination sites are S atoms in HP1 and HP3, whereas the dominant coordination site in HP2 is the N atom. Smartphone-captured RGB signals are converted into Euclidean distance (d-value) and processed using the machine-learning technique of linear discriminant analysis (LDA), achieving multiplex quantification with detection limits of 3.76 nM (Cd2+), 6.33 nM (Pb2+), 4.19 nM (Hg2+), 7.84 nM (Cr6+), and 6.42 nM (As3+) across a linear range of 0.01 to 5 μM for all five heavy metal ions. The platform demonstrates exceptional specificity against interferents and robust discrimination for binary to quinary heavy metal mixtures. This integration of rationally designed hydrogel probes, a 3D-printed device, and machine learning technology establishes a sensitive, accurate, and low-cost strategy for POCT (point-of-care testing) of multiple coexisting toxic heavy metal ions in environmental and food safety applications.
10.1016/j.cej.2026.176278.title: S/N induced coordination isomerism hydrogels on 3D-printed device for machine learning-assisted multiplex detection of heavy metal ions
10.1016/j.cej.2026.176278.source: ScienceDirect official citation and abstract BibTeX export

10.1016/j.cej.2026.176276.abstract: Wearable hydrogel sensors often suffer from poor environmental stability and mechanical mismatch under temperature fluctuations, leading to signal drift and unreliable performance in real-world applications. To overcome these limitations, we developed a skin-inspired multifunctional hydrogel based on a green deep eutectic solvent (DES) system reinforced with cellulose nanofibrils (CNFs). The hydrogel was fabricated via UV-initiated polymerization of polyacrylamide (PAM) and gelatin methacryloyl (GelMA), with phytic acid and CNFs forming a dynamically cross-linked network through covalent, hydrogen-bonding, and ionic interactions. The incorporation of DES provides stable ionic conductivity and enhanced environmental tolerance, while CNF reinforcement significantly improves mechanical robustness. As a result, the PDGCP hydrogel exhibits high tensile strength (0.65 MPa), large stretchability (1862%), and stable sensing performance over thousands of cycles. The hydrogel also exhibits antibacterial activity and excellent biocompatibility. As a wearable strain sensor, it achieves a wide sensing range (up to 1200%) and enables reliable monitoring of human motion as well as high-fidelity ECG and EMG signals. In addition, the hydrogel can function as a smart window component with bidirectional temperature responsiveness. By integrating machine learning algorithms, the system enables real-time recognition of complex ice-skating motion postures with an accuracy of 98.25%. This work highlights a sustainable DES-based hydrogel platform with enhanced mechanical stability and environmental adaptability, offering promising applications in wearable electronics, intelligent sports monitoring, and adaptive building systems.
10.1016/j.cej.2026.176276.title: Nanocellulose-reinforced deep eutectic solvent-based smart hydrogel sensor for adaptive window regulation and machine learning-assisted low-temperature motion monitoring
10.1016/j.cej.2026.176276.source: ScienceDirect official citation and abstract BibTeX export

10.1016/j.cej.2026.176333.abstract: Single-crystal Ni-rich cathodes possess a monolithic structure that effectively suppresses the formation of microcracks, even under repeated volumetric changes during charge–discharge cycling. However, these single-crystal cathodes often exhibit slow Li-ion diffusion kinetics and poor rate capability, primarily due to the long diffusion pathways within the micron-sized particles. In this study, we introduce a simple and scalable one-pot method for applying an expanded-graphite (EG) surface coating to single-crystal Ni-rich cathodes. EG forms a uniform and conductive carbon layer through ball milling after surface activation with 3-aminopropyltriethoxysilane. This conductive coating significantly enhances the electrical conductivity of the cathode and effectively suppresses electrolyte-induced side reactions, thereby improving cycling stability while maintaining compatibility with existing industrial regeneration processes. A data-driven optimization approach based on Gaussian-process-based Bayesian optimization was employed to determine the optimal EG loading for maximizing electrochemical performance. The method is further demonstrated at kilogram scale, highlighting its feasibility for large-scale manufacturing. Overall, this work presents a practical approach for producing high-performance single-crystal Ni-rich cathodes and provides a promising route toward commercially viable cathode regeneration beyond laboratory-scale studies.
10.1016/j.cej.2026.176333.title: Scalable expanded-graphite coating for high-performance single-crystal Ni-rich cathodes with data-driven optimization
10.1016/j.cej.2026.176333.source: ScienceDirect official citation and abstract BibTeX export

10.1016/j.cej.2026.176384.abstract: This study proposes a hybrid approach that integrates a black-box model with an equation-based mechanism verification model to identify the causative reactants of side reactions occurring in hydrogenation reaction systems and to derive their mechanisms. Due to the complex reaction network inherent in hydrogenation systems, exhaustive exploration and prediction of all side reactions are practically difficult, and such predictive uncertainty can lead to deterioration in product quality and economic losses. Accordingly, this study constructed a reliable dataset by performing preprocessing steps to remove missing values and outliers based on actual operating data, and designed an Artificial Neural Network (ANN) model. As a result of enhancing the generalization performance of the model through data transformation that reflects domain knowledge in the form of reaction rate expressions, the coefficient of determination (R2) improved to 0.97, and the root mean squared error (RMSE) decreased markedly to 0.04. In addition, the influence of each reactant was quantified and visualized using eXplainable AI (XAI) techniques, based on which the side reaction mechanisms were derived. To verify the derived mechanisms, reaction rate expressions were formulated using the Langmuir–Hinshelwood (L–H) and Power Law models, and a Monte Carlo-based mathematical model was developed. The validation results showed very high performance for all products, with R2 values greater than 0.98 and mean absolute percentage error (MAPE) lower than 2.31%. This study has academic and industrial significance in that it systematically elucidates actual side reaction mechanisms while presenting a highly reliable predictive model applicable to reaction control design.
10.1016/j.cej.2026.176384.title: Data-driven mechanism derivation in hydrogenation reaction systems: A hybrid approach integrating machine learning and mathematical models
10.1016/j.cej.2026.176384.source: ScienceDirect official citation and abstract BibTeX export

10.1016/j.cej.2026.176214.abstract: Continuum surgical robots demand high flexibility, good stretchability, and stable shape sensing. Traditional metallic and conductive polymer sensors for continuum robots face challenges in large deformation, effective encapsulation, and aqueous stability. This study proposes a Neuro-Ionic Hydrogel Fiber Sensor (NIH-FS) and constructs a Bio-Neural Sensing Hydrogel Network (BNSHN) for three-dimensional (3D) shape sensing in continuum surgical robots. First, Neuro-Ionic Hydrogel (NIH) with multi-layered physicochemical crosslinking is developed, achieving high conductivity (11.1 S/m), good stretchability (>500%), and excellent mechanical stability. Coaxial silicone encapsulation provides enhanced stability and long-term water retention, enabling NIH-FS to achieve linear, repeatable, and low-drift strain-resistance response. Experiments demonstrate that NIH-FS exhibits stable and repeatable strain sensing over a wide deformation range, with good linearity in the 0–120% strain range and enhanced sensitivity at larger strains. The BNSHN, constructed using a 3 × 3 multi-channel NIH-FS array, can be stably integrated onto a continuum robot. Through multi-point strain fusion under the Frenet-Serret framework, it achieves 3D shape reconstruction with the tip position error and global average shape error controlled within the millimeter range. These results highlight the potential of NIH-FS and BNSHN for continuum surgical robots, soft medical devices, and wearable systems, offering a novel material and structural strategy to develop high-performance flexible shape sensing platforms.
10.1016/j.cej.2026.176214.title: Bio-Neural Sensing Hydrogel Network (BNSHN) based on NIH-FS for 3D shape sensing of continuum surgical robots

10.1016/j.cej.2026.176516.abstract: The simultaneous perception of multiple physical stimuli is essential for intelligent soft robotics and personalized healthcare. However, the concurrent detection of strain and temperature is fundamentally hindered by signal crosstalk, which compromises accuracy and reliability. Existing solutions, often relying on heterogeneous integration or intricate circuitry, inevitably sacrifice mechanical stability and scalability. Here, we introduce a sensing paradigm that leverages intrinsic material properties to achieve physical signal orthogonality. We design a solvent-free ion-conductive elastomer that exhibits antagonistic electrical responses to strain and temperature: its resistance increases but capacitance decreases upon stretching, whereas both resistance and capacitance increase with heating. This inherent signal decoupling stems from distinct ion migration and interfacial polarization mechanisms under mechanical and thermal stimuli. To translate this orthogonal relationship into precise quantitative readings, we employ a random forest regression model that directly maps the coupled resistance-capacitance signals to strain and temperature values, bypassing the need for complex analytical inversion. Our sensor achieves high-fidelity decoding, with determination coefficients of 0.90 for strain and 0.94 for temperature. It also maintains robust performance over 300 stretching cycles. We further demonstrate its practical utility in a firefighter safety warning system that simultaneously monitors body motion and detects extreme heat exposure. This work establishes a material-centric and algorithm-powered roadmap for multi perception, paving the way for high-fidelity sensing in complex environments.
10.1016/j.cej.2026.176516.title: Machine-learning assisted decoupling of strain and temperature via an antagonistic sensing ionic elastomer

10.1016/j.cej.2026.176308.abstract: The tribovoltaic effect, which directly converts mechanical energy into electricity at dynamic semiconductor interfaces, presents a novel pathway for intrinsic mechanical sensing. Here, we materialize the “surface-as-sensor” paradigm by harnessing this effect to create a self-sensing bearing. This is achieved through a spontaneously formed molybdenum disulfide (MoS₂) layer on the bearing races, which establishes dynamic Schottky contacts with the steel balls, effectively turning the bearing surface itself into the sensing element. Mechanical friction at these interfaces directly generates a continuous stream of real-time electrical signals via the tribovoltaic effect. We analyze the underlying mechanism of this effect within the dynamic bearing system and demonstrate that the magnitude and characteristics of the resulting tribovoltaic outputs are intrinsically modulated by operational conditions, serving as highly sensitive and direct fingerprints of rotational speed and load. By employing explainable machine learning and deep learning to decode these signals, we achieve accurate monitoring of operational states, such as rotation speed, with the identification accuracy exceeding 96%, and further demonstrate its capability in early fault diagnosis. This work successfully establishes the tribovoltaic effect as a practical and powerful sensing mechanism, validating the “surface-as-sensor” concept as a pathway to a new generation of embedded, self-sensing intelligent machinery.
10.1016/j.cej.2026.176308.title: Smart bearings enabled by the tribovoltaic effect and machine learning

10.1016/j.cej.2026.176509.abstract: Accurate analysis of droplet and particle hydrodynamics is crucial for understanding flow, mass transfer, and heat transfer in liquid-liquid-solid (LLS) systems. However, simultaneously characterizing multiple dispersed phases remains challenging. This study proposes a machine learning framework integrating You Only Look Once (YOLO) and ByteTrack to simultaneously identify, segment, and track droplets and particles. YOLO11n is identified as the optimal model, achieving an F1 score of 0.883, mAP50–95 of 0.702, and processing speed of 20 ms per image. The model demonstrates strong generalization across various multiphase systems. In LLS systems, the effects of solid phase mass fraction, oil phase volume fraction, rotational speed, and particle mean diameter on droplet size distribution, Sauter mean diameter, and motion characteristics are investigated. An empirical correlation d32,dD=0.01671+40.4991ωsdpD0.01141+22.4046φoWe−0.2131 is developed to predict droplet Sauter mean diameter, with most deviations within 10%. This method enhances the understanding of LLS system hydrodynamics and facilitates reactor optimization, and scale-up.
10.1016/j.cej.2026.176509.title: Identification, segmentation and tracking: Hydrodynamic research in liquid-liquid-solid systems via machine learning

10.1016/j.cej.2026.176704.abstract: Major depressive disorder (MDD) is primarily diagnosed based on clinical symptoms, reflecting the absence of reliable molecular markers. Although cortisol has been implicated in MDD, its clinical relevance remains unclear, partly due to reliance on single time-point measurements that overlook circadian dynamics. Here, we develop an iontronic platform that enables sensitive profiling of salivary cortisol and permits systematic evaluation of its diurnal variation. The sensing strategy integrates aptamer-based molecular recognition with a transcription-driven amplification pathway, converting weak cortisol-binding events into measurable modulation of ion transport under nanoconfinement, achieving a detection limit of 3.4 pM. Using this approach, we analyzed cortisol rhythms in healthy individuals and patients with MDD. In addition to elevated basal levels, MDD patients exhibited markedly increased diurnal amplitude, indicating disrupted neuroendocrine rhythmicity. Notably, dynamic features of cortisol fluctuation provided substantially greater discriminatory power than static concentration values. When combined with basic clinical parameters and evaluated using a support vector machine model, these rhythm-based signatures enabled reliable differentiation between MDD and control groups. These findings identify amplified diurnal cortisol fluctuation as a quantifiable neuroendocrine phenotype of MDD. Rather than emphasizing absolute hormone levels, this work highlights temporal dysregulation as a potential molecular marker and provides a noninvasive framework for objective neuroendocrine assessment in psychiatric research.
10.1016/j.cej.2026.176704.title: Machine learning-assisted iontronic detection of diurnal cortisol rhythm for neuroendocrine assessment of major depressive disorder

10.1016/j.cej.2026.176625.abstract: Polymer recycling is a significant challenge in the development of sustainable materials, motivating the design of strategies that balance recyclability with performance. Here, we present a unified method that links an integrated kinetic Monte Carlo (kMC) model with a Bayesian optimization routine to determine synthesis conditions for poly(methyl methacrylate) (PMMA) that balance recyclability with target molecular weight requirements. Validated against experimental benchmarks, the model explicitly correlates synthesis conditions with microstructural defects and subsequent depolymerization kinetics. Mechanistic analysis reveals that aggressive synthesis conditions increase polymerization process and defect density, which hinders depolymerization process and may yield polymer too short chains for practical application. To address this, we developed an autonomous three-dimensional optimization routine that efficiently navigates the design space, identifying a synthesis protocol that minimizes the total processing time while maintaining target molar mass strictly. This work establishes an effective, data-driven methodology for the rational design of closed-loop recycling polymers.
10.1016/j.cej.2026.176625.title: A unified kinetic Monte Carlo and Bayesian optimization framework for the circular design of poly(methyl methacrylate): From synthesis to recycling

10.1016/j.cej.2026.176592.abstract: Flexible piezoelectric hydrogel skins are promising for wearable health monitoring, human-machine interaction and soft robotics. However, their application faces a critical challenge in reconciling tissue-level compliance with bias-free, high-SNR, and environment-resilient outputs, while simultaneously circumventing the need for bulky power supplies. Here we introduce a dual-network PAAM/PVDF-TrFE hydrogel via solvent-exchange processing that promotes β phase formation and dipole-dipole alignment, enabling mechanically robust piezoelectric skins. The resulting sensors exhibit linearity within the range of 1–600 kPa, with sensitivities of 2.76 mV·kPa−1 below 280 kPa and 1.11 mV·kPa−1 in the secondary regime above 280 kPa, while demonstrating fast response and recovery times (43 ms and 63 ms, respectively) and robust cyclic stability over 6500 cycles. Functionally, the sensors can decode finger-joint and facial micro-movements, precisely resolve arterial pulse waveforms (P1/P2/P3), and drive a five-pad array for object recognition using a lightweight RBF-SVM. By bridging molecular dipole alignment with machine-learning, this materials-to-algorithms platform advances the frontier of bias-free, self-powered sensing and low-power human-machine interfaces, showing significant potential for multi-element arrays and soft-robotic manipulation.
10.1016/j.cej.2026.176592.title: Strong dipole-dipole interaction-enhanced dual-network piezoelectric hydrogels for long-term pulse monitoring and machine learning-based object recognition

10.1016/j.cej.2026.176775.abstract: The achievable purity in crystallization is limited by a multiscale structural transition, where loose aggregates densify into bridged agglomerates that readily entrap impurities. A specialized machine learning model applied to in situ microscopy images yields a time-resolved fractal dimension that quantifies the evolving morphology of crystal aggregates and serves as a descriptor of their structural state. We embed this descriptor into a turbulence-informed breakage formulation for crystal aggregates and couple it with the system's aggregation and breakage dynamics, defining a multiscale framework that identifies the structural threshold at which loose aggregates transition into bridged, impurity-entrapping agglomerates. Building on this mechanism, we develop the Morphology–Evolution-informed Purity Strategy (MEPS), which identifies an extraction window before the formation of bridged agglomerates, thereby yielding crystals formed from loose aggregates that readily release entrapped mother liquor, in contrast to the several-fold higher retention of mother liquor observed at later extraction times. This approach provides a mechanistic basis for determining optimal extraction timing, offering a practical route for suppressing impurity entrapment in crystallization processes.
10.1016/j.cej.2026.176775.title: Dynamic aggregation control via machine learning-integrated PBM for minimizing impurity entrapment

10.1016/j.cej.2026.176825.abstract: Over the past decade, extensive research has focused on surface engineering and multi-layer approaches to enhance the contact electrification and electrostatic induction of triboelectric nanogenerators (TENGs). However, most of these techniques involve time-consuming, multi-step fabrication processes, highlighting the need for innovative approaches. In this study, we introduce a core-shell nanofiber (NF) architecture composed of a polystyrene (PS) core embedded with silver nanowires (Ag NWs) and a polyvinylidene fluoride (PVDF) shell. This core (PS/Ag)-shell (PVDF) structure significantly enhanced both charge trapping and β-phase induction. Systematic optimization demonstrated that embedding 0.04 vol% Ag NWs into the PS core increased the average peak-to-peak voltage to 319.9 V, representing a 94.3% enhancement compared with pristine core-shell NFs. Comprehensive analysis confirmed that the core-loaded structure outperformed its shell-loaded counterpart because the spatial confinement of Ag NWs within the PS core, together with shielding by the PVDF shell, enhanced charge storage and suppressed leakage current. The core–shell structure also exhibited faster charge accumulation, which is particularly advantageous in applications where external mechanical work is supplied momentarily. Finally, a model trained on triboelectric voltage data achieved 98.3% classification accuracy for five distinct materials, highlighting the potential of this self-powered TENG sensor for intelligent material recognition.
10.1016/j.cej.2026.176825.title: Ag nanowire-embedded core (PS)-shell (PVDF) nanofibers for high-performance triboelectric nanogenerators and artificial intelligence-driven material recognition

10.1016/j.cej.2026.176811.abstract: In implantable treatments for central nervous system injuries, efficient stem cell proliferation within scaffolds and their sustained survival and function in the inflammatory microenvironment are critical. An in situ-forming silk fibroin-hyaluronic acid hydrogel (PF + BMSCs@Gel) was constructed by co-delivering bone marrow mesenchymal stem cells and paeoniflorin, through which a suitable elastic modulus and a three-dimensional environment for survival of stem cells were provided. Proteomic analysis revealed that neuroplasticity was regulated by the hydrogel and was associated with folate response and mitochondrial homeostasis. PF + BMSCs@Gel inhibited inflammation through multiple pathways, including the Toll-like receptor and complement systems, and acted on Wnt, ERK5, Hippo, and MAPK signaling pathways to improve neuroplasticity and promote neurogenesis and reconstruction. PF + BMSCs@Gel promoted mitochondrial autophagy via the KLF4 and PINK1-Parkin pathways, thereby alleviating oxidative stress and inflammatory responses. Furthermore, it facilitated remyelination and axonal regeneration and promoted the proliferation and migration of neural stem cells. As a result, the sensorimotor and cognitive functions of TBI mice were significantly improved, and the depressive symptoms were alleviated.
10.1016/j.cej.2026.176811.title: In situ bioactive silk fibroin-hyaluronic acid hydrogel co-delivering BMSCs and paeoniflorin for neural regeneration and repair after traumatic brain injury

10.1016/j.cej.2026.177046.abstract: This study presents a data-efficient digital twin framework for a liver-on-a-chip (LoC) integrated optical biosensor platform that integrates a computational microfluidics solver with a physiologically based pharmacokinetic-pharmacodynamic (PBPK-PD) model to predict doxorubicin-induced hepatotoxicity. A learning-based model discrepancy term, trained on glutathione S-transferase alpha (GST-α) release as a biomarker, corrects structural mismatches and aligns simulations with measurements. The microfluidics module computes steady, incompressible, laminar velocity fields and transient advection-diffusion-reaction of drugs and oxygen, providing spatiotemporal concentration profiles that inform the PBPK-PD compartments. A hybrid uncertainty quantification approach, combining Bayesian inference to calibrate transport and kinetic parameters from sparse data with an XGBoost discrepancy model that captures residual bias, estimates posterior predictive intervals that account for both epistemic and aleatoric uncertainties. The calibrated twin reproduces time-resolved GST-α trajectories at various dose levels, with observed responses falling within the posterior intervals. For the high-dose doxorubicin condition (20 μM), the predicted GST-α concentration shows a relative deviation of about 9% for the 2D model and 5–6% for the 3D model compared to the filtered experimental measurements. The learned discrepancy extends to previously unseen drug concentrations, enabling conservative extrapolation within quantified uncertainty bounds. Overall, the framework addresses common issues of data scarcity and model-experiment mismatch in organ-on-a-chip studies, informing preclinical decision-making for drug safety and toxicity assessments.
10.1016/j.cej.2026.177046.title: A digital twin framework for predictive modeling of liver-on-a-chip system dynamics using limited experimental data

10.1016/j.cej.2026.177125.abstract: With the development of neuroscience and engineering, neural implants have been serving as the critical interface for high-fidelity neural signal recording and targeted regulation in brain-computer interface (BCI) systems, holding immense potential for treating neurological disorders and restoring lost functions. This review comprehensively summarizes the evolutionary progress of neural implant materials, transitioning from traditional rigid metals to flexible polymers, carbon-based nanomaterials, and conductive hydrogels - all engineered to mitigate mechanical mismatch with soft neural tissue and reduce chronic inflammatory responses. We further elaborate on key biointerface strategies, including structural imitation of neural tissue, bioactive/bioinert surface modifications, and localized therapeutic regulation, which collectively enhance biocompatibility and long-term stability. Additionally, the review addresses core challenges in neural signal processing, such as noise reduction, and highlights breakthroughs in deep learning-driven algorithms and hardware-integrated signal amplification. Furthermore, a critical analysis of prevalent clinical failure cases and technical bottlenecks is presented based on the clinical perspective. Finally, we outline future research directions, encompassing device miniaturization, wireless power supply innovation, intelligent closed-loop systems and the establishment of cross-center clinical databases. By synthesizing advancements in materials science, bioengineering, and signal processing, this work provides a holistic perspective on optimizing neural implant performance, paving the way for reliable, clinically translatable BCI technologies.
10.1016/j.cej.2026.177125.title: Research progress of neural implants: Toward robust brain-computer integration

10.1016/j.cej.2026.176909.abstract: Touch is fundamental to human material perception, involving diverse receptors and complex cognitive processing. However, existing studies are often limited to single-modal sensing and stop at recognizing material type. In this work, multimodal sensing is integrated with a large language model (LLM) to improve material recognition accuracy and enable deeper thinking. The proposed compact flexible multimodal sensor can simultaneously acquire pressure, thermal, and dielectric signals, achieving an overall recognition accuracy of up to 99.13% across 23 representative materials. Based on the recognition results and task requirements, the LLM generates robot control decisions. Augmented reality (AR) provides system visualization and user control, enabling intuitive human–robot interaction. This system demonstrates intelligent robotic sorting driven by material recognition in real-world scenarios and may inspire the application of multimodal sensors in embodied intelligence.
10.1016/j.cej.2026.176909.title: Sense, think, and robot control: Multimodal material recognition sensing integrated with large language model reasoning

10.1016/j.cej.2026.177109.abstract: Triboelectric nanogenerators (TENGs) are promising energy harvesting devices that convert wasted energy into electrical energy from ambient environments, especially in the form of friction. However, they have a few drawbacks, such as low output and severe wear. To address these drawbacks, we adopt a phenomenon known as electric discharge. Rotation is a representative input form for mechanical components, and we are inspired by a thrust bearing structure for generating our TENG as bearings are widely used in many industries and are constantly rotating. In this paper, a thrust ball bearing TENG (TBB-TENG) is proposed. The TBB-TENG exhibits characteristic patterns on the stator by modifying its surface to induce an electric discharge and ultimately enhance the output. Additionally, a mechanical stability analysis is performed theoretically in response to the modification. Furthermore, parametric studies are conducted to optimize the proposed TBB-TENG. Finally, we present the practical use of TBB-TENG as a self-powered defect diagnosis sensor using a one-dimensional convolutional neural network (1D-CNN), demonstrating its high accuracy.
10.1016/j.cej.2026.177109.title: Smart thrust bearing with integrated discharge-based energy harvesting and deep-learning fault detection

10.1016/j.cej.2026.177313.abstract: Nickel cobalt phosphide (NiCoP) has emerged as a promising electrode material for supercapacitors due to its strong redox activity, high conductivity, low cost, and excellent chemical/thermal stability. This study proposes a high-precision hybrid machine learning model, CNN (Convolutional Neural Networks)-BiGRU(Bidirectional gated recurrent unit)-Attention model, for predicting the capacitance of NiCoP-based electrode materials. The dataset consists of 803 experimental instances with 9 input parameters: Ni and Co molar ratios, morphology, specific surface area, current collector, electrolyte concentration, potential window, current density and the output parameter of the supercapacitors' capacity. The relationship between material composition, microstructure, electrochemical properties, and capacitance was successfully fitted. After normalization, R2, RMSE, and MAE values of the CNN-BiGRU-Attention algorithm reach 0.98, 0.021, and 0.18, respectively, demonstrating exceptional model accuracy and fitting capability. The generalization ability of the model was verified through experiments with a mean relative error of 9.20%, indicating remarkable stability and reliability. Furthermore, a novel NiCoP electrode material with a nonstoichiometric ratio of Ni1.3Co0.55P was screened out by searching the space generation method, which exhibits an outstanding specific capacitance of 2263.3 F/g at a current density of 1 A/g. This work provides an innovative and effective method for predicting NiCoP performance, while significantly optimizing of multicomponent phosphide-based supercapacitors with enhanced specific capacitance.
10.1016/j.cej.2026.177313.title: Capacity prediction of cobalt nickel phosphide supercapacitors based on machine learning

10.1016/j.cej.2026.177068.abstract: Revealing the mechanism of CO2 electroreduction (CO2R) to multicarbon (C2+) products remains challenging, especially at the complex electrode−liquid interface and under potential-dependent energy conditions. This study presents comprehensive density functional theory calculations and data-driven screening of CO2R to ethylene and acetamide over Cu-based bimetallic nanoparticles (NPs) loaded on a CuBa surface. Given that 1-butyl-3-methylimidazolium tetrafluoroborate ([Bmim][BF4]) can promote local enrichment and activation of CO2 under potential-dependent energy conditions and achieve efficient CO2R, 25 electric double layer models were constructed using CuBa@CuM NP catalysts and [Bmim][BF4] ionic liquid (IL) in an acidic explicit solvent microenvironment. The Gibbs free energy profile for each proton-coupled electron transfer process of CO2 was calculated via potential-dependent energy integration, with the IL solvent model considered under a constant potential. First CO2 is reduced to CO, after which C–C coupling can occur in *CO–*CHO and *CO–*COH or during *CO direct dimerization toward ethylene synthesis, while C–N coupling in *CCO–*NH3 is most feasibly favored toward acetamide synthesis. CuZr, CuPd, CuPt, and CuBi NPs loaded on CuBa demonstrated outstanding activity, with limiting potential (UL) values of −1.27, −1.21, −1.28, and −1.37 V, respectively, which were smaller than those of other catalysts used in ethylene and acetamide synthesis. Then, based on structural, thermodynamic, and electronic calculations, various quantitative indicators of the structure–activity relationship were established, such as correlations between Bader charge transfer and the binding energy of the intermediate, d-band center difference, and UL of the maximum free energy change step. These results were quantitatively related to CO2R reaction activity through key species interactions and electronic property descriptors. Furthermore, ab initio molecular dynamics simulations were performed in the NVT ensemble at 300 K for 10 ps to estimate CO2 activation over different CuBa@CuM NP catalysts, including the radial distribution function, coordination number of O–H, bond length (C=O), and bond angle (OCO) variations in the CO2 molecule. Finally, various machine learning models were adopted to predict the optimal UL of CO2R to ethylene in a Python3 environment. The coefficient of determination and mean absolute error were employed to evaluate model performance, with values of 0.92 and 0.16 for the extreme gradient boosting model, respectively, indicating its optimal ability to predict catalytic activity. By combining high-performance computing and big data screening for complex catalytic reaction mechanisms, the study provides a better understanding of the catalytic process and offers guidance for future catalyst design for C2+ product synthesis via CO2R.
10.1016/j.cej.2026.177068.title: Data-driven discovery of targeted CuM nanoparticles on 2D CuBa for CO2 fixation: Synergistic effects of ionic liquids in C–C/N coupling

10.1016/j.cej.2026.177249.abstract: The discovery of efficient enzymes for specific biotransformation remains a rate-limiting step in synthetic biology, traditionally relying on laborious experimental screening. Here, we demonstrate how artificial intelligence (AI) dramatically accelerates this process by establishing a streamlined pipeline for sulfotransferase (SULT) discovery and engineering. We leveraged the deep learning model UniKP to predict enzyme kinetic parameters from protein sequences alone, enabling rapid in silico prioritization of candidate SULTs for sulfotyrosine (sTyr) synthesis. This AI-guided approach identified active enzymes with a 50% success rate from a random pool and outperformed traditional BLAST selection from a library of 1000 homologs. An AI-prioritized SULT was successfully engineered through directed evolution, yielding a variant with 7.25-fold enhanced activity while maintaining broad substrate promiscuity. When integrated into engineered Escherichia coli (E. coli), this evolved enzyme enabled high-level sTyr production (1578 μM). Our work establishes AI as a powerful tool to shortcut the enzyme discovery and optimization timeline, serving as a case study that illustrates how AI can be integrated into the rapid development of biocatalysts.
10.1016/j.cej.2026.177249.title: An AI-guided framework for discovery and evolution of sulfotransferases enables efficient sulfotyrosine bioproduction

10.1016/j.cej.2026.177268.abstract: The rapid and accurate monitoring of sulfur dioxide (SO2) derivatives and biogenic amines presents a considerable challenge in food safety, primarily owing to the limitations in sensitivity, portability, and real-time analytical capabilities of existing methods. We introduce a dual-functional fluorescent probe RQB-RM, which is capable of detecting SO2 and biogenic amines with high brightness and ultrasensitivity. The quantum yields of RQB-RM were 22.34% and 17.98%, with limits of detection of 5.18 and 35.20 nM. Based on RQB-RM, a series of smart sensing materials (R-Lab, R-Gel, and R-Ele) were developed, eventually creating two integrated platforms, bridging the material and digital realms: (i) the smartphone-assisted platform enabled the quantitative detection of SO2 derivatives without requiring specialized equipment, and (ii) the dual-channel artificial intelligence (AI)-based freshness monitoring platform with R-Gel exhibited exceptional accuracy in the real-time assessment of shrimp spoilage through autonomous learning of signal dynamics. In addition to its application in food monitoring, this probe was comprehensively validated for its precise mitochondrial targeting and cellular imaging capabilities. We combined sensing materials and AI, providing crucial technological support and a paradigm reference for interdisciplinary innovation in fields such as food quality monitoring and biomedical analysis.
10.1016/j.cej.2026.177268.title: Dual-functional sensing materials for smartphone quantification of sulfur dioxide derivatives and AI-based monitoring of biogenic amines for meat freshness

10.1016/j.cej.2026.177457.abstract: To address the issue of suboptimal hydrogen production efficiency resulting from particle agglomeration and channeling during biomass fluidized bed gasification, this paper presents a method for process intensification and prediction that integrates multiscale flow analysis with deep learning. Initially, pressure pulsation signals are decomposed using power spectral density (PSD) and wavelet transforms to identify the system's eigenfrequencies. The mechanisms by which pulsed gas flows are intensified across the micro, meso, and macroscales are examined. This involves overcoming diffusion limitations at the microscale, disrupting bubbles and particle agglomerates at the mesoscale, and enhancing bed mixing and promoting reaction equilibrium at the macroscale. Secondly, the multiscale coupling relationship between flow complexity and hydrogen yield is elucidated. The trends of wavelet flow-reaction entropy and gas yield exhibit synchronization with increasing pulsation frequency. This study establishes wavelet flow-reaction entropy as a key feature characterizing the correlation between flow complexity and reaction performance. Finally, a two-level Deep Neural Network model driven by wavelet flow-reaction entropy is developed. This model follows the flow trends of the fluidized bed system and enables the accurate prediction of hydrogen yield under various operating conditions, achieving an overall R2 of 0.969. Furthermore, the optimal pressure and pulsation frequency ranges (Zones A and B) are identified, enhances hydrogen production performance. The predicted maximum H2 yield is 12.67 mol/kg-biomass under conditions of 4.4 bar and 3.5 Hz. This study not only unveils the multiscale flow-reaction coupling mechanism underlying pulsed fluidized hydrogen production but also offers a novel theoretical foundation for the intelligent control of biomass pyrolysis gasification processes.
10.1016/j.cej.2026.177457.title: Multiscale pulsating intensification and wavelet entropy-driven AI optimization of fluidized biomass hydrogen production

10.1016/j.cej.2026.177732.abstract: Hydrogel sensors hold great potential for flexible wearable devices. However, their practical application in complex environments is limited by several shortcomings, such as the inability to detect tensile and compressive stimuli with high accuracy, insufficient frost resistance, and a lack of self-adhesiveness. Herein, we incorporated trehalose into a dual-network hydrogel system composed of polyacrylamide, agarose, and carbon nanotubes through a simple one-pot method to produce a novel composite hydrogel. The addition of trehalose significantly enhances both the mechanical properties and frost resistance of the composite hydrogel to deliver ultrahigh flexibility, superior stretchability and compressibility, strong adhesion, excellent biocompatibility, and reliable frost resistance. Sensors assembled from the composite hydrogel provide high sensitivity with antifreeze performance to temperatures as low as −30 °C. The optimized strain sensor delivers a gauge factor of 9.84 within the 60–90% strain range, a low detection limit (0.1%), and a broad sensing range (0.1–90%). The optimized pressure sensor exhibits high sensitivity (3.46 kPa−1 in the 1–3 kPa region), a wide detection range (39.4 Pa to 100 kPa), fast response (70 ms), and reproducible performance over 1000 cycles. In practical applications, the sensors successfully detect diverse physiological signals, ranging from arterial pulse pressure to heavy foot-treading pressure. Further integration with the Multi-Layer Perceptron (MLP) machine-learning algorithm results in exceptional prediction accuracy of gesture recognition, achieving 99.44%. All these features testify to promising prospects in motion assistance, health monitoring, and wearable electronics with high sensitivity and reliability.
10.1016/j.cej.2026.177732.title: Polyacrylamide/agarose/trehalose/carbon nanotubes composite hydrogel with stretchability and compressibility for high-performance wearable strain/pressure sensors and machine-learning-assisted gesture recognition
10.1016/j.cej.2026.177732.source: ScienceDirect official citation and abstract BibTeX export

10.1016/j.cej.2026.177874.abstract: The conductive hydrogels always suffered from large hysteresis, low toughness and poor capability of accurately predicting physical deformation, which seriously restricted their application in smart wearable devices. Herein, a novel conductive hydrogel was fabricated using water-soluble chitosan-modified halloysite nanotubes (CS@HNTs) as an organic-inorganic hybrid crosslinker, which imparts high resilience, superior toughness, and excellent fatigue resistance to the resulting material. Through abundant multiple hydrogen bonds, electrostatic interactions between polymer chains and CS@HNTs, and coordination between aluminum ions and carboxyl groups, this system effectively organizes the polymer network without significantly increasing crosslinking density, thereby conferring remarkable mechanical properties (91.4% resilience and a toughness of 1.25 MJ/m3). The hierarchical energy dissipation mechanisms, dynamic mechanical response behavior, and network structure evolution of the materials were systematically characterized by rheology and low-field (LF) nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR) spectroscopy. Concurrently, the fully physically crosslinked network facilitates efficient ionic conduction and enables rapid degradation under alkaline conditions. The hydrogel-based sensor also demonstrates a notable thermal response, with a temperature coefficient of resistance of −1.95%°C−1, allowing for precise monitoring of ambient temperature. Furthermore, we constructed a self-powered sensing system for identifying various human motions and, separately, developed an information security system that integrates deep learning algorithm to achieve highly efficient and accurate (98%) information encryption and decryption based on Morse code. This work provides a promising strategy for constructing high-performance, sustainable, and intelligent flexible wearable platforms.
10.1016/j.cej.2026.177874.title: A degradable, highly tough, and resilient nanocomposite hydrogel for self-powered wearable sensors and a deep learning-assisted recognition system
10.1016/j.cej.2026.177874.source: ScienceDirect official citation and abstract BibTeX export

10.1016/j.cej.2026.177780.abstract: Multi-objective optimization plays a critical role in chemical reactor design, where conflicting objectives and complex constraints pose challenges. Traditional optimization methods heavily rely on manual modeling and tuning. To this end, we develop a generative reasoning framework by fine-tuning distilled large language models (LLMs) and designing domain knowledge-embedded prompts for both continuous-variable and mixed-variable optimization of chemical reactors, covering a methanol-steam-reforming fixed bed reactor, a methanol-to-olefins fluidized bed reactor, a multipolar‑magnesium electrolyzer, and two organic flow reactors. Results demonstrate that full-scale LLMs can effectively generate Pareto-optimal solutions but face deployment barriers due to hardware constraints. To improve practical usability, we further design structured chain-of-thought prompts and adopt a quantized low-rank adaptation method to fine-tune locally deployed distilled LLMs. We find that the fine-tuned distilled LLMs significantly enhance multi-objective reasoning performance, improving Pareto frontier identification accuracy from 25% to 79% for the 7B model and from 44% to 91% for the 14B model relative to the corresponding baseline distilled LLMs without fine-tuning. The novelty of this study lies in integrating structured chain-of-thought prompting with parameter-efficient fine-tuning of locally deployable streamlined LLMs, thereby providing a practical LLM-assisted framework for multi-objective optimization of chemical reactors.
10.1016/j.cej.2026.177780.title: Chemical reactor optimization leveraging distilled LLM enhanced by prompt design and fine-tuning strategy

10.1016/j.cej.2026.178054.abstract: As an important vehicle for the next generation of interactive technologies, the human-machine interaction system deeply integrates flexible electronics, the Internet of Things and artificial intelligence technologies. It shows great potential in many areas such as medical surveillance and smart wearable devices. This study developed a conductive ion hydrogel-based triboelectric nanogenerator (PGL-TENG) and its associated intelligent sensing and communication system, using a deep learning model to assist in identifying human motion status. The hydrogel, prepared from PVA, Gel, and LiCl, exhibited excellent mechanical strength, conductivity, and water retention, and served as the electrode, while VHB tape was used as the friction layer. The assembled PGL-TENG achieved an open-circuit voltage of 200 V, a short-circuit current of 13 μA, and a power density of 1040 mW m−2. A deep learning platform was established to extract voltage features and achieve accurate classification of human motion states, significantly improved gait recognition accuracy, highlighting the potential of deep learning for self-powered sensing and multimodal motion recognition. In addition, an intelligent sensing and communication system was developed, which uses Morse code to identify and transmit various signals, and its dual alarm mechanism uses visual and audio alarms to achieve efficient and reliable transmission of the “SOS” distress signal. This offers a promising technical approach for the development of intelligent wearable devices and intelligent communication systems.
10.1016/j.cej.2026.178054.title: Triboelectric nanogenerator-based intelligent sensing communication and deep learning motion recognition system based on ionic hydrogel

10.1016/j.cej.2026.177998.abstract: In chemical engineering applications, gas-liquid two-phase flow patterns have a direct impact on reaction kinetics, mixing efficiency, and overall system stability. Accurate flow pattern identification enables engineers to predict pressure drops, optimize residence time distributions, and enhance interfacial contact between phases, thereby effectively improving the yield of chemical processes. In this study, a novel distributed optical fiber sensing technology, i.e., optical carrier microwave interferometry (OCMI), is applied for horizontal gas-liquid two-phase flow pattern identification, in combination with time-frequency domain analysis and support vector machine (SVM). Several statistical metrics are employed to characterize the frequency domain features. Through threshold-based methods, bubble/elongated bubble flow and partial wave flow can be recognized, while identifying slug flow and stratified flow remains challenging. To address this challenge, the Hilbert-Huang transform (HHT) is applied to the reconstructed time-series signal to extract discriminative time-frequency spectral features, enabling effective differentiation among all flow patterns. An SVM-based intelligent recognition model is then constructed, leveraging the extracted time-frequency domain features as input, achieving a high classification accuracy of 96.9%. By pioneering the integration of distributed OCMI sensing with HHT-based feature extraction and machine learning, this work establishes a new paradigm for multiphase flow diagnostics that overcomes the inherent limitations of conventional point-wise or local sensing methods through continuous distributed monitoring along the pipeline.
10.1016/j.cej.2026.177998.title: Gas-liquid two-phase flow pattern identification based on HHT and SVM-assisted optical carrier microwave interferometry

10.1016/j.cej.2026.177940.abstract: Atomic Layer Deposition (ALD) of silicon nitride (Si3N4) is critical in advanced semiconductor manufacturing, yet predicting film thickness uniformity remains challenging due to the inherent multiscale nature of the process. This study introduces a comprehensive Density Functional Theory–Kinetic Monte Carlo–Computational Fluid Dynamics (DFT–kMC–CFD) framework that connects atomic-scale surface kinetics with reactor-scale transport phenomena for Si3N4 ALD using dichlorosilane (DCS) and ammonia (NH3). A kMC model for the β-Si3N4(0001) surface was developed from DFT-derived cluster energies and calibrated against experimental data, yielding activation energies consistent with literature values. The validated kMC model was integrated with three-dimensional CFD simulations through two-way coupling. By discretizing the wafer surface into 109 zones, the framework enabled high-resolution prediction of growth-per-cycle (GPC) distributions. Applications to single-wafer and multi-wafer batch reactors revealed that operating parameters—including wafer rotation, precursor exposure time, wafer spacing, and carrier gas flow rate—critically influence film uniformity. This framework provides a practical tool for quantitative prediction of uniformity, reactor design, and process optimization in semiconductor manufacturing.
10.1016/j.cej.2026.177940.title: Atomistic-to-reactor digital twin for silicon nitride atomic layer deposition via bidirectional kinetic Monte Carlo-computational fluid dynamics coupling

10.1016/j.cej.2026.178208.abstract: Wearable intelligent health monitoring platforms exhibit substantial application potential in domains such as telemedicine and posture sensing. However, constrained by the interfacial instability and deformation mismatch issues in energy storage systems, ensuring stable and continuous power supply for the monitoring platform under various mechanical deformations remains a major challenge. Here, we report the design and validation of a flexible integrated energy and analysis platform (FIEAP) that provides continuous and stable energy supply and machine learning-based intelligent analysis for wearable systems. This platform employs a synergistic dual-network crosslinking strategy utilizing hydrogen bonding and coordination interactions to enhance interfacial stability by creating a polyacrylamide/sodium alginate (PAM/SA) composite hydrogel electrolyte with strengthened interfacial adhesion, enhanced mechanical compliance, and uniform Zn2+ deposition. With PAM/SA, Zn||Zn battery delivers areal capacity of 5 mAh cm−2 with 99% retention after 1600 h, demonstrating the ultralong cycling stability of the PAM/SA. It is then combined with a series-parallel arranged zinc anode, manganese dioxide cathode, and flexible printed interconnects to make a modular zinc-ion battery array. Combined with a thin-film pressure sensor and Bluetooth low energy, it enables acquisition, transmission, and intelligent analysis of body surface pressure variations for practical applications. We show that the FIEAP can achieve high-accuracy recognition of six walking postures, with an accuracy rate of up to 96.7%. The platform paves the way for the design and application of stable integrated energy systems in wearable intelligent devices, enabling widespread utility for daily motion tracking and disease treatment evaluation.
keywords: Flexible integrated energy and analysis platform
10.1016/j.cej.2026.178208.title: Configurable flexible energy storage system for machine learning-powered multimodal health surveillance

10.1016/j.cej.2026.178300.abstract: Per-and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS) have become a severe threat to aqueous environmental safety due to their ultra-high persistence, bioaccumulation, and strong mobility. Herein, a cross-scale strategy combining density functional theory (DFT) and interpretable machine learning (ML) was employed to reveal the adsorption mechanism of PFAS on biochar (BC) and identify the key governing factors. DFT calculations demonstrate a pronounced chain-length dependence for PFAS adsorption. Longer chains enable more extensive molecular spreading on BC surfaces. This physical spreading drives a continuous buildup of van der Waals forces. Consequently, the interfacial binding strength increases significantly. Subsequently, DFT-derived quantum descriptors were integrated with a dataset of 1961 experimental adsorption samples for modeling. The CatBoost model achieves optimal predictive performance after Bayesian optimization with a coefficient of determination of 0.9196 and an RMSE of 9.4227. The five-fold cross-validation yields a mean coefficient of determination of 0.8292 (±0.0255),which confirms reliable model generalization ability. SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) analysis quantitatively identified initial concentration, adsorption time, average pore size of BC, and the HOMO-LUMO gap of PFAS as the dominant factors. Operational parameters contributed up to 46.89%, significantly higher than BC physicochemical properties (36.31%) and molecular descriptors (16.8%). This study provides a comprehensive microscopic mechanism underlying chain-length-dependent PFAS adsorption, offering fundamental theoretical guidance for the rational design and targeted optimization of BC to enhance the removal of diverse PFAS in aqueous environments.
10.1016/j.cej.2026.178300.title: Unraveling the adsorption mechanism of PFAS on biochar: A cross-scale integration of DFT calculations and interpretable machine learning

10.1016/j.cej.2026.178259.abstract: Objective and reproducible biomechanical monitoring is important for race-walking training and technical assessment, yet flexible triboelectric sensors still suffer from poor unit-to-unit consistency caused by manual fabrication and limited validation under sports-relevant wearing conditions. Herein, we propose a standardized fused deposition modeling–flexible printed circuit (FDM–FPC) hybrid manufacturing strategy for batch-manufacturable triboelectric sensor arrays toward smart-insole sensing. In this design, FDM-printed thermoplastic elastomer structures define the elastic spacer and triboelectric layer, while FPC electrodes provide reproducible electrode geometry and integrated interconnection. The resulting sensors showed a low coefficient of variation of 1.45% among 25 devices from five independent batches, markedly lower than that of manually fabricated controls (9.67%). With optimized surface morphology and stable device architecture, the sensor responded to plantar-level loads from 2 to 250 N and captured weak physiological signals, including pulse and respiration. Application-relevant reliability was further verified through 20,000 loading cycles at 200 N, 5000 bending cycles, and temperature, humidity, and artificial-sweat tests. By integrating three sensing units into a smart insole, a seven-channel plantar triboelectric signal representation and a multi-scale convolutional neural network–bidirectional gated recurrent unit (CNN-BiGRU) model were established for race-walking state recognition. Based on six volunteers and 9331 sliding-window samples, Leave-One-Subject-Out Cross-Validation (LOSO-CV) achieved 94.6% accuracy and a 94.3% macro-F1 score for five-class recognition. This work provides a reproducible and application-oriented triboelectric smart-insole platform for auxiliary race-walking technical assessment and wearable sports analytics.
10.1016/j.cej.2026.178259.title: Standardized batch-manufacturable triboelectric sensor arrays for deep learning-enabled race-walking state recognition

10.1016/j.cej.2026.178324.abstract: The efficient biosynthesis of cytidine-5′-diphosphocholine (CDP-choline), a vital pharmaceutical intermediate, relies on a sequential two-step pathway catalyzed by choline kinase (CKI) and CTP:phosphocholine cytidylyltransferase (CCT). However, this bioprocess is largely bottlenecked by the sluggish kinetics of CCT, an amphipathic membrane-bound enzyme whose rational engineering is severely hindered by the lack of solved crystal structures. To alleviate this kinetic limitation, this study established a physics-informed and evolution-guided integrated strategy. First, a sequence-structure-dynamics three-dimensional funnel screening workflow was constructed. By combining AlphaFold2-based structural topology filtering with DLKcat kinetic pre-screening, we successfully captured a high-potential candidate CCT from Maudiozyma saulgeensis (MsCCT), with superior chassis compatibility, which showed an 8.69-fold increase in total catalytic activity compared to the control CCT from Saccharomyces cerevisiae (ScCCT). Subsequently, we employed a multi-view integrated Protein Language Model (PLM) zero-shot prediction method. Through the cross-validation of ProGen (evolutionary perspective), SaProt (global structural perspective), and ProSST (local micro-environmental perspective), combined with a domain-focusing strategy, the mutant MsCCTM3 was identified, exhibiting a 2.4-fold catalytic enhancement over the wild-type MsCCT. Upon integrating the evolved MsCCTM3 into a metabolically optimized Bacillus subtilis chassis, multi-omics analysis deciphered a critical kinetic mismatch, revealing that the hyper-active enzyme shifted the metabolic bottleneck to upstream substrate transport and precursor supply capacity. Ultimately, the engineered strain achieved a high titer of 5.65 g/L with a space-time yield of 0.202 g/(L·h) in a 5 L bioreactor, representing a 34.7% improvement over the control strain. This work not only provides an efficient strain for the industrial production of CDP-choline but also offers an integrated data-driven workflow that demonstrates promising potential for engineering complex membrane proteins lacking structural templates.
10.1016/j.cej.2026.178324.title: AI-guided evolution of membrane-associated cytidylyltransferase and systems metabolic engineering enable high-titer CDP-choline biosynthesis

10.1016/j.cej.2026.178298.abstract: The increasing threat of multidrug-resistant bacterial infections demands new antimicrobial agents and efficient discovery strategies. Amphibians represent a rich yet underexplored source of antimicrobial peptides, but systematic mining of amphibian genomes remains limited. In this study, a deep learning-based framework was applied to the genome of Nanorana parkeri to identify seven candidate antimicrobial peptides. Among them, c_AMP2 exhibited the strongest and broad-spectrum antibacterial activity, including potent inhibition of multidrug-resistant Pseudomonas aeruginosa (MRPA, MIC = 6.25 μM). Rational optimization of c_AMP2 generated two analogs, RR18 and VR18, with enhanced cationicity and amphipathicity. Structural characterization confirmed that both peptides adopt stable amphipathic α-helical conformations, with optimized hydrophobic and cationic segregation. Notably, VR18 exhibited an improved amphipathic distribution, whereas both analogs formed short rod-like nanostructures as revealed by AFM and SEM analyses. Functionally, both of the peptides showed improved activity against MRPA (MIC = 3.13 μM) and rapid bactericidal kinetics. Mechanistic analyses supported a membrane-targeting mode of action, as indicated by molecular simulations and biophysical assays demonstrating membrane binding, depolarization, and permeabilization. In a murine pneumonia and sepsis model induced by MRPA, RR18 exhibited favorable safety and significantly reduced the bacterial burden, alleviated pathology, and suppressed pro-inflammatory cytokine production. These findings demonstrate the potential of amphibian genomic mining for antimicrobial peptide discovery and identify RR18 as a candidate against drug-resistant P. aeruginosa.
10.1016/j.cej.2026.178298.title: Discovery of novel AMPs from Nanorana parkeri: A deep learning approach to combating multidrug-resistant P. aeruginosa infection

10.1016/j.cej.2026.178547.abstract: Reliable manipulation in soft robotics requires sensing systems that can simultaneously resolve deformation, force direction, and temperature while remaining robust to cross-interference. Here we report an all-resistive dual-modal flexible sensor that, in combination with machine learning-based inference, enables decoupled perception of strain magnitude, strain direction, and temperature for robotic grasping. The sensor employs a tri-channel rosette architecture in which two channels provide temperature-invariant strain sensing, while a third channel encodes coupled strain-temperature information. This physical encoding allows directional deformation to be extracted from purely resistive signals using a compact and scalable design. To address nonlinear coupling under dynamic loading, we develop a task-specific machine learning framework that achieves recognition accuracies exceeding 91% across all sensing dimensions. Integrated onto a soft robotic gripper, the system enables real-time identification of grasping direction, slip-related deformation, and object temperature during manipulation. By combining minimal hardware complexity with data-driven interpretation, this work advances multifunctional sensing skins for safe, adaptive, and intelligent robotic manipulation in unstructured environments.
10.1016/j.cej.2026.178547.title: Machine learning-enabled decoupling of strain and temperature for multifunctional sensing in soft robotic manipulation

10.1016/j.cej.2026.178551.abstract: The integration of sustainable energy harvesting and intelligent sensing is essential for next-generation self-powered systems. Here, a Cu-nanosheet (Cu-NS) and thermoplastic polyurethane synergistically wrapped plant fiber sponge (PFS@TPU-Cu) is fabricated via a simple ball-milling and impregnation strategy. The incorporation of Cu-NS induces a tip-enhanced electric field that intensifies interfacial polarization and promotes efficient charge transfer during contact–separation. The resulting PTC-TENG achieves an open-circuit voltage of 125 V, short-circuit current of 4.2 μA, and power density of 0.16 W m−2, sufficient to charge a 4.7 μF capacitor to 3 V within 110 s and power 738 LEDs. The device exhibits 80% compressibility, rapid response (46/54 ms), and durability over 5000 cycles, enabling reliable mechanical adaptability. Moreover, integrated with a convolutional neural network, the self-powered sensor attains 95.25% gesture recognition accuracy, demonstrating strong potential in sign language recognition and wearable human-machine interfaces. This work establishes a scalable, field-enhanced triboelectric platform for energy-autonomous intelligent electronics.
10.1016/j.cej.2026.178551.title: Cu–nanosheet wrapped plant fiber sponge with tip-enhanced electric field for self–powered triboelectric gesture recognition via convolutional neural network

10.1016/j.cej.2026.178696.abstract: Decellularized extracellular matrices derived from neural tissue exhibit specific bioactivity for spinal cord regeneration, yet their therapeutic potential is hampered by weak mechanical strength, rapid degradation, and absence of topological guidance. To overcome these drawbacks, herein, a bioinspired core-shell-structured fiber was fabricated by coaxial electrospinning, featuring a mechanically supportive poly(ε-caprolactone) (PCL) core uniformly coated with a bioactive decellularized extracellular matrix (dECM) sheath. The coaxial dECM/PCL fibers demonstrated improved tensile moduli, enhanced degradation stability, and maintained bioactivity. Notably, the aligned electrospun fibers, comprising a decellularized spinal cord matrix shell and PCL core (referred to as A-DSCM/PCL), exhibited good cytocompatibility, effectively supporting cell adhesion, proliferation, and neuronal differentiation of primary neural stem/progenitor cells (NSPCs). Transcriptomic analysis showed that the A-DSCM/PCL fibers can promote neural lineage progression, potentially through activation of the Wnt signaling pathway. Additionally, the customized biomimetic scaffold was created by incorporating a central region loaded with an NT-3-integrated DSCM sponge, surrounded by dECM/PCL coaxial fibers, thereby mimicking both gray and white matter in spinal cord tissue. Once implanted into a complete spinal cord transection model in rats, the A-DSCM/PCL-S scaffolds significantly stimulated endogenous neurogenesis, promoted axonal regeneration, and improved motor functional recovery. This study presents an advanced biofabrication strategy using dECM, establishing a promising therapeutic platform for spinal cord injury repair through coordinated lineage steering of NSPCs.
10.1016/j.cej.2026.178696.title: Bioinspired core-shell structured electrospun fibers guide neural stem/progenitor cell lineage development for spinal cord injury repair

10.1016/j.cej.2026.178744.abstract: The efficient capture of CO2 from humid gas streams remains a major challenge for carbon-mitigation technologies because water vapor induces strong competitive adsorption in porous adsorbents. Elucidating the underlying mechanisms of CO2 selective adsorption under humid conditions is essential for the rational design of adsorbents in realistic environments. This study integrates machine learning-based multicomponent (CO2, H2O and N2) adsorption modeling, experimental methods and molecular simulations to investigate the key factors governing CO2 separation in humid mixed-gas environments. The results show that the narrow micropore volume and specific surface area are the dominant structural factors governing the CO2 adsorption capacity of porous materials, whereas nitrogen doping primarily enhances CO2 capture capacity and selectivity under low-pressure and high-temperature conditions. The adsorption mechanism of H2O exhibits pronounced differences across humidity ranges. At relative humidity (RH) < 60%, adsorption is dominated by hydrogen bonding or electrostatic interactions at oxygen polar sites. Under high-humidity conditions (RH > 60%), water molecules progressively form clusters and undergo pore filling, with mesopores providing sufficient space for cluster growth and thus becoming the dominant factor governing adsorption. In addition, surface hydrophobic modifications such as silanization and fluorination can markedly suppress H2O adsorption and enhance the selectivity of CO2. Based on these findings, we synthesized a hydrophobic microporous carbon-based adsorbent with a water contact angle of 144.07°. The material exhibits dynamic separation coefficients of 0.229 for CO2/H2O and 6.694 for CO2/N2 in a CO2/H2O/N2 (0.15/0.05/0.80) mixed-gas system. This study establishes a predictive framework for CO2 capture in porous materials under humid conditions and elucidates the synergistic effects of physicochemical properties on adsorption performance, providing guidance for the rational design of moisture-resistant CO2 adsorbents.
10.1016/j.cej.2026.178744.title: Explainable machine learning-driven design of porous adsorbents for CO2 capture under humid conditions
