10.1016/j.cej.2026.178531.abstract: A versatile PEI-PAN-GO nanofiber membrane was successfully fabricated via electrospinning for the efficient removal of anionic and cationic dyes, namely, Congo Red (CR) and Methylene Blue (MB), and the antibiotic ciprofloxacin (CIP), from aqueous solutions. The membrane exhibited significantly improved mechanical strength, hydrophilicity, and adsorption capacity owing to the synergistic interactions among polyethyleneimine (PEI), polyacrylonitrile (PAN), and graphene oxide (GO). Batch adsorption experiments revealed a strong pH dependence, with maximum removal efficiencies for CR and CIP achieved at pH 2, and for MB at pH 8. The highest removal efficiency was observed for CIP (96.5%), followed by CR (93.2%) and MB (77.4%). Kinetic studies conformed to the pseudo-second-order model, with activation energies of 13.22, 16.01, and 7.69 kJ/mol for CR, MB, and CIP, respectively, indicating a predominantly non-covalent adsorption mechanism (physisorption) with low kinetic barriers, consistent with electrostatic, hydrogen bonding, and π–π stacking interactions. Among the tested isotherm models, the Dubinin–Radushkevich (D–R) model provided the best fit to the experimental data. The thermodynamic parameters confirmed that the adsorption process was spontaneous (ΔSο < 0) and endothermic (ΔHο > 0). Furthermore, the membrane demonstrated excellent reusability, retaining a high removal efficiency with only a 12% decline after five consecutive adsorption–desorption cycles. Four machine learning models were developed to predict removal efficiency across all pollutants, incorporating operational parameters and a coded pollutant type feature (0, 1, or 2). BPNN and Random Forest demonstrated excellent generalization (test R2 = 0.95–0.96, RMSE ≈ 7%), effectively modeling complex pH-dependent interactions, while SVM and XGBoost exhibited overfitting (test R2 = 0.83–0.87) due to CIP amphoteric behavior. The superior performance of BPNN and Random Forest confirms the PEI-PAN-GO membrane as a high-performance adsorbent for the removal of dyes and antibiotics.
10.1016/j.cej.2026.178531.title: Smart adsorption systems: Combining electrospun PEI-PAN-GO membranes with deep learning models for real-time prediction and optimization of pollutant removal efficiency

10.1016/j.cej.2026.179020.abstract: Simultaneously integrating high sensitivity, a wide linear range, and robust cyclic stability into a single flexible strain sensor remains a critical yet unresolved challenge for wearable electronics. Herein, we report a facile and scalable strategy to fabricate a MXene/PDMS sensor that employs isotropic wrinkle microstructures to guide the formation of a maze-like crack network (MCN). A critical “peak pinning” effect induced by these wrinkles effectively suppresses catastrophic crack propagation while promoting the progressive generation of the MCN, which inherits the meandering characteristics of the wrinkles. By precisely tuning the MXene deposition density (0.5–4 g m−2), both the wrinkle and crack geometry as well as the resultant piezoresistive properties can be tailored. Consequently, the optimized sensor achieves an exceptional balance of performance metrics: a high gauge factor of 518.7, a broad linear working range of 62.2%, fast response and recovery times (13 ms and 42 ms, respectively), and robust durability exceeding 1000 cycles. The device demonstrates versatile monitoring capabilities across a full spectrum of human activities, spanning subtle physiological signals (e.g., arterial pulse waves and laryngeal vibrations) to large-amplitude joint movements. Furthermore, when integrated with an XGBoost ensemble machine learning algorithm, the sensor enables a smart sensing system that achieves 95.0% classification accuracy for complex hand gestures. Collectively, this work presents a synergistic approach combining scalable fabrication, engineered microstructures, and artificial intelligence (AI)-enhanced data processing to advance the development of next-generation human-machine interfaces.
10.1016/j.cej.2026.179020.title: Maze-like crack networks guided by wrinkles in MXene/PDMS for machine learning-assisted flexible strain sensing

10.1016/j.cej.2026.179026.abstract: The practical implementation of slurry-based photocatalytic reactors is limited by catalyst separation and operational stability. In this regard, sodium-alginate (SA) aerogel beads loaded with Bi12O15Cl6/Fe2O3@C (BFC-II) photocatalyst (BFC-II/SA-aerogel beads) were prepared and tested for the visible-light-driven degradation of ofloxacin (OLX), both in batch and continuous mode. BFC-II/SA-aerogel beads were fabricated by introducing BFC-II photocatalyst into the alginate matrix during hydrogel preparation, and thereafter freeze-dried to obtain a porous aerogel framework. Under optimal conditions, 94.4% of OLX degradation on BFC-II/SA-aerogel beads (batch mode) was recorded after 150 min of reaction time, ascribed to their porous structure, which improved BFC-II photocatalyst dispersion and reduced agglomeration. Moreover, the polymeric framework promotes light scattering and efficient charge transfer. In continuous operation, OLX degradation was slightly lower than in batch mode. Nevertheless, the photocatalytic system exhibited stable performance over multiple cycles, with a degradation efficiency loss of less than 10%. The radical scavenging study, supported by electron paramagnetic resonance (EPR) analysis, revealed that O2•− primarily facilitated the photocatalytic degradation of OLX. Nearly half of the degradation products (DPs) of OLX, were found to be outside the toxic range. In addition, the possible transformations of DPs under abiotic environmental conditions were determined using BioTransformer 3.0, and the subsequent changes in ecotoxicity were evaluated in silico. Lastly, machine learning models were employed to model the experimental data, among which XGBoost demonstrated the best predictive performance with the highest R2 value (~ 0.99).
10.1016/j.cej.2026.179026.title: Alginate-aerogel-framework integrated with bismuth oxyhalide-based Z-scheme heterostructure for the photocatalytic degradation of ofloxacin: Mechanistic insights and machine learning modeling

10.1016/j.cej.2026.179115.abstract: The escalating threat of multidrug resistant microorganisms and biofilm infection calls for potent alternatives to conventional antibiotics. Artificial intelligence is transforming antimicrobial material discovery and optimization by enabling high throughput screening, guiding rational design, accelerating candidate prioritization, and elucidating mechanisms of action. This review outlines a full pipeline for AI-driven antimicrobial screening/design across diverse material classes, including antimicrobial peptides, metal–phenolic networks, hydrogels, and nanozymes and beyond. It begins by introducing fundamental principles of antimicrobial mechanisms and AI methodologies, then systematically dissects the AI-driven research workflow encompassing data handling, feature engineering, model training, experimental validation, and iterative refinement. Subsequent sections illustrate the application of this pipeline to each material class through representative case studies, followed by a cross-class comparison that identifies convergent design principles. It then discusses how AI strategies tackle long-standing challenges including biofilm complexity, selective targeting, resistance circumvention, and the trade-off between antimicrobial efficacy and host compatibility. The review further emphasizes how AI enables application-specific customization, translating varying antimicrobial clinical demands (e.g., those from orthopaedics, wound care, pulmonary infections, and ocular diseases) into quantifiable design parameters and criteria. Moreover, it analyzes the future opportunities and challenges for research innovation and clinical translation. By bridging data and biology, this review provides insights to guide rational development of next-generation antimicrobial therapeutics for advanced healthcare.
10.1016/j.cej.2026.179115.title: Artificial intelligence-driven discovery and rational design of antimicrobial materials: Bridging data and biology

10.1016/j.cej.2026.179116.abstract: Iron minerals play a critical role in regulating the geochemical cycling of pollutants, yet quantitative prediction of inorganic ion retention at the mineral–water interface remains challenging due to the predominant focus on adsorption while overlooking the desorption process. Herein, an integrated machine learning (ML) framework was established to model both adsorption and desorption behaviors across diverse iron mineral–inorganic ion systems, enabling a quantitative evaluation of the long-term retention capacity and binding stability. A comprehensive adsorption–desorption database was compiled, and separate models were constructed to predict adsorption and desorption efficiencies, achieving strong predictive performance (R2 = 0.948 and 0.917; MAE = 4.772 and 5.317, respectively). SHAP analysis revealed distinct factors controlling these two processes. Adsorption was primarily influenced by environmental conditions and ion properties, while desorption was mainly governed by mineral properties, particularly specific surface area (SSA). Although SSA enhanced both adsorption and desorption, its net influence on binding stability was ambiguous, indicating that the long-term retention capacity cannot be reliably inferred from adsorption alone. Employing model predictions, binding stability was quantified through retention amount and hysteresis index (HI), revealing strong release tendencies for heavy metal cations such as Cd(II), Co(II), and Cu(II), and limited immobilization capacity of magnetite for most inorganic ions. This work established a unified adsorption–desorption modeling framework that advanced the quantitative prediction of inorganic ion retention and mobility at the mineral–water interface, offering a novel approach for stability-aware environmental risk assessment.
10.1016/j.cej.2026.179116.title: Coupled adsorption–desorption machine learning modeling for predicting inorganic ion retention on iron minerals

10.1016/j.cej.2026.179251.abstract: Collagen is widely used as a biomaterial in tissue engineering and regenerative medicine. However, growing concerns over animal-derived sources have motivated the development of synthetic human collagen to minimize associated risks. Here, we present a synthetic biology strategy for microbial production of human type I collagen (hCOL1) fragment, integrating machine learning with biofoundry-driven workflows. Using an ESM-2 protein language model combined with biofoundry-based strain development, context-dependent synthetic signal peptides (SP) were designed and evaluated. This approach achieved the production and secretion of hCOL1 fragments in Corynebacterium glutamicum as an industrial host at 24.3 ± 3 mg/L after the third round of strain engineering, representing a 4.9-fold increase compared with the native SP in the first round. Next, scalable hCOL1 fragment production was demonstrated in 5-L fermenters, achieving titers of 857 ± 75 mg/L in fed-batch cultivations using glucose. To validate its potential as a tissue engineering biomaterial, the collagen-based biocomposite scaffolds were fabricated and used to culture human adipose-derived stem cells. The engineered matrices significantly enhanced proliferation and stemness marker expression, surpassing conventional animal-derived collagens. Active learning for context- and host-dependent SP design can facilitate the secretion of not only collagen but also other proteins of interest.
10.1016/j.cej.2026.179251.title: Machine learning-guided sustainable human type I collagen fragment production in engineered microbial cells for tissue engineering

10.1016/j.cej.2026.179136.abstract: Rapid and efficient removal of MPs from stormwater runoff is essential for mitigating MPs pollution risks in aquatic environments. However, the applicability of conventional adsorption models to MPs capture by superhydrophobic materials and precise machine-learning prediction tools remain underexplored. In this study, experimental studies combined with artificial neural network (ANN) modeling were conducted to investigate the adsorption behavior and mechanism of typical MPs in stormwater runoff. The results showed that MOF-modified superhydrophobic quartz could achieve rapid and efficient capture of PP, PE, and PET within 15 min, with maximum removal efficiency reaching 98.89%, 98.54%, and 97.33%, respectively. The adsorption dynamics were appropriately described by the pseudo-second-order kinetic model. For isotherms, the Sips model outperformed Langmuir and Freundlich models, whereas conventional models showed significant deviations in adsorption capacity at higher equilibrium concentrations, highlighting the limitations in capturing secondary adsorption from hydrophobic aggregation of MPs. To overcome the shortcomings of back-propagation (BP) neural networks, a sparrow search algorithm–optimized ANN (SSA-BP-ANN) was applied for MPs adsorption system and three prediction models were constructed. The R2 values of these models were 0.9922, 0.9989, and 0.9965, outperforming LR, RF, and GBR, which accurately predicted the removal efficiencies of PP, PE, and PET. SHAP analysis indicated that initial MPs concentration and adsorbent dosage had the most significant impacts on the removal efficiency, followed by pH and contact time, whereas temperature contributed the least. This study expanded our understanding of MPs removal from stormwater by MOF-modified superhydrophobic materials and provided valuable insights into adsorption modeling and machine-learning prediction.
10.1016/j.cej.2026.179136.title: Rapid particulate microplastics removal from stormwater: Distinct adsorption behavior and data-driven intelligent prediction

10.1016/j.cej.2026.179303.abstract: As critical electrical equipment in power grids, power transformers pose substantial operational risks and financial losses once major faults occur. Traditional detection methods, relying primarily on manual inspection, are unable to provide real-time monitoring of transformer operational states. In this work, we develop a self-powered vibration online monitoring system of power transformers designed for continuous condition surveillance. Central to this system is the proposed composite spring-type triboelectric nanogenerator vibration sensor (CST-TEVS), which can effectively capture vibration signals with low accelerations (0–0.6 g) and broadband (100–500 Hz) characteristics of transformer operation. Building on this, an intelligent diagnostic framework integrating Hierarchical Decremental Multi-scale convolution (HD-Multiscale) and a Squeeze-and-Excitation enhanced Residual network is developed, achieving transformer condition identification accuracy exceeding 99%. Furthermore, a dedicated visualization interface enables real-time presentation of vibration signals and diagnostic outcomes. This work demonstrates a reliable and scalable route for intelligent, autonomous substation monitoring—effectively bridging vibration sensing, intelligent diagnostics, and visualization into a unified system.
10.1016/j.cej.2026.179303.title: Self-powered vibration online monitoring of power transformers enabled by triboelectric nanogenerator

10.1016/j.cej.2026.179296.abstract: Fiber-based sensors have attracted extensive attention in wearable electronics owing to their high conductivity, exceptional flexibility and the structural versatility of one-dimensional architectures. Despite significant advancements in hydrogel fiber fabrication techniques, the continuous production of multifunctional conductive hydrogel fibers (CHFs) simultaneously endowed with good mechanical properties, high conductivity, anti-freezing capability, anti-swelling performance, and a broad sensing range remains challenging. In this study, a dynamic crosslinking spinning (DCS) strategy consisting of a two-step photo-crosslinking process and a post-drawing technique was employed to construct a multi-crosslinked composite network structure and further achieve the oriented arrangement of polymer networks, thereby successfully fabricating continuous multifunctional CHFs. The two-step photo-crosslinking process achieved continuous spinning from solution to gel fibers. The post-drawing process induces the alignment of randomly distributed network structure in CHFs along the stretching direction, thereby enhancing their mechanical properties (with a breaking strength of up to 12.62 MPa). Moreover, the incorporation of ionic liquids (ILs) and Zr4+ not only improves the conductivity of CHFs but also endows them with excellent anti-freezing capability (about −45 °C). Furthermore, supramolecular interactions such as hydrogen bonding, electrostatic interactions, and metal coordination bonds within CHFs contribute to their remarkable anti-swelling performance in various solvents. The fiber sensor exhibits a wide detection range (0–1300%) and high sensitivity (gauge factor, GF = 5.29), enabling it to detect human motions and physiological signals such as pulse waves. Additionally, we demonstrate the application of the fiber sensors in human-machine interaction (HMI), as well as for sign language recognition and translation through a deep learning-assisted recognition system.
10.1016/j.cej.2026.179296.title: Multifunctional conductive hydrogel fibers with high stretchability, anti-freezing, and anti-swelling for wearable strain sensors and deep learning-assisted sign language recognition

10.1016/j.cej.2026.179363.abstract: Deep learning-based non-invasive blood pressure (BP) estimation is emerging for cardiovascular disease management, yet it remains constrained by the scarcity of biomedical data and the difficulty of building physiologically faithful training datasets from limited cohorts. In this study, a hybrid framework integrating physiologically grounded PDA-based data augmentation, CNN-LSTM architecture, and MXene-based pseudocapacitive iontronic pressure sensor is presented for BP estimation from radial artery pulse waveforms. The sensor, incorporating MXene electrodes and an ionic liquid/polymer dielectric layer, exhibited high sensitivity (101 kPa−1), fast response time (43 ms), and mechanical durability exceeding 10,000 load cycles. With a high areal capacitance of 161.9 mF/cm2, the sensor enabled stable acquisition of radial artery waveforms. To overcome the data limitations of biomedical research, the proposed simulator was utilized to expand the limited reference cohort within its physiological distribution, enabling the hybrid architecture to jointly learn time-series pulse characteristics and BP features. The model achieved R2 values of 0.907 and 0.904 for systolic and diastolic BP, with mean absolute errors of −2.16 and 2.99 mmHg, respectively. The proposed framework thus offers a physiologically grounded approach to BP estimation that addresses biomedical data limitations, with the potential to be applied to other limited cohorts in clinical and biomedical research.
10.1016/j.cej.2026.179363.title: Hybrid dataset of real-and-simulated pulse waveforms for deep learning-driven blood pressure estimation using MXene-based iontronic sensors

10.1016/j.cej.2026.179339.abstract: Due to the high heterogeneity of substrates and the inherent complexity of enzymatic hydrolysis, the structure–activity relationships governing lignocellulosic saccharification exhibit strong nonlinearity and remain a major prediction bottleneck. In this study, a machine learning framework was developed using a multi-dimensional dataset of 150 lignocellulosic samples to quantify the nonlinear relationships between substrate characteristics and sugar yield. The CatBoost algorithm achieved superior predictive accuracy (R2 > 0.91), outperforming conventional regression models. SHAP analysis identified feedstock origin and cellulose crystallinity as the dominant factors governing hydrolysis kinetics, while Generalized Additive Models revealed optimal operating ranges for each parameter. Critically, the resulting prediction platform enables real-time estimation of enzymatic efficiency for diverse feedstocks. This data-driven approach accelerates the transition from lab-scale biomass conversion to scalable industrial applications in biorefinery.
10.1016/j.cej.2026.179339.title: Machine learning-enabled prediction of enzymatic saccharification of agricultural residues for biorefinery

10.1016/j.cej.2026.179562.abstract: Flexible pressure sensors with porous architectures have attracted extensive attention owing to their excellent stability and sensing performance, demonstrating great potential in applications such as electronic skin and healthcare monitoring. However, most existing sensors are often limited to single-modal signal transduction, and achieving synergistic multifunctionality within a unified signal platform remains a significant challenge. Humidity, as an essential environmental and physiological parameter, plays a vital role in enabling advanced interactive perception. Therefore, integrating high-performance humidity sensing with flexible pressure sensing has emerged as an important research direction. Herein, a polydimethylsiloxane (PDMS) composite foam (PRPP) modified with polypyrrole (PPy), reduced graphene oxide (rGO), and polydopamine (PDA) was fabricated through sequential in-situ polymerization combined with ultrasonication. The PRPP exhibits excellent mechanical resilience (1% plastic deformation after 500 compressions, 0.13 energy loss coefficient at 80% strain), rapid response/recovery time (80 ms/100 ms) and a low detection limit (0.1% strain). Benefiting from the in-situ growth of PPy, PRPP also shows remarkable humidity sensitivity, enabling real-time environmental monitoring. Furthermore, a dual-mode human-machine interface based on a PRPP array is developed for contact pressure sensing and non-contact humidity perception, providing a strategy for flexible sensors in intelligent interactive systems.
10.1016/j.cej.2026.179562.title: Machine learning-enabled bimodal flexible tactile sensors for intelligent contact-noncontact recognition

10.1016/j.cej.2026.179607.abstract: Flavonoids are a key class of natural polyphenols that serve an important role in human health; therefore, their accurate detection is crucial. However, their structural diversity and often low concentrations in complex media make their rapid, ultrasensitive detection and measurement very challenging. To address this concern, a fluorescence-sensing platform using Carbon dots (C-dots) has been developed. In this study, C-dots were synthesised using alginic acid via a hydrothermal approach. The synthesised C-dots exhibited brilliant blue emissions, and various characterisation methods were used to investigate their structure and shape. The fluorescence experiment further showed that the C-dots displayed selective and unique fluorescence quenching in the presence of polyphenol flavonoids (quercetin and rutin), with LODs of 0.0158 nM (15.8 pM) for quercetin and 0.005413 nM (5.413 pM) for rutin, respectively. Quenching behaviour at 360 nm can help identify flavonoid polyphenols, such as quercetin and rutin. Furthermore, Real-time analysis is conducted using red wine and onion juice, demonstrating the practical application of the prepared sensor. Moreover, it was possible to predict flavonoid concentrations with accuracy using a combination of several machine learning algorithms (RF, MLP, and XGBoost) with the sensor array. The Random Forest (RF) technique achieved 94% accuracy, outperforming the others. This increased prediction accuracy demonstrates the utility of these techniques for rapid, sensitive measurement, thereby improving flavonoid quantification.
10.1016/j.cej.2026.179607.title: Machine learning enabled fluorescence sensing platform via alginic acid carbon dots for ultrasensitive polyphenol flavonoid quantification

10.1016/j.cej.2026.179757.abstract: Expanded granular sludge bed (EGSB) reactors employing sulfate-reducing bacteria (SRB) are widely used for treating acid mine drainage (AMD) characterized by low pH, high sulfate, and heavy metal content, owing to their excellent mass transfer efficiency and shock load resistance. However, conventional prediction models typically rely solely on operational and physicochemical parameters to evaluate sulfate removal efficiency, failing to adequately incorporate high-dimensional microbial functional data, which limits both predictive accuracy and mechanistic interpretation. To address these limitations, this study developed an Environment-Biology (EB) integrated model based on 120-day EGSB reactor experimental data, using FAPROTAX functional annotation to reduce the dimensionality of microbial features. This model achieved a prediction R2 of 0.76 for sulfate removal efficiency, representing a 31% improvement over environment-only models. Analysis revealed sulfate metabolism abundance as the most important predictor (42.7% contribution), with C/S ratio and pH jointly regulating the removal process. Furthermore, a staged modeling strategy was implemented: first establishing a predictive model between environmental parameters and sulfate metabolism abundance (R2 = 0.80), then using the predicted abundance as a biological proxy variable alongside environmental parameters in sulfate removal efficiency prediction. The final model achieved comparable performance (R2 = 0.78) to models using directly measured microbial data. This chained modeling approach enables reliable system simulation and optimization without high-throughput sequencing, providing a novel methodology for accurate prediction and control of complex biological treatment systems.
10.1016/j.cej.2026.179757.title: Unveiling microbial sulfate reduction in Acid Mine Drainage Treatment using a Chained Environmental-Microbial machine learning approach

10.1016/j.cej.2026.179531.abstract: Diabetic wound healing necessitates coordinated interactions among diverse cell types within a dynamic microenvironment. However, how biomaterial-based interventions regulate immune-angiogenic-neural responses at single-cell resolution remains poorly understood. In this study, we engineered bio-inspired hydrogels co-delivering neural stem cells (NSCs) and metformin, which promotes pro-regenerative remodeling in diabetic wounds. Single-cell RNA sequencing revealed that the NSC/metformin hydrogel orchestrates a positive immune-angiogenic-neural niche. Our hydrogel formulations actively inhibit excessive NETs formation, promote inflammation resolution, and macrophage-mediated efferocytosis. Simultaneously, they protect endothelial cells from oxidative and mitochondrial stress and modulate the neural phenotypes of Schwann cells. By effectively integrating immune regulation with angiogenesis and neurogenesis, these coordinated actions culminate in significantly improved wound repair in diabetic mice. This work provides a mechanistic framework linking hydrogel-mediated microenvironmental remodeling to functional tissue repair, highlighting a promising therapy for chronic diabetic wounds.
10.1016/j.cej.2026.179531.title: Co-delivery of NSC and metformin for efficient diabetic wound healing via coordination of immune-angiogenic-neural networks

10.1016/j.cej.2026.179924.abstract: The pharmaceutical industry's transition towards smart manufacturing is hindered by the challenge of identifying multi-dimensional Critical Quality Attributes (CQAs) and integrating heterogeneous sensing data into actionable insights. To bridge the gap between data abundance and information scarcity, this study introduces a Systematic Quality Data (SQD) engineering framework that unifies three core dimensions: functionalization, visualization, and digitization. This framework was realized through a data-driven interactive diagnostic system for manufacturing artificial calculus bovis. Specifically, four novel high electron mobility transistor (HEMT) biosensors were developed to achieve functional characterization of CQAs. Simultaneously, a cross-scale imaging and chemical quantification system was employed to extend CQAs analysis from conventional 2D space into high-resolution 3D digital space. These efforts produced a comprehensive multi-modal dataset of over 1.3 million data points, capturing measurement-level feature richness across 30 independent industrial batches. To overcome data fragmentation, a progressive multimodal fusion strategy was designed, integrating disparate physical, chemical, and biological indicators into a unified diagnostic model. Results show that this SQD-based fusion strategy significantly outperforms single-modality approaches in detecting process instabilities and batch anomalies, thereby improving the sensitivity of anomaly screening in industrial practice. This work offers a scalable theoretical and technical solution for systematic quality control and advanced digital management of complex pharmaceutical systems.
10.1016/j.cej.2026.179924.title: A data-driven multimodal diagnostic framework for quality evaluation of artificial calculus bovis based on HEMT biosensors and systematic quality data engineering
10.1016/j.cej.2026.179924.source: ScienceDirect official citation and abstract BibTeX export

10.1016/j.cej.2026.179936.abstract: Plants maintain continuous gaseous exchange with their surroundings, and the volatile organic compounds (VOCs) they emit can act as indicators of plant physiological status. As an important plant organ, fruit maintains active physiological metabolism, including during the postharvest stage. Therefore, the detection of volatile compounds in postharvest fruits can be used to evaluate the quality and monitor their spoilage during storage and transportation. However, current gas detection instruments are mostly benchtop devices that are bulky and costly, making them unsuitable for practical industrial applications. Thus, developing gas-based rapid maturation assessment technologies for fruits is growing increasingly essential. In this study, we developed an intelligent monitoring system for fruit ripening process monitoring, with mangoes chosen as the research subject. Specifically, ethylene, ethanol, ethyl acetate and dipentene were identified as four target gases based on the detection results of VOCs released by mangoes during storage via solid-phase microextraction combined with gas chromatography–mass spectrometry. To detect these signals, a 4-sensor array was constructed using SnO2 nanospheres functionalized with palladium nanoparticles, leveraging resistance variations to capture the dynamics of gases. Density functional theory calculations and comprehensive characterization were employed to elucidate the sensing mechanism. The Tabular Prior-data Fitted Network, a Transformer-based deep learning model, was used to analyze four target gases and their multicomponent mixtures. This method achieved high-precision classification (94.8%) for the gases and their mixtures, as well as accurate concentration regression (R2 = 0.839) for the target components. Finally, the system was integrated into a portable platform, enabling the on-site identification of mango maturity across different storage durations. This work establishes a robust framework for sensor design and intelligent fruit quality monitoring.
10.1016/j.cej.2026.179936.title: Deep learning-assisted chemiresistive sensor arrays for postharvest maturity identification via fruit-emitted mixed gas monitoring
10.1016/j.cej.2026.179936.source: ScienceDirect official citation and abstract BibTeX export

10.1016/j.cej.2026.179912.abstract: Low-concentration acetone detection is important for environmental monitoring, industrial safety, and non-invasive breath analysis, but conventional ZnO-based sensors often suffer from limited response and slow kinetics at low operating temperatures. Herein, porous ZnO/Co₃O₄ composite nanofibers were prepared by electrospinning followed by thermal calcination, with controlled Co/Zn molar ratios to regulate surface oxygen chemistry and heterointerfacial charge modulation. The optimized CZ-2 sensor exhibited the best acetone-sensing performance at 150 °C, delivering a high response of 66 toward 50 ppm acetone, a low estimated detection limit of 11 ppb, and fast response/recovery times of 10/36 s. The sensor also showed good selectivity, stable operation over 100 days with response fluctuation within 6%, and repeatable response over 50 consecutive cycles with fluctuation within 5%. Structural and electronic analyses indicate that the enhanced performance arises from the combined effects of porous one-dimensional transport channels, defect-related/adsorbed oxygen species, and ZnO/Co₃O₄ p–n heterointerfaces. These heterointerfaces amplify gas-induced resistance modulation while preserving ZnO-dominated n-type conduction. In addition, machine-learning analysis based on transient sensing features enabled effective discrimination of multiple volatile organic compounds, with the random forest model achieving approximately 96.0% accuracy. This work demonstrates an interface-engineered ZnO/Co₃O₄ nanofiber platform for sensitive low-temperature acetone detection and data-assisted gas recognition.
10.1016/j.cej.2026.179912.title: Porous ZnO/Co₃O₄ nanofibers for low-temperature ppb-level acetone sensing and machine learning-assisted VOC discrimination
10.1016/j.cej.2026.179912.source: ScienceDirect official citation and abstract BibTeX export

10.1016/j.cej.2026.180082.abstract: Global challenges in water scarcity, environmental pollution, and industrial decarbonization demand materials innovation faster than trial-and-error approaches can provide. Membrane technologies enable energy-efficient separations for water treatment, chemical recovery, and resource extraction. However, data-driven membrane design remains constrained because critical synthesis–structure–performance knowledge is embedded in unstructured literature rather than structured datasets. Here we present an interpretable framework integrating large language models (LLMs) with knowledge graphs (KGs) to recover and organize latent procedural knowledge. The workflow combines PDF parsing, schema-guided LLM extraction, semantic consolidation of extracted entities, frequency-based selection of KG-derived descriptors, predictive modeling, SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) analysis, and graph-topology interpretation. Using pervaporation membranes as a representative example, we constructed a pervaporation KG from 342 peer-reviewed articles, comprising 796 canonical nodes and 282 directed relationships. The KG-derived descriptors were integrated with expert-curated features for predictive modeling. The hybrid model reduced the root-mean-square error from 0.811 to 0.640 for separation-factor prediction and from 0.577 to 0.495 for total-flux prediction. SHAP-based interpretation identified synthesis and processing parameters, including crosslinker ratio, drying temperature, and polymerization degree, as influential predictors that are commonly omitted from conventional datasets. In a temporally separated set of 22 pervaporation studies published in 2025, high-importance features appeared at an average frequency of 16.02%, compared with 5.89% for low-importance features (P = 0.0001), indicating alignment with experimental priorities. We further developed an interactive web platform for real-time KG exploration and on-demand analysis of uploaded publications. This framework provides a scalable approach for transforming unstructured literature into structured, interpretable knowledge for data-driven materials discovery.
10.1016/j.cej.2026.180082.title: Literature-derived knowledge graphs powered by large language models for mechanism-informed membrane design
10.1016/j.cej.2026.180082.source: ScienceDirect official citation and abstract BibTeX export

10.1016/j.cej.2026.179818.abstract: Nanospheres hold strong promise as drug-delivery carriers but face challenges in precisely achieving target particle sizes required for specific biomedical applications. Here, we present a novel strategy that leverages the synergy between Design of Experiments (DoE) and Machine Learning (ML) to optimize and predict poly(lactic-co-glycolic acid) (PLGA) nanosphere synthesis in a continuous ultrasonic microreactor. DoE screening and optimization were first performed to maximize information gain while minimizing experimental runs, generating 41 statistically designed experiments for ML model training. Hyperparameters of five traditional ML models and one deep learning model were then systematically optimized using this dataset. To independently evaluate model performance, 12 additional experiments were conducted to assess predictive accuracy and computational efficiency. Among all models, k-nearest neighbours achieved the highest accuracy (R-sq = 0.92) with the shortest computation time. Overall, this work demonstrates an efficient DoE-ML framework for rapid, accurate, and data-driven tuning of nanosphere size for nanomedicine applications.
10.1016/j.cej.2026.179818.title: Optimizing PLGA nanosphere synthesis in a continuous ultrasonic microreactor: A design of experiments and machine learning joint approach

10.1016/j.cej.2026.180228.abstract: To clarify the individual and coupled roles of multi-walled carbon nanotube (MWCNT) incorporation and water-induced porosity in triboelectric sensing and address the challenge of wearable human action recognition with limited training data, a porous MWCNT/polydimethylsiloxane (PDMS)-based triboelectric nanogenerator (PMP-TENG) was developed. The effects of MWCNT concentration and deionized (DI) water addition on triboelectric output and pressure-sensing performance were systematically investigated. Based on the overall performance, the PMP-TENG containing 0.75 wt% MWCNTs and 12.5 wt% DI water was selected. The device operated over 3–200 kPa and exhibited normalized sensitivities of 0.0581 and 0.109 kPa−1 at 3–70 and 70–200 kPa, respectively. Comparative dielectric, mechanical, and sensing analyses showed that MWCNT incorporation enhanced dielectric polarization, output amplitude, and effective force-response range, whereas DI-water-induced porosity reduced the apparent compressive modulus, increased compressive deformability, and promoted the force-dependent evolution of the effective contact area, thereby improving low-force sensitivity and delaying response saturation. Their cooperative effects enabled the PMP-TENG to maintain relatively high triboelectric output while enhancing pressure sensitivity and sensing range. The device also exhibited frequency-independent voltage responses and stable output over more than 20,000 cycles. When mounted on the hand, multiple PMP-TENGs generated graded voltage responses to different finger and wrist movements. Using a random forest classifier, nine representative hand actions were recognized with mean test accuracies of 99.58% and 96.67% using 220 and 18 training samples, respectively. These results demonstrate the potential of the PMP-TENG for self-powered pressure sensing and machine-learning-assisted hand action recognition with limited training data.
10.1016/j.cej.2026.180228.title: Water-induced porous MWCNT/PDMS-based triboelectric nanogenerator for small-sample machine learning-assisted hand action recognition
10.1016/j.cej.2026.180228.source: ScienceDirect official citation and abstract BibTeX export

10.1016/j.cej.2026.180220.abstract: Fecal sludge (FS) contains recoverable organic matter, nitrogen, and phosphorus alongside pathogens, antibiotic resistance genes (ARGs), microplastics, and micropollutants. FS treatment technologies are often evaluated as isolated unit operations, obscuring how phase partitioning governs resource recovery and residual risks. This review summarizes current evidences within a phase-specific resource–risk framework integrating solid–liquid separation, stream-specific valorization, terminal hazard mitigation, safety verification, and data-driven control. Primary separation generally concentrates particulate organic matters, phosphorus, particle-associated pathogens, intracellular ARGs, microplastics, and hydrophobic micropollutants in the solid fraction, whereas the liquid fraction contains ammonium, soluble organic matters, free viral particles, extracellular ARGs, and hydrophilic contaminants. This partitioning establishes distinct treatment priorities. Anaerobic digestion enables biogas recovery, composting produces soil amendments, and liquid-phase processes target nutrient recovery and contaminant removal. However, biological treatment alone cannot reliably eliminate pathogens, ARGs, or persistent micropollutants. Process intensification can improve resource conversion, whereas advanced oxidation processes and thermochemical treatments can strengthen hazard attenuation but may increase energy and reagent demand, generate byproducts, or reduce agronomic value. Treatment trains should therefore align phase-specific recovery objectives with multiple safety endpoints. Data-driven models may support adaptive operation by linking process variables to resource recovery, hazard attenuation, and product quality, but FS-specific datasets, sensor reliability, model transferability, and full-scale validation remain limited. This framework supports risk-informed treatment-train design for safer resource recovery.
10.1016/j.cej.2026.180220.title: Fecal sludge treatment for resource recovery and biological hazard control: Phase partitioning, process intensification, and data-driven optimization
10.1016/j.cej.2026.180220.source: ScienceDirect official citation and abstract BibTeX export

10.1016/j.cej.2026.180141.abstract: It is of great significance to detect fatty acids odors and assess its effect on cardiomyocytes. Herein, a biomimetic olfactory sensor was constructed using primary cardiomyocytes as biosensitive materials and the microelectrode array as the transducer for the quantitative detection of fatty acids odors. The endogenous olfactory receptor OR51E1 was verified by RT-qPCR and the immunofluorescence staining in primary cardiomyocytes. Five fatty acids odors were selected from potential ligands of OR51E1 and tested by the cardiomyocytes-based biomimetic olfactory sensor. These odors can reduce the firing signals of cardiomyocytes, including decanoic acid, 4-methylnonanoic acid, nonanoic acid, heptanoic acid and pentanoic acid. The detectable threshold concentrations of five odors were determined to be 10 μM, 40 μM, 10 μM 10 μM, 10 μM, respectively. After removing each odor, the firing signals of cardiomyocytes can recover to some extent in 12 min, the average values of the recovery rate reached 85.21%, 60.96%, 80.53%, 93.47% and 108.03%, respectively. Moreover, silencing OR51E1 of cardiomyocytes further confirmed that OR51E1 played a crucial role in the specific recognition of fatty acid odors. Different odors were successfully classified and predicted by supervised learning discrimination calculation-support vector machine (DC-SVM), with the average accuracy rate of 92.97 ± 2.42% and an average AUC of 97.64%. In conclusion, the biomimetic olfactory sensor was successfully developed for the detection and discrimination of fatty acid odors with the aid of DC-SVM, which has great prospects for the drug screening in cardiovascular diseases.
10.1016/j.cej.2026.180141.title: DC-SVM-based analysis of responsive signals from a biomimetic olfactory sensor for assessing the effect of fatty acids odors on cardiomyocytes
10.1016/j.cej.2026.180141.source: ScienceDirect official citation and abstract BibTeX export

10.1016/j.cej.2026.180254.abstract: While nanozyme sensor arrays are capable of simultaneously recognizing and quantifying various target analytes, boosting the catalytic activity of nanozymes to improve their sensing performance still represents a critical technical challenge. Herein, we discovered that two laccase mediators (HBT, 4-PA) with N-OH functional groups can distinctly promote the laccase-like (LAC) behavior of copper-based nanozymes (SA-Cu, TA-Cu), thus elevating the catalytic efficiency toward diverse phenolic acids (PAs). According to the above fascinating experimental findings, an innovative mediator-boosted four-channel nanozyme sensor array (2 nanozymes × 2 mediators = 4 sensing channels) was established, enabling the effective discrimination of seven PAs. Furthermore, by optimizing multiple machine learning (ML) models, the precision of the concentration-independent categorization system built on this array was boosted from 43.56% to 100%, facilitating the discrimination of unknown samples. Ultimately, with the adoption of the Visual Geometry Group 16 (VGG-16) model, an intelligent sensor platform assisted by ML was additionally constructed to enhance the practicability of the recognition of PAs. The present research is not only carries great significance for promoting the recognition of PAs in complicated samples, but also opens up innovative directions for enhancing the catalytic activity of LAC nanozymes.
10.1016/j.cej.2026.180254.title: Deep learning-assisted mediator-regulated copper-based nanozyme sensor array for visual on-site identification of phenolic acids
10.1016/j.cej.2026.180254.source: ScienceDirect official citation and abstract BibTeX export

10.1016/j.cej.2026.180445.abstract: Rapid and accurate detection of single-nucleotide polymorphisms (SNPs) is essential for personalized medicine and infectious disease surveillance. Although loop-mediated isothermal amplification (LAMP) provides outstanding speed and sensitivity, the highly concatenated and heterogeneous structure of LAMP amplicons has historically limited reliable probe-based melting curve analysis for SNPS discrimination. Here, we present a robust LAMP–Melting platform that exploits the intrinsic “DNA breathing” dynamics of LAMP amplicons to enable allele-specific genotyping without reliance on predefined loop regions or complex strand-displacement probe designs. After isothermal amplification, transient dissociation–rehybridization fluctuations allow fluorescent probes to intermittently access nominally double-stranded target regions, generating distinct and reproducible melting fingerprints for single-base variants. Using this mechanism-driven strategy, we successfully genotyped the human MTHFR C677T polymorphism and the SARS-CoV-2 D614G mutation with high analytical sensitivity, achieving limits of detection of 1 ng/μL for gDNA and 10 RNA copies per reaction. To address the biochemical complexity and signal heterogeneity inherent to isothermal amplification products, a XGBoost–based machine-learning framework was integrated to suppress artifacts and enhance melting curve classification. Moreover, the assay exhibits excellent compatibility with lyophilized reagents and portable fluorescence detection instruments, enabling a one-pot, closed-tube workflow suitable for decentralized and point-of-care testing. Collectively, this work redefines probe–amplicon interactions in isothermal systems by shifting from static hybridization to dynamic, fluctuation-enabled recognition and establishes a versatile, mechanism-guided framework for next-generation molecular diagnostics.
10.1016/j.cej.2026.180445.title: Machine-learning assisted one-tube LAMP melting analysis for SNPs genotyping
10.1016/j.cej.2026.180445.source: ScienceDirect official citation and abstract BibTeX export

10.1016/j.cej.2026.180440.abstract: Timely and accurate freshness assessment of aquatic products with complex matrices remains significant challenge. Hypoxanthine (Hx)-based monitoring methods using colorimetric sensing with smartphone are widely used but affected by variable lighting conditions throughout the food supply chain, causing detection results remain inaccurate. Here, a colorimetric/photothermal dual-mode Hx detection and freshness prediction platform was constructed by cascading a thermostable 2D Fe/Ni-MOF nanosheet with xanthine oxidase, enabling stable and sensitive on-site detection of Hx. A linear response to Hx was exhibited in the range of 0.2–100 μM, with detection limits of 0.12 μM (colorimetric mode) and 4.21 μM (photothermal mode), respectively. To address ambient lighting effects, seven lighting conditions (∼50, ∼100, ∼500, ∼1000, ∼5000, ∼10,000, and ∼50,000 lx) were simulated to construct a dataset integrating lighting, colorimetric, and photothermal information for the model training and testing. A light-adaptive multimodal fusion network based on YOLOv11 and Multi-Layer Perceptron (MLP) achieved a prediction accuracy of 98% in freshness classification, remarkably higher than that of the single colorimetric (89%) and photothermal (93%) modes, when trained on 4536 labeled images and 108 photothermal data points, demonstrating strong robustness under complex and varying lighting conditions. Coupled with the self-developed “Food Track” application, this work not only provides a practical and reliable approach for the early freshness prediction in aquatic products, but also highlights the potential of multimodal fusion algorithms to handle lighting variations in food supply chains.
10.1016/j.cej.2026.180440.title: A colorimetric and photothermal dual-mode nanozyme platform: Multimodal deep learning guided real-time freshness sensing and predicting of aquatic products under challenging lighting conditions
10.1016/j.cej.2026.180440.source: ScienceDirect official citation and abstract BibTeX export

10.1016/j.cej.2026.180241.abstract: The diagnosis of pathogens is often challenged by their etiological diversity and overlapping clinical presentations, highlighting an urgent need for high-performance Point-of-Care Testing (POCT) platforms in resource-limited settings. To address this, microfluidic platforms provide an ideal foundation by automating complex biochemical processes at the microscale, while nanozymes—acting as stable and designable alternatives to natural enzymes—serve as powerful signal amplifiers. This review presents a comprehensive landscape of nanozyme-enhanced microfluidic systems, with a specific emphasis on the emerging role of Artificial Intelligence (AI) in overcoming the inefficiencies of traditional trial-and-error design paradigms. We first classify microfluidic architectures based on their liquid propulsion mechanisms, covering continuous-flow, centrifugal, paper-based, and digital microfluidics. Subsequently, we elucidate the catalytic mechanisms of nanozymes and their diverse signal transduction pathways. Then, the discussion focuses on AI's role in empowering system design and intelligent pathogen detection, including architecture optimization, nanozyme engineering, and signal readout. Finally, we summarize current applications and future perspectives, aiming to provide a valuable reference for the development of next-generation diagnostic tools.
10.1016/j.cej.2026.180241.title: Artificial intelligence-driven nanozyme-enhanced microfluidic systems for pathogen diagnostics: Current status and future perspectives
10.1016/j.cej.2026.180241.source: ScienceDirect official citation and abstract BibTeX export

10.1016/j.cej.2026.180463.abstract: Organic thermofluorochromic materials (TFMs) hold great promise for large-area, flexible thermal indication and anti-counterfeiting, yet their utility at high temperatures is severely hindered by poor solid-state thermofluorochromism, inaccurate temperature readout, and severe thermal quenching. Herein, we report three heat-resistant TFM films based on distinct thermochromic mechanisms: stepwise stacking modulation with delayed fluorescence and nonadiabatic vibrational coupling (tBu-DHPPO), high-barrier tautomerization (HBT-TPA), and suppression of energy transfer in their hybrids (tBu-DHPPO/HBT-TPA). Leveraging their enhanced thermal robustness, these TFM films deliver outstanding thermometric performance across a wide temperature range (20–300 °C), exhibiting high maximum relative sensitivities of 2.46, 5.87 and 2.49% °C−1 above 150 °C and remarkable optimal temperature resolutions of 0.05–1.07, 0.21–1.26, and 0.05–1.01 °C, respectively. By integrating these three cross-validated TFMs with machine learning, we established a smartphone-based optical readout platform that achieves ultrahigh-accuracy temperature prediction, with a near-perfect coefficient of determination (R2) of 0.99997 and a low root-mean-square error (RMSE) of 0.4682 °C. Furthermore, these TFM films enable naked-eye, non-invasive thermal imaging, patterning, and anti-counterfeiting encryption under ambient conditions. These findings demonstrate a new strategy that bridges multiple robust thermofluorochromic films and accessible machine learning, paving the way for next-generation intelligent thermal reading and anti-counterfeiting systems.
10.1016/j.cej.2026.180463.title: Thermofluorochromic materials via distinct mechanisms for machine learning-enhanced triple cross-validated accurate high-temperature prediction and advanced anti-counterfeiting encryption

10.1016/j.cej.2026.180606.abstract: The strength–toughness trade-off limits the simultaneous enhancement of mechanical and bonding properties in epoxy resins, while traditional trial-and-error approaches yield only incremental improvements with low efficiency and fail to decipher the underlying structure–property relationships. Herein, an integrated data-driven multiscale paradigm was proposed to address the above challenges, which integrates experimental design, machine learning, and multi-objective optimization. Through systematic formulation design, precise control over the phase-separated domain sizes of epoxy thermosets with polyhedral oligomeric silsesquioxane-capped poly(ε-caprolactone)s (POSS-PCLn) was achieved across nearly three orders of magnitude, spanning from nano- to submicro- and micro-scales, thereby constructing a high-quality dataset. By combining interpretable machine learning with multi-objective optimization, phase-separated domains in the 100–600 nm range were identified for the first time as optimal for toughening. Moreover, POSS-PCLn synergistically improved bonding strength through a combination of toughening and interfacial compatibility mechanisms. Guided by these mechanistic insights, enabling maximum bonding strength of 40.1 MPa (47% improvement) and maximum fracture toughness of 1.74 MPa·m1/2 (145% improvement), the formulation with optimally balanced performance simultaneously achieved fracture toughness of 1.31 MPa m1/2, tensile strength of 73.6 MPa, and bonding strength of 31.7 MPa, outperforming most reported epoxy systems in terms of both single-property extremes and comprehensive performance. This integrated paradigm not only elucidates the multiscale structure–property relationships, but also achieves significant performance enhancement, providing a generalizable strategy for the rational design of high-performance polymers.
10.1016/j.cej.2026.180606.title: Unlocking multiscale structure-property relationships in epoxy thermosets: A machine learning-driven approach to superior multi-objective performance
10.1016/j.cej.2026.180606.source: ScienceDirect official citation and abstract BibTeX export

10.1016/j.cej.2026.180789.abstract: The high toxicity and persistence of anthropogenic organic compounds (AOCs) in water environments pose a serious threat to water body environmental safety, which has become an urgent problem to be solved in current wastewater treatment. However, due to the limitations of the forward osmosis (FO) membrane itself and the physicochemical properties of the water environment, as well as the limited experimental data set, accurately predicting and regulating the non-linear transport behavior of these organic compounds still faces significant challenges. To solve this problem, we deployed a TabPFN-2.5 framework, which leverages a prior-trained Transformer architecture for zero-shot tabular inference, evaluated on an experimental FO dataset (N = 616). The test results demonstrate superior performance compared to the integrated model (test R2 = 0.90, RMSE = 6.90%), significantly reducing the burden of empirical parameterization. More importantly, this study has also constructed a multi-level interpretable machine learning architecture to quantitatively decouple the boundary between molecular size exclusion and electrostatic repulsion: there is a S-shaped spatial steric hindrance threshold at 210–220 Da for molecules, and a critical electrostatic barrier failure point occurs when the Zeta potential is close to −4 mV. Through high-throughput virtual screening, the study establishes a multi-objective Pareto-optimal frontier for balancing water flux and rejection rate, providing practical operational benchmarks for advanced FO systems. This work bridges the gap between machine learning-based abstract representations and conventional membrane physics mechanisms, offering a systematic methodological reference for data-driven design of highly selective forward osmosis membranes.
10.1016/j.cej.2026.180789.title: Data-driven prediction of organic rejection in forward osmosis: Incorporating hydrophobic and dynamic transport effects

10.1016/j.cej.2026.180921.abstract: Flexible neural electrodes can reduce mechanical mismatch, but their chronic use remains limited by high interfacial impedance, coating instability, and difficult deep-brain insertion. Here, we report a polyimide-based 3D helical neural electrode integrating Pt/PEDOT:PSS interface modification and a low-dose silk-fibroin (SF)-doped polyethylene glycol (PEG) transient support coating. Sequential Pt/PEDOT:PSS deposition reduced the 1 kHz impedance from 1.93 MΩ to 24 kΩ (98.7%) and increased the charge-storage capacity by 23.5-fold. After 2000 cyclic-voltammetry cycles, the composite-modified electrodes showed a 22.6% impedance increase, compared with 129.4% for PEDOT:PSS-only electrodes. Helical devices retained stable impedance and phase responses after 2000 cycles of 10% tensile strain. Among all tested formulations, PEG/SF (50:1) achieved a 60.8% increase in critical buckling force and maintained a force above 0.8 N after 20 s of immersion in phosphate-buffered saline (PBS), with no detectable in vitro cytotoxicity observed. Pure-PEG-coated probes were implanted in M1 and PEG:SF-coated probes in CA1; because coating formulation and brain target were varied together, these experiments are presented as separate feasibility demonstrations rather than a direct coating comparison. Whisker stimulation elicited region-specific LFP responses. Over 120 days of chronic implantation, the electrodes retained stable impedance, steady signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) of 5.5–6.5 dB, and intact single-unit waveforms. These findings validate the effectiveness of our integrated strategy for electrochemical stabilization, structural compliance improvement, and transient insertion assistance.
10.1016/j.cej.2026.180921.title: Pt/PEDOT:PSS modification and SF-doped PEG transient coating of helical neural electrodes for deep-brain implantation and long-term stable recording

10.1016/j.cej.2026.180875.abstract: Spinal cord injury (SCI) is refractory mainly because persistent inflammation and glial scarring disrupt the local regenerative microenvironment and limit neural stem cell (NSC)-mediated tissue repair. To address this challenge, we engineered a glial-Scar-Responsive Peptide-Modified Lipid Nanoparticle (SRP-LNP) for targeted delivery of interleukin-10 mRNA (IL-10 mRNA) to lesion sites, aiming to regulate the inflammatory-regenerative microenvironment after SCI. The constructed SRP-LNP@IL-10 exhibited favorable physicochemical stability and enhanced cellular uptake. In vitro, SRP-LNP@IL-10 effectively inhibited macrophage M1 polarization and improved the inflammatory microenvironment; in immune-NSC co-culture models, it promoted NSC proliferation and neural-lineage differentiation while suppressing glial differentiation. In a rat contusion SCI model, combinatory therapy with SRP-LNP@IL-10 and NSCs attenuated inflammation and CSPG deposition, increased BDNF, NF200, and MBP expression, and improved motor function. Integrated transcriptomic, proteomic, and metabolomic analyses suggested that this system regulates inflammation and neural regeneration through the STAT3-SOCS3-BDNF signaling axis and energy-metabolism remodeling. Multi-omics and Transwell separation validation further indicated that SRP-LNP@IL-10 mainly reshaped macrophage SOCS3/Arg1/iNOS immune responses and promoted BDNF/Tuj1/GFAP-associated neural differentiation programs in NSCs. Overall, SRP-LNP@IL-10 provides a potential RNA-nano-cell combinatorial strategy for targeting the inflammatory microenvironment and promoting SCI repair.
10.1016/j.cej.2026.180875.title: SRP-LNP@IL-10 nanotherapy combined with neural stem cells couples inflammation suppression with neural regeneration after spinal cord injury via the STAT3-SOCS3-BDNF axis

10.1016/j.cej.2026.180769.abstract: Water-induced adhesion failure and swelling compromise the viability of conventional hydrogel electrodes for long-term muscle fatigue monitoring under dynamic and humid conditions. To address these limitations, we report an anti-swelling Janus hydrogel with an asymmetric architecture that simultaneously ensures robust interfacial adhesion and high signal fidelity. The design comprises an adhesive layer of acrylic acid (AA) and lauryl methacrylate (LMA) copolymer with incorporated poly(vinyl alcohol) (PVA) and a non-adhesive layer of pure PVA. Freezing initiates PVA microcrystallization to form the primary network, while subsequent heat annealing further densifies microcrystal formation at the interface. Crucially, the synergistic hydrophobic association and dense physical cross-linking restrict the swelling ratio to below 7% to prevent network dilution. The dynamic hydrogen bonding yields a robust interfacial adhesion of 67 kPa on skin to minimize motion artifacts. This dual stability directly translates into an exceptional initial signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) of 31 dB (versus 22 dB for commercial alternatives) and a sustained SNR of 25 dB even after a 30-day immersion period. When coupled with a Gradient Boosting Decision Tree algorithm, the acquired signals support autonomous muscle fatigue classification with 92.6% accuracy. This anti-swelling Janus strategy establishes a reliable material-algorithm interface for long-term wearable electromyography.
10.1016/j.cej.2026.180769.title: Anti-swelling Janus hydrogels enable long-term muscle fatigue monitoring via machine learning-assisted signal analysis

10.1016/j.cej.2026.181092.abstract: While vacuum pressure swing adsorption (VPSA) provides a simple and energy-efficient route for removing trace CO from hydrogen to produce high-purity H2 for fuel cell applications, the coupling of kinetic and thermodynamic effects under multi-component competitive adsorption compromises adsorbent bed utilization and separation efficiency. Herein, an active learning-assisted strategy was proposed for optimizing the VPSA process by decoupling thermodynamic and kinetic parameters to achieve ultra-deep CO removal (<0.05 ppmv) from a multi-component gas mixture (N2/CH4/CO/CO2/Ar/H2). A new optimized composite bed consisting of activated carbon, zeolite 13×, and zeolite 5 A was explored to enhance adsorption performance using an artificial neural network model. The reliability of the model was further validated through dynamic adsorption and four-bed VPSA experiments on a pilot scale, in which CO was successfully reduced to below 0.062 ppmv from mixture gas containing 1000 ppmv CO. To further clarify the influence of the other impurities, a six-bed VPSA model was established, and active learning was employed to optimize the operating parameters for evaluating CO separation performance. Based on further multi-objective optimization, a simulation of purified gas with CO less than 0.05 ppmv was achieved under pilot-scale multi-component competitive adsorption conditions. This study provides an effective strategy for the production of fuel cell-grade hydrogen from complex gas mixtures.
10.1016/j.cej.2026.181092.title: Active learning-driven optimization and pilot-scale validation of a composite-bed vacuum pressure swing adsorption process for ultra-deep CO removal from hydrogen

10.1016/j.cej.2026.181118.abstract: Smart textiles for personal microenvironment management face a fundamental trilemma: integrating multimodal sensing, active thermal regulation, and autonomous energy supply without compromising breathability or skin comfort. Conventional additive strategies, such as layer stacking or patching, inevitably lead to interfacial failure, pore occlusion, and heavy reliance on rigid batteries. We bypass these constraints by functionally decoupling these roles across a tri-layered asymmetric Janus nanofibrous membrane, MXene-assisted Janus smart cloth (MJSC). Fabricated via sequential electrospinning, MJSC features a hydrophobic (129°)-to-hydrophilic (26°) gradient that actively pumps sweat unidirectionally while maintaining high air permeability (53.482 cm3 m−2 d−1 Pa−1). By spatially partitioning MXene and partially oxidized MXene (MXO, primarily MXene nanosheet/rutile composites), we engineer an optical asymmetry that enables passive radiative cooling (reflecting up to 91% of the solar spectrum and absorbing up to 96% of the atmospheric window) while capturing energy via a moisture-responsive ionic core. This architecture eliminates external power dependencies by harvesting triboelectric and moisture-electric energy, delivering self-powered signals that a convolutional neural network classifies with over 99% accuracy. Furthermore, the MXO-enriched surface provides photocatalytic self-cleaning, removing over 80% of methylene blue from water within 2 h. MJSC provides a material paradigm for next-generation wearables prioritising both capability and physiological comfort.
10.1016/j.cej.2026.181118.title: Customized MXene integrated Janus membrane for energy-efficient machine learning-assisted sensing and personal microenvironment management

10.1016/j.cej.2026.180900.abstract: Most tumors, such as > 90% of pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) and > 50% of triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC), are immunosuppressive, which are known as cold tumors and derive little benefit from emerging therapies. A photodynamic nanoparticle JFCN was developed to enable cold tumors to profit by immunotherapy, targeted extracellular matrix (ECM) modulation, and photodynamic therapy (PDT) simultaneously. To be more effective in forming three-component nanoparticle, an AI-driven-designed programmed cell death ligand-1 (PD-L1) inhibitor J30 was customized efficiently to self-assemble with photosensitizer Ce6 and fibroblast activation protein (FAP) inhibitor UAMC-1110. Contributed to passive targeting of nanoparticle and active targeting of FAP & PD-L1, JFCN demonstrated precise accumulation at the tumor site and achieved robust inhibition of tumor growth (TGI > 85%) in both orthotopic 4 T1 TNBC model and PADC model (co-implanting Panc02+ NIH3T3 cells). The extracellular matrix (ECM) was remolded by reducing FAP, TGF-β and CXCL12, accompanied with photodynamic-induced immunogenic cell death (ICD) effect, which promoted the infiltration of oxygen and T cells, thereby facilitating PDT and immunotherapy. In addition, JFCN effectively counteracts the upregulation of PD-L1 induced by PDT to overcome adaptive immune resistance. Overall, JFCN, an AI-driven, de novo designed all-in-one nanoplatform, provides a new sight for the refractory cold tumor.
10.1016/j.cej.2026.180900.title: An AI-driven, de novo designed all-in-one nanoplatform for cold tumor therapy

10.1016/j.cej.2026.181086.abstract: With the development of embodied artificial intelligence (EAI) technology, the use of humanoid robots for human care and rehabilitation has demonstrated application feasibility. Among them, the accurate perception and evaluation of the motion performance of humans and humanoid robots is of great importance. As an emerging electromechanical conversion technology, triboelectric nanogenerators (TENGs) have shown extraordinary application potential in high-entropy energy harvesting and intelligent Internet of Things (IoT) sensing. Firstly, the current status of non-TENG motion performance evaluation methods for the human body and robots is analyzed. The deficiencies of existing research and the feasibility of human-robot transfer are clarified. Secondly, a systematic analysis is performed on the typical structures of TENGs for multi-scenario sensing, including joint rotation, tactile and trajectory tracking, inertia and vibration sensing, gait sensing, and grasping and twisting of objects, for both humans and robots. It conducts a detailed analysis of design strategies for various TENG devices, including their operating principles, structural configurations, electrode channel counts, and installation positions, and explores how different designs influence the feasibility and universality of detecting motor performance degradation. Afterward, it analyzes existing TENG-based motion function evaluation systems for upper and lower limbs, as well as complex sports games. Finally, a summary of transferable EAI motion performance evaluation systems for humans and humanoid robots is provided. This review aims to promote the practical application and standardization of TENGs for sensing and evaluating human and robot motion performance.
10.1016/j.cej.2026.181086.title: Triboelectric nanogenerator motion sensing for embodied artificial intelligence: A review of performance evaluation between human and humanoid robots

10.1016/j.cej.2026.181182.abstract: Existing 3D textile-based self-powered pressure sensors often suffer from performance degradation during long-term service, largely limited by porous interface delamination and liquid-phase conductive percolation. To address this, we developed a warp-knitted spacer fabric-based triboelectric pressure sensor (WTPS) and smart insole (WTPS-Insole) via an integrated in-situ coating strategy, ensuring electromechanical stability and lightweight characteristics. By suppressing graphene percolation via polymer rheological confinement, a robust liquid-solid conductive network was constructed, simultaneously inducing a polydimethylsiloxane (PDMS) micro-topological triboelectric layer. This architecture drastically elevates the mechanical robustness, under a 50% compressive strain, the optimized device (at a 65% filling ratio) withstands an ultra-high load of 1416.33 N, representing a 100-fold enhancement. Meanwhile, the WTPS exhibits remarkable environmental adaptability, maintaining up to 98% performance recovery after rigorous washing cycles. Furthermore, a 20-unit smart insole sustained 8000 mechanical cycles with less than 5% thickness loss. The sensing array features ultrafast response and recovery times of 93 ms and 45 ms, respectively. It stably captures signals from conventional gaits (walking, jogging, jumping) and complex spatial maneuvers, including standing-sitting-squatting transitions and 180° turns. By coupling the sensory signals with machine learning algorithms, the system achieves highly accurate predictions of seven distinct locomotive states. Ultimately, this integrated fabrication strategy highlights the immense potential of 3D textile-based self-powered sensors for gait recognition, laying a robust empirical foundation for next-generation wearable sports and health monitoring systems.
10.1016/j.cej.2026.181182.title: Rheological confinement-enabled micro-topological 3D textile triboelectric pressure sensor array for AI-assisted gait monitoring

10.1016/j.cej.2026.181260.abstract: Sophorolipids (SLs) are eco-friendly biosurfactants with broad industrial applications. However, their market competitiveness against conventional fossil-based surfactants is often limited by high production costs associated with first-generation feedstocks. To address this issue, this study investigated the synergistic co-utilisation of food waste hydrolysate (FWH) and waste cooking oil (WCO) as the sole carbon sources for lactonic SL production. Notably, FWH outperformed pure glucose in lactonic SL synthesis, and its available free amino nitrogen (FAN) level was enough for the bioprocess, reducing reliance on external nitrogen supplementation. Furthermore, response surface methodology (RSM) and artificial neural network–genetic algorithm (ANN-GA) models were developed to optimise key fermentation parameters, and their predictive performance was compared. Results showed that, among the tested optimisation routes, the ANN-GA model trained on the extended dataset achieved the lowest optimum-point validation error, with a relative error of 3.7% between the predicted (56.4 g/L) and actual (54.4 g/L) lactonic SL titres. In contrast, ANN-GA trained only on the restricted RSM dataset showed a much higher error (62.5%), highlighting the importance of dataset size in AI-assisted bioprocess optimisation. This study not only demonstrated the full replacement of first-generation carbon sources with waste streams for sustainable biosurfactant production, but also provides broader methodological insights into the integration of experimental data and ANN-GA for complex bioprocess optimisation.
10.1016/j.cej.2026.181260.title: Sustainable bioconversion of food waste and waste cooking oil into Sophorolipids: Process optimisation using Response Surface Methodology (RSM) and Artificial Neural Network–Genetic Algorithm (ANN-GA)

10.1016/j.cej.2026.181350.abstract: Solid oxide electrolysis cells (SOECs) are promising platforms for green hydrogen production, but their performance and durability are affected by heterogeneous electrode microstructures that govern coupled transport and reaction processes. Here, we develop a digital twin framework that integrates microstructural quantification, 1D homogeneous full-cell modeling, and 3D heterogeneous modeling of a region of interest. This framework combines the computational efficiency of 1D modeling with the spatial fidelity of microstructure-resolved 3D modeling, enabling consistent evaluation of both global cell behavior and local electrochemical heterogeneity. As a representative application, LSCF-GDC composite air electrodes with different LSCF:GDC volume ratios were systematically analyzed. The framework quantitatively links phase connectivity, tortuosity, and reaction site density to current density localization, activation overpotential heterogeneity, and electrochemical heat generation. The results reveal that imbalanced compositions induce localized electronic or ionic transport pathways and spatially non-uniform reactions, whereas the near-equimolar composition provides balanced charge transport, reduced activation overpotential heterogeneity, and suppressed heat generation gradients. These findings demonstrate that the proposed framework can resolve microstructure-induced local phenomena that remain hidden in conventional bulk-averaged characterization and homogeneous modeling. The established digital twin framework provides a computationally efficient pathway for microstructure-informed optimization of durable and high-performance SOEC electrodes.
10.1016/j.cej.2026.181350.title: Revisiting local heterogeneity in solid oxide electrolysis cells through a digital twin framework
