10.1016/j.cej.2026.181317.abstract: Surface-enhanced Raman spectroscopy (SERS) is a promising trace detection technique, yet its practical application in environmental pollutant analysis remains severely restricted by insufficient electromagnetic enhancement and weak adsorption capacity toward target analytes. Herein, a novel hybrid SERS substrate with dual electromagnetic enhancement and highly efficient molecular enrichment was facilely fabricated, featuring a hierarchical structure of Au film–poly(ionic liquid) (PIL) nanohole–SiO2 nanosphere–Au nanosphere. In this system, the waveguide optical modes of the Au film–PIL nanohole–SiO2 nanosphere structure induce the primary electromagnetic enhancement, while Au nanospheres are precisely positioned in the primary enhancement regions to deliver a secondary electromagnetic enhancement through localized surface plasmon resonance (LSPR), thereby realizing a high enhancement factor of 2.35 × 107 for pyrene. Meanwhile, PIL nanoholes facilitate specific adsorption and enrichment of polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons (PAHs) within hotspots via the hydrophobic effect and π-π stacking interactions, significantly amplifying the SERS response of analytes. The hybrid substrate exhibits excellent analytical performance, with limits of detection (LODs) as low as 5.33 × 10−10 mol/L for pyrene and 3.97 × 10−10 mol/L for anthracene, respectively. Furthermore, a combined principal component analysis (PCA) and support vector machine (SVM) algorithm was employed to efficiently extract spectral features and reduce data dimensionality, achieving a prediction accuracy exceeding 94% for varying concentrations and species of PAHs in actual river water samples. Taken together, the combination of this hybrid SERS substrate and the PCA-SVM algorithm provides a novel sensing platform, enabling ultrasensitive, accurate, and intelligent trace-level detection of environmental pollutants in complex matrices.
10.1016/j.cej.2026.181317.title: Dual electromagnetic enhancement engineering of hybrid Au film–poly(ionic liquid) nanohole–SiO2 nanosphere–Au nanosphere substrates integrated with machine learning algorithm for ultrasensitive SERS detection
10.1016/j.cej.2026.181317.source: ScienceDirect official citation and abstract BibTeX export

10.1016/j.cej.2026.181473.abstract: Erectile dysfunction (ED) is a prevalent male sexual disorder that often requires nocturnal penile tumescence (NPT) monitoring to differentiate psychogenic from organic ED. However, conventional NPT systems are limited by poor comfort and inadequate suitability for long-term monitoring. Herein, this study developed a wearable penile tumescence (PT) sensor based on a hydrogel, termed PGTBA, for wearable NPT monitoring and auxiliary ED assessment. The hydrogel was fabricated through a freeze–thaw-induced physical crosslinking strategy, forming a porous multicomponent network with electrical conductivity, stretchability, toughness, and intrinsic reprocessability. As a resistive strain sensor, PGTBA exhibited stable electromechanical responses over a broad strain range (0–130%) with a gauge factor of 3.006, together with cyclic stability and deformation tolerance. The sensor enabled real-time monitoring of human motions. In vitro and in vivo evaluations demonstrated favorable cytocompatibility, antibacterial activity, and biosafety. Specially PGTBA supported the survival of L929 fibroblast cells while inhibiting the growth of Staphylococcus aureus and Escherichia coli. In a penile tumescence–detumescence simulation model, the ring-shaped PGTBA sensor generated resistance-response patterns corresponding to normal erection and different ED subtypes. Integrated with support vector machine and XGBoost algorithms, preliminary erectile-state classification was achieved for noninvasive screening and intelligent male reproductive-health management.
10.1016/j.cej.2026.181473.title: A biosafe nano-antimicrobial composite hydrogel sensor for penile erection monitoring and AI-assisted diagnosis
10.1016/j.cej.2026.181473.source: ScienceDirect official citation and abstract BibTeX export

10.1016/j.cej.2026.181611.abstract: Hydrogels serve as flexible sensing materials for robotics or wearable devices. To address the challenges of low mechanical strength, slow response, and poor degradability in conventional hydrogels, a fully physically crosslinked polyelectrolyte hydrogel is designed in this work. Based on hydrophobic association and multiple crosslinking strategies, the polymer backbone is formed by copolymerizing the anionic hydrophilic monomers 2-acrylamido-2-methylpropane sulfonic acid (AMPS) and acrylamide (AM), while the cationic surfactant CTAB is introduced to construct hydrophobic association domains, resulting in a dense physically crosslinked network. Low-field (LF) nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR) spectroscopy and rheology are employed to elucidate the intermolecular interactions and the evolution of heterogeneous network structures within the hydrogel physically crosslinked by hydrophilic chains and CTAB aggregates. The sulfonic acid groups on the polymer chains together with the free H+ concentration within the network not only enhance electrostatic interactions among chains but also increase the internal ionic concentration, thereby establishing efficient pathways for ion transport. The dynamic and reversible physical crosslinking network endows the hydrogel with excellent mechanical properties (strain up to 1644%), fatigue resistance, and rapid response characteristics (response time 55 ms, recovery time 49 ms). Moreover, the fully physically crosslinked network confers good oxidative degradability, effectively avoiding environmental pollution. As a multifunctional flexible platform, the hydrogel enables smart touch control and supercapacitor applications. Furthermore, when integrated with a deep learning system, the sensor achieves handwriting recognition and information extraction with a recognition accuracy as high as 95.2%. This work provides an effective strategy for developing degradable hydrogel sensors that combine fast response with excellent electrical performance.
10.1016/j.cej.2026.181611.title: A fully physically crosslinked hydrogel with high toughness, fast response, and degradability for deep learning-assisted handwriting recognition
10.1016/j.cej.2026.181611.source: ScienceDirect official citation and abstract BibTeX export

10.1016/j.cej.2026.181670.abstract: Solid-state polymer electrolytes (SPEs) are essential components in solid-state Li-polymer batteries, governing ion-transport dynamics. However, SPE design has long relied on empirical trial-and-error, resulting in weak theoretical guidance and low screening efficiency. Herein we report a data-driven approach based on polymer informatics to screen high-performance polymer hosts. A cascade filtering framework is constructed to systematically evaluate five key descriptors across 2488 polymer candidates, efficiently identifying poly (vinylidene fluoride-trifluoroethylene-chlorofluoroethylene) (P(VDF-TrFE-CFE), PVTC) as a potential target. Experimentally, we introduce unsaturated backbone defects into PVTC through controlled dehydrochlorination, reconstructing crystalline-amorphous structural network. As a result, defective PVTC (GPVTC) electrolyte achieves a high room-temperature Li+ transference number of 0.81 and ionic conductivity of 1.64 × 10−3 S cm−1. The remarkable ionic conductivity arises from refined nanocrystalline domains and enhanced microdomain polarization, which promote Li-salt dissociation and lower activation energy barrier of Li+ migration. Graphite|GPVTC|LiFePO4 battery delivers 154.3 mAh g−1 at 0.1C and retains 62.8% of its initial capacity at 5C. Graphite|GPVTC|Li(Ni0.8Co0.1Mn0.1)O2 battery also delivers 204.3 mAh g−1 at 0.1C and retains 64.3% of its initial capacity at 5C. These results guide the design of solid-state polymer electrolytes for high-rate solid-state Li-ion batteries.
10.1016/j.cej.2026.181670.title: Data-driven screening and defect engineering of fluorine-rich polymer electrolytes for high-rate solid-state Li-ion batteries

10.1016/j.cej.2026.181890.abstract: Detection of trace hydrogen sulfide (H₂S) is important for environmental monitoring and breath-based disease diagnostics, yet achieving strong ppb-level signal modulation and reliable gas discrimination remains challenging for conventional metal oxide sensors. Herein, MOF-derived NiO-Fe₂O₃ composites were synthesized by thermal conversion of Ni-incorporated Fe-BDC precursors to construct porous heterostructured sensing materials. The MOF template provides a hierarchical porous architecture that promotes gas diffusion and exposes abundant reactive sites, while controlled Ni incorporation generates dispersed NiO domains and p-n heterojunction interfaces with Fe₂O₃. Structural, spectroscopic, and electrochemical analyses support the formation of NiO-Fe₂O₃ composites with composition-dependent electronic interactions and modified interfacial charge transport. Gas-sensing measurements reveal a volcano-type composition dependence, with the composite prepared at a nominal Ni:Fe molar ratio of 0.05 delivering the best H₂S sensing performance. At 175 °C, this optimized composite exhibits a high response of 42% toward 5000 ppb H₂S, detectable transient signals below 20 ppb, and fast response/recovery times of 2.1/20.1 s. The sensor also shows good selectivity, repeatability, long-term stability, humidity tolerance, and proof-of-concept discrimination between healthy breath and H₂S-spiked simulated breath. Furthermore, a machine-learning-assisted multi-scale temporal representation framework was developed to improve single-sensor gas discrimination. By integrating multi-scale dynamic features with correlation-based descriptors, the framework improves gas classification under the present controlled testing conditions, as validated by feature-space visualization, confusion matrices, and ROC curves. The enhanced performance is likely associated with the synergistic effects of MOF-derived porosity, defect−/adsorbed‑oxygen-enriched surface chemistry, and heterojunction-induced band modulation.
10.1016/j.cej.2026.181890.title: MOF-derived porous NiO-Fe₂O₃ heterostructures with machine-learning-assisted signal discrimination for ppb-level H₂S detection and breath analysis

10.1016/j.cej.2026.181967.abstract: Stable implantable neural interfaces require implantable electrodes that combine electrochemical stability, tissue compatibility, and durable interfacial integration. Platinum‑iridium (PtIr) electrodes are widely used owing to their conductivity, chemical stability, and biocompatibility, but their planar metal/electrolyte interface limits the electrochemically active area and ion-accessible charge storage. Although poly(3,4-ethylenedioxythiophene): poly(styrenesulfonate) (PEDOT:PSS) coating can improve these properties, its retention on metallic substrates remains challenging under prolonged mechanical and electrochemical stress. Here, we present a femtosecond-laser-enabled interfacial volume engineering strategy that introduces graded internal microhole arrays into PtIr electrode sites before PEDOT:PSS electrodeposition. The microholes provide internal deposition volumes that accommodate and geometrically confine PEDOT:PSS, converting a conventional surface coating into a three-dimensional polymer–metal interface. The optimized electrodes show enhanced charge storage capacity of 65.20 mC·cm−2 and charge injection limit of 9.55 mC·cm−2, while exhibiting improved functional retention during mechanical testing and accelerated aging. Furthermore, in vivo evaluations demonstrate that the modified electrodes successfully capture high-fidelity somatosensory evoked potentials (SEPs) and elicit motor evoked potentials (MEPs) via low-current stimulation, while the microhole electrodes showed better signal-to-noise-ratio retention than planar controls during a 3-month implantation period in rabbits. These results show that femtosecond laser microholes improve the electrochemical performance and interfacial retention of PEDOT:PSS on PtIr electrodes, supporting chronic cortical recording and electrical stimulation.
10.1016/j.cej.2026.181967.title: Femtosecond-laser interfacial volume engineering for stable PEDOT: PSS/PtIr neural interfaces

10.1016/j.cej.2026.181941.abstract: The development of flexible sensors requires hydrogel materials with high mechanical strength, electrical conductivity, and multifunctional adaptability. However, achieving simultaneous enhancement of mechanical and electrical properties remains challenging due to the trade-off between network reinforcement and charge transport. Herein, a modular conductive hydrogel strategy based on metal-ion coordination regulation is proposed. A tannic acid-reduced graphene oxide (TA@rGO) conductive filler is incorporated into a polyacrylamide/sodium alginate (PAM/SA) double-network hydrogel, and the resulting PAM/TA@rGO/SA hydrogel is denoted as PTGS. Subsequently, dynamic coordination interactions between Cu2+/Fe3+ ions and oxygen-containing groups of SA, as well as polyphenolic sites of TA, are utilized to prepare PTGS-Cu2+ and PTGS-Fe3+ hydrogels with tunable properties. Metal-ion coordination significantly improves the mechanical performance, with PTGS-Fe3+ achieving tensile and compressive strengths of 1100 kPa and 3330 kPa, respectively. Unlike conventional ion-conducting hydrogels, where enhanced crosslinking generally suppresses conductivity, TA@rGO-mediated electronic pathways allow metal-ion coordination to simultaneously improve conductivity, reaching 17.8 S m−1 for PTGS-Fe3+. Moreover, different coordination states endow the hydrogels with distinct sensing characteristics, including wide-range strain detection, balanced sensitivity and detection range, and high sensitivity at low strain. Combined with machine learning algorithms, the hydrogels enable material-state recognition and accurate classification of diverse human motions. This work provides a modular strategy for designing multifunctional conductive hydrogels with tunable sensing capabilities.
10.1016/j.cej.2026.181941.title: Metal-ion coordination-regulated TA@rGO dual-network hydrogels for synergistic mechanical-electrical enhancement and machine-learning-assisted motion recognition

10.1016/j.cej.2026.182060.abstract: Perfluorooctanoic acid (PFOA), as a typical persistent organic pollutant resistant to degradation. Piezo-assisted mechanochemical degradation technology enables efficient PFOA defluorination under mild conditions, demonstrating promising application potential. However, this process is governed by the coupled effects of multiple factors, including ball milling speed, ball-to-powder ratio, and co-agent dosage, and its nonlinear interaction mechanisms remain poorly understood. In this study, ball milling speed, ball-to-powder ratio, mass ratio of KOH to PFOA, and mass ratio of piezoelectric material to PFOA were used as input features, and the defluorination kinetic constant k (k_defluorination) of PFOA was set as the target output. A dataset comprising 300 experimental samples was constructed. Based on predictive accuracy and interpretability requirements, the eXtreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost) model was selected and hyperparameter-optimized. Model interpretability analysis was conducted using SHAP (SHapley Additive exPlanations). Results show that the optimized XGBoost model achieves a R2 of 0.974, an RMSE of 0.186 h−1 and an MAE of 0.139 h−1 on the test set, demonstrating excellent generalization capability. SHAP analysis reveals the importance ranking of factors affecting defluorination rate as: ball milling speed > mass ratio of piezoelectric material to PFOA > ball-to-powder ratio > mass ratio of KOH to PFOA. For the first time, data-driven evidence shows that fluctuations in KOH dosage barely affect the reaction rate under excess KOH conditions. Further analysis identifies a significant synergistic effect between rotation speed and piezoelectric material dosage, defining the critical parameters for reaction initiation and the optimal process control range. The established model enables accurate prediction of PFOA mechanochemical defluorination kinetics, and its interpretability analysis reveals inherent nonlinear regulation mechanisms from a data-driven perspective, providing theoretical support and decision-making basis for process optimization and engineering application.
10.1016/j.cej.2026.182060.title: Machine learning modeling and interpretability analysis of piezo-assisted mechanochemical defluorination of PFOA

10.1016/j.cej.2026.182309.abstract: The limited biocompatibility of conventional flexible electrode materials often triggers host immune responses, manifesting as glial encapsulation and the overproduction of reactive oxygen species (ROS). Meanwhile, ROS accumulation further exacerbates local inflammation and induces irreversible cellular damage. Therefore, constructing a highly biocompatible electrode-tissue interface and developing multi-modal microelectrodes capable of recording and regulating in-vivo ROS concentrations are critical for alleviating immune responses and clarifying the underlying mechanisms of electrode failure. In this work, we proposed a novel modification strategy for micro-electrocorticography (micro-ECoG) electrodes to enable multi-modal neural recordings (ECoG and ROS) and regulations (drug deliver and ROS catalyze). For this purpose, the electrode surface is modified with Cu-metal-organic framework (Cu-MOF)-doped poly(3,4-ethylenedioxythiophene): polystyrenesulfonate (PEDOT:PSS), denoted as PEDOT-MOF. Additionally, a highly biocompatible polypeptide coating loaded with anti-inflammatory drugs is introduced to further suppress immune reactions. In vitro experiments reveal that PEDOT-MOF exhibits excellent electrochemical performance and detection sensitivity to H₂O₂, indicating its multifunctionality to catalyze the ROS for mitigating oxidative stress and monitor dynamic changes in ROS concentration in real time. In vivo implantation studies confirm that microelectrodes modified with the drug-loaded polypeptide coating exhibit lower interface impedance and higher SNR. Collectively, these results highlight the significant application potential of PEDOT-MOF-modified micro-ECoG electrodes combined with a drug-loaded polypeptide coating, which may address key challenges in current implantable neural electrode technology. It should be noted that, due to partial channel attenuation over chronic implantation and spatial diffusion effects of dexamethasone, this platform is more suited for monitoring relative ROS dynamic trends. Future optimizations will further advance the capability toward accurate in-vivo ROS absolute quantification.
10.1016/j.cej.2026.182309.title: Bio-compatible PEDOT-MOF/(PHE)2 enhanced micro-ECoG electrode for multi-mode neural recording and regulation

10.1016/j.cej.2026.182165.abstract: Antimicrobial resistance represents one of the most urgent challenges in modern biology, yet our ability to prospectively predict resistance emergence remains profoundly limited. Here, we present an integrated artificial intelligence (AI) framework combining transformer-based deep learning for genomic analysis with geometric graph neural networks for three-dimensional protein-ligand modeling, achieving 96.5% accuracy in prospectively forecasting resistance mutations—substantially exceeding existing approaches (73–89%). Through large-scale automated evolution of 1000 independent bacterial lineages across 15 clinically-relevant species over 300 generations, we demonstrate prospective prediction of resistance-associated mutations before their experimental emergence during controlled laboratory evolution, thereby enabling earlier identification of adaptive trajectories and supporting AI-guided antimicrobial detection. We validated 15 AI-predicted variants through high-resolution structural biology (X-ray crystallography and cryo-EM, 1.68–2.6 Å), revealing how single amino acid substitutions reduce drug binding affinity by 4.4–6.3 kcal/mol predominantly through allosteric conformational perturbations. Extensive molecular dynamics simulations (800 ns per system) quantified how resistance mutations increase structural flexibility (RMSF 2.5–4.5 Å versus 1.5–2.0 Å for wild-type) and flatten conformational energy landscapes, enabling entropy-driven resistance. Leveraging these mechanistic principles, we designed 12 novel antimicrobial candidates' scaffolds using generative chemistry, of which 10 showed no substantial resistance emergence (<2-fold MIC drift) after 500 generations of selection, contrasting with 32–512-fold resistance observed for conventional antibiotics under identical conditions. Whole-genome sequencing of evolved lineages (7000 complete genomes) revealed universal evolutionary constraints: resistance mutations impose 6.7–25.6% fitness costs, structuring adaptation pathways. Biophysical characterization by surface plasmon resonance and isothermal titration calorimetry revealed a decreased ligand-binding affinity and altered binding thermodynamics for the TEM-1 M182T variant, providing mechanistic insight that allowed rational antimicrobial design and optimization of hydrogen-bonding interactions. Our framework integrates four scales—from atomic interactions through protein dynamics and genomic plasticity to population-level trajectories—establishing AI-guided antimicrobial resistance prediction and evolutionary analysis applicable to cancer drug resistance.
10.1016/j.cej.2026.182165.title: Deep learning forecasts and experimentally validates antimicrobial resistance evolution, enabling design of mutation-refractory therapeutics

10.1016/j.cej.2026.182263.abstract: The cyclization of aryl pentazoles suffers from competing pathways, transient intermediates, and unstable products, leading to low yields. These features hinder mechanistic characterization and selectivity regulation. To address these bottlenecks, we develop an AI-assisted multi-spectroscopic characterization technique to uncover the reaction mechanism of this complex system. High-fidelity dynamic data covering the entire reaction process were acquired by in situ infrared spectroscopy. Combined with an intelligent analysis framework established based on the GPT-5.2 model, two key aryl pentazene intermediates were identified for the first time under practical reaction conditions, and their temperature-dependent concentration evolution was systematically clarified. Density functional theory calculations confirm that the E,Z-isomer serves as the dominant precursor for cyclization, possessing significantly lower formation and conversion energy barriers than the E,E-isomer, which is in excellent agreement with spectroscopic experimental results. Multi-modal characterization with quantitative NMR kinetic tracking further verifies the specific stabilization effect of phenoxide anions on aryl pentazoles. Precise temperature control at −10 °C selectively promotes the target cyclization and inhibits side reactions, finally boosting the yield up to 45%. This work not only provides a feasible strategy for the efficient synthesis of pentazole-type compounds, but also demonstrates the application merits of AI-assisted multi-spectroscopic characterization for highly-reactive complex reaction systems, offering a new paradigm for mechanistic elucidation of intricate chemical reactions.
10.1016/j.cej.2026.182263.title: Online detection toward transient intermediates and reaction-selectivity modulation in aryl pentazole cyclization: AI-assisted multi-spectroscopic technology

10.1016/j.cej.2026.182386.abstract: Hydrogel-based wearable electronics are pivotal for human-machine interfaces; however, their performance in aquatic environments is fundamentally limited by osmotic swelling and interfacial hydration layers, leading to signal instability and mechanical delamination. Herein, a molecularly engineered rosin-derived gel was synthesized via a streamlined one-pot strategy, strategically utilizing maleic rosin as a “molecular spacer” to regulate the hierarchical crosslinking density. The resulting gel architecture features hydrophobic microencapsulation, which effectively excludes interfacial water molecules, enabling an underwater adhesive strength of 0.25 MPa and a low water permeability (3%). By integrating carbon black and multi-walled carbon nanotubes into a “bridge-island” conductive framework, the sensor delivers high sensitivity (Gauge Factor = 3.0) and dielectric stability over 400 cycles under submersion. Leveraging these synergistic properties, a self-powered communication platform that couples a high-output triboelectric nanogenerator (Voc = 269.2 V) with a deep-learning-assisted decoding framework was developed. This system achieves a remarkable 99% accuracy in underwater Morse-code translation and 97% accuracy in “Behavioral DNA” handwriting recognition, bypassing the acoustic interference of traditional maritime communication. Furthermore, life cycle assessment (LCA) confirms the material's circularity and environmental advantage, establishing a sustainable design paradigm for next-generation flexible electronics in marine exploration, secure digital notarization, and zero-power intelligent biometrics.
10.1016/j.cej.2026.182386.title: Regenerable, molecularly engineered bio-based rosin gels for resilient underwater sensing and deep learning-augmented intelligent biometrics

10.1016/j.cej.2026.182481.abstract: Aqueous zinc-ion batteries (AZIBs) are promising for large-scale energy storage owing to their intrinsic safety and low cost; however, their practical operation is restricted by hydrogen evolution, corrosion, byproduct accumulation, and dendritic Zn growth at the Zn anode. Considering the structural complexity of polymer additives and the difficulty of direct high-accuracy calculations, in this work, an integrated “oligomer-based density functional theory (DFT) calculation-machine-learning- assisted energy evolution analysis-experimental validation” framework for polylysine chain-length-dependent energetics was developed. Lysine oligomers were used as model systems to calculate the molecular energy, additive-water-binding energy, and adsorption energy on Zn surfaces, which were further correlated with the degree of polymerization, functional-group density, charge distribution, and molecular size. The analysis revealed a nonlinear chain length–dependent energy evolution of polylysine, whereas ε-polylysine (ε-PL) lies within a relatively stable energy-response region. Owing to its chain-like multidentate structure, ε-PL synergistically reconstructs the hydrogen-bonding network of water and protects the Zn interface. The experimental results demonstrate that ε-PL facilitates interfacial Zn2+ kinetics involving ion transport, partial desolvation, and charge-transfer processes, while forming an N/O-rich interfacial environment that suppresses parasitic reactions and nonuniform Zn deposition. Consequently, the ε-PL-modified electrolyte enabled Zn||Cu cells to cycle for 2000 cycles with a Coulombic efficiency of 99.2%, enabled Zn||Zn symmetric cells to operate for more than 4000 h, and enabled Zn||AlVO-NMP full cells to retain 70.63% capacity after 6000 cycles. This study provides a new strategy for the machine learning-assisted design of polymer electrolyte additives for AZIBs.
10.1016/j.cej.2026.182481.title: Machine-learning-assisted energy evolution analysis of lysine oligomers reveals ε-polylysine as an electrolyte additive for stable aqueous zinc batteries

10.1016/j.cej.2026.182469.abstract: Flexible pressure sensors with high sensitivity and good conformability are important for wearable health monitoring, human-machine interaction, and virtual reality (VR) haptics. However, conventional planar or single-stage microstructure sensors usually suffer from limited sensitivity and poor contact with curved soft surfaces under weak pressures, mainly due to single-scale deformation that induces contact stiffening and restricts stress transfer. Here, a flexible resistive pressure sensor based on three-stepped microcones and a silver-coated PDMS/MXene composite is reported. The stepped microcone structure allows progressive compression under applied pressure, which helps delay contact hardening and improve stress transfer. Meanwhile, the silver-coated PDMS/MXene composite provides stable conductive pathways for resistance variation. The sensor exhibits high sensitivity (131 kPa−1) at low pressures (0–0.4 kPa) and maintains excellent cyclic stability (about 5000 cycles). With the assistance of deep learning, the device distinguishes facial micro-expressions, gait patterns, and vigorous movements with an accuracy of 98.1%. Furthermore, the sensor could detect subtle touch signals from plant leaves, enabling plant species identification and immersive VR tactile simulation. This work provides a flexible pressure-sensing platform for human motion analysis and plant touch perception, showing potential for wearable electronics and agricultural sensing applications.
10.1016/j.cej.2026.182469.title: Deep learning-assisted three-stepped microconical flexible pressure sensor for efficient motion recognition and plant haptic perception

10.1016/j.cej.2026.182511.abstract: Nitration in mixed acids, the ternary HNO3-H2SO4-H2O system, is among the most industrially important and hazardous reaction classes in organic chemistry, yet its kinetic behavior remains incompletely rationalized after more than a century of investigation. The central difficulty is not merely experimental: it is structural. In a strongly non-ideal medium where the concentration of the active electrophile, the nitronium ion (NO2+), depends nonlinearly on acid composition, temperature, and water activity, any kinetic parameter measured under one set of conditions carries limited predictive value under another. This review examines the problem of kinetic modeling in mixed-acid nitration from a framework perspective, organizing the available approaches, i.e. empirical rate laws, activity-corrected mechanistic models, thermodynamic-kinetic coupled descriptions, computational pre-screening, and data-driven methods, according to their underlying assumptions, data requirements, and transferability. The Marziano acidity function (Ma) and the related transformation of observed rate constants (kobs) into intrinsic rate constants (k*) are identified as the most powerful currently available tools for obtaining kinetic parameters that are independent of acid composition and transferable across substrates and reactor configurations. The role of continuous flow microreactor technology as an enabling platform for reliable kinetic determination is critically assessed. Persistent gaps, including the absence of standardized protocols, the scarcity of validated thermodynamic models for ionic species, and the limited coverage of non-aromatic substrates, are identified, and directions toward a unified, multiscale kinetic framework for mixed-acid nitration are outlined.
10.1016/j.cej.2026.182511.title: Kinetic modeling of mixed-acid nitration: From measurable rate constants to transferable parameters

10.1016/j.cej.2026.182490.abstract: Rapid, sensitive, and accurate detection of heavy metals (HMs) in soil is of importance for ensuring food security and advancing smart agriculture. However, conventional detection methods face numerous limitations, such as complicated operations and time-consuming procedures. This study proposed a novel method using AuAg nanoclusters (AuAgNCs)-modified nanofibrous membranes combined with double-pulse LIBS (DP-LIBS) for the sensitive detection of available cesium (Cs), strontium (Sr), and cobalt (Co) in soil. The AuAgNCs-modified nanofiber membranes were utilized to efficiently adsorb Cs+, Sr2+, and Co2+ from soil solution, with simultaneous DP-LIBS detection. The results revealed that the limits of detection (LODs) for Cs, Sr, and Co in soil reached 0.078 mg/kg, 0.085 mg/kg, and 0.16 mg/kg, respectively. Furthermore, a one-dimensional convolutional neural network (1D-CNN) model was developed for accurate quantitative analysis and exhibited excellent predictive performance. The residual predictive deviations (RPDs) for Cs, Sr, and Co in soil were 6.0121, 5.1844, and 6.7082, respectively. This method holds great application potential in HMs monitoring, soil risk assessment, and human health protection.
10.1016/j.cej.2026.182490.title: Deep learning-assisted double-pulse laser-induced breakdown spectroscopy and AuAg nanocluster-modified nanofiber membranes for detection of Cs, Sr, and Co in soil

10.1016/j.cej.2026.182690.abstract: Arsenic-contaminated wastewater poses a persistent threat to public health and ecological safety, while conventional remediation materials often involve trade-offs among performance, sustainability, and economic feasibility. Here, biomolecule-coated iron-based nanoparticles (Ib-FeNPs) were synthesized from Ipomoea batatas (I. batatas) leaf extract through a green one-pot route for the simultaneous removal of As(III) and As(V). In a mixed‑arsenic system, Ib-FeNPs achieved removal efficiencies of 92.4% for As(III) and 100.0% for As(V) after 360 min at a dosage of 0.3 g·L−1. These values exceeded those obtained with bare FeNPs (10.3% and 60.1%), the isolated capping layer (21.5% and 92.0%), and their physical mixture (26.5% and 83.8%). Time-resolved liquid chromatography-atomic fluorescence spectrometry detected the partial conversion of initially added As(III) to As(V). Analysis of the As 3d X-ray photoelectron spectra identified both species on the reacted material. A decrease in the surface Fe(III) fraction accompanied by an increase in Fe(II) was consistent with the participation of Fe-containing sites in redox processes. The component and physical-mixture controls showed that assembly of the Fe-containing phase and plant-derived coating improved simultaneous arsenic removal. Material characterization revealed Fe-containing surface environments and organic functional groups. Liquid chromatography-quadrupole time-of-flight mass spectrometry identified 18 major plant-derived biomolecules. Six regression algorithms were compared using a four-factor experimental dataset, and SHapley additive explanations (SHAP) were applied to the selected models to assess the contributions of operating variables to predicted removal efficiencies within the investigated range. Together, these findings support an adsorption-oxidation-fixation pathway at the process level. Ib-FeNPs also showed good reusability over five cycles and achieved 80.0% total arsenic removal in a fixed-bed experiment with acid mine drainage (AMD). Overall, Ib-FeNPs provide a plant-mediated platform for arsenic-contaminated water remediation, while the integrated machine-learning and characterization framework offers a transferable approach to developing bio-nano adsorbents from underutilized biomass.
10.1016/j.cej.2026.182690.title: Bioengineered iron nanoparticles for arsenic remediation: Unraveling the adsorption-oxidation-fixation pathway via SHAP-interpretable machine learning and LC-AFS speciation tracking

10.1016/j.cej.2026.182664.abstract: The escalating environmental and health threats from hazardous pesticide residues demand integrated strategies that combine real-time monitoring with effective removal. Herein, we report a bifunctional fluorescent nanohybrid of Au22-ZIF constructed by immobilization of Au22(SG)18 nanoclusters onto ZIF-8. The confinement effect substantially enhances fluorescence quantum yield and photostability. The nanohybrid enables sensitive thiram detection via competitive coordination-induced fluorescence quenching, achieving a limit of detection as low as 0.90 μM. Furthermore, a flexible hydrogel-based sensor fabricated by melt-reduction allows on-site produce analysis. To overcome the limitations of conventional RGB-based image interpretation, an interpretable machine learning (ML) framework that autonomously extracts multidimensional latent features from sensor images is proposed, delivering robust and accurate thiram concentration predictions (R2 = 0.95) with full model transparency. Concurrently, the inherently high surface area and porous architecture of ZIF-8 together with the active binding sites of Au22(SG)18 provide exceptional adsorptive removal of residual thiram with outstanding recyclability over multiple cycles. In addition, the hydrogel sensor enables real-time dynamic monitoring of thiram residue evolution on vegetables. By synergizing optical sensing, ML-driven data analytics, and pollutant sequestration within a single portable platform, this work establishes a paradigm for next-generation smart systems aimed at on-site pesticide surveillance and food safety control.
10.1016/j.cej.2026.182664.title: Interpretable machine learning-assisted fluorescence-enhanced Au22-ZIF material for simultaneous detection and removal of hazardous substances

10.1016/j.cej.2026.182554.abstract: Thiophene compounds are sulfur containing organic substances present in industrial wastewater and fuels, and are closely associated with environmental pollution. Therefore, it is urgently required to develop a rapid and convenient detection method. In this study, we developed a machine learning-based peroxidase-like sensor array for the efficient discrimination and sensitive detection of five thiophene compounds. By employing platinum‑iron nanowires (PtFe NWs) with peroxidase-like activity and 3,3′,5,5′-tetramethylbenzidine (TMB) as the chromogenic substrate, the sensor array generated diverse absorbance fingerprint patterns under three pH conditions (3.6, 4.0 and 4.6). Density functional theory (DFT) calculations revealed that thiophene compounds generally exhibit stronger adsorption energies on the PtFe NWs surface than H₂O₂, indicating their preferential adsorption onto the nanozyme surface. The adsorbed thiophene molecules inhibit the peroxidase-like activity of PtFe NWs to different extents through π–d interactions between the benzene or thiophene rings and Pt atoms, as well as PtS chemical bonding. These differential inhibitory effects generate unique absorbance fingerprint patterns across the three pH sensing channels. The proposed sensor array enables not only the qualitative identification of five thiophene compounds but also their quantitative determination through machine learning methods such as linear discriminant analysis (LDA) and hierarchical cluster analysis (HCA). Moreover, the recognition capability toward thiophene mixtures, resistance to interference, and practical applicability of the sensor array were successfully validated. This work demonstrates the promising application potential of three-channel PtFe NWs sensor arrays for thiophene compounds discrimination.
10.1016/j.cej.2026.182554.title: Machine learning-based peroxidase-like sensor arrays for the discrimination of thiophene compounds
10.1016/j.cej.2026.182554.source: ScienceDirect official citation and abstract BibTeX export

10.1016/j.cej.2026.182857.abstract: Rapid and reliable identification of diverse pollutants in edible oils remains challenging due to complex matrices and insufficient sensing dimensionality. Herein, we report a multifunctional copper-based nanozyme (Cu-TTPDC) constructed via coordination between Cu2+ ions and a thiadiazole-containing aromatic dicarboxylate ligand, which integrates intrinsic fluorescence with peroxidase (POD)-, laccase (LAC)-, and superoxide dismutase (SOD)-like activities within a single framework. Unlike conventional sensor arrays assembled from multiple sensing elements, Cu-TTPDC provides four complementary optical responses—three catalytic colorimetric channels and one fluorescent channel—thereby simplifying array construction while retaining multidimensional sensing information. The single-material array generates distinct response fingerprints for eight representative pollutants spanning heavy-metal, phenolic-compound, and pesticide categories, including lead(II) ions (Pb2+), gossypol (GSP), fenthion (FEN), aldicarb (ALD), glyphosate (GLY), flusilazole (FLZ), fluorodifen (DCF), and 2-cyclohexyl-4,6-dinitrophenol (DCP). To decode the correlated and nonlinear multichannel patterns, a feature-fusion cascaded classification network (FFCCN) was developed. The network learns a shared representation directly from the four response channels and concatenates this representation with the predicted pollutant-probability vector in the concentration branch, thereby conditioning concentration-level discrimination on pollutant identity without using the true pollutant label. Under four-fold nested cross-validation, the model achieved out-of-fold accuracies of 91.3% for pollutant identification and 88.1% for five-level concentration discrimination, with an 84.4% joint accuracy. Detection limits as low as 0.15 μg·mL−1. This single-material four-channel array coupled with cascaded learning provides a compact approach for multidimensional screening of chemically diverse hazards in edible oils.
10.1016/j.cej.2026.182857.title: Feature-fusion cascaded neural network (FFCCN)-assisted optical sensor array for simultaneous detection of multiple pollutants in edible oil based on four-signal fluorescent copper-based nanozyme
10.1016/j.cej.2026.182857.source: ScienceDirect official citation and abstract BibTeX export

10.1016/j.cej.2026.182677.abstract: Surface-enhanced Raman scattering (SERS) is widely used in cancer liquid biopsy due to its rapid, sensitive, and non-invasive nature. In this study, bimetallic silver and gold nanoparticles (Ag NPs/Au NPs) were uniformly deposited onto cellulose filter paper (CFP) via three-phase liquid-liquid interface self-assembly. Subsequently, a polyurethane (PU) coating was applied to the CFP surface to obtain a high-performance PU-Ag NPs/Au NPs-CFP SERS sensor for rapid colorectal cancer (CRC) screening. Sensor stability was improved by the PU coating, and the PU-Ag NPs/Au NPs-CFP substrate exhibited stronger SERS enhancement than the uncoated substrate under various conditions, including temperatures from −80 °C to 60 °C and hydrogen peroxide solutions (≤ 3.00%). After 270 days, 87.49% of the initial SERS signal was retained, indicating long-term usability. The substrate also maintained stable SERS signals over five cycles, with a relative standard deviation (RSD) of 3.08%, showing potential for recyclability. More importantly, the PU coating effectively reduced protein interference during serum detection. As confirmed by comparative spectral analysis, this allowed accurate identification of diagnostic metabolite fingerprints in the serum. SERS spectra of serum samples from 50 CRC patients and 50 healthy controls (HC) were acquired using a portable Raman spectrometer, and four machine learning (ML) algorithms were applied for classification. Among them, the support vector machine (SVM) model performed best. At the spectral level, it achieved 94.25% accuracy and 88.50% specificity; at the patient level, it achieved 95.00% accuracy and 90.00% specificity. This study integrates a recyclable and stable SERS sensor with ML, offering a new solution for efficient, non-invasive, and low-cost CRC screening.
10.1016/j.cej.2026.182677.title: Label-free SERS diagnosis of colorectal cancer assisted by machine learning and integrated with recyclable polyurethane sensor chips

10.1016/j.cej.2026.182858.abstract: Accurate identification and quantitative analysis of antioxidants in complex biological fluids are the keys to the early detection of severe diseases. The single-channel sensors suffer from weak specificity and critical multi-component signal crosstalk, which hardly meet the accurate analytical requirements. Herein, an intelligent colorimetric sensing platform of bimetallic mixed-valence nanozyme was integrated with machine learning (ML) to improve the analytical precision. Fe/Cu nanosheets of mixed valence were successfully acquired through Cu2O-coordinated anchoring in situ into iron porphyrin (TCPP(Fe)). This mixed-valence strategy effectively promoted the synergistic catalysis and valence cycling among the metal active sites, thereby significantly enhancing the peroxidase (POD)-like activity of the Cu2O/Cu-TCPP(Fe) (Vmax as high as 8.107 × 10−7 M·s−1 and Km as low as 0.913 mM). DFT calculations indicated that the introduction of Cu2O promoted strong Cu 3d and Fe 3d orbital hybridization and an upshift of the Cu d-band center, accelerating interfacial electron transfer and Fe/Cu valence cycling, thereby revealing the intrinsic mechanism underlying the enhanced catalytic activity. Taking the differential catalytic responses of the nanozyme with two different substrates, a highly sensitive dual-channel sensor array was designed with machine learning. Combined with algorithms of artificial neural network (ANN), random forest (RF), and support vector machine (SVM), etc., 100% accurate qualitative discrimination of six antioxidants was remarkably completed. Relying on the outstanding capability of the Random Forest (RF) algorithm to remarkable robustness in handling high-dimensional sample datasets, the sensor array successfully established a precise quantitative model for multiple antioxidants in complex samples, remarkably and intelligently sensing the diverse components in urine and serum. This work paved a new way for highly active bimetallic nanozymes to construct a trustworthy sensing platform as a diagnostic tool for the intelligent profiling of multi-component biomarkers in complex matrices.
10.1016/j.cej.2026.182858.title: Machine learning-assisted mixed-valence Fe/Cu nanozyme dual-channel sensing platform for high-throughput discrimination of antioxidants

10.1016/j.cej.2026.182965.abstract: Multifunctional conductive hydrogels show great potential for flexible bioelectronics, but their performance is often limited by trade-offs between mechanical strength, environmental stability, and functional integration. To address this, we propose a three-step preparation strategy combining thermal polymerization, freeze-thaw cycling, and LS post-treatment to regulate a multiscale network structure. This approach combines a chemically crosslinked polymer matrix, freeze-thaw treatment, and lignosulfonate (LS) incorporation to obtain a mechanically robust multicomponent hydrogel. An ethylene glycol (EG)/water binary solvent system further enhances the hydrogel's environmental adaptability. The resulting PPSH-L hydrogel exhibits optimized mechanical and functional properties, including high strength (0.86 MPa), large stretchability, excellent fatigue resistance, and remarkable anti-swelling and anti-freezing capabilities (down to −22.6 °C). Its stable conductive network ensures high sensitivity, broad response range, rapid signal response, and excellent stability under repeated deformation. The incorporation of zwitterionic SBMA and LS provides an antibacterial interface with >95% efficiency and good biocompatibility. Leveraging these advantages, the hydrogel supports multifunctional sensing for motion monitoring, non-verbal patient-clinician communication, intestinal tactile sensing, and abnormal tissue palpation. Combined with a Transformer model, it enables intelligent recognition of tissue mechanical properties, offering a new approach for minimally invasive diagnosis. In simulated colonoscopy applications, the hydrogel effectively detects mechanical changes in abnormal intestinal tissues, enhancing early-stage lesion detection. This strategy overcomes the performance trade-offs in hydrogels and advances their applications in intelligent healthcare and flexible electronics.
10.1016/j.cej.2026.182965.title: Anti-swelling and antibacterial multifunctional conductive hydrogel for flexible sensing, intestinal palpation and machine learning-assisted recognition

10.1016/j.cej.2026.181768.abstract:
Cutin is the structural biopolyester that scaffolds the plant cuticle, forming a thermosetting matrix. It is insoluble in conventional solvents, chemically resilient and presents excellent barrier properties, preventing water loss, regulating gas permeability and protecting plants against environmental hazards. Conventional valorisation relies on batch processing with harsh chemicals that destroy the native architecture, yielding monomers rather than branched oligomers for polyester materials, and limiting mechanistic insight. Here we report a controlled depolymerisation strategy based on continuous supercritical-water hydrolysis that achieves complete solubilisation of the insoluble cutin network into soluble branched polyester oligomers (Mw ≈ 7.35 kDa) within 10.5 s of reaction time. Continued treatment further reduces Mw to ≈ 1.82 kDa at 120 s, approaching the limit of 24 h alkaline hydrolysis (≈ 1.22 kDa). Precise control of residence time reveals a hierarchical cleavage mechanism in which secondary esters at branching points hydrolyse preferentially over primary backbone esters. FTIR, NMR, GPC and GC–MS identify 10,16-dihydroxyhexadecanoic acid as the dominant monomeric unit and reveal 16-hydroxy-9Z-hexadecenoic acid as a novel SCW-specific product, consistent with a carbocation-driven dehydration pathway inaccessible under alkaline conditions. A structurally constrained network model depicts cutin as a heterogeneous crosslinked polyester dominated by 10,16-dihydroxyhexadecanoic acid, with glycerol as a branching node, C18 hydroxy acids and α,ω-diacids as linkers, and fatty acids as chain terminators. With an E-factor of 0.8 against 4.1 for alkaline hydrolysis, this process-intensified approach resolves the native architecture of cutin and establishes a scalable platform for plant polyester valorisation.
Problem statement
Cutin, considered the third most abundant biopolymer after cellulose and lignin, remains largely underutilised as a renewable polyester feedstock due to its highly cross-linked, insoluble structure, which severely limits processability and scalable valorisation [1]. Conventional depolymerisation strategies such as alkaline, acidic, or enzymatic hydrolysis rely on long reaction times, stoichiometric reagents, and multistep downstream processing [1], [2], leading to high material consumption, salt generation, and limited control over product characteristics. Although supercritical water presents a unique opportunity in biomass processing by functioning simultaneously as solvent and reaction medium [3], its use for the depolymerisation of cutin into tunable polyester fractions remains largely unexplored. As a result, a critical gap exists in the development of fast, catalyst-free, and environmentally efficient processes capable of converting cutin-rich agro-industrial residues into functional polyester building blocks with defined molecular characteristics. Also, a data-driven model is proposed to infer representative structures of depolymerised products from experimental data.
10.1016/j.cej.2026.181768.title: From native tomato cutin to branched polyesters: Structural insights from supercritical-water depolymerisation

10.1016/j.cej.2026.182935.abstract: Degradative solvent extraction (DSE) is an effective approach for the mild demineralization and upgrading of low-rank coals. However, the inherent high dimensionality and nonlinearity of the DSE reaction system hinder identification of consistent relationships between key predictors and product yields, thereby limiting a deeper understanding of the process. To overcome this limitation, a machine-learning-assisted multidimensional kinetics (ML-MK) framework was developed. This framework combines the predictive capability of machine learning with the interpretability of lumped kinetic models for interpreting apparent pathway behavior. A predictive model for DSE yield was established (R2 = 0.92), enabling quantitative assessment of predictor contributions to model outputs and providing multidimensional insights into the reaction system. The model-derived patterns indicate a temperature-dependent shift in the relative contributions of different processes. The low-temperature response is consistent with solvent-assisted transport and physical dissolution at 25–300 °C. Thermally activated coal-matrix conversion becomes increasingly important at 300–360 °C, followed by greater competition between hydrogen-assisted radical stabilization and condensation above 360 °C. Within the 300–400 °C range, the fitted fractional pathway contributions suggest an approximate, model-derived crossover near 340 °C. Below this approximate crossover, URC cracking contributes more strongly; above it, EX–UCactual interconversion has the larger modeled contribution. Overall, the ML-MK framework provides a novel and effective approach for achieving an in-depth understanding of DSE reaction processes. Moreover, the framework has application potential in fields characterized by complex reaction networks and numerous real components, such as coal liquefaction, petroleum refining, and biomass thermochemical conversion.
10.1016/j.cej.2026.182935.title: Machine-learning-assisted multidimensional kinetics and reaction mechanism for degradative solvent extraction of low-rank coal

10.1016/j.cej.2026.183139.abstract: Phenylethanoid glycosides (PhGs), such as verbascoside and echinacoside, are valuable plant natural products with significant pharmacological potential. Their sustainable supply remains a challenge due to the limitations of plant extraction and chemical synthesis. In this study, we report high-level de novo production of complex PhGs in Escherichia coli from glucose by combining machine learning-aided enzyme engineering with systematic metabolic engineering. To overcome the catalytic bottleneck of the BAHD acyltransferase SiAT1, we developed a computational pipeline that integrated deep learning with mechanistic constraints to select candidate variants for experimental screening. Subsequent experimental screening and mechanistic analysis identified Lys30 as a critical acceptor-gating residue, and the SiAT1K30A variant exhibited a 243-fold enhanced affinity for salidroside. We systematically engineered the E. coli chassis by constructing a high-yield supply module for the key precursors salidroside and p-coumaric acid, optimizing the expression of SiCYP98A20 and its reductase AaCPR, expanding the intracellular UDP-sugar pool, and introducing the RgTALS9N/A11Y mutant to redirect flux toward p-coumaric acid and alleviate the upstream supply imbalance. This integrated platform enabled fed-batch fermentation in 5-L bioreactors to achieve gram-scale de novo production of verbascoside (1.84 g/L) and echinacoside (1.35 g/L), along with an unprecedented accumulation of the key intermediate osmanthuside B (12.91 g/L). This work establishes E. coli as a scalable industrial host for complex PhGs and provides a potentially generalizable, data-driven framework that synergistically combines AI-assisted enzyme engineering with systematic metabolic engineering for the biomanufacturing of high-value plant natural products.
10.1016/j.cej.2026.183139.title: Gram-scale de novo biosynthesis of phenylethanoid glycosides in Escherichia coli via mechanism-guided AI-assisted engineering of a BAHD acyltransferase

10.1016/j.cej.2026.183008.abstract: Traumatic brain injury (TBI) is accompanied by severe neuronal loss, neuroinflammation, oxidative stress, and disruption of the neural microenvironment, resulting in limited endogenous neural regeneration and neuro-logical dysfunction. Herein, we developed a leonurine-functionalized injectable in situ-forming dual-crosslinked hydrogel (OSA-g-leo/Ca2+/Gel) for promoting neural regeneration and functional recovery after TBI. Oxidized sodium alginate (OSA) was first synthesized through NaIO4 oxidation and subsequently grafted with leonurine via EDC/NHS coupling. After the introduction of gelatin and Ca2+, a dynamic double-network hydrogel was formed through Schiff-base covalent crosslinking and Ca2+-mediated ionic coordination. The obtained hydrogel exhibited porous microstructure, sustained leonurine release, degradability, and enhanced mechanical properties. The hydrogel significantly promoted neuronal maturation of neural stem cells (NSCs), as evidenced by increased Tuj1 and MAP2 expression and decreased GFAP expression, indicating enhanced neuronal lineage commitment and suppressed astrocytic differentiation. The synergistic effects of the hydrogel microenvironment and sustained leonurine delivery contributed to improved neural differentiation through anti-inflammatory and antioxidative regulation. In TBI model of SD rats, the injectable OSA-g-leo/Ca2+/Gel hydrogel effectively filled TBI lesion cavities and significantly improved neurological recovery. Behavioral assessments, including Morris water maze, open field, novel object recognition, and motor coordination tests, demonstrated substantial improvements in spatial learning, recognition memory, locomotor activity, and motor coordination following OSA-g-leo/Ca2+/Gel treatment. Histological analyses further revealed reduced tissue loss, improved cortical integrity, enhanced NeuN-positive mature neuron survival, and increased DCX-positive neurogenesis, demonstrating that the OSA-g-leo/Ca2+/Gel hydrogel provided both structural support and sustained local regulation for TBI repair, effectively promoting neuro-regeneration and functional recovery. This functionalized dual-crosslinked hydrogel represented a promising biomaterial platform for neural tissue engineering and TBI therapy.
10.1016/j.cej.2026.183008.title: Leonurine-grafted dual-crosslinked hydrogels orchestrate neural stem cell differentiation and promote neurorepair after traumatic brain injury

10.1016/j.cej.2026.183114.abstract: Real-time monitoring of pH and humidity is essential for evaluating food freshness. However, changes in humidity can affect ion migration, interfere with resistive pH sensing signals, and significantly hinder simultaneous accurate quantification of the two parameters. To address this challenge, a dual-mode sensing patch that combines fluorescence and resistive sensing, coupled with a cascaded machine learning framework, was developed for monitoring food freshness. The fluorescence response unit consists of a cellulose/polyvinyl alcohol composite system embedded with AuNCs. Additionally, graphene electrodes were fabricated on both sides using 3D printing technology to facilitate the simultaneous acquisition of optical and electrical signals. The fluorescence intensity increases as humidity decreases, whereas the resistance signal exhibits a linear response within the pH range of 6.0 to 9.0. To mitigate cross-interference between the dual-mode signals, a cascaded machine learning framework was developed, including random forest model and Bayesian ridge regression. Humidity information was first extracted from fluorescence features and subsequently introduced as a compensation parameter for pH prediction based on resistance signals. This hierarchical analysis framework approach effectively decoupled the coupled humidity and pH signals, enabling accurate quantification of both parameters. This strategy enables intelligent food freshness monitoring and flexible multi-parameter signal decoupling.
10.1016/j.cej.2026.183114.title: Dual-modal signal decoupling strategy based on cascaded machine learning for intelligent food freshness monitoring

10.1016/j.cej.2026.183460.abstract: Communication barriers faced by patients with laryngeal disorders due to voice limitations have become a significant challenge in clinical diagnosis, and medical-patient communication, which could be potentially addressed by the wearable sensors. However, currently reported wearable sensors generally suffer from high manufacturing costs, slow response time, and limited stability. Here, inspired by “brick-mortar” porous structures, we report a MXene/cellulose nanofibers/polyvinyl alcohol (MCP) aerogel-based pressure sensor and develop the wearable smart glove to assist real-time and efficient communication during medical interactions. The pressure sensor features an ultra-low pressure detection limit (3.3 Pa), fast response and recovery time (66 ms /64 ms), a wide detection range (0–80 kPa), outstanding stability over 8000 compression cycles, and excellent thermal insulation properties at temperatures around 1600 °C, surpassing existing MXene-based aerogels pressure sensors. Further, a wearable smart glove was developed by using prepared pressure sensor array to realize multifunctional applications such as synchronized human-machine interaction (HMI) and remote media control. Combined with deep learning algorithms, the smart glove system achieved 100% recognition accuracy of 10 hand gestures. These findings provide an effective solution to the communication challenges faced by patients with speech disorders.
10.1016/j.cej.2026.183460.title: High-performance “brick-mortar” MXene/CNF/PVA aerogel pressure sensors for deep-learning-assisted gesture recognition and medical communication

10.1016/j.cej.2026.183331.abstract: The growing adoption of smart food packaging, processing, and storing units demands advanced sensing systems capable of real-time food quality monitoring to enhance safety and reduce waste. This research presents a wireless miniaturized resistive gas sensor based on a mesoporous Cr2O3-In2O3 heterostructure, engineered for the highly sensitive and selective detection of 3-Hydroxy-2-Butanone (3H2B), which is a key volatile organic compound (VOC) marker of microbial spoilage in perishable foods such as dairy and meat. The synergistic interface between Cr2O3 and In2O3 optimises charge transfer and surface reactivity, enabling outstanding sensor performance with a detection limit of about 50 ppb and rapid response times under 12 s, while maintaining measurable response across a wide humidity range. These results are achieved through interdigitated electrodes with a spacing of 100 μm, enhancing sensitivity and signal stability. The mesoporous nanostructure offers high surface area and interconnected pores for rapid adsorption and diffusion, enabling consistent detection across wide concentration ranges. Wireless connectivity integrates the sensor into IoT-enabled smart packaging, processing lines, and storage facilities, streaming data to mobile, cloud, and automated control systems. AI models for supervised classification deliver instant spoilage alerts, continuous QA, and predictive inventory management across industrial and commercial supply chains. By combining advanced nanomaterials with scalable fabrication and IoT integration, this work advances the vision of intelligent, waste-minimising food systems and offers a platform for broader applications in large-scale food processing and cold-chain logistics. Data collected from multiple devices is periodically aggregated on a central server to refine the detection models. It predicts remaining shelf life from thousands of data points in order to improve predictive food quality control and also support safer and more sustainable operations.
10.1016/j.cej.2026.183331.title: AI-enabled wireless gas sensor based on mesoporous Cr2O3-In2O3 heterostructure for rapid detection of 3-hydroxy-2-butanone

10.1016/j.cej.2026.183235.abstract: Accurate prediction of breakthrough curves (BTCs) remains a major challenge in scaling up fixed-bed adsorption systems, as conventional models often fail to generalize across operating conditions. Here, we propose a hybrid deep learning framework based on explicit decomposition of BTCs into normalized shape and characteristic timescale components. The normalized BTC shape is learned using a bidirectional long short-term memory (BiLSTM) model in a dimensionless time domain, while the characteristic breakthrough time is predicted using a multilayer perceptron (MLP). The full BTC is reconstructed through a scaling-based mapping of these two components. Trained on lab-scale datasets, the proposed model achieved high predictive accuracy for unseen pilot-scale conditions (R2 = 0.975, RMSE = 0.053), reducing prediction errors by up to 3–5 times compared to conventional end-to-end models. Interpretability analyses using Shapley additive explanations (SHAP) and accumulated local effects (ALE) reveal that the characteristic timescale is primarily governed by influent concentration and hydrodynamic conditions, with nonlinear and interaction effects consistent with expected adsorption behavior. These results demonstrate that separating intrinsic dynamics from temporal scaling provides a structurally effective and interpretable approach for robust and transferable BTC prediction, offering a new pathway for data-efficient scale-up in adsorption-based water treatment systems.
10.1016/j.cej.2026.183235.title: Scale-up prediction of breakthrough curves via shape–timescale decomposition in a hybrid deep learning framework

10.1016/j.cej.2026.183548.abstract: Hydrogel strain sensors are promising for soft robotics and wearable electronics, but their sensing accuracy is often compromised by hysteresis arising from irreversible chain rearrangement and energy dissipation. Here, we develop a multiple reversible physical crosslinking strategy to regulate polymer-chain topology and reinforce a polymerized network through reversible multivalent interactions, thereby producing a low-hysteresis and highly stretchable (LHS) conducting polymer hydrogel. The optimized hydrogel exhibits a low Young's modulus of approximately 17 kPa, comparable in magnitude to the modulus reported for soft brain tissue, together with an elongation at break of approximately 2200%, and an electrical hysteresis ratio of 0.76% at 400% strain. The resultant strain sensor provides reversible strain-dependent resistance responses, a maximum gauge factor of 2.4, and stable operation. When four sensors are integrated into a robotic hand, the multichannel signals capture fruit-specific grasping characteristics. Coupling these signals with a lightweight one-dimensional convolutional neural network enables the classification of five fruits with an accuracy of 98.66%. These results demonstrate that hyperbranched topology regulation offers an effective route for constructing low-hysteresis conducting polymer hydrogels for high-fidelity robotic perception.
10.1016/j.cej.2026.183548.title: Hyperbranched network engineering enables tissue-soft, low-hysteresis and ultrastretchable hydrogel strain sensors for machine learning-assisted fruit recognition

10.1016/j.cej.2026.183637.abstract: Low melting-point salts may lower auxiliary-heating demand and increase the operational flexibility of thermal-energy-storage systems. Reliable machine learning (ML) screening of low melting point molten salts requires exploiting broad literature evidence while calibrating predictions against standardized measurements. Here, a fidelity-aware ML framework based on fidelity-separated fine-tuning is developed for nitrate/nitrite salts by pretraining a composition-based neural model on 5892 records from 593 publications and recalibrating only its final prediction layer using 107 unified-protocol measurements. Four neural data-utilization strategies and two regularized regression baselines are compared through composition-grouped cross-validation; the four neural strategies are further evaluated using an independent post-development measurement set comprising six predefined salt families (S1–S6). The conventional neural strategies show residual average bias or a larger fitted-to-held-out error increase on the standardized dataset. The fidelity-aware strategy achieves a held-out-group mean absolute error (MAE) of 17.9 °C, a mean signed error of +1.1 °C, and a 3.0 °C fitted-to-held-out MAE gap. At the predefined 150 °C cutoff for this screening task, it retains all five candidate families subsequently confirmed below the cutoff, whereas literature-only, standardized-data-only, and direct-mixing strategies would have rejected four, three, and two families, respectively. Among the four neural strategies assessed independently, only the fidelity-aware strategy retains salt families S3 and S4, which are experimentally confirmed with family mean transition temperatures of 130.9 and 99.2 °C. Across six independent family means, the model achieves an MAE of 19.9 °C and a root mean square error of 23.9 °C. These results support separating broad representation learning from standardized final-scale calibration for candidate retention in nitrate/nitrite screening on the measurement scale used here.
10.1016/j.cej.2026.183637.title: Fidelity-aware machine learning for reliable screening of low melting-point molten salts from heterogeneous experimental data

10.1016/j.cej.2026.183547.abstract: Early diagnosis and timely treatment of esophageal cancer (EC) remain challenging due to the lack of ultrasensitive, high-throughput, rapid, and minimally invasive approaches for multiplex protein biomarker detection in biofluids. In this study, we developed a highly efficient carbon dots (CDs)-assembled immunoassay biochip for the simultaneous detection and evaluation of six EC-related biomarkers, including CEA, CA199, CA724, HSP70, IL6, and IL8. The assembled CDs enhanced the biochip substrate by enabling high-density immobilization of capture antibody barcodes through π–π stacking and hydrogen bonding, while their surface-proximity-dependent fluorescence quenching capability effectively reduced nonspecific background fluorescence. This design achieved both high capture antibody immobilization efficiency and efficient quenching of nonspecific signals. The immunoassay biochip enabled rapid multiplex detection with a total assay time of approximately 45 min, with limits of detection (LODs) reaching the pg/mL level. The combined biomarker panels exhibited superior diagnostic capability in terms of sensitivity and specificity, with the six-marker combination providing the highest diagnostic accuracy. Furthermore, machine-learning analysis demonstrated the diagnostic potential of the six-biomarker panel for distinguishing EC patients, including different TNM-defined subgroups, from healthy donors, with accuracies generally exceeding 90%. Owing to its excellent stability, ultrasensitivity, high throughput, and reproducibility, this immunoassay biochip holds great promise for minimally invasive EC diagnosis, disease-stage assessment, and evaluation of therapeutic outcomes.
10.1016/j.cej.2026.183547.title: Self-assembled carbon dot-based biochip for ultrasensitive multiplex biomarker detection and machine learning-assisted diagnosis of esophageal carcinoma

10.1016/j.cej.2026.183729.abstract: Supercapacitors are promising energy-storage devices whose specific capacitance (SC) can be effectively improved through the proper design of electrode materials. Coal-derived carbon materials have attracted increasing attention as supercapacitor electrode candidates, yet their design remains heavily dependent on trial-and-error experimentation, making the optimization of SC performance inefficient and costly. Herein, a machine learning-assisted approach is proposed for SC prediction and regulation of coal-based carbon materials. Specifically, an XGB-SC model is developed to rapidly predict the SC, showing good predictive performance (R2 = 0.87, RMSE = 24.57 F g−1), thereby enabling the rapid screening of high-performance electrode candidates. Interpretable analysis methods further identify specific surface area (SSA) as the dominant feature governing SC prediction and reveal its favorable range, thereby providing guidance for the design of electrode materials. A workflow integrating the XGB-SC model, the XGB-SSA model and a coal property dataset is then constructed to demonstrate the data-driven design of high-SC coal-based activated carbon electrodes. Using this workflow, a Yulin coal sample is identified as a promising precursor among more than 100 coal samples. The resulting activated carbon delivers a SC of 354.5 F g−1 at 0.5 A g−1 in a three-electrode system and also exhibits favorable performance in a symmetric device. This work may facilitate the screening and development of coal-based carbon electrodes with high SC, while providing a useful reference for the rational design of supercapacitor electrode materials.
10.1016/j.cej.2026.183729.title: Machine learning-guided prediction and design of coal-based carbon materials toward enhanced specific capacitance for supercapacitors

10.1016/j.cej.2026.183770.abstract: Lead-free BaTiO3-based dielectrics are candidates for high-power pulse capacitors, yet the high-entropy (Ba,A)(Ti,B)O3 compositional space at 1 mol% resolution exceeds 105 plausible combinations, making exhaustive experimental screening impractical. Here, we integrate physical constraints, including composition windows, charge balance, tolerance factor, and configurational entropy, into a machine-learning workflow to navigate this compositional space. Using a dataset of 126 reported BaTiO3-based ceramics, we construct a 61-feature physicochemical descriptor set spanning A-/B-site elemental properties, local bonding, structural stability, and thermodynamic characteristics, and reduce it to 11 core descriptors by correlation filtering and recursive feature elimination. Compared with a field-only baseline, incorporating the intrinsic compositional descriptors increases the pooled out-of-fold R2 from 0.744 to 0.842 and reduces the mean absolute error (MAE) by 29.9%, demonstrating that the model captures composition-related information beyond the field-dependent trend. SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) analysis further identifies the applied electric field and B-site local bonding descriptors as the dominant predictors of recoverable energy density. The model-predicted optimal composition, (Ba0.65Bi0.30Ca0.05)(Ti0.70Mg0.15Zr0.15)O3, forms a pseudocubic perovskite with homogeneous elemental distribution and relaxor dielectric behavior, delivering Wrec = 6.6 J cm−3 and η = 91.7% at 540 kV cm−1. The ceramic exhibits stable frequency (10–500 Hz), temperature (20–180 °C), and cycling (104 cycles) responses, while Weibull breakdown analysis indicates reliable dielectric breakdown behavior associated with the dense microstructure and homogeneous solid solution. This work shows that physically constrained machine learning can effectively navigate high-entropy perovskite composition space, providing an interpretable and transferable route for designing lead-free ABO3 capacitive energy-storage ceramics.
10.1016/j.cej.2026.183770.title: Physically constrained machine-learning design of high-entropy BaTiO₃-based ceramics for capacitive energy storage

10.1016/j.cej.2026.183750.abstract: Flexible thermoelectric sensors that combine temperature sensitivity, mechanical compliance, and long-term stability are important for wearable electronics. Herein, we fabricated a flexible single-walled carbon nanotube (SWCNT)/Ni3(HITP)2-polydimethylsiloxane (PDMS) film (SNPF) via an ultrasound-assisted, water bath-confined in situ growth method followed by single-sided PDMS encapsulation. Ni3(HITP)2 nanocrystals were anchored onto the surfaces of SWCNT forming an integrated conductive network. Benefiting from the unique interfacial structure of SWCNT/Ni3(HITP)2, the optimized SNPF exhibited a Seebeck coefficient of 44.7 μV/K. The SNPF device exhibited exceptional temperature sensing performance, featuring a high resolution (0.5 K) and outstanding long-term stability over 500 cycles, rendering it suitable for both contact/non-contact thermal source identification and passive respiratory monitoring. Furthermore, a multilayer SNPFs device constructed by vertically stacking and electrically connecting five films demonstrated an enhanced equivalent Seebeck coefficient of 221 μV/K. When worn on the arm outdoors, this device generated an open-circuit voltage of 1.33 mV and an output power of 0.67 nW. In addition, transient thermoelectric responses generated during contact with seven materials were analyzed using machine-learning algorithms. The ExtraTrees model achieved a test accuracy of 98.04% under the present recording-level data-splitting protocol. These results demonstrate that SWCNT/Ni3(HITP)2 composites can serve as flexible thermoelectric platforms for temperature sensing, low-level body-heat-derived signal generation, and thermoelectric material recognition.
10.1016/j.cej.2026.183750.title: Flexible temperature sensor based on SWCNT/Ni3(HITP)2 thermoelectric materials for respiratory monitoring and machine learning-assisted material identification

10.1016/j.jmsy.2025.11.016.abstract: In commercial aircraft manufacturing, process planning serves as a crucial bridge between design and production, ensuring the accurate realization of design concepts and significantly improving manufacturing efficiency and product quality. With the development of knowledge graph technologies, significant progress has been made in using historical process documentation for commercial aircraft manufacturing process planning. However, traditional deep learning-based methods for constructing knowledge graph heavily rely on manual object selection and label assignment, making the process highly time-consuming. Additionally, the methods often face challenges in the field of process planning, including low domain-specific terminology recognition rates and incomplete entity extraction. To tackle these challenges, this paper introduces a hybrid approach that integrates large and small language models to construct an aircraft process planning knowledge graph. Initially, clustering-based multi-agent approach is employed to pre-annotate the process planning dataset, with domain experts re-annotate the defect data to create a high-quality process planning dataset. Subsequently, a knowledge extraction framework for aircraft process planning, KE-LSM, was constructed using the small language model trained on this dataset, together with the LLM. Experimental results show that KE-LSM outperforms existing named entity recognition models. Finally, KE-LSM is applied in a commercial aircraft manufacturing company, accompanied by the development of a prototype system designed to facilitate intelligent process planning. It is hoped that the research can provide valuable insights and support for the application of LLM-based solutions in the field of aircraft manufacturing.
10.1016/j.jmsy.2025.11.016.title: Aircraft assembly process planning based on knowledge graph constructed by integrating LLMs and SLMs
