10.1016/j.cej.2026.183802.abstract: The development of multiple-resonance thermally activated delayed fluorescence emitters is critical for advancing organic light-emitting diodes. However, navigating the highly constrained chemical space of these emitters requires moving beyond empirical trial-and-error. Here, we present an experimentally validated, machine-learning-guided molecular-design workflow to accelerate the targeted optimization of double‑boron MR-TADF materials. We constructed a database of over 400 MR-TADF molecules from scratch and trained an XGBoost model (test R2 = 0.77) to establish a statistical framework. This framework systematically quantifies the multi-parameter trade-offs associated with boron substitution patterns, π-conjugation positions, and heterocycle conjugation degrees. To validate this predictive workflow, we synthesized a double‑boron derivative, DPAC-DB, which possesses a moderate experimental ΔEST of 0.14 eV, close to our estimated value of 0.17 eV. Vacuum-deposited OLEDs based on DPAC-DB achieved a maximum external quantum efficiency of 35.6%, significantly outperforming its mono‑boron parent. By successfully translating computational prioritization into a highly efficient physical device, this work establishes a robust, data-driven paradigm for the rational optimization of MR-TADF emitters.
10.1016/j.cej.2026.183802.title: Machine learning-optimized design principles for multiple-resonance TADF emitters in organic light-emitting diodes

10.1016/j.cej.2026.183906.abstract: Precision treatment of lung cancer relies on accurate mutation profiling. Although minimally invasive, liquid biopsy is constrained by low ctDNA abundance and insufficient sensitivity for low-frequency mutations. To address this challenge, a catalytic hairpin assembly (CHA)-triggered magnetic surface-enhanced Raman scattering (SERS) system was developed to accurately identify dual EGFR mutation subtypes in serum samples simultaneously. Driven by a target-initiated CHA reaction, a core-satellite nanostructure is constructed, which integrates plasmonic magnetic nanoparticles (NPs) embedded with a silent-region Raman internal standard and SERS-encoded Au@gap@Au NPs. Integrating hierarchical hot spots with internal calibration enhances quantitative reliability, enabling a broad dynamic range and enzyme-free attomolar sensitivity within a 2-h isothermal reaction. To further improve analytical precision, the narrow Raman spectral footprints were coupled with an OPLS-DA algorithm, achieving exceptional classification accuracy with an AUC of 1.00 for distinct EGFR mutation subtypes in cellular assays. Clinical proof-of-concept validation in a serum cohort comprising 39 individuals showed reliable profiling performance, with concordance of next-generation sequencing results. Owing to its robust one-pot multiplexing capability, low instrumental demands and stable analytical performance, the machine learning-assisted, CHA-triggered magnetic SERS system offers a powerful strategy for ctDNA genotyping, holding significant promise for advancing personalized and precision medicine in lung cancer.
10.1016/j.cej.2026.183906.title: One-pot, ultrasensitive duplex genotyping of ctDNA in lung cancer via machine learning-assisted SERS spectral decoding

10.1016/j.jmsy.2025.11.020.abstract: Intelligent operation and maintenance of energy equipment represents a critical component in ensuring the stable performance of new-generation power systems. Faced with complex operational conditions and nonlinear fault characteristics, conventional manual maintenance suffers from delayed perception and ambiguous causality. However, while digital twin technology can establish a virtual-real interaction space, its static modeling approach exhibits prediction failure in dynamic scenarios. To address these challenges, this study proposes an intelligent maintenance methodology based on cognitive agents and virtual-real co-evolution: constructing a dynamic environment representation model to achieve spatiotemporal feature correlation of equipment states and operational condition migration; designing a memory-planning-decision architecture to enhance causal reasoning capabilities for equipment faults and integrating with digital twin models for virtual-real interaction. The methodology is validated through an 18-month case study of a gas-steam boiler in a combined heat and power plant, utilizing 5.2 million historical operational records. Experimental results demonstrate that this approach achieves a 97.3 % accuracy rate in diagnosing non-stationary faults for gas-steam boiler equipment, realizes a 20-fold improvement in knowledge update time (from 48 to 2.3 h), and attains significant performance enhancements including 31.2 % cost efficiency improvement, 3-fold early warning lead time extension (from 24 to 72 h), and 16.2 % overall collaborative performance improvement (from 82.2 % to 95.5 %). The research validates the engineering value of dynamic cognitive paradigms in intelligent maintenance of power equipment, providing a feasible solution for autonomous decision-making in high-real-time scenarios.
10.1016/j.jmsy.2025.11.020.title: Agentic digital twin-embedded maintenance methodology for energy equipment: A self-evolving operational paradigm
10.1016/j.jmsy.2025.11.020.source: ScienceDirect official citation and abstract BibTeX export

10.1016/j.jmsy.2025.11.019.abstract: In the human-oriented context of Industry 5.0, human-robot collaboration (HRC) has become the core driving force for innovating the production model of assembly systems by integrating human flexibility ability with the precision and repeatability of robots. As the core link to achieve efficient collaboration, task planning is facing multiple challenges in dynamic and complex scenarios. On the one hand, it is hard to perform cognition of multimodal human-robot-environment in HRC assembly scenarios. On the other hand, heterogeneous capabilities of humans and robots (e.g., flexible decision-making by humans and precise execution by robots) are hard to be fully used to achieve reasonable task allocation and timing optimization in dynamic and complex HRC assembly scenarios. To address these issues, a Vision Language Model (VLM)-enhanced deep reinforcement learning-driven task planning approach is proposed towards Augmented Reality (AR)-assisted HRC assembly system. Firstly, a self-trained VLM is proposed through the integration of domain-specific knowledge and real-time situational data to enable context-aware in HRC assembly system. Through the fine-tuning of role configuration parameters for the pre-constructed VLM via prompt engineering, VLM can possess cognition of multi-dimensional assembly scenario elements. Reinforcement learning model can be endowed with the eyes to perceive HRC assembly scenarios through VLM-enhanced cognition of the dynamic HRC environment. Based on the VLM-enhanced cognition of the dynamic HRC environment, an improved multi-agent reinforcement learning-based HRC assembly task planning model is established to achieve humanized task planning, which can consider the competitive relationship between humans and robots with multi-agent conflict mechanism. Based on the HRC assembly task planning result, AR can enable operators to accomplish visual HRC assembly guidance through virtual-real mapping of HRC assembly information (e.g., HRC assembly procedures) and interact seamlessly with the VLM. Finally, experimental results show that the proposed method can improve the efficiency and well-being of HRC in human-centric assembly systems.
10.1016/j.jmsy.2025.11.019.title: AR-assisted human-robot collaborative assembly system: Integrating visual language model and deep reinforcement learning for task planning and seamless interactive guidance

10.1016/j.jmsy.2025.12.008.abstract: Against the background of low-carbon and efficient sustainable manufacturing, production scheduling must not only focus on efficiency and delivery times but also balance energy consumption and carbon emission constraints. However, modern manufacturing workshops commonly adopt a model where batch production and trial production coexist. Production orders and equipment load evolve over time, with frequent occurrences of order insertion, maintenance. At the same time, workshop data exhibits multisource, heterogeneous, and time-varying characteristics. It leads to underutilized production information and delayed scheduling decisions, resulting in efficiency losses and redundant energy consumption. To address the above issues, a deep reinforcement learning approach driven by temporal knowledge graph is proposed in this paper. Firstly, a knowledge graph-based workshop scheduling framework is established to perform unified semantic modeling of production factors and the scheduling relationships. It constructs a multidimensional information matrix with temporal rule constraints. Then, a temporal knowledge-driven LSTM-TD3 algorithm is proposed by replacing the original policy network with an LSTM and employing dual Q-networks with policy delay updates to improve training convergence in continuous action spaces. On this basis, an adaptive weighting mechanism for reward functions targeting different production events is defined to achieve a reasonable balance and dynamic decision-making among multiple objectives. Finally, a case study is conducted with a boiler screen tube production line, and a prototype system is built. The results indicate that compared to historical production data, the average energy consumption of production line equipment decreased by 4.10 %, and the overall efficiency of the workshop increased by 14.29 %, validating the effectiveness of this approach.
10.1016/j.jmsy.2025.12.008.title: A deep reinforcement learning approach driven by temporal knowledge graph for dynamic scheduling in discrete manufacturing workshops
10.1016/j.jmsy.2025.12.008.source: ScienceDirect official citation and abstract BibTeX export

10.1016/j.jmsy.2025.12.007.abstract: Modern manufacturing often requires collaboration across multiple factories due to the dispersion of specialized equipment and differences in processing capacity. In such scenarios, jobs must be processed across different sites, and cross-factory transfers significantly impact scheduling performance. This paper studies the distributed job shop scheduling problem with transfers and proposes an Extended Graphical Method with Reinforcement Learning (EGMRL) to effectively address it. The main innovations of EGMRL are fourfold. First, a transfer-zone is introduced into the graphical method, enabling explicit modeling of both intra-factory and inter-factory transportation times. Second, a layered path search algorithm is developed to accelerate path exploration, thereby improving computational efficiency while maintaining accuracy. Third, a Q-learning–based adaptive strategy dynamically guides job deletion and reinsertion according to the inter-factory state, enhancing adaptability across different problem scales. Finally, a tabu search module is integrated as a local improvement strategy to refine factory-level schedules and prevent premature convergence. Comprehensive experiments on 240 extended benchmark instances and a real-world engineering case study demonstrate that EGMRL consistently outperforms four competitive algorithms in terms of solution quality and stability. Furthermore, the results suggest that the extended graphical method provides promising new solution approaches for tackling scheduling problems with other practical constraints, such as worker–machine collaboration and sequence-dependent setup times.
10.1016/j.jmsy.2025.12.007.title: An extended graphical method with reinforcement learning for distributed job shop scheduling problems with transfers

10.1016/j.jmsy.2025.12.016.abstract: As the manufacturing industry evolves towards greater intelligence and flexibility, multi-agent manufacturing systems encounter critical challenges, including frequent dynamic disruptions, inefficient inter-agent collaboration, and underutilized manufacturing knowledge. To address these issues, this paper proposes an LLM-enhanced embodied multi-agent system that integrates embodied perception, analysis, and decision-making to establish a novel self-organizing production paradigm. First, an LLM-driven embodied machine agent is developed. Through the precise mapping of physical entities to internal functional modules, these agents are endowed with the capability for context-aware comprehension of manufacturing domain information. Second, an LLM-enhanced multimodal embodied perception mechanism is designed. By deeply integrating continuous data acquisition with implicit domain knowledge, this mechanism equips the system with the sensory capabilities necessary to capture dynamic disturbances in real time. Building on this, an LLM-driven embodied analysis method is developed for dynamic disturbances. This method, which involves systematic data preprocessing, domain knowledge-integrated multimodal data correlation analysis, and predictive model construction, forms the system’s core ability to identify production schedule anomalies and predict failure trends. Finally, an LLM-integrated embodied decision-making framework is established. This framework balances local autonomy with global goal consensus through self-organizing negotiation and dynamic game mechanisms. It further integrates human problem-solving expertise with the efficiency of machine intelligence to generate optimal production strategies, thereby providing the foundational support for high-level autonomous collaboration among embodied agents. Experimental results demonstrate that this self-organizing mode supported by LLM-enhanced embodied agents can achieve a faster response speed than conventional decision-making methods (e.g., Deep Q-Network) and standalone LLMs (e.g., GPT-4). The proposed system effectively overcomes bottlenecks throughout the perception-analysis-decision-making process, successfully establishing a novel self-organizing production paradigm.
10.1016/j.jmsy.2025.12.016.title: LLM-enhanced embodied multi-agent manufacturing system: A novel self-organizing production paradigm for embodied perception, embodied analysis and embodied decision

10.1016/j.jmsy.2026.01.004.abstract: Amid the transformation driven by Industry 4.0 and 5.0, manufacturing is rapidly advancing toward greater intelligence and flexibility. Reconfigurable Matrix-structured Manufacturing Systems (RMMS) improve adaptability through dynamic structural and resource reconfiguration, while Integrated Process Planning and Scheduling (IPPS) jointly optimizes process routes and scheduling for optimal resource allocation and responsiveness. This study focuses on Dynamic IPPS with Reconfigurable Manufacturing Cells (DIPPS-RMC) in RMMS, and proposes a real-time scheduling approach based on multi-agent Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO) to reduce average tardiness and enhance system efficiency. A Mixed Integer Linear Programming model is established to address the complexity of process flows and dynamic scheduling, providing a solid theoretical foundation. The scheduling problem is further formulated as a Partially Observable Markov Decision Process to capture the uncertainty and partial observability of real manufacturing environments. To alleviate the credit assignment problem and enhance inter-agent coordination, a delayed reward-sharing mechanism is designed. A multi-agent PPO algorithm with centralized training and decentralized execution is introduced, leveraging parallel environment sampling to improve training efficiency and generalization. Extensive experiments on 270 cases across 27 scenarios show that the proposed method outperforms state-of-the-art multi-agent reinforcement learning algorithms in training speed, generalization, and scheduling performance. Its application to real-world cases further demonstrates effective handling of dynamic job arrivals and RMC breakdowns, validating its robustness and practical utility. These results confirm the method’s effectiveness and applicability in dynamic, complex manufacturing environments, offering an innovative solution for real-time scheduling in RMMS.
10.1016/j.jmsy.2026.01.004.title: Real-time dynamic integrated process planning and scheduling with reconfigurable manufacturing cells via multi-agent reinforcement learning

10.1016/j.jmsy.2025.12.027.abstract: As manufacturing scales up and demand for customization grows, computer-aided inspection technologies face increasing pressure to enhance efficiency and capability. Inspection path planning (IPP) for touch-trigger probes on coordinate measuring machines (CMMs) still suffers from heavy reliance on manual rules and poor coordination among planning stages. To address these limitations, this paper proposes a novel approach for IPP based on a hybrid planning framework, called Inspection Path Optimization via Deep Reinforcement Learning & Heuristic Search (InPO-DRLHS). InPO-DRLHS leverages hierarchical reinforcement learning (HRL) to generate collision-free paths (CFPs) while accounting for probe orientation changes, and integrates this architecture with heuristic-based optimization of measurement sequence to improve global planning efficiency. Specifically, within the HRL module: the lower-level agent employs an improved deep Q-learning approach to generate optimal CFPs under fixed probe orientations; the higher-level agent predicts optimal probe rotation positions from a voxelized scene representation, guiding orientation adjustments for the lower-level planning. Furthermore, the value function learned by the HRL module serves as a surrogate heuristic estimate within the heuristic algorithm during sequence planning, enabling path quality assessment without explicit CFP generation. Experimental results show that the proposed method achieves over 90% success rate in 3D CFP planning and reduces total measurement time by 21.7% compared to conventional approaches, indicating substantial gains in inspection efficiency.
10.1016/j.jmsy.2025.12.027.title: An inspection path planning approach based on hierarchical reinforcement learning

10.1016/j.jmsy.2025.12.015.abstract: Low-carbon smart industrial parks face challenges such as the high volatility of renewable energy, highly uncertain load demands, and the pronounced dynamic complexity of multi-energy coupled systems. However, current scheduling systems heavily rely on expert knowledge and statistical correlations, which generally suffer from insufficient accuracy, low efficiency, and poor transparency in decision-making. To address these issues, this paper proposes an energy causality-driven digital twins multi-agent scheduling system, named MCMAS, aimed at achieving high-precision, reliable, and interpretable multi-energy coordinated optimization under complex operating conditions. Initially, a multi-energy causal dynamic model is proposed, which initializes the causal model by integrating conditional mutual information with domain knowledge and applies causal intervention to effectively eliminate spurious correlations, thereby accurately characterizing the high-fidelity causal topology of the system. Subsequently, a causality cognition-driven multi-agent collaborative decision-making mechanism is designed, where a cooperative reward function, integrating local rewards, upstream penalties, and downstream incentives, guides global cooperative strategies of agents, thereby enhancing the economic efficiency and reliability of the scheduling system. Finally, a large language model-driven dual-cross evaluation mechanism is designed, which integrates process mining and counterfactual causal inference to conduct dual-cross validation of scheduling strategies, thereby quantifying confidence levels and enhancing the interpretability of decision-making schemes. Comparative experiments conducted in a representative smart industrial park in Shanghai demonstrate that, compared with benchmark models such as MPC and QMIX-MAS, MCMAS reduces total operating costs by approximately 37.04 %, decreases carbon emissions by 45.19 %, and improves the Sharpe Ratio by 37.3 %. The results indicate that MCMAS can effectively coordinate multi-energy supply and dynamic production loads across different scenarios, reducing operational costs and carbon emissions.
10.1016/j.jmsy.2025.12.015.title: MCMAS: Causality-driven collaborative optimization in low-carbon industrial parks with large language models-empowered multi-agent systems

10.1016/j.jmsy.2026.01.001.abstract: The machining of high-performance, difficult-to-cut materials poses a critical challenge in advanced manufacturing. While laser-assisted machining (LAM) has emerged as a viable solution, its effectiveness is often compromised in practice by insufficient synchronization between laser heating and cutting operations, leading to processing defects. To address this limitation, this study develops an intelligent collaborative LAM system based on digital twin technology. By integrating Unity3D with deep learning techniques, a systematic architecture suitable for laser-thermal-assisted machining is constructed. A dynamic multi-physics field coupling model is established to achieve real-time control of laser incidence posture along with simultaneous monitoring and prediction of the temperature distribution in the machining region. This integrated system exhibits enhanced laser positioning agility, reduced thermal fluctuations, improved laser energy utilization efficiency, and consistent processing quality. Experimental validation conducted on forged superalloy Inconel 718 and SiCp/Al composites demonstrates remarkable improvements in both surface integrity and dimensional accuracy. Moreover, machine learning-based reliability assessment reliability assessment confirms only minor deviations in experimental outcomes, thereby providing a robust intelligent process assurance mechanism for machining difficult-to-process components such as aero-engine blades.
10.1016/j.jmsy.2026.01.001.title: Design of laser-assisted processing digital twin system

10.1016/j.jmsy.2026.01.003.abstract: Advanced Planning and Scheduling (APS) for manufacturing systems is becoming more complex against the backdrop of intelligent transformation and increasing demand for customisation. In real-world APS applications subject to multi-source dynamics, objective alterations, constraints removals/additions, algorithm upgrades are inevitable. Such structural changes of APS, requiring seamless coordination among experts such as production managers, modelling engineers, algorithm developers, are often lengthy and less flexible. This poses new challenges in cross-domain/inter-process coordination and rapid multi-disciplinary knowledge integration/reuse. This paper proposes a novel Agentic AI-Assisted APS (A4PS) framework, utilising Large Language Models (LLMs) and agents to assist modification/update processes of APS. Firstly, a multi-agentic AI-enabled workflow is designed following standard operating procedure of APS to facilitate the cross-domain agent coordination. Secondly, a multi-step knowledge augmentation method is proposed to endow LLM agents with specialised APS knowledge. Thirdly, a Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) and Chain of Thought (CoT)-enhanced method is developed for knowledge use and interaction. Experiments are conducted with an APS dataset which is created based on classical APS cases and manufacturing researchers. Compared with basic LLMs, A4PS exhibited substantially superior performance across both basic and complex cases in metrics such as modelling task success rate, absolute percentage error of solution results, optimisation algorithm code logic completion rate, and code executability rate. Case study demonstrates that A4PS enables LLMs to coordinate, learn APS knowledge, and imitate experts in the reasoning process, and ultimately realise APS assistance using natural language. This work proposes a novel solution that uses LLMs and agentic AI to assist APS modification/update process, contributing to AI-driven smart manufacturing in Industry 4.0.
10.1016/j.jmsy.2026.01.003.title: A4PS: Agentic AI-assisted advanced planning and scheduling with large language models for smart manufacturing

10.1016/j.jmsy.2026.01.016.abstract: The Machining Process Knowledge Base (MPKB) is foundational to intelligent process decision-making, directly impacting manufacturing efficiency and quality. While Large Language Models (LLMs) have shown promise in automated MPKB construction, they face a critical challenge in manufacturing: industrial knowledge graph (KG) schemas often exceed the context windows of lightweight LLMs deployable by small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs). This limitation forces the construction process to operate with incomplete schema information, leading to missed entity relationships, semantic heterogeneity, and conceptual ambiguities in the MPKB. This study proposes an improved LLM-KG collaborative framework that overcomes these limitations through: (1) employing a staged, schema-decoupled extraction strategy, which enables open triple collection without injecting the full schema; (2) introducing a Code-Style knowledge representation method that efficiently encodes complex machining schemas, reducing the semantic load while maintaining structural integrity; and (3) constructing a retrieval-driven pipeline for semantic standardization that integrates dynamic schema segmentation and bidirectional validation, utilizing LLMs to achieve interpretable synonym merging and eliminate heterogeneity. This study empirically validated the proposed approach using machining process data provided by an aviation enterprise. Experimental results demonstrate that our framework achieves at least a 3.3% improvement in MPKB construction quality and a 25% increase in machining process quality metrics compared to the other baseline models. The implementation and data have been made available on GitHub to facilitate reproducibility and further research.
10.1016/j.jmsy.2026.01.016.title: An improved large language model and knowledge graph integration method for automated machining process base construction

10.1016/j.jmsy.2026.01.011.abstract: The integration of large language models (LLMs) into human-robot collaboration (HRC) represents a paradigm shift toward cognitive manufacturing under Industry 5.0. This systematic review analyzes 1278 publications to elucidate the enabling mechanisms, application hierarchies, and persistent challenges of LLM-enhanced HRC. We identify three agent paradigms, each tailored to structured, interactive, and sensor-rich scenarios, respectively. Furthermore, we propose a layered training framework combining domain-adaptive pre-training and scenario-specific fine-tuning to bridge general LLMs capabilities with industrial demands. Our findings reveal that LLMs significantly advance HRC in environmental perception, long-horizon task planning, and embodied interaction, yet face critical challenges in dynamic adaptability, multimodal fusion, and value alignment. This study provides a structured reference for developing robust, interpretable, and human-centric collaborative systems, outlining five key research directions to guide future advancements in cognitive manufacturing.
10.1016/j.jmsy.2026.01.011.title: Large language models in human-robot collaboration: A systematic review, trends, and challenges

10.1016/j.jmsy.2026.01.009.abstract: Human-Centric Smart Manufacturing (HCSM) has become a central theme of Industry 5.0, promoting collaborative interactions between humans and intelligent systems. Nevertheless, HCSM technologies have been struggling to reach their full potential due to the lack of digital literacy among manufacturing workers, particularly in real-time machine monitoring. Current monitoring systems with rigid interfaces limit the operators to handle Industrial Internet of Things (IIoT) systems to directly query manufacturing data for further analysis without external technical support. To address such bottlenecks, we propose CNC-Talks, a conversational machine monitoring framework that integrates Large Language Models (LLMs) to enable natural language-driven interactions with real-time Computer Numerical Control (CNC) machine data. Leveraging LLM-based multi-agent collaboration and Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG), CNC-Talks interactively retrieves data from real-time IIoT database while also supporting context-aware responses based on the collected data, which reduces reliance on technical support from software engineers. As CNC-Talks allows rapid adaptation of LLM Application Programming Interfaces (APIs) via prompting techniques, its performance is evaluated across multiple versions, each combining different LLMs and prompts, using various types of questions. Notably, our framework demonstrates its reliability in human-data interaction for industrial applications, achieving 93.3 % accuracy in responding to complex queries that require advanced data inference like production tracking. Furthermore, possible failure modes are thoroughly analyzed based on interaction scenarios among multiple LLM-based agents. Such results highlight the potential of the framework as a cornerstone for HCSM.
10.1016/j.jmsy.2026.01.009.title: CNC-talks: Conversational machine monitoring via large language model and real-time data retrieval augmented generation
10.1016/j.jmsy.2026.01.009.source: ScienceDirect official citation and abstract BibTeX export

10.1016/j.jmsy.2026.01.005.abstract: The conventional Industry 4.0 architecture of manufacturing and warehousing is hardware-centric, limiting flexibility and adaptability. The material handling systems deploy heterogeneous multiple agents that have an application or environment-specific discrete control layer. This work presents the concept of a Software-Defined Factory and its control system for a software-centric control. The software-defined factory integrates industrial hardware and software systems, hosting the control system, AI, simulation, and digital twins to enable seamless material flow throughout the factory through heterogeneous multi-agent control. The presented control system has a centralized architecture designed with a bottom-up approach for commercial systems. It manages communication, localization, navigation, and task allocation in a heterogeneous multi-vendor fleet deployed in real-world scenarios. The latency, accuracy, repeatability, planning-level scalability, and path execution evaluations of the proposed system were conducted with heterogeneous fleets. The operation of overhead hoist transport vehicles with automated guided vehicles on a scaled semiconductor manufacturing shop floor demonstrated heterogeneous hardware integration for material handling in industrial settings. The proposed system has potential to mitigate major challenges in deployment, data interoperability, and hardware dependency for diverse industrial applications, including manufacturing, warehousing, and inspection.
10.1016/j.jmsy.2026.01.005.title: Heterogeneous multi-agent fleet control system for material handling in a Software-Defined Factory
10.1016/j.jmsy.2026.01.005.source: ScienceDirect official citation and abstract BibTeX export

10.1016/j.jmsy.2026.02.011.abstract: Personalized customization increases the complexity of the hybrid flow shop production environment, which is characterized by the presence of variable discrete events. The buffer capacities of machines and the transportation times between processing stages and the warehouse influence the overall production process. Therefore, the research problem addressed in this paper is the real-time scheduling problem for hybrid flow shops with limited buffers and transportation time. To effectively tackle this challenging scheduling problem, this paper proposes a discrete-event-driven heterogeneous cooperative multi-agent deep reinforcement learning (HC-MADRL) framework. Within this framework, two types of heterogeneous scheduling agents are designed: the Job Agent (JA) and Stage-Machine Agents (SMAs). The JA employs an integrated LSTM-Pointer Network (LPN) architecture to select the most appropriate job based on the current job sequence states in real time. In contrast, the SMAs utilize a Transformer-based weighted network (TWN) incorporating a machine mask mechanism to assign the selected job to the optimal machine according to the state of its processing stage. Then, eight real-time job states and five generic stage-machine states are designed for the JA and SMAs, respectively. Meanwhile, a multi-level reward mechanism with reward shaping is proposed to guide the agents in learning to optimize the scheduling objective. Based on this, this paper presents an independent multi-agent proximal policy optimization (I-MAPPO) training algorithm that integrates two critic networks for heterogeneous multi-agent systems. Lastly, the experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method exhibits superior scheduling performance and real-time responsiveness compared with four benchmark real-time scheduling methods: PDRs, DQN, PPO, MAPPO and other two advanced multi-agent schedulers.
10.1016/j.jmsy.2026.02.011.title: The end-to-end real-time scheduling method for hybrid flow shop based on heterogeneous cooperative multi-agent deep reinforcement learning
10.1016/j.jmsy.2026.02.011.source: ScienceDirect official citation and abstract BibTeX export

10.1016/j.jmsy.2026.02.013.abstract: Human-robot collaborative (HRC) assembly has emerged as a core pivotal technology for the high-efficiency manufacturing of complex products. Nevertheless, existing systems still face critical challenges: the difficulty in translating unstructured user assembly intent into standardized task execution, insufficient scenario-specific perceptual understanding of assembly contexts, and the lack of robust safety guarantees and intuitive operational guidance. To address these critical challenges, a novel embodied multi-agent system (MAS) integrated with a vision-language model (VLM) for digital twin (DT)-enabled HRC assembly is proposed in this paper, which constructs a closed-loop workflow encompassing multi-modal perception and reasoning (“insight”) as well as autonomous robot execution and collaboration (“action”). First, a collaborative embodied multi-agent framework is constructed to encompass task management, perception, reasoning, robot execution, and augmented reality (AR) execution, enabling seamless transition from unstructured assembly intent to standardized HRC implementation. Second, domain knowledge fine-tuning is performed on the VLM to achieve end-to-end understanding of visual inputs and semantic alignment with textual descriptions in assembly scenarios, thereby providing precise scenario-adapted perceptual support. Third, a cyber-physical mapping environment is built using DT technology to facilitate simulation verification of robot motion planning and real-time scene mapping for AR-guided operations. The experimental results verify that the proposed system effectively mitigates the limitations of existing HRC assembly systems, enabling efficient, adaptive, and safe collaborative assembly while laying a solid foundation for the intelligent upgrading of complex product assembly processes.
10.1016/j.jmsy.2026.02.013.title: From insight to action: Embodied multi-agent system integrating vision language model for digital twin-assisted human-robot collaborative assembly
10.1016/j.jmsy.2026.02.013.source: ScienceDirect official citation and abstract BibTeX export

10.1016/j.jmsy.2026.02.010.abstract: Aircraft tooling serves as the positioning reference for component assembly, and its real-time displacement monitoring and evaluation are critical to ensuring assembly quality and efficiency. However, existing laser- and vision-based inspection methods struggle to meet the requirements of real-time monitoring due to limited accessibility and low efficiency in confined and occluded assembly environments. To address these pressing engineering needs and current technical limitations, a digital twin-enabled system for real-time interactive monitoring and evaluation of aircraft tooling (DTSAT) in the assembly process is proposed. Based on the proposed DTSAT framework, key enabling methods were developed to achieve ms-level full-field displacement monitoring using only sparse local measurements, while also supporting interactive anomaly alerts throughout the assembly process. In addition, the system integrates a high-performance data storage and retrieval mechanism to ensure full traceability of assembly-related information. A case study on the front spar assembly of an aircraft horizontal tail demonstrates the system’s performance and robustness in monitoring, evaluation, data processing, and traceability, offering a valuable reference for the development of monitoring and evaluation systems under complex manufacturing conditions.
10.1016/j.jmsy.2026.02.010.title: A digital twin-enabled system for real-time interactive monitoring and evaluation of aircraft tooling in the assembly process
10.1016/j.jmsy.2026.02.010.source: ScienceDirect official citation and abstract BibTeX export

10.1016/j.jmsy.2026.02.016.abstract: As industrial equipment is increasingly applied in manufacturing, it is necessary to adopt advanced maintenance techniques to ensure stable equipment operation. Maintenance decision support is essential for industrial equipment, but information fragmentation and complex reasoning hinder its progress. To address these challenges, we propose MAKG (Multi-Agent and synergistic Knowledge Graph), a framework that synergizes Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) with a multi-agent system for intelligent industrial equipment maintenance. The MAKG framework uses these Large Language Models (LLM) agents to work together, drawing information from a diverse knowledge base to produce coordinated responses to equipment faults. Our method focuses on fine-tuning the embedding models with domain-specific data. This approach avoids the high computational cost of re-training the entire LLM and improves performance in the specific industrial context. In the experimental study, the MAKG framework was validated using real-world industrial operation and maintenance data, achieving a reasoning accuracy of 90.1% and demonstrating its potential for intelligent maintenance of industrial equipment. Code is available at https://github.com/LAM2360/MAKG_demo/tree/master.
10.1016/j.jmsy.2026.02.016.title: A Multi-Agent and synergistic Knowledge Graph retrieval-augmented generation framework for intelligent maintenance

10.1016/j.jmsy.2026.02.007.abstract: Identifying feature points in G code is crucial for improving machining accuracy and efficiency in CNC machining. Traditional methods rely on engineers’ experience and predefined geometric thresholds, which commonly fail to account for the actual kinematic and kinetic conditions of the machine tool. This paper proposes a novel, data-driven approach to feature point identification by leveraging both kinematic and geometric information from G code trajectories. A five-phase jerk-limited S-shape interpolation algorithm is employed to generate kinematic characteristics for each point along the trajectory, while three key geometric features are defined to support accurate identification. Building on this, we propose a CNC Machining Data Flow-based Long Short-Term Memory (CMDF-LSTM) model that combines both kinematic and geometric data to automate feature point identification. A training dataset consisting of 12 workpieces and over 105 G code files is generated using Mastercam, with more than 107 setpoints computed through interpolation. The cutting experiments are conducted to verify that the machining defects occur at the feature points identified by our method, and the real-time feed rate recorded during machining process and cutting forces monitored by intelligent spindle system further demonstrate the effectiveness. The cutting experiments are conducted to verify that the machining defects occur at the feature points identified by our method, and quantitative surface roughness measurements at the machined surface further enhance the credibility of experimental conclusions. In addition, the real-time feedrate recorded during machining process and cutting forces monitored by intelligent spindle system demonstrate the effectiveness from multiple dimensions. This approach provides a scalable and efficient solution for feature point identification in real-world CNC machining applications.
10.1016/j.jmsy.2026.02.007.title: CMDF-LSTM-driven feature point identification of CNC G code leveraging geometric and kinematic information

10.1016/j.jmsy.2026.02.008.abstract: Smart manufacturing is transforming manufacturing landscapes through the integration of advanced information and communication technologies. The emergence of large language models (LLMs) has revolutionized artificial intelligence (AI). However, the application of LLMs in smart manufacturing remains underexplored to address the domain-specific challenges. This paper presents a comprehensive survey and analysis of LLM-enabled smart manufacturing. The latest advancements in LLM for smart manufacturing and the key techniques in LLMs are first reviewed. Subsequently, the key enablers for deploying LLM for smart manufacturing are explored, which include the knowledge graph (KG), agent system, and model context protocol (MCP). Then, the capability across four critical manufacturing domains, including product design, process optimization, predictive maintenance, and remanufacturing are systematically analyzed. Finally, the challenges and opportunities of scaling laws, data privacy and security concerns, the interpretability of LLMs, and the domain-specific knowledge integration within the manufacturing context are also discussed. The outcomes of this research contribute to a responsible and efficient adoption of LLMs, laying a foundation for advancing smart manufacturing practices.
10.1016/j.jmsy.2026.02.008.title: Leveraging large language models for smart manufacturing: Reviews, enablers, challenges, and opportunities
10.1016/j.jmsy.2026.02.008.source: ScienceDirect official citation and abstract BibTeX export

10.1016/j.jmsy.2026.02.009.abstract: Efficient recycling and reuse of end-of-life products through robot-assisted disassembly has attracted widespread attention in sustainable manufacturing industry. In the robot-assisted disassembly system, the high-precision identification of products and their components is the premise of autonomous disassembly. A series of product identification methods based on deep learning in literature can well identify specific categories of components such as screws. However, different service conditions make products in industrial scenarios highly uncertain in terms of component status, shape and position changes, which make it impossible to predefine categories for products and components, and to obtain high-quality training data sets for new categories in advance. These obstacles make the application of the identification methods to industrial scenarios still challenging. In this paper, a two-stage product identification method based on neural–symbolic reasoning is proposed. In the first stage, deep learning-based methods are used to detect component primitives with limited categories, rather than directly detecting components whose categories cannot be predefined. In the second stage, the logic rules embedded in the word vector space are used to program the detected primitives to infer the semantics of the component to be detected. In addition, a primitive sampling method is proposed to generate new rules by sampling existing rules in the word vector space to improve the generalization of the proposed identification method. The results show a significant increase from 20.01% to 80.89% in successful component identification for the PC product family, along with considerable improvement for others. Code and data are available at http://github.com/nowheresin/neural-symbolic-reasoning-product-identification/.
10.1016/j.jmsy.2026.02.009.title: Neural–symbolic reasoning for end-of-life product identification in robot-assisted disassembly
10.1016/j.jmsy.2026.02.009.source: ScienceDirect official citation and abstract BibTeX export

10.1016/j.jmsy.2026.01.014.abstract: The rapid rise of Industry 4.0 and the Internet of Things (IoT) has elevated digital twins from a novel concept to an indispensable tool for real-time monitoring, prediction, and optimization in complex systems. Yet, maintaining the accuracy and reliability of digital twins remains a formidable challenge. As physical entities evolve and operational environments shift, especially in data-driven and resource-constrained contexts, digital twins are prone to degradation, reducing their value and trustworthiness. To address these challenges, in this paper, we introduce a framework that integrates a Separated-Feature Dual-Branch Pose Network (SFDPoseNet) with a credible evolution mechanism. The architecture disentangles and extracts both long-term and short-term features of the twin system in parallel. Specifically, Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) networks capture long-range temporal dependencies, while Temporal Convolutional Networks (TCN) extract multi-scale local patterns. We propose a lightweight residual Feedforward Neural Network (FFN) that integrates features from dual branches to achieve robust and expressive multivariate time-series forecasting. Complementing this hybrid model, an uncertainty-aware online evolution strategy ensures adaptability. Real-time prediction errors trigger dynamic model updates, while incremental learning with Fisher information–based regularization stabilizes the adaptation process and mitigates catastrophic forgetting. Extensive validation on a quadrotor UAV (unmanned aerial vehicle) flight dataset confirms that the proposed method significantly outperforms state-of-the-art temporal prediction models in both forecasting accuracy and adaptability. Additional ablation studies highlight the distinct contributions of the dual-branch architecture and the evolution mechanism, underscoring the framework’s capability to sustain digital twin reliability under dynamic conditions.
10.1016/j.jmsy.2026.01.014.title: An SFDPose network with credible evolution mechanism for digital twin systems in industrial applications
10.1016/j.jmsy.2026.01.014.source: ScienceDirect official citation and abstract BibTeX export

10.1016/j.jmsy.2026.02.019.abstract: The docking of the nozzle and combustion chamber is a critical process in the assembly of solid rocket motors. Currently, docking assembly largely relies on manual operations, which constrains production efficiency. To address this, a digital twin-based high-quality assembly method for large-diameter cabin sections is proposed. First, a digital twin model is established using 3D scanning of the physical components. To tackle the challenge of detecting complex 3D assembly features, a feature target-guided digital modeling approach is introduced. By incorporating geometrically marked targets and constructing a digital model with identifiable feature points, the reconstruction of complex feature information is achieved. Subsequently, a collaborative virtual–physical assembly method is developed, employing a multi-camera system for online tracking of the physical components via the digital model. An elliptical cone model is constructed to resolve the misalignment between the center of a perspectively projected ellipse and the actual spatial circle center. The iterative closest point (ICP) based relative pose estimation method is applied to enhance the speed and accuracy of multi-camera vision pose measurement. Finally, a platform was built to validate the accuracy and efficiency of the proposed method. Experimental results demonstrate that the digital twin-based assembly approach enables high-efficiency assembly, while also allowing online monitoring and collision warning in visually obscured areas during the process.
10.1016/j.jmsy.2026.02.019.title: Digital twin-based high-precision assembly method for large-diameter cabin section docking

10.1016/j.jmsy.2026.02.017.abstract: The rapid evolution of smart manufacturing has led to an explosion of multimodal data generated from sensors, such as vibration signals, acoustic waves, and surface images. However, traditional learning models often focus on single-modal analysis and lack interpretability, limiting their generalization across different industrial tasks. To address these challenges, this study proposes industrial AI copilot QwIndustry, a multimodal large language model (LLM) designed for industrial tasks, including defect detection and fault diagnosis. The framework integrates a Knowledge-guided Mixture-of-Experts (K-MoE) architecture, which selects different expert neural networks based on the specific industrial task. The parameter-efficient Low-Rank Adaptation (LoRA) is adopted to fine-tune Qwen2.5VL, and Chain-of-Thought (COT) distillation to facilitate knowledge-driven multimodal reasoning, enabling the model to achieve reasoning capabilities at a low computational cost. Five diverse industrial datasets involving signal, image, and text modalities were employed to train and evaluate the model. Experimental results show that the proposed QwIndustry with thinking mode achieves superior accuracy over 98% on same-domain tasks and strong cross-domain transferability with accuracy around 95%, maintaining high recognition accuracy on unseen datasets without retraining. Moreover, the model provides human operators with accessible, interpretable reasoning results through natural-language interaction, eliminating the need for deep technical expertise. These results indicate that the Industrial AI Copilot provides an effective and scalable pathway toward knowledge-augmented, human-centric, and interpretable industrial intelligence.
10.1016/j.jmsy.2026.02.017.title: Knowledge-guided multimodal LLM with mixture-of-experts for interpretable defect detection and fault diagnosis: An industrial AI copilot

10.1016/j.jmsy.2026.03.002.abstract: Manufacturing process planning is a progressive design process where designers use digital modeling information as a starting point to meticulously plan and optimize the product manufacturing workflow. This process involving repeated consideration of elements such as processing units, manufacturing operations and operation steps. Process planning is characterized as a hierarchical design process driven by stage-specific task objectives, in which decision constraints evolve progressively. The knowledge requirements for tasks at different stages not only influence the prioritization of knowledge focus but also impose differentiated demands on knowledge granularity, association patterns, and reasoning approaches. Thus, supporting multi-stage, multi-type decision-making simultaneously within a unified knowledge organization framework presents a critical and complex challenge. This study proposes a knowledge service model for process planning based on multi-layer knowledge graph. An iterative interaction model between knowledge evolution and process planning is proposed, in which four representative planning scenarios are explicitly characterized to reflect cross-stage reasoning requirements. Four process-planning-oriented retrieval strategies are defined, enabling differentiated retrieval mechanisms to accommodate heterogeneous task demands and planning objectives. A collaborative workflow integrating large language models (LLMs) and knowledge graphs is adopted to achieve unified semantic modeling and structured knowledge extraction of multi-source process knowledge. The proposed method was validated using civil aircraft bracket component manufacturing process planning tasks as verification cases.
10.1016/j.jmsy.2026.03.002.title: An LLM-enhanced knowledge service methodology for manufacturing process planning based on task- guided multi-layer knowledge graph

10.1016/j.jmsy.2026.02.021.abstract: Industrial systems are moving away from the efficiency-driven mindset of Industry 4.0 towards the more human-focused approach of Industry 5.0, which emphasizes symbiotic manufacturing, resilience, and sustainability. As part of this shift, flexible workshop scheduling needs to continuously adapt and make decisions that are both explainable and responsive to disruptions like fluctuating processing times, equipment failures, and changing order arrivals. This paper highlights the shortcomings of current heuristic methods and introduces a new approach—a Multi-agent, Human–machine Collaborative Resilient Scheduling (MHCRS) system tailored for Industry 5.0. The system uses cognitive digital twins to create a realistic pool of potential disturbances, ensuring consistency between offline learning and real-time operations. Based on this, a Large Reasoning Model (LRM) generates structured and actionable scheduling rules within a defined set of possibilities. A multi-armed bandit mechanism speeds up the process of screening, integrating, and refining rules under conditions with limited data, allowing the rules to evolve smoothly over time while supporting human–machine collaboration and compliance checks. The experiments show that the system, using a process of “LRM generation–Bandit self-evolution–twin evaluation”, can automatically uncover robust rules with better generalization, achieving performance similar to advanced swarm intelligence algorithms. It does so while reducing the time spent searching for solutions by almost ten times, making it highly efficient and practical for real-time rescheduling needs in factory workshops. This work offers a solid framework for scheduling in Industry 5.0, combining resilience, transparency, and continuous evolution.
10.1016/j.jmsy.2026.02.021.title: Digital twin-integrated bandit learning for LRM-driven multi-agent resilient production scheduling

10.1016/j.jmsy.2026.03.007.abstract: As a crucial step in steel manufacturing, process planning significantly improves production efficiency and product quality. With the development of knowledge graph (KG) technologies, significant progress has been made in using historical knowledge for intelligent process planning. However, existing KG-based methods mostly rely on static knowledge reuse, which fails to accommodate real-time fluctuations of smelting conditions in steel manufacturing. Moreover, the generation of process planning strategies remains heavily dependent on human expertise, making it time-consuming and labor-intensive. To address these challenges, this paper proposes a dynamic-static KG-enhanced Large Language Model (LLM)-based intelligent process planning method for steel manufacturing. Firstly, a static smelting process KG (SSPKG) is introduced to organize historical smelting knowledge using a convolutional block attention mechanism-enhanced partitioned fusion Kolmogorov-Arnold network (CBAM-PFKAN). Then, a dynamic smelting condition KG (DSCKG) is established to convert the real-time smelting conditions into structured knowledge triples based on predefined rules. Secondly, a plan-and-solve (PS) prompting strategy is designed to guide LLMs in decomposing complex process optimization queries, retrieving both static and dynamic knowledge from the KGs, and generating process schemes step-by-step. Finally, the proposed method is validated through an industry case study. Compared to baseline methods, the proposed approach achieves superior performance in process knowledge extraction, improving the accuracy of generated process strategies by 11.13% on DeepSeek and 8.63% on ChatGPT-3.5, respectively.
10.1016/j.jmsy.2026.03.007.title: Dynamic-static knowledge graph enhanced LLM reasoning for intelligent process planning in steel manufacturing

10.1016/j.jmsy.2026.03.011.abstract: Equipment fault-investigation documents contain rich semantic information that implicitly describes causal states and failure mechanisms of key components. However, due to the high complexity of equipment faults and the dynamic evolution of causal chains after interventions, current LLMs struggle to model long-chain causal relations and multi-coupled composite-fault semantics. These limitations hinder accurate inference of intervention effects and constrain effective root-cause localization and solution decision-making. To address these challenges, we propose the long causal chain-of-thought (LC-CoT) method, which enhances hypergraph-based Causal-LLM intervention reasoning for compound fault diagnosis (CFD). First, a few-shot LC-CoT prompting strategy guides the LLM to analyze fault trees hierarchically and automatically construct a causal knowledge hypergraph (CKH). Second, a reinforcement learning strategy with causal-intervention feedback is employed to train the Causal-LLM for long-chain causal reasoning and dynamic intervention. Third, an LC-CoT reasoning algorithm integrates fine-grained CKH retrieval with intervention reasoning, enabling accurate diagnosis in compound fault scenarios. Finally, a CKH was constructed based on a bridge-crane case study, and 47,466 triplets were employed to train the Causal-LLM. Ablation and comparative experiments on CFD tasks further demonstrated the superiority and effectiveness of the proposed method in root-cause analysis, solution decision-making, and intervention reasoning.
keywords: Reinforcement learning with causal intervention feedback
10.1016/j.jmsy.2026.03.011.title: Long causal chain-of-thought for compound fault diagnosis: enhancing hypergraph-based Causal-LLM intervention reasoning

10.1016/j.jmsy.2026.03.019.abstract: Robotic multiple peg-in-hole assembly faces challenges stemming from high-dimensional spatial coupling with complex constraints, difficulties in visual localization, force sensing and compliant control, and limited policy generalization. To address these issues, we develop a hierarchical strategy learning method that integrates diffusion-based deep reinforcement learning with admittance control. Specifically, to realize expert-guided insertion behaviors for assembly, the overall policy is decomposed into a high-level decision layer and a low-level execution layer. The high level employs a conditional diffusion policy to generate subgoals and updates them using an SAC value function, thereby accelerating learning and improving generalization. The low level adopts a TD3 continuous controller whose actions are fused online with admittance-based compliant control under physical constraints. During training, to reduce cross-layer optimization mismatch, an off-policy correction mechanism is introduced to mitigate instability due to optimization mismatch between layers and to rectify distributional bias. Comparative evaluations and experiments show that, relative to PPO and PPO+AC, the proposed method increases assembly success rate by 18.7% and 7.9%, respectively, while reducing the number of assembly steps by 130.7% and 38.0%. Compared with DDPG, it achieves success rate improvements of 32.5% and 15.8%, with step reductions of 261.5% and 54.9%. The method achieves smaller contact forces and fewer steps, with repeated trials attaining a 95% success rate; the maximum normal contact force along the Z axis is about 5 N and the maximum torque is about 0.2 N m, validating that the proposed hierarchical strategy yields superior skill learning and higher assembly success.
10.1016/j.jmsy.2026.03.019.title: Diffusion-guided hierarchical reinforcement learning with admittance control for multiple peg-in-hole robotic assembly

10.1016/j.jmsy.2026.03.015.abstract: Real-time monitoring and precise quality prediction in modern manufacturing face severe challenges due to the dynamic time-varying characteristics of production systems. To address the limitations of traditional methods in adapting to these characteristics and the disjointedness between event identification and quality prediction, a collaborative prediction framework based on a Time-Varying Digital Twin System (TV-DTS) is proposed. First, a key event identification method that fuses temporal reconstruction deviations with multi-dimensional dynamic statistical features is designed to simultaneously capture global dynamic pattern deviations and local fluctuations during system operation. Second, by combining rule-based reasoning with mutual information analysis, an event-scenario matching mechanism is established to achieve an effective association between key events and production scenario semantics. Finally, event information and scenario semantics were incorporated into a quality prediction model to form an event-scenario fusion-driven quality prediction approach. A case study on the tobacco loosening and conditioning process demonstrated that the proposed framework effectively distinguished complex anomaly patterns, improved the accuracy of key event identification, and significantly reduced quality prediction errors, indicating its potential applicability for continuous manufacturing processes with similar time-varying characteristics.
10.1016/j.jmsy.2026.03.015.title: Digital twin-driven key events and product quality prediction for time-varying manufacturing system

10.1016/j.jmsy.2026.03.013.abstract: Additive Manufacturing (AM) offers great design freedom, enabling the fabrication of geometrically complex, multi-material, multi-scale, and functionally optimized parts. However, it also introduces unique challenges regarding manufacturability constraints and complicated interdependencies among design, manufacturing process, and material properties. Recent advances in Generative Artificial Intelligence (GenAI) offer new opportunities to enhance AM workflow through data-driven approaches. This paper presents a comprehensive review of GenAI in AM, examining how advances in visual generative models and large language models, ranging from adversarial, variational, and diffusion-based architectures to foundation models like GPT, are reshaping design generation, process intelligence, and knowledge-driven manufacturing workflows. By integrating AM-specific insights into the generation process, VGMs enable generative design for AM, future build status prediction, process monitoring image enhancement, and data synthesis for downstream model training. Meanwhile, the powerful reasoning capabilities of LLMs enable knowledge acquisition, text-guided script synthesis for design and executable code generation, and adaptive process optimization. The review systematically assesses model architectures, applications, and performance across AM workflows, highlighting current challenges in data availability, constraint integration, three-dimensional (3D) generation, multi-source information fusion, and benchmarking. Future research directions toward context-aware, physics-informed, unified, and trustworthy GenAI frameworks are discussed to advance material design and enable smart, adaptive AM systems.
10.1016/j.jmsy.2026.03.013.title: A review of Generative Artificial Intelligence for additive manufacturing: Bridging design, process monitoring, and beyond
10.1016/j.jmsy.2026.03.013.source: ScienceDirect official citation and abstract BibTeX export

10.1016/j.jmsy.2026.03.012.abstract: The energy-efficient multi-objective dynamic planning problem (EEMODPP) of hot rolling production is a pivotal production management task in steel enterprises. In particular, the dynamic nature and multiple conflicting objectives of the EEMODPP necessitate an intelligent planning approach that can rapidly respond to disruptions in the production environment while making effective trade-offs. To address this, a deep reinforcement learning (DRL)-based predictive-reactive framework is proposed to efficiently generate an initial plan and reactive plans in response to five types of dynamic events, including urgent order insertion, order property modification, machine deterioration, downstream requirements, and periodical replanning. First, a novel mathematical model for the EEMODPP is established to minimize production cost, tardiness, energy consumption, and schedule instability simultaneously. Second, to efficiently solve each replanning problem, a multi-objective pointer network with knowledge transfer (MOPN-KT) is developed. Specifically, the EEMODPP is reformulated as a series of Markov decision processes after decomposition into scalarized subproblems, where DRL policies are parameterized as pointer networks to make sequential decisions by forming probability distributions over unplanned orders. Third, variable neighborhood search (VNS) is integrated into the training process of MOPN-KT to enhance policy learning, while an incremental reference vector activation-based knowledge transfer strategy is proposed to accelerate training. Ablation experiments validate the effectiveness of the VNS integration and the knowledge transfer strategy. Comparative tests against state-of-the-art multi-objective optimization methods on synthetic instances demonstrate the superiority of MOPN-KT in terms of solution quality and running time. Finally, a real-world case study from a steel company verifies its practical applicability.
10.1016/j.jmsy.2026.03.012.title: Reinforcement learning for energy-efficient multi-objective dynamic planning of hot rolling production
10.1016/j.jmsy.2026.03.012.source: ScienceDirect official citation and abstract BibTeX export

10.1016/j.jmsy.2026.02.014.abstract: The rapid advances in Large Language Models (LLMs) have the potential to transform the manufacturing industry by optimizing processes, enhancing efficiency, and enabling innovation at an unprecedented scale. This paper presents a comprehensive study of LLM integration into the manufacturing domain, highlighting their ability to automate and enhance key tasks across the product lifecycle—including product design, quality control, supply chain management, and talent development. We introduce a systematic taxonomy of LLM applications aligned with manufacturing stages, and evaluate the performance of state-of-the-art models (e.g., GPT-4V) in tasks such as document analysis, code generation, design automation, and multimodal reasoning. Our study further explores the use of LLMs in manufacturing education, robotics programming, and the industrial metaverse, supported by real-world case studies and visual frameworks. Key contributions of this work include: (1) a task-aligned framework that bridges LLM capabilities with domain-specific manufacturing challenges, (2) in-depth comparative evaluations with traditional approaches, and (3) a critical discussion of limitations, deployment challenges, and future research directions. By consolidating emerging use cases and practical insights, this paper serves as a foundational reference for researchers and practitioners aiming to harness LLMs for next-generation intelligent manufacturing.
10.1016/j.jmsy.2026.02.014.title: Large Language Models for manufacturing
