10.1016/j.jmsy.2026.03.017.abstract: As the artificial intelligence (AI) driven by large language models (LLMs) evolves rapidly, collaborative product development (CPD) is experiencing a paradigm shift toward intelligence and automation. However, direct deployment of LLMs in CPD faces inherent limitations: standalone LLM reasoning fails to guarantee controllability and reliability in complex design processes, while traditional CPD suffers from inefficient cross-stage collaboration and knowledge fragmentation. To address these dual issues, a novel intelligent CPD paradigm (CPDTeam) for structured collaboration and iterative optimization in complex CPD scenarios is proposed in this study. Specifically, a node-wise human feedback mechanism is embedded to rectify AI deviations, while a self-evolution mechanism is integrated into LLMs to upgrade domain-specific design capabilities. For concrete implementation of the CPDTeam, a knowledge graph (KG) is first constructed with a customer requirements-function-behavior-structure orientation. Subsequently, an automatic design scheme generation framework embedded with retrieval-augmented generation (RAG)-chain-of-thought (CoT) dual-driven mechanism is presented to enhance the domain compliance and structural rationality. Then, the generated design schemes are optimized by the role-specific LLM-based multi-agent system, in which a knowledge-attention dual-critic multi-agent deep deterministic policy gradient (KADC-MADDPG) algorithm serves as a dynamic strategy optimizer. This endows the process with quantifiable criteria and adaptability, boosting the credibility of optimized schemes. Finally, a case study of new energy vehicle development is conducted, where LLM configuration for CPDTeam is selected via comparison of diverse LLMs. Furthermore, CPDTeam is benchmarked against representative multi-agent frameworks, demonstrating its superior design quality, consistency and robustness.
10.1016/j.jmsy.2026.03.017.title: CPDTeam: A KG-RAG-CoT dual-driven and deep reinforcement learning-augmented multi-agent framework for intelligent collaborative product development
10.1016/j.jmsy.2026.03.017.source: ScienceDirect official citation and abstract BibTeX export

10.1016/j.jmsy.2026.03.021.abstract: In hot strip rolling (HSR) production, strip profile quality is critical to product performance and subsequent processing. Compared with finite element and mechanistic models that depend on prior assumptions, machine learning (ML) can efficiently capture the complex nonlinear relationships between process parameters and profile, thereby offering significant advantages in predictive accuracy. However, most existing strip profile prediction approaches rely on single “black-box” ML models and are limited to mean value prediction, which fails to simultaneously capture the overall evolution of the strip full-length profile and its local fluctuations. This limitation primarily arises from the inherent residuals of single ML model predictions, which are often associated with long-term process drifts or short-term disturbances during rolling. Furthermore, the lack of transparent physical interpretability in “black-box” models restricts their trustworthy deployment in industrial practice. To address the above challenges, we propose a novel paradigm for high-precision and interpretable strip profile prediction, which integrates efficient profile feature extraction, light gradient boosting machine (LightGBM)-based multi-scale residual correction regression, and shapley additive explanations (SHAP)-driven post-hoc interpretability analysis, thereby achieving a balance among predictive accuracy, robustness, and transparency. This framework has been successfully deployed on a 2250 mm HSR production line. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed feature extraction method achieves superior reconstruction accuracy compared with both the sixth-order polynomial fitting method and the legendre polynomial fitting method. In industrial applications, the proposed framework demonstrated high prediction accuracy for C40, with more than 93% of the coils showing prediction errors within ±4 μm. Moreover, the SHAP-based feature contribution analysis revealed the key process variables governing strip profile formation, thereby ensuring both transparency and reliability of the proposed prediction paradigm.
10.1016/j.jmsy.2026.03.021.title: Interpretable data-driven framework with multi-scale residual correction and SHAP analysis for strip profile prediction in hot rolling steel industry
10.1016/j.jmsy.2026.03.021.source: ScienceDirect official citation and abstract BibTeX export

10.1016/j.jmsy.2026.04.003.abstract: Real-time performance analysis and optimization of complex, multi-station assembly lines are critical for maintaining a competitive advantage in modern manufacturing. While traditional methods such as discrete-event simulation or full-scale digital twins can provide high-fidelity analysis, they are often computationally prohibitive to support rapid decision-makings. Surrogate models offer a data-driven, computationally efficient alternative. However, accurately predicting system-level throughput requires capturing intricate spatio-temporal dependencies in a production line. This paper proposes a novel surrogate digital twin framework based on Spatio-Temporal Graph Neural Networks (ST-GNNs) to address this. The assembly line is conceptualized as a graph to explicitly model spatial relationships, while its temporal evolution is captured using a recurrent neural network architecture like a Bidirectional Long Short-Term Memory (Bi-LSTM) network. This study also investigates the impact of temporal data granularity by evaluating model performance on data aggregated at one-minute, ten-minute, and thirty-minute intervals, respectively. A comprehensive comparative study is conducted, evaluating the proposed ST-GNN against baseline models like Linear Regression, Random Forest, XGBoost, Deep Neural Networks (DNN) and standard LSTMs. Results demonstrate that a Graph Attention Network (GAT) combined with a Bi-LSTM network and a temporal attention mechanism achieves superior performance. The proposed model achieves the highest prediction accuracy with an R² score of 0.80 using a 30-minute data aggregation step, highlighting the importance of both model architecture and appropriate data resolution for creating effective digital twin surrogates.
10.1016/j.jmsy.2026.04.003.title: Spatio-temporal graph neural network based digital twin surrogate for throughput estimation in general assembly lines
10.1016/j.jmsy.2026.04.003.source: ScienceDirect official citation and abstract BibTeX export

10.1016/j.jmsy.2026.04.013.abstract: Precision micro-milling is widely used in advanced manufacturing, but accurately predicting its power consumption is challenging due to the high cost and time required to collect data under industrial monitoring conditions. This limits data availability and reduces the prediction accuracy of traditional machine and deep learning models. This study addresses the data-constrained prediction problem by proposing an assembly data augmentation strategy combined with a temporal convolutional network-Transformer (TCN-Transformer) model for micro-milling power consumption prediction. The assembly data augmentation treats time-series generative adversarial networks (TGAN), amplitude adjusted Fourier transform (AAFT) surrogates and Gaussian noise injection (GNI) as complementary parallel branches: TGAN learns the nonlinear distribution of power signals, AAFT preserves key spectral characteristics, and GNI enhances local variability. Their outputs are then combined with optimized weights to enrich the temporal and frequency information contained in small-sample datasets. On top of the augmented data, the TCN-Transformer model first uses TCN layers to extract multi-scale local temporal patterns and then applies a Transformer encoder to capture global dependencies between power trajectories and machining parameters, while Bayesian optimization is adopted to tune key hyperparameters. Validation on three-axis micro-milling experiments shows that the optimal augmentation ratio (50% TGAN, 25% AAFT, 25% GNI) significantly improves prediction and that the proposed TCN-Transformer achieves an R² of 0.896, outperforming competing baselines. These results demonstrate that the proposed framework effectively mitigates data collection constraints and provides a practical tool for non-invasive micro-milling energy prediction in precision machining.
10.1016/j.jmsy.2026.04.013.title: A novel temporal convolutional network-transformer framework with assembly data augmentation for accurate micro-milling energy prediction
10.1016/j.jmsy.2026.04.013.source: ScienceDirect official citation and abstract BibTeX export

10.1016/j.jmsy.2026.03.024.abstract: Reconstructing industrial mechanical parts from a single image is challenging when the output must be a CAD-compatible triangular mesh and usable in downstream CAD/CAE workflows after standard cleanup. We propose DOGREAT3D, a CAD-oriented mesh reconstruction pipeline that combines pose-conditioned multi-view diffusion with reliability-aware multimodal fusion and topology-preserving test-time refinement to enforce cross-view geometric consistency. Starting from one image (and an optional short industrial prompt), DOGREAT3D synthesizes posed views, derives geometry cues via cross-view depth alignment, and fuses RGB evidence with depth-derived normals (and optional text priors) through confidence-weighted cross-modal attention. It then initializes a watertight mesh using screened Poisson reconstruction and refines geometry and appearance with a four-stage, topology-preserving schedule that preserves sharp features and sensitive thin structures. On a wheel-hub benchmark of 1500 parts, DOGREAT3D reduces Chamfer Distance by 14.1% and improves F-score@1 mm from 0.453 to 0.526 over the strongest baseline under a unified evaluation protocol. On unseen part categories and on GSO, the geometric components transfer beyond the training distribution, improving F-score@τ from 0.647 to 0.667.
10.1016/j.jmsy.2026.03.024.title: DOGREAT3D: Multimodal 3D reconstruction of complex mechanical parts with diffusion models and geometric refinement strategies
10.1016/j.jmsy.2026.03.024.source: ScienceDirect official citation and abstract BibTeX export

10.1016/j.jmsy.2026.04.014.abstract: Biologics represent a class of therapeutic agents produced via biotechnology, characterized by high specificity, precise targeting, rapid efficacy, and significant therapeutic outcomes. However, their development and production involve complex, multidimensional influencing factors and inherent stability challenges. Traditional trial-and-error methods and process screening approaches incur high costs and low efficiency. Machine learning, as a powerful data-driven artificial intelligence technology, efficiently uncovers hidden relationships among intricate process parameters and enables accurate prediction of critical quality attributes, thereby substantially reducing development costs. With the proliferation of computational pharmaceutics, Machine learning-assisted development is becoming a mainstream paradigm. This article first briefly reviews the fundamentals and classification of machine learning, spanning from basic concepts to mainstream supervised learning algorithms and their applications in biopharmaceuticals. It then delves into the standardized workflows underpinning machine learning implementation. Subsequently, based on representative literature from the past five years covering upstream to downstream processes and formulation in biopharmaceuticals, a comprehensive analysis of machine learning specific applications is presented. Finally, an in-depth discussion was conducted regarding the challenges of data availability, model quality, and the application of machine learning in biomanufacturing. A prospective overview of emerging technologies was also provided, highlighting the potential application trends of transfer learning, hybrid modeling, digital twins, and process analytical technologies, with a view to achieving the realization of Biopharmaceutical 4.0.
10.1016/j.jmsy.2026.04.014.title: Accelerating biopharmaceutical innovation: A review of machine learning across the manufacturing pipeline
10.1016/j.jmsy.2026.04.014.source: ScienceDirect official citation and abstract BibTeX export

10.1016/j.jmsy.2026.04.004.abstract: Digital Twin (DT) technologies are transforming manufacturing by enabling real-time prediction, monitoring, and control of complex processes. Yet, applying DT to deformation-based metal forming remains challenging because of the strongly coupled spatial–temporal behavior and the nonlinear relationship between toolpath and material response. For instance, sheet-metal forming by the English wheel, a highly flexible but artisan-dependent process, still lacks digital counterparts that can autonomously plan and adapt forming strategies. This study presents an adaptive DT framework that integrates Proper Orthogonal Decomposition (POD) for physics-aware dimensionality reduction with a Koopman operator for representing nonlinear system in a linear lifted space for the real-time decision-making via model predictive control (MPC). To accommodate evolving process conditions or material states, an online Recursive Least Squares (RLS) algorithm is introduced to update the operator coefficients in real time, enabling continuous adaptation of the DT model as new deformation data become available. The proposed framework is experimentally demonstrated on a robotic English Wheel sheet metal forming system, where deformation fields are measured and modeled under varying toolpaths. Results show that the adaptive DT is capable of controlling the forming process to achieve the given target shape by effectively capturing non-stationary process behaviors. Beyond this case study, the proposed framework establishes a generalizable approach for interpretable, adaptive, and computationally-efficient DT of nonlinear manufacturing systems, bridging reduced-order physics representations with data-driven adaptability to support autonomous process control and optimization.
10.1016/j.jmsy.2026.04.004.title: Adaptive digital twin of sheet metal forming via proper orthogonal decomposition-based Koopman operator with model predictive control
10.1016/j.jmsy.2026.04.004.source: ScienceDirect official citation and abstract BibTeX export

10.1016/j.jmsy.2026.04.001.abstract: While Large Language Models (LLMs) demonstrate impressive capabilities in complex sequence generation and in-context pattern matching, their application to combinatorial optimization problems, such as the Job Shop Scheduling Problem (JSSP), remains challenging. This limitation arises from a fundamental mismatch: the autoregressive mechanism of LLMs optimizes local token probabilities for linguistic coherence, whereas industrial scheduling requires strict adherence to physical constraints and global optimization objectives. Consequently, standard LLMs often generate schedules that are semantically fluent but physically infeasible. To address this gap, we propose a dual-enhancement framework designed to ground LLM generation in physical feasibility. First, we introduce a six-step structured reasoning strategy that explicitly decomposes the decision-making process into formalized logical stages, guiding the model to sequentially verify state transitions rather than relying on statistical patterns. Second, we implement a task-oriented fine-grained loss function that aligns training with global optimization goals. This mechanism converts discrete, non-differentiable hard constraints into continuous gradient signals, effectively penalizing physical violations during the training phase. We validated our approach using JSSP-4 W (https://github.com/LakeForestCloud/LLM-JSSP), a curated instruction-tuning dataset of 40,000 instances enriched with structured reasoning annotations. Experimental evaluations demonstrate a 97% validity rate and a competitive makespan gap (5.14%–19.27%), comparable to meta-heuristics and LLM-driven Hyper-Heuristic (LLH) methods. Furthermore, the framework exhibits exceptional adaptability in dynamic environments, effectively translating high-level semantic instructions into robust, constraint-compliant decisions.
10.1016/j.jmsy.2026.04.001.title: A dual-enhancement framework for constraint-aware job shop scheduling with large language models
10.1016/j.jmsy.2026.04.001.source: ScienceDirect official citation and abstract BibTeX export

10.1016/j.jmsy.2026.04.017.abstract: Collaborative manufacturing in distributed synchronized manufacturing systems (DSMSs) increasingly relies on digital twins to support state awareness, coordinated optimization, and trustworthy data interaction. However, heterogeneous data across factories and partners result in digital twin data integration approaches that remain largely stage-isolated and insufficiently aligned with manufacturing hierarchies and lifecycle value flow, which limits the scalability and decision effectiveness in collaborative settings. To address these challenges, we propose a systematic data integration framework for collaborative manufacturing digital twins (CMDTs) that transforms multi-source heterogeneous digital twin data into traceable, standardized, and decision-oriented digital assets across distributed units. The framework advances beyond conventional stage-isolated integration by proposing an edge–fog–cloud-based architecture that aligns data integration functions with data granularity and collaboration scope, thereby enabling scalable and coordinated cross-unit data orchestration. Then, a five-stage data integration operational mechanism is established to tightly couple hierarchical architecture with lifecycle-oriented data value transformation, with blockchain embedded to enhance traceability and trust for CMDTs. Finally, three enabling methodologies targeting key bottlenecks are proposed: (i) a multi-objective edge caching model to jointly optimize low-latency data availability and load balancing; (ii) an LLM-aided data processing approach for efficient heterogeneous data standardization; (iii) a double-auction-based data sharing model for effective cross-unit collaboration. A coating manufacturing case study demonstrates that the proposed framework achieves consistent improvements in latency, load balancing, and data sharing efficiency compared with representative benchmarks. This research provides a structured and scalable foundation for digital twin data integration and data-driven optimization in collaborative manufacturing.
10.1016/j.jmsy.2026.04.017.title: A management framework for systematic data integration empowered for digital twin in collaborative manufacturing
10.1016/j.jmsy.2026.04.017.source: ScienceDirect official citation and abstract BibTeX export

10.1016/j.jmsy.2026.04.023.abstract: Retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) empowered by large language models is emerging as a promising approach for industrial knowledge analysis and decision support. However, in knowledge-intensive industrial domains, existing RAG frameworks often struggle with incomplete or noisy retrieval results, which limits their effectiveness in supporting high-precision industrial applications. To address this challenge, this study proposes an intent-constrained hybrid RAG (IC-HRAG) framework based on an ontology-enhanced domain-specific knowledge graph. The framework constructs a knowledge graph by integrating text classification with knowledge extraction based on large language models, followed by entity disambiguation and graph completion to improve graph quality. An intent-constrained hybrid retrieval algorithm projects queries onto the ontology space, guiding retrieval to balance evidence completeness and relevance. IC-HRAG unifies structured knowledge and unstructured text, enabling high-density, low-noise evidence organization. A case study involving a technical analysis task for superplastic forming equipment was conducted. Experimental results demonstrate that IC-HRAG consistently outperforms various baseline methods, achieving a superior precision of 97.22% and a peak F1 score of 92.72%. Moreover, comprehensive evaluations of decision performance, generation quality, and retrieval evidence quality further confirm its effectiveness, thereby supporting reliable intelligent analysis and decision-making in knowledge-intensive industrial domains.
10.1016/j.jmsy.2026.04.023.title: LLM-based domain-specific knowledge graph construction and hybrid retrieval-augmented generation
10.1016/j.jmsy.2026.04.023.source: ScienceDirect official citation and abstract BibTeX export

10.1016/j.jmsy.2026.04.022.abstract: In the dawn of Industry 5.0, flexible manufacturing systems (FMSs) need to operate under multi-source information, heterogeneous resources, and dynamic environments, thus traditional approaches can hardly achieve adaptability, robustness and interpretability in cross-task collaborative scheduling. To address this challenge in collaborative scheduling of FMS (CSFMS), this paper proposes a framework that comprises large language model (LLM)-based orchestrator-workers agents (OWAs) to perform multi-objectives CSFMS, including heterogeneous manufacturing resource management, multitask orchestration, and multi-process collaboration. To efficiently manage heterogeneous manufacturing resources, an OWA consisting of a planning-level agent and execution-level agents, which are deployed on the dispatching systems of machines and automated guided vehicles (AGVs), and augmented reality (AR) equipped by workers, is developed. To enhance cross-task (i.e. FMS knowledge mapping, agent skills for algorithms, and semantic reasoning and decision making) orchestration capabilities and reduce parameters interference across multitask of LLM, a data generation method based on meta-framework is introduced, as well as a multitask fine-tuning (MFT) with core parameters freezing and drop and rescale (DARE). Moreover, an LLM-based OWA (LLM-OWA) is designed with perception and self-coordination to close-loop collaborative decision. The enhancement of MFT strategies for integrated scheduling LLM (ISLLM) under multi-task scenarios is confirmed by the ablation experiment. For the scheduling results across 33 extended benchmark instances show that the solution space of LLM-OWAs improves stability (with 18.06% standard deviation reduce at least) and quality (with 3.03% average value improvement at least) over baselines (e.g. NSGA-Ⅱ, NSGA-Ⅲ). Under the impact of abnormal events like state failure, task time failure, and emergency order insertion, the proposed method further achieves 0.9146 decision consistency value and 0.9496 interpretability score. This work demonstrates the potential of agentic AI to support next-generation CSFMS.
10.1016/j.jmsy.2026.04.022.title: Multitask fine-tuning agentic AI based collaborative scheduling for flexible manufacturing systems
10.1016/j.jmsy.2026.04.022.source: ScienceDirect official citation and abstract BibTeX export

10.1016/j.jmsy.2026.04.015.abstract: Improving throughput in manufacturing systems requires not only the accurate identification of bottleneck processes, but also a plan that determines the order in which to improve them and how to allocate limited resources. Although bottleneck detection has been extensively studied, determining – under resource constraints – the improvement sequence and the amount of resources (e.g., engineering hours for maintenance activities) to allocate to each bottleneck remains a challenging task. In practice, industry often adopts a simple greedy strategy that sequentially addresses the most severe bottleneck first. However, due to interdependencies among processes, prioritizing a single bottleneck can cause bottleneck shifting to other processes, thereby limiting system-level performance gains. In contrast, distributing modest improvements across multiple bottlenecks can sometimes be more effective. However, obtaining the optimal improvement sequence for such distributed enhancements is highly challenging, since the number of feasible plans grows exponentially as the system size increases, making it a complex combinatorial optimization problem, and furthermore, because the objective function and constraints are not given in an explicit mathematical form, it becomes a black-box optimization problem with a high-dimensional and nonlinear search space. This study proposes a Multi-Stage Bayesian Optimization (BO) framework that integrates bottleneck detection with resource-constrained optimization to address this highly complex black-box optimization problem and derive the most effective improvement sequence and resource allocation. Within the framework, we combine (1) Gaussian Process fitting with Noise Expected Improvement for robust candidate scoring in the presence of noise, (2) Sobol’-based active-set screening for dimension reduction, and (3) Knowledge Gradient per cost policy for adaptive stage-wise budget allocation to systematically evaluate trade-offs among multiple bottlenecks and maximize overall throughput. Simulation results show that the proposed method outperforms conventional greedy and myopic strategies, enabling more efficient utilization of limited improvement resources.
10.1016/j.jmsy.2026.04.015.title: Multi-stage Bayesian optimization for throughput improvement in stochastic manufacturing systems
10.1016/j.jmsy.2026.04.015.source: ScienceDirect official citation and abstract BibTeX export

10.1016/j.jmsy.2026.04.031.abstract: To address the characteristics of complex aviation assembly process knowledge, including diverse knowledge types, complex hierarchical structures, strong semantic correlations, and continuous evolution, a top-down construction method for an assembly process knowledge graph (KG) is proposed. First, a multi-level assembly process ontology is developed to provide unified and standardized modeling of product information, assembly process knowledge, tools and equipment, historical cases, and their cross-level relationships, enabling structured knowledge representation and semantic consistency enforcement. Second, to cope with the semantic complexity of assembly process texts, a large language model (LLM)-based multi-agent collaborative triple information extraction method is proposed. By integrating ontology constraints and a self-consistency chain-of-thought (CoT) mechanism, the stability, accuracy, and interpretability of extraction results are significantly improved. Finally, a semantic embedding-based dynamic KG update strategy is adopted to maintain entity uniqueness and semantic consistency during continuous knowledge evolution. Experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness and applicability of the proposed method in complex aviation assembly process scenarios.
10.1016/j.jmsy.2026.04.031.title: MA-APKG: A multi-agent LLM-based method for construction aviation product assembly process knowledge graph
10.1016/j.jmsy.2026.04.031.source: ScienceDirect official citation and abstract BibTeX export

10.1016/j.jmsy.2026.04.032.abstract: 3D digital processes provide intuitive guidance for practical disassembly operations. However, current 3D process planning relies on manual intervention and suffers from low automation. With the powerful reasoning and generative capabilities of large language models and their recent rapid application in 3D tasks, we propose a multimodal large language model-driven framework for the intelligent generation of 3D disassembly processes. Textual descriptions, multi-view images, and semi-structured data are extracted from the 3D virtual scene. Three methods employing different prompt templates are designed to guide the multimodal large language model in generating 3D processes across different formats. The generated processes are converted into the keyframe representation for evaluation. To enhance the generation performance, few-shot prompting and Chain-of-Thought reasoning are integrated. Six metrics are utilized to evaluate the quality and efficiency of generated processes. Finally, we collect typical mechanical product models from public assembly datasets and conduct generation experiments. Manually designed 3D disassembly processes serve as the ground-truth. Results show that the proposed framework generates reasonable 3D disassembly processes based on data from the 3D scene, validating its effectiveness and practical potential for intelligent process planning.
10.1016/j.jmsy.2026.04.032.title: Intelligent generation of 3D disassembly processes driven by multimodal large language models

10.1016/j.jmsy.2026.04.019.abstract: Artificial Intelligence/Machine Learning, Industrial Internet of Things (IIoT), and Cloud Manufacturing technologies, along with rapidly evolving computing infrastructure, require that the fifty-year-old CNC architecture be reexamined to better address the changing needs of manufacturing automation as it evolves from programmed to perceptual automation. This paper introduces Cloud-Direct Numerical Control (C-DNC), an architecture that recruits the services of different computing (cloud, edge, and embedded/real-time) resources, matched to different tasks in the NC workflow. It introduces the concept of a ‘compiled motion program’ to reduce the workload on real-time computing resources by eliminating the repetitive tasks of interpreting G-codes and performing real-time trajectory interpolation. A portion of the freed-up real-time resource bandwidth is used to demonstrate NC-embedded monitoring and IIoT services that not only provide high-bandwidth data collection but also ensure tight temporal alignment of this data with machine instructions. The remaining bandwidth can be used for real-time inferencing and advanced controls to realize truly intelligent NC systems. Finally, this cloud-integrated version of Direct Numerical Control reduces investment costs through the efficient shared use of computing resources, enables new modes for the democratization of NC via subscription and pay-per-use models, and integrates with upstream design and planning software tools.
10.1016/j.jmsy.2026.04.019.title: Cloud-Direct NC: A new generation of numerical control technology

10.1016/j.jmsy.2026.04.037.abstract: Tool wear monitoring system (TWMS)in the machining process can improve production efficiency. The existing TWMS has the characteristics of poor generalization ability of detection model, strong dependence on data, and difficulty in adapting to complex cutting conditions. Therefore, this paper proposes a tool wear monitoring digital twin system (TWM-DTS) using contrastive learning. Firstly, the user interaction and virtual-real linkage are realized through the digital twin system front end (DTS-FE), and the tool state can be perceived in real-time to obtain machining parameters and store them in the buffer. Secondly, this paper proposes a milling force calculation model accounting for tool wear. The digital twin system back end (DTS-BE) can calculate the milling force of different wear conditions in real time through the data of buffer. Finally, this paper proposes a contrastive learning model. By comparing the similarity between the measured milling force (MMF) and the calculated milling force (CMF), the tool wear monitoring under variable working conditions is completed, which provides a judgment basis for the tool change of the digital twin system (DTS) anti-control machine tool. The contrastive model is cross-validated, and the mathematical analysis of the verification results proves that the model has high accuracy and generalization ability. The actual effect of virtual and real combination, tool wear monitoring and system anti-control machine tool change is realized, which lays a foundation for the application of digital twin in intelligent manufacturing.
10.1016/j.jmsy.2026.04.037.title: Research on tool wear monitoring based on digital twin and contrastive learning
