10.1016/j.jmsy.2026.09.022.abstract: Accurate perception of machining states is essential for intelligent Computer Numerical Control (CNC) systems, yet modeling key process variables remains challenging due to the nonlinear and multi-modal nature of cutting processes. Empirical models lack adaptability, while purely data-driven methods often neglect physical constraints. Direct measurement of cutting force is challenging in practice, as complex workpiece geometries, limited ranges of detection instruments, and high deployment costs make large-scale force data acquisition difficult. Therefore, spindle current is adopted as a more practical and accessible variable for state perception. In consideration of this problem, this study proposes a physics–data fusion multi-modal deep learning framework for spindle current prediction in a Digital Twin (DT)-driven environment. The framework integrates multi-modal inputs, including acceleration signals, STEP-NC semantic metadata, and cutter-workpiece engagement (CWE) geometric descriptors derived from the 3D engagement volume, into a unified representation that is processed by a data-driven branch for feature extraction. The architecture features a Sequence Head for residual regression and an attention-pooled Point Head for next-step prediction. Spindle dynamics constrain sequence outputs through a physics-informed module. Conditioned on process embeddings, a multi-objective loss adaptively balances dual heads and physical heuristics. The framework, deployed in a DT environment, supports synchronized multi-source data acquisition and real-time prediction. Experimental validation on a dedicated DT platform confirms framework feasibility, consistently maintaining R2>0.95 and superior error metrics across diverse machining regimes.
10.1016/j.jmsy.2026.09.022.title: Physics-data fusion multi-modal deep learning for spindle current prediction in digital twin-driven machining state perception

10.1016/j.cossms.2025.101243.abstract: Additive friction stir deposition (AFSD) is an emergent solid-state additive manufacturing (AM) technique that operates below the melting point temperature of the materials, resulting in lower residual stresses and reduced susceptibility to defects like porosity and hot-cracking compared to fusion-based methods. These benefits position AFSD as a viable alternative to traditional forging for large-scale applications in the aerospace, automotive, marine, and nuclear industries. The interest on AFSD is progressing at a rapid pace and a periodic comprehensive review of the state-of-the-art is of major interest. This comprehensive review presents a detailed summary of key fundamentals, including material flow behaviour and heat generation mechanisms, alongside a critical evaluation of microstructural evolution. Comparative analyses across aluminum, magnesium, titanium, steels, nickel-based superalloys, and high entropy alloys illustrate the diverse grain refinement mechanisms and structural responses that govern the final properties of AFSD-fabricated components. The review places further emphasis on emerging strategies for process modeling and optimization, with particular attention to the integration of machine learning approaches that offer promising insights into real-time defect detection and adaptive process control. The review concludes by addressing the key challenges limiting the industrial translation of AFSD, including surface quality, dimensional accuracy, consistency in multi-material builds, and sustainable material utilization. Perspectives are offered on the development of integrated digital frameworks and real-time monitoring systems. By providing a comprehensive and focused synthesis, this review aims to support the wider adoption of AFSD and foster innovation in solid-state additive manufacturing. It is believed that an advancement of the substantive understanding will expedite the potential industrial implementation of the AFSD technique.
10.1016/j.cossms.2025.101243.title: State-of-the-art review of additive friction stir deposition: microstructural evolution, machine learning applications, and future directions

10.1016/j.jmsy.2026.10.011.abstract: With the advent of Industry 5.0, human-robot collaborative assembly has become a core production paradigm that combines human cognitive flexibility with robotic operational efficiency. Single-robot systems cannot meet the diverse requirements of complex assembly tasks. Therefore, collaboration between human operators and heterogeneous multi-robot teams is required for flexible and efficient manufacturing. However, current collaborative systems are limited by fragmented perception-reasoning-execution pipelines. Poor generalization of general-purpose models in industrial environments is also observed. Additionally, integrated safety mechanisms for dynamic shared workspaces remain insufficient. These challenges indicate the need for embodied intelligence, through which agents can perceive, reason, and act seamlessly in physical environments. To address these issues, a vision-language model (VLM)-enabled, digital twin-assisted polymorphic embodied agent framework was proposed in this paper. A complete closed loop of embodied cognition, embodied reasoning, and embodied execution was established for human-heterogeneous multi-robot collaborative assembly. In the embodied cognition layer, a domain-specific VLM was developed to achieve robust real-time perception of human behaviors, assembly components, and environmental states, with integrated depth information for accurate spatial localization and collision detection. In the embodied reasoning layer, a digital twin system with bidirectional virtual-to-real mapping enables virtual pre-simulation and optimal task scheduling that effectively leverages the complementary strengths of human and robots. In the embodied execution layer, the model directly generates executable control code for heterogeneous robots, which is pre-verified in the digital twin environment before physical deployment. Comprehensive experimental results demonstrate that the proposed framework outperforms traditional visual algorithms and mainstream general-purpose vision-language models on all evaluation benchmarks. The system achieves three tiered latency indicators for decoupled functional modules. It delivers ultra-low single-frame perception delay below 150 ms for environmental safety sensing, and attains outstanding reasoning accuracy paired with an online task reasoning latency of 0.75 s to support real-time human-robot closed-loop interaction. The 4.8 s full assembly code generation delay only takes effect during offline pre-generation before task startup. This offline process is isolated from the online control loop and imposes no negative impact on the system’s real-time dynamic response and obstacle avoidance capacity. Continuous robotic operation was ensured. Human comfort and safety were maintained through differentiated task allocation. This paper provides a practical and effective solution for intelligent and safe collaborative assembly. It also offers important implications for the development of next-generation intelligent manufacturing systems.
10.1016/j.jmsy.2026.10.011.title: Bridging cognition, reasoning and action for polymorphic embodied agents towards human-heterogeneous multi-robot collaborative assembly with vision-language model and digital twin

10.1016/j.cossms.2025.101249.abstract: The rapid development of graphene-based sensors has significant implications for addressing the urgent need for highly sensitive, responsive and reusable sensors in all areas of life. Its excellent electrical performance and mechanical flexibility make it the ideal material in the field of intelligent sensors. In addition, the interfacial adjustability of graphene materials further expands the boundary of application. This review provides a detailed review of the progress of graphene-based sensors. It conducts in-depth research on the working principle and systematically explores the applications of graphene-based sensors in four aspects: environmental monitoring, healthcare diagnostics, food safety and industrial applications. With the advancement of Industry 4.0, manufacturing systems are increasingly emphasizing intelligent interconnectivity, automation and decisions informed by data. It has created a growing demand for sensors with greater adaptability and improved accuracy. In response to these evolving requirements, artificial intelligence has become one of the essential technologies supporting this new industrial paradigm. By combining experimental data with intelligent algorithms, this approach not only predicts changes in material properties but also optimizes the structural design of sensors.
10.1016/j.cossms.2025.101249.title: Graphene-based sensors for multiscenario applications: from functional interface engineering to artificial intelligence-driven optimization

10.1016/j.foodhyd.2026.112422.abstract: This study presents an artificial intelligence–driven approach to predicting the printability and textural attributes of 3D-printed food models before the printing process. To enable formulation-based and non-destructive prediction, 12 key features were experimentally extracted from the ink formulation. Building on these data, the research proposes a novel multi-stage deep learning framework, consisting of three specialized neural network models. The first model, a binary classifier, provides an initial screening to determine whether the ink is printable. Upon positive determination, the ink proceeds to the second model, a printability rating classifier that categorizes printability into high, moderate, or low levels, offering a more refined evaluation rarely addressed in previous studies. In parallel, the same input features are used by a third model to simultaneously predict multiple textural properties of the final product — hardness, springiness, gumminess, and cohesiveness — representing a significant advancement toward pre-printing quality assessment. Using a dataset compiled from systematically collected samples, the three models each achieved an average accuracy of nearly 90%. This research streamlined pre-printing evaluations and non-destructive assessments of 3D-printed food items, while also laying the groundwork for future advancements in the field.
10.1016/j.foodhyd.2026.112422.title: Artificial intelligence-driven pre-estimation of printability and textural properties of starch-based gels in 3D food printing

10.1016/j.foodhyd.2026.112555.abstract: Conventional methods of pea protein extraction are resource-intensive, involving multiple purification steps that remove co-existing components such as starch. In contrast, we investigate how minimally processed yellow pea protein extracts that retain residual carbohydrates form thermally induced gels. Contrast-variation small-angle neutron scattering, rheology, and differential scanning calorimetry show that salt-extracted samples form a unified gel matrix through co-gelation of protein and carbohydrate components, as evidenced by a shared contrast match point in the final network. Ultra-small-angle neutron scattering reveals mesoscale heterogeneity, with structural features persisting up to 2 μm, indicative of a particulate, protein-rich network within the composite gel. Rheological and calorimetric analyses suggest that gelation proceeds via a kinetic pathway in which protein aggregation precedes unfolding, ultimately shaping network architecture and viscoelastic properties. These findings demonstrate that minimal processing can yield structurally integrated protein–starch gels and clarify how composition and processing determine network architecture and mechanical performance.

10.1016/j.foodhyd.2026.112751.abstract: Pectin and polyphenols are naturally occurring bioactive molecules in plant systems that have received extensive attention due to their unique structures and biological activities. They can form complexes through non-covalent and covalent forces. The interactions between them are influenced by various factors, such as the structure of the pectin, the type of polyphenols, the temperature and pH of the system. Pectin and polyphenols can significantly enhance their functional properties (such as improving the gelation performance, emulsification properties, and film-forming capacity of pectin) and biological activities (such as regulating intestinal flora and enhancing antioxidant capacity) through interaction, exerting a significant impact on the processing characteristics, sensory properties, nutritional functions, and stability of food. This article aims to systematically expound the pectin-polyphenol interaction mechanism, advanced characterization techniques, and their interaction on the function and biological properties of constructed complex. The research and potential applications of artificial intelligence (AI) in the field of pectin-polyphenol complexes are also discussed, providing a solid theoretical foundation and practical direction for the effective utilization of these complexes in food processing.
10.1016/j.foodhyd.2026.112751.title: Pectin-polyphenol interactions: A comprehensive review of interaction mechanism, characterization and synergistic effect in functionality and bioactivity integrating with AI perspectives

10.1016/j.biomaterials.2026.124758.abstract: Human brain organoids recapitulate neurodevelopment but suffer from stochastic self-organization, producing high phenotypic variability that limits their reproducibility as experimental models. Here, we engineer micropatterned agarose hydrogel microchannels that impose meningeal-like geometric confinement on developing human cerebral organoids. This biomaterial platform converts fragmented neural rosettes into continuous, planar, polarized neuroepithelia, reducing transcriptional dispersion along PC1 by over 40% and enforcing deterministic tissue architecture. Mechanistically, confinement triggers downregulation of the mechanosensor YAP1 and enhances early induction of the transcription factor BRN2 independently of exogenous extracellular matrix. BRN2 induction is functionally essential: shRNA-mediated knockdown completely abolishes confinement-driven neuroepithelial continuity. Curvature-based stress modeling identifies curvature maxima as deterministic nucleation sites that link physical constraints to predictable tissue architecture, validated by an AI-augmented morphometric pipeline across 99 organoids. Together, our findings establish a programmable hydrogel platform that uses geometric confinement as a design parameter to direct neuroepithelial morphogenesis, and highlight YAP1 and BRN2 as key molecular regulators associated with early human brain development.

10.1016/j.cej.2026.183914.abstract: Persistent neurological deficits and substantial clinical burdens arise from traumatic neural injuries, which encompass traumatic brain injury (TBI), spinal cord injury (SCI), and peripheral nerve injury (PNI). Shared regenerative barriers notwithstanding, divergence in tissue mechanics, lesion architecture, inflammatory progression, and intrinsic regenerative capacity imposes distinct requirements on hydrogel network formation, mechanical compatibility, mass transport, and degradation. Critical appraisal of bioactive hydrogels for traumatic neural repair proceeds through an engineering framework connecting pathological constraints, polymer network design variables, coupled material properties, potential failure modes, and functional verification. Conductive, immunomodulatory, therapeutic delivery, self healing, cell laden, extracellular vesicle laden, extracellular matrix mimetic, and three dimensionally bioprinted hydrogels receive examination, with emphasis on polymer functionalization, crosslinking chemistry, viscoelasticity, network architecture, and manufacturing reproducibility. Conformal filling of irregular brain lesions, longitudinal bridging of spinal cord defects, and directional regeneration within peripheral nerve conduits define distinct engineering priorities. Intrinsic material effects require separation from those arising from incorporated therapeutic agents, electrical stimulation, or scaffold geometry. Conceptual mapping of functional integration, rather than chronological progression or evidence of superior efficacy, frames the four generation framework. Translational analysis addresses critical quality attributes, process scalability, regulatory classification, and indication specific safety and functional endpoints. Connecting material design decisions with experimentally verifiable mechanisms and translational constraints yields a critical engineering perspective on neural regenerative hydrogel development.
10.1016/j.cej.2026.183914.title: Bioactive hydrogel systems orchestrating traumatic neural microenvironments for functional restoration

10.1016/j.cej.2026.183974.abstract: The vast combinatorial space of multi-element M2AlC MAX phases renders systematic experimental exploration intractable. Here, we fine-tune the MACE-MP-0 foundation model on a compact training set of M2AlC compositions with N = 1–3 M-site elements to obtain MACE-MAX, a machine learning interatomic potential that predicts the formation energies of N = 3–6 compositions with an MAE of 5.3 meV/atom at ~70-fold lower cost than DFT. Combined with Monte Carlo M-site sampling, MACE-MAX screens all 465 equimolar compositions in a nine-element (Ti, V, Zr, Nb, Hf, Ta, Cr, Mo, W) design space, identifies ten synthesis candidates and reveals valence electron concentration and atomic size mismatch as the dominant stability descriptors. Synthesis and characterization of the ten candidates and a Group VIB substitution series validate the predictions on three scales. The IVB/VB compositions with the lowest Ehull form the MAX phase as the main product, whereas none of the compositions containing a Group VIB element does; EPMA confirms the predicted decomposition pathways; and atomic-resolution HAADF-STEM and EDS resolve, for the first time, M-site solid-solution disorder in a six-element HE-MAX phase, (TiVZrNbHfTa)2AlC. MACE-MAX thus provides a validated computational–experimental framework for HE-MAX discovery and for selecting precursors of high-entropy MXenes.
10.1016/j.cej.2026.183974.title: MACE-MAX: A fine-tuned machine learning interatomic potential for high-throughput screening and experimental validation of high-entropy M2AlC MAX phases

10.1016/j.cej.2026.183842.abstract: This study employed plant extracts as precursors to synthesize a volcanic rock-supported Fe/Ni bimetallic nanocatalyst via pyrolysis for efficient activation of periodate (PI). The results demonstrate that, at a low catalyst dosage (0.1 g⋅L−1), the system effectively activates PI (1 mM), achieving over 95% removal of sulfamethoxazole (SMX, 2 mg⋅L−1) within 120 min. Quenching experiments and electron paramagnetic resonance (EPR) analysis confirmed that singlet oxygen (1O2) is the dominant reactive species, indicating that the reaction proceeds mainly via a non-radical oxidation pathway. Volcanic rock support optimizes Fe/Ni nanoparticle dispersion and inhibits aggregation; structural characterization verified enhanced defect density and abundant active sites, while the constructed mineral-metal interface accelerates electron transfer and PI activation. Machine learning analysis further identified defect degree (ID/IG) and pore structure as the key factors affecting catalytic performance. LC-MS analysis revealed that SMX degradation mainly proceeds via sulfonamide bond cleavage, aromatic oxidation, and isoxazole ring opening. Application tests using real swine wastewater demonstrated that the catalyst maintains high stability and strong anti-interference capability under complex conditions, sustaining considerable degradation efficiency during continuous-flow operation and repeated cycles. This study offers novel insights into the design of mineral-supported bimetallic catalysts for advanced water treatment applications.
10.1016/j.cej.2026.183842.title: Volcanic rock-supported zero-valent Fe/Ni bimetal activated periodate for the degradation of sulfamethoxazole: Performance, mechanism, and machine learning application

10.1016/j.cej.2026.184090.abstract: This work couples statistical synthesis optimization with AI-guided electrode-design to boost the electrochemical performance of additively manufactured rGO-Cobalt oxide supercapacitor electrodes. The optimal synthesis conditions found using a full-factorial design of experiments (DoE), yielding a nanocomposite with well-dispersed Co3O4 and CoO domains embedded on a conductive rGO matrix to be further applied in inks. To decouple geometry-dependent effects from material contributions, 30 printed electrode architectures were systematically evaluated, producing specific capacitances of 59.7–96.2 F/g and establishing electrode topology as a first-order performance determinant. Machine-learning models based on Multiple Linear Regression (MLR) and Random Forest Regression (RFR) were developed using geometric descriptors extracted from the 30 architectures, yielding R2 values of 0.71 and 0.85 for MLR and RFR, respectively, with corresponding Root Mean Square Error (RMSE) and Mean Absolute Error (MAE) values of approximately 8 and 6 F/g for MLR and 5.5 and 4 F/g for RFR, respectively. The RFR model was subsequently used to identify an optimized electrode architecture, which was experimentally fabricated and achieved a specific capacitance of 104.8 F/g by cyclic voltammetry, representing an approximately 9% improvement over the best-performing architecture in the original pattern library under identical conditions. The optimized electrode further delivered a rate-capability retention of ~92%, an estimated gravimetric energy density of ~12.5 Wh/kg. These findings demonstrate that coupling DoE-validated synthesis control with AI-generated electrode topology enables simultaneous improvement of capacitance, rate performance, and energy/power metrics without chemical reformulation, establishing a scalable and transferable digital-design framework for next-generation high-performance supercapacitor electrodes.
10.1016/j.cej.2026.184090.title: AI and additive manufacturing driven design of rGO-cobalt oxide nanocomposite electrodes for supercapacitors

10.1016/j.cej.2026.184041.abstract: The prevalence of irreversible vision-impairing ophthalmic diseases remains high, while current diagnostic methods heavily rely on expert experience, limiting their accessibility in primary care settings. To address this, the present study utilizes iron oxide semiconductor as a scaffold to precisely engineer a multidirectional energy-amplified coral nanomatrix. Combined with nanomatrix-assisted laser desorption ionization mass spectrometry (NMALDI-MS), this approach enables high-resolution metabolic fingerprint mapping of ophthalmic diseases in a single batch analysis. The nanomatrix integrates the semiconductor's superior band structure with a high-density three-dimensional(3D) synaptic tip array, which synchronously amplifies local electric fields across the entire matrix and enhances light absorption capability, significantly promoting the separation of photogenerated charge carriers. The 3D interlaced optical trap structure on the material surface extends the effective light path, further increasing light utilization efficiency. Abundant binding sites strengthen molecular–matrix interactions, accelerating ionization and deionization processes, achieving up to 103-fold signal enhancement compared with other iron oxide morphologies. Leveraging a neural network-based deep learning platform, high-throughput processing and diagnosis of metabolic fingerprint maps were rapidly completed for 398 patients with diverse ophthalmic diseases, leading to the identification of multiple potential metabolic biomarkers. This strategy provides a low-cost, high-throughput, and easily standardized universal diagnostic solution for ophthalmic diseases, demonstrating strong potential for large-scale deployment in primary healthcare institutions.
10.1016/j.cej.2026.184041.title: AI-revealed metabolic fingerprinting of ophthalmic diseases via a 3D energy-amplified coral nanomatrix

10.1016/j.cej.2026.184014.abstract: Ionically conductive hydrogels (ICHs) are promising candidates for flexible sensors and artificial skins, but their conductivity and comprehensive properties are poor in special sensing scenarios. Herein, ICHs containing poly(ethylene glycol) (PEG) side chains are developed. In such ICHs, PEG chains exhibit high freedom of motion and hydrophilicity, providing abundant bonding sites for water and cations. The ICHs are prepared by a macromonomer copolymerization method and amphiphilic triblock copolymer is introduced to enhance their mechanical properties. Conductivity of such ICHs is increased by increasing feeding content and molecular weight of double bond end-capped PEG macromonomers and a conductivity of 57.9 mS/cm has been achieved. Interestingly, such ICHs are promising in constructing flexible mechanosensors exhibiting multi-mode response ability, fast response speed, high sensitivity and stability. On the basis of a signal processing model and a machine learning algorithm, piezoresistive pressure sensors of such ICHs are demonstrated in Morse code communication and input of various contents (e.g., letters and numbers). Overall, this work provides a new clue to develop high-performance ICHs by molecular structure design of hydrogel network and candidate materials for for flexible sensing devices.
10.1016/j.cej.2026.184014.title: Ionically conductive hydrogels containing PEG side chains for mechanical signal sensing, Morse code communication and machine-learning-assisted input

10.1016/j.cej.2026.184069.abstract: Hydrothermal liquefaction (HTL) of sewage sludge offers a promising route for waste valorization and renewable fuel production. However, existing machine learning studies on sewage sludge HTL remain constrained by insufficient sludge-specific analysis, inadequate multi-output prediction and optimization, and poor model interpretability. To address these gaps, this study developed a machine learning-assisted framework integrating model development and optimization, model interpretation, feature elimination, and Pareto-based multi-objective optimization using a PRISMA-guided literature-derived HTL dataset comprising 594 data points from 120 peer-reviewed studies. Statistical analysis revealed that substantial variations in both input features and output variables among the four clearly defined sludge types, highlighting the importance of sludge-specific characteristics. The optimized models achieved reliable multi-target prediction, while SHAP analysis identified temperature, sludge type, and H content as the dominant predictors for yield, oil quality indicators, and energy recovery, respectively. Feature elimination reduced input variables by 38.9–66.7% while preserving predictive performance and maintaining consistent dominant features and response trends, demonstrating the robustness and interpretability of the simplified models. Pareto-based multi-objective optimization further identified a balanced HTL condition at 353.79 °C, 12.29 min, and a liquid/solid ratio of 41.01 mL/g, corresponding to a predicted biocrude oil yield of 43.76%, HHV of 34.63 MJ/kg, energy recovery of 90.14%, nitrogen and oxygen contents in oil of 2.84% and 19.55%, respectively. This work provides new insights and a data-driven strategy for accelerating engineered HTL toward desired biocrude oil production, offering a valuable reference for sustainable sewage sludge management, waste valorization, and renewable fuel development.
10.1016/j.cej.2026.184069.title: Machine learning-assisted optimization of sewage sludge hydrothermal liquefaction for balanced biocrude oil yield, quality, and energy recovery

10.1016/j.cej.2026.184042.abstract: Molecularly imprinted polymer (MIP) technology has emerged as a promising alternative to conventional biological recognition elements because it provides molecular selectivity, chemical stability, and cost-effective fabrication. However, the performance of MIP-based electrochemical sensors remains sensitive to multiple interdependent fabrication parameters, making one-factor-at-a-time optimization inefficient and unable to resolve interactions between variables. Herein, we report a joint Bayesian surrogate-modeling framework for MIP-based electrochemical sensors, demonstrated for vitamin C detection, in which o-phenylenediamine (o-PD) concentration, template concentration, cyclic voltammetry (CV) cycle number, and rebinding pH are modeled jointly rather than independently, and a single-round, uncertainty-aware Bayesian recommendation step is used to select an untested fabrication condition. Twenty-five fabrication conditions generated by Latin hypercube sampling were used to train a four-dimensional Gaussian process regression (GPR) surrogate model, benchmarked against polynomial, support vector, and random forest regression by leave-one-out cross-validation. GPR was retained not for superior point-prediction accuracy but for its native predictive uncertainty, which enables an Expected Improvement acquisition function to recommend fabrication conditions that have not been measured; a recommended condition absent from the training set was confirmed experimentally, and, at five further GPR-recommended conditions, GPR's predictions remained close to the measured responses (R2 = 0.863) while predictions from the fixed, untuned PR and SVR models deviated more substantially under this GPR-conditioned validation. SHAP-based analysis quantified the relative contribution of each parameter to the predicted response, and two-dimensional response surfaces of the joint model visualized conditional response patterns between parameter pairs. Under the identified conditions, the sensor exhibited a linear range from 10 nM to 1 mM, a calculated limit of detection of 778 pM, and high selectivity against structurally related interferents. Detection was demonstrated in human serum and artificial urine, and a preliminary proof-of-concept in real urine collected after vitamin C intake showed good agreement with a commercial ELISA assay. Coupling joint multi-parameter modeling with uncertainty-guided recommendation offers a data-efficient route to the rational optimization of MIP-based electrochemical sensing interfaces.
10.1016/j.cej.2026.184042.title: Data-driven multi-parameter optimization of molecularly imprinted polymers for pico-level vitamin C detection

10.1016/j.cej.2026.184058.abstract: Predicting the relative abundance of DNRA-associated taxa may support microbial monitoring in anammox-based systems. However, the suitability of different predictive models and their taxon-specific predictor contribution patterns under low-carbon, nitrogen-rich conditions remain insufficiently characterized. Here, we analyzed 1292 environmental observations and 94 microbial profiles collected over 62 months from laboratory-scale anammox reactors. Multiple machine-learning models were compared to characterize relationships between environmental conditions and taxon relative abundance. Across the evaluated random train–test splits, ensemble models generally outperformed linear approaches, although the best-performing model varied by taxon. Multiple linear regression predicted Candidatus Kuenenia best, whereas random forest or extreme gradient boosting models predicted Candidatus Jettenia, Fimbriimonadaceae, Limnobacter, and Alicycliphilus best under their respective splits. This contrast revealed distinct predictive response structures among taxa within the same engineered environment. SHAP analysis identified taxon-specific predictor contribution patterns: predictions for Candidatus Jettenia and Limnobacter were primarily associated with influent NH4+ and NO2−, whereas Fimbriimonadaceae and Alicycliphilus showed broader distributions of SHAP contributions. Nitrogen loading rate and inorganic nitrogen species (NH4+, NO2−, and NO3−) were important predictors within the fitted models, but their individual contributions were interpreted cautiously because of predictor collinearity. Organic carbon variables showed comparatively limited predictive contributions within the low-carbon operating conditions represented in the dataset. Overall, this study provides a comparative evaluation of taxon-specific abundance prediction models and a descriptive interpretation of their predictor contributions. The findings support hypothesis generation and the selection of variables for microbial monitoring, while independent and temporally structured validation is needed to assess model transferability, and controlled experiments are required to evaluate ecological mechanisms.
10.1016/j.cej.2026.184058.title: Machine learning reveals interaction-driven ecological responses of DNRA-associated taxa toward data-driven operation of anammox systems

10.1016/j.cej.2026.184173.abstract: Reliable design of multicomponent fluids requires property-prediction methods applicable to unmeasured mixture systems. Kinematic viscosity is a challenging prediction target because of its sensitivity to intermolecular interactions and non-ideal composition effects. We developed a physics-guided, McAllister-inspired neural network that combines explicit, permutation-invariant n-body composition aggregation with a shared nonlinear mapping from molecular descriptors and pure-component properties to interaction contributions. We evaluated extrapolative performance on ternary mixtures spanning regular solutions and strongly non-ideal water-containing systems using nested leave-one-component-out (LOCO) validation that excluded each of 20 organic components from model development. Diagnostic fits showed that the McAllister n-body form accurately represented composition dependence, whereas a compact shared parameterization constrained the generalized McAllister model's expressiveness. The best-performing 4-body excess-log-viscosity neural network achieved component-macro average absolute relative deviations of 6.47% overall under LOCO and 9.98% for challenging water-containing systems. Under identical data and validation conditions, its errors were approximately half those of two representative general-purpose machine-learning baselines. Ablation analysis identified permutation invariance as the largest source of improvement, with an additional gain from explicit McAllister-type n-body aggregation and a suggested benefit of 4-body interactions in water-containing systems. Combining nonlinear interaction representations learned from molecular structure and pure-component information with physically structured composition aggregation enabled accurate, broadly applicable modeling of non-ideal mixtures. The architecture can accommodate additional components without increasing its trainable parameter count and may provide a general design principle for data-driven prediction of non-ideal mixture properties.
10.1016/j.cej.2026.184173.title: A physics-guided neural network with McAllister-inspired multibody aggregation: Generalizing viscosity prediction to unseen organic components in strongly non-ideal mixtures

10.1016/j.cej.2026.184234.abstract: Early detection of pancreatic cancer is hampered by the lack of a sensitive, non-invasive diagnostic platform. Although SERS-based approaches have been proposed for pancreatic cancer diagnostics, most volumetric SERS substrates rely on deeply confined hotspots near polymer templates, where limited analyte accessibility and substrate-derived Raman background can compromise spectral fidelity. Here, we introduce an interstitially localized plasmonic nanostar (IPN) platform that redistributes electromagnetic enhancement into analyte-accessible hot volumes above a three-dimensional Au/polystyrene architecture. Selective nanostar localization within interstitial regions enhances analyte–field overlap while suppressing polymer-derived Raman interference, enabling uniform, reproducible, and trace-level SERS detection. To resolve the complex signals of urine spectra, statistically selected Raman features were integrated with a logistic regression classifier, enabling discrimination between pancreatic cancer patients and healthy controls with an AUC of 0.991 and an accuracy of 96.0%. In parallel, spectral deconvolution using a reference library of urinary metabolites estimated metabolite-associated spectral contributions linked to cancer-related metabolic alterations. This integrated IPN-based SERS–machine learning strategy provides a practical route for non-invasive urinary pancreatic cancer screening and interpretable analysis of complex biofluid spectra.
10.1016/j.cej.2026.184234.title: Interstitial hot-volume plasmonics for machine learning-assisted urinary SERS diagnosis of pancreatic cancer

10.1016/j.cej.2026.184259.abstract: The discovery of electrolyte additives for high-voltage sodium-ion batteries (SIBs) remains constrained by the inefficiency of empirical trial-and-error screening across vast molecular landscapes. Here we report a machine learning (ML)-driven pipeline that bridges this gap, integrating RDKit molecular descriptors with a multilayer perceptron (MLP) regressor trained on 87,301 molecules to predict molecular oxidation potential (OP). Under a standardized benchmarking protocol spanning 11 regression algorithms, the MLP model achieved an R2 of 0.97 on the held-out test set and showed the lowest errors and the least severe underestimation in the sparsely populated high-OP region among the evaluated algorithms. Deploying this model across 1.03 million PubChem entries yielded 2291 candidates with predicted OP values of 4.0–6.0 V. From this pool, ifosfamide (IFO) was selected for experimental validation. The cells incorporating the IFO-containing electrolyte delivered 107.23 mAh g−1 after 100 cycles at 120 mA g−1, surpassing the baseline electrolyte (99.82 mAh g−1). SHAP analysis, parallel coordinate visualization, and 2D partial dependence plots revealed that the MLP model integrates fragment-level descriptors, molecular topology, conformational flexibility, and surface electronic properties to render its predictions, providing molecular-level insight into candidate prioritization. These findings highlight the effectiveness of ML in narrowing down large chemical libraries and identifying experimentally viable electrolyte additives for SIBs.
10.1016/j.cej.2026.184259.title: A machine learning-driven pipeline uncovers superior electrolyte additive for high-voltage sodium-ion batteries

10.1016/j.jmsy.2026.10.015.abstract: Human–machine collaboration is becoming a defining feature of human-centric manufacturing under Industry 5.0, in which operators participate as indispensable scheduling resources alongside machines. This study addresses the human–machine collaborative flexible job shop scheduling (HMCFJS) problem, where each operation must be matched with a feasible machine-operator combination, and operator assistance precedes machine processing. Compared with conventional flexible job shop scheduling, HMCFJS expands the decision from operation-machine pairs to operation-machine-operator triplets, introducing heterogeneous resource coupling and strong operator competition. To solve this problem, a state-aware priority and goal-conditioned heterogeneous graph reinforcement learning method is proposed. First, a heterogeneous scheduling graph models operations, machines, and operators as three node types connected by precedence and bipartite compatibility edges, forming a tripartite scheduling abstraction in which the operator is an independent capacity-constrained resource. Second, a state-aware priority-guided policy decomposes triplet evaluation into operation selection and machine-operator resource pairing, guiding the policy toward high-potential candidates within the enlarged action space. Third, a goal-conditioned mechanism maps the current scheduling state to a state-dependent goal vector that scalarizes a multi-component reward and conditions graph representation learning for makespan minimization. The framework is trained end-to-end with proximal policy optimization. Finally, experiments show that SGHGRL outperforms the evaluated learning baselines in average makespan across instance scales and generates schedules within seconds after offline training. On large instances, its results are closest among these baselines to the lower makespans obtained by CP-SAT with FIFO initialization and a search budget of 1800 s per instance.
10.1016/j.jmsy.2026.10.015.title: State-aware priority and goal-conditioned heterogeneous graph reinforcement learning for human–machine collaborative flexible job shop scheduling

10.1016/j.cej.2026.184315.abstract: Biodegradable self-powered sensing systems are highly attractive for intelligent logistics and smart packaging. However, their sensing performance is often limited by inadequate control of fiber morphology and insufficient utilization of the piezoelectric responses associated with different crystal phases. In this work, a strategy combining machine learning with crystal phase engineering was developed to fabricate high-performance cellulose acetate (CA)/Ba(Zr0.2Ti0.8)O3-(Ba0.7Ca0.3)TiO3 (BCZT) piezoelectric nanogenerators (PENGs). A machine-learning prediction model was developed to correlate electrospinning parameters with fiber diameter, providing quantitative guidance for regulating fiber morphology. The resulting fibrous structure was associated with relatively uniform dispersion of BCZT fillers, increased interfacial contact, and improved stress transfer, potentially contributing to enhanced interfacial polarization and electromechanical coupling. Among the investigated compositions, the CA-R5T5 composite exhibited the highest piezoelectric output. An intelligent packaging system was further constructed by placing tetragonal-phase PENGs on the top and bottom surfaces to monitor vertical impacts, and rhombohedral-phase PENGs on the sidewalls to detect vibration and tilt. The integrated sensing system achieved real-time transportation monitoring without an external power supply. This work provides an effective strategy for developing sustainable piezoelectric sensing materials by coordinating the optimization of processing parameters, microstructure, and crystal phase, offering promising potential for intelligent packaging and logistics monitoring.
10.1016/j.cej.2026.184315.title: Data-driven fiber morphology optimization and phase-engineered piezoelectric nanogenerators for sustainable intelligent transportation monitoring

10.1016/j.cej.2026.184278.abstract: The trade-off between sustained bacterial growth and cell survival poses a fundamental challenge for efficient biomanufacturing. Challenges such as diminished cell density and compromised viability often arise during the mid-to-late stages of fermentation, thereby hindering the sustained synthesis of target compounds. The quorum sensing (QS) system, via the autoinducer-2 (AI-2) signaling molecule, detects fluctuations in cell density and environmental conditions, thereby triggering the expression of specific genes that orchestrate bacterial behavior. Here, we demonstrate that disruption of Lsr-dependent AI-2 uptake and processing can regulate cell division, thereby improving cell density and viability during fermentation. As a result, the maximum biomass of Escherichia coli Suc260 during fermentation increased by 30.70%, and the titers of the target products increased by 17.91%. This work underscores the critical role of the QS system in regulating bacterial growth and metabolism, offering valuable insights for advancing sustainable biofermentation strategies.
10.1016/j.cej.2026.184278.title: Disruption of Lsr-dependent AI-2 uptake and processing promotes high-density cultivation and chemical production in Escherichia coli

10.1016/j.jmsy.2026.10.020.abstract: Job shop scheduling is a core execution stage decision interface that connects production requirements with shop-floor execution in intelligent manufacturing systems. Existing studies have mainly improved schedule quality for well-defined scheduling tasks, focusing on efficient and feasible operation plans. However, real manufacturing systems require an end-to-end scheduling process that spans requirement understanding, task modeling, algorithm adaptation, and execution feedback, which still lacks systematic support. Large language models (LLMs), with strengths in natural language understanding, contextual reasoning, and interactive feedback, offer a technical path for strengthening key stages of this process. In response to this trend, this survey reviews recent progress in applying LLMs to job shop scheduling and builds a workflow-oriented analytical framework. It analyzes the technical basis and capability boundaries of LLMs in scheduling systems, discusses their role in transforming unstructured shop-floor requirements into entity relations, constraints, and objective expressions, and clarifies how they enhance scheduling reasoning through candidate schedule generation and assistance to existing optimization algorithms. The survey further examines how LLMs extend from offline scheduling support to dynamic execution, where multi-agent collaboration improves the response of scheduling systems to shop-floor disturbances. The review shows that LLMs connect key stages of the scheduling process, enabling intelligent manufacturing systems to better understand unstructured requirements, explain scheduling results, and support human-machine collaborative decisions. However, current research still faces limitations in output reliability, traceable explanation, real-time deployment, cross-scenario generalization, and industrial data security. Future research should further explore domain knowledge enhancement, human-centered scheduling, multi-agent systems, and sustainable manufacturing, enabling LLMs to become trustworthy, controllable, and deployable scheduling components for intelligent manufacturing systems.
10.1016/j.jmsy.2026.10.020.title: Large language models for intelligent job shop scheduling systems: A survey of problem modeling, decision-making, and dynamic rescheduling
10.1016/j.jmsy.2026.10.020.source: ScienceDirect official citation and abstract BibTeX export

10.1016/j.jmsy.2026.10.017.abstract: The effective operation of manufacturing systems fundamentally relies on the efficient flow and control of materials across the shop floor. However, existing approaches primarily focus on functional execution while neglecting the spatial–temporal context of production processes, resulting in limited traceability and weak interpretability. To bridge this gap, this paper introduces the concept of spatial–temporal intelligence (STI) into shop-floor manufacturing and proposes a unified implementation framework with corresponding enabling technologies. To support STI, a CPI-constrained standardized traceability representation, together with a handshake mechanism, is developed to achieve cyber–physical alignment of heterogeneous manufacturing data. On this basis, a domain-specific knowledge graph (KG) is constructed to capture production knowledge, and a spatial–temporal context construction method is developed to integrate real-time localization data, event information, and process dependencies into a coherent representation. Building upon the KG and constructed context, a large language model (LLM)-driven reasoning framework is designed to generate structured, knowledge- and constraint-grounded explanations of operational deviations and their downstream impacts. Experiments conducted in a pilot-scale physical shop-floor testbed demonstrate that the proposed method achieves an explanation correctness of 0.96, exceeding the strongest baseline by 11.8 percentage points, while the cyber–physical alignment mechanism reliably distinguishes compliant, inconsistent, and authorized reconfigured executions. The proposed framework provides a unified foundation for integrating spatial–temporal perception and intelligent reasoning, advancing the development of next-generation smart manufacturing systems.
10.1016/j.jmsy.2026.10.017.title: Towards spatial–temporal intelligence on the shop floor: A cyber–physical internet constrained approach for LLM-based explainable traceability

10.1016/j.foodhyd.2026.113573.abstract: In vitro digestion models enable the study of gastrointestinal processes. In this study, we investigate protein digestion dynamics using hydrogels as substrates together with machine learning (ML) techniques for video-based image analysis to predict digestive conditions. Gelatin hydrogels were crosslinked with transglutaminase (TGase) and immersed in simulated gastric media with varying pH, ionic strength, and pepsin concentration. Their swelling behavior and degree of hydrolysis (DH) were monitored over time. In parallel, videos of the immersed hydrogels were acquired using a camera probe. The videos were analyzed by applying a comparison between a standard feature extraction method of hue saturation values (HSV) and applying representational learning employing a convolutional neural network (CNN) before performing the final classification of the digestion conditions with a multi-layered-perceptron (MLP). TGase-crosslinked gelatin hydrogels exhibit varying swelling and digestion rates, influenced by pH level, ionic strength, and pepsin concentration. Both the CNN-based and the HSV-based approaches determined the DH well over time. The CNN-based approach outperformed the HSV-based approach in identifying pH and ionic strength of the media, while the HSV-based approach better classified the pepsin concentration. The best results were achieved using a 60-minute degradation interval; nevertheless, 20-minute intervals already show predictive performance. The results demonstrate the potential of video-based ML-driven image analysis to monitor protein hydrogel digestion, even with limited data collection, and lay the way for non-invasive in vivo techniques to study digestion.
10.1016/j.foodhyd.2026.113573.title: Predicting in vitro digestion of gelatin hydrogels using machine learning and representation learning for image processing
